body.text: SBV I 5

Bhikṣus desire to know
  the origin of the Śākyas
body.translated_text: The monks desire to know the origin of the <s>Śākyas</s>:

body.text: buddho bhagavān kapilavastuni viharati nyagrodhārāme / atha saṃbahulānāṃ kāpilavāstavānāṃ śākyānāṃ saṃsthāgāre saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ saṃnipatitānām ayam evaṃ rūpo 'bhūd antarākathāsamudāhāraḥ / kuto nirjātā bhavantaḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca śākyānāṃ paurāṇakulavaṃśaś ca / sacet kaścid asmākam upasaṃkramyaivaṃ pṛcchet: kuto nirjātā bhavantaḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca teṣāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti / evaṃ pṛṣṭā vayaṃ kiṃ vyākuryāmaḥ / na ca punar jānīmaḥ kuto nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca teṣāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti / ete vayaṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāmāmaḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavantam etam evārthaṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ, yathā cāsmākaṃ bhagavān vyākaroti tathainaṃ dhārayiṣyāmaḥ iti / atha saṃbahulāḥ kāpilavāstavāḥ śākyā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ / ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ saṃbahulāḥ kāpilavāstavāḥ śākyā bhagavantam idam avocan / ihāsmākaṃ bhadanta saṃbahulānāṃ kāpilavāstavānāṃ śākyānāṃ saṃsthāgāre saṃniṣaṇṇānāṃ saṃnipatitānām ayam evaṃrūpo 'bhūd antarākathāsamudhāhāraḥ / kuto nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca teṣāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśaḥ / sacet kaścid asmākam (
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Kapilavastu</s> in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park. Now, many <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, sitting and assembled in the assembly hall, had this sort of conversation arise among them: 'Whence have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? Who are their foremost [ancestors]? What is their lineage? And what is the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>? If someone were to come to us and ask thus: "Whence have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? Who are their foremost [ancestors]? What is their lineage? And what is their ancient family-dynasty?" — when asked thus, what would we answer? For we do not know whence the <s>Śākyas</s> arose, who their foremost [ancestors] are, what their lineage is, or what their ancient family-dynasty is. Let us approach the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, let us ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> about this very matter; and as the <s>Bhagavān</s> explains to us, so shall we remember it.' Then many <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the many <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here, Venerable Sir, many of us <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, sitting and assembled in the assembly hall, had this sort of conversation arise among us: "Whence have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? Who are their foremost [ancestors]? What is their lineage? And what is their ancient family-dynasty? If someone were to come to us (

) upasaṃkramyaivaṃ pṛcchet kuto nirjātā bhavantaḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca teṣāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti / evaṃ pṛṣṭā vayaṃ kiṃ vyākuryāmaḥ / na ca punar jānīmaḥ kuto nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca teṣāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti / ete vayaṃ yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkramāmaḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavantam etam evārthaṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ, yathā cāsmākaṃ bhagavān vyākariṣyati tathainaṃ dhārayiṣyāmaḥ iti / te vayam etam evārthaṃ paripṛcchāmaḥ: kuto bhagavan nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca śākyānāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti / atha bhagavata etad abhavat / saced ahaṃ śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kuryāṃ sthānam etad vidyate: yad anyatīrthikaparivrājakā evaṃ vadeyuḥ ātmaślāghī śramaṇo gautamo yad icchati tad vyākarotīti / atha ko nu mama śrāvakaḥ
body.translated_text: ) and ask thus: 'Whence have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? Who are their foremost [ancestors]? What is their lineage? And what is their ancient family-dynasty?' — when asked thus, what would we answer? For we do not know whence the <s>Śākyas</s> arose, who their foremost [ancestors] are, what their lineage is, or what their ancient family-dynasty is. Let us approach the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, let us ask the <s>Bhagavān</s> about this very matter; and as the <s>Bhagavān</s> explains to us, so shall we remember it." We are asking about this very matter: Whence, <s>Bhagavan</s>, have the <s>Śākyas</s> arisen? Who are their foremost [ancestors]? What is their lineage? And what is the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'If I myself were to give a doctrinal discourse concerning the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>, it is possible that wandering ascetics of other schools would say: "The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is a self-praiser who declares whatever he wishes." Now, which of my disciples would be capable of giving a doctrinal discourse to the monks concerning the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>?' At that time, the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> was seated and assembled in that very assembly.

body.text: pratibalaḥ syād yaḥ śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya bhikṣūṇāṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kuryāt; tena khalu samayenāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas tasyām eva pariṣadi saṃniṣaṇṇo 'bhūt saṃnipatitaḥ

children.text: The Buddha asks Maudgalyāyana to narrate
children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> asks <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> to narrate:

children.text: tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate: pratibhātu te maudgalyāyana śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya bhikṣūṇāṃ dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kartum / pṛṣṭhaṃ me āvilāyate / tat tāvad āyāmayiṣyāmīti / adhivāsayaty āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvena / atha bhagavān āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā gaṇapuṭāṃ saṃghāṭīṃ śirasy upanidhāya dakṣiṇapārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayati pāde pādam ādhāyālokasaṃjñī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānann utthānasaṃjñām eva manasikurvāṇaḥ / athāyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasyaitad abhavat / yanv ahaṃ tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpadyeyaṃ (

) yathā samāhite citte śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam avalokayeyaṃ kuto nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ kimagraṇyāḥ kimanvayāḥ kaś ca śākyānāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśa iti / athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam avalokayati / adrākṣīd āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam avalokya yato nirjātāḥ śākyāḥ yadagraṇyāḥ yadanvayāḥ yaś ca śākyānāṃ paurāṇaḥ kulavaṃśaḥ / dṛṣṭvā ca punas tasmāt samādher vyutthāya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ / niṣadyāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyānaḥ kapilavāstavāṃś chākyān āmantrayate
children.translated_text: ) that with concentrated mind I may survey the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s> — whence the <s>Śākyas</s> arose, who their foremost [ancestors] are, what their lineage is, and what the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s> is.' Then the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> that with concentrated mind he surveyed the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>. The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> surveyed the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s> and saw whence the <s>Śākyas</s> arose, who their foremost [ancestors] were, what their lineage was, and what the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s> was. Having seen, he then emerged from that <s>samādhi</s> and sat upon a seat prepared before the assembly of monks. Having sat down, the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> addressed the <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>:

There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'It would be fitting for you, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, to give a doctrinal discourse to the monks concerning the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>. My back is aching; I shall rest it for a while.' The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s> by his silence. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>'s assent through his silence, placed his folded outer robe (<s>saṃghāṭī</s>) at his head, lay down on his right side placing foot upon foot, mindful with the perception of light, clearly comprehending, directing his mind to the perception of rising. body.text: The beings in the region of the Ābhāsvara Devas
body.translated_text: The beings in the region of the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> gods:

body.text: bhavati gautamā sa samayo yad ayaṃ lokaḥ saṃvartate; saṃvartamāne loke yadbhūyasā satvā ābhāsvare devanikāye upapadyante; te tatra bhavanti rūpiṇo manomayāḥ avikalā ahīnendriyāḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetāḥ śubhā varṇasthāyinaḥ svayaṃprabhā vihāyasaṃgamāḥ prītibhakṣāḥ prītyāhārāḥ dīrghāyuṣo dīrgham adhvānaṃ tiṣṭhanti / tena khalu samayeneyaṃ mahāpṛthivī ekodakā bhavaty ekārṇavā / yaḥ khalu <ekodakāyā> mahāpṛthivyā ekārṇavāyā upari vāyunā saraḥ saṃgacchati saṃmūrchati santanoti tadyathā payasaḥ pakvasya śītībhūtasya upari vāyunā saraḥ saṃgacchati saṃmūrchati santanoti / evam ekodakāyā mahāpṛthivyā ekārṇavāyā upari vāyunā saraḥ saṃgacchati saṃmūrcchati santanoti / sa bhavati pṛthivīraso varṇasaṃpanno gandhasaṃpanno rasasaṃpannaḥ; evaṃrūpo varṇena tadyathā navanītam; evaṃrūpo rasena tadyathā kṣaudramadhv aneḍakam / bhavati gautamā sa samayo yad ayaṃ loko vivartate; vivartamāne loke tata eke satvā āyuḥkṣayāt karmakṣayāt puṇyakṣayād ābhāsvarād
body.translated_text: There is a time, O <s>Gautamas</s>, when this world contracts (<s>saṃvartate</s>). When the world is contracting, for the most part beings are reborn in the <s>Ābhāsvara</s> (Radiant) divine abode. There they exist as form-beings, mind-made, complete, with unimpaired faculties, endowed with all major and minor limbs, beautiful, established in [radiant] complexion, self-luminous, moving through the sky, feeding on joy, nourished by joy, long-lived, abiding for a long duration. At that time, this great earth becomes a single mass of water, a single ocean. Upon that great earth that is a single mass of water, a single ocean, by the action of the wind, a crust forms, solidifies, and spreads — just as upon boiled milk that has cooled, by the action of the wind, a skin forms, solidifies, and spreads. Just so, upon this great earth that is a single mass of water, a single ocean, by the action of the wind, a crust forms, solidifies, and spreads. That is the earth-essence (<s>pṛthivīrasa</s>), endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, endowed with flavor. Such is its color — like fresh butter. Such is its flavor — like pure, unadulterated bee-honey. There is a time, O <s>Gautamas</s>, when this world evolves (<s>vivartate</s>). When the world is evolving, some beings, through the exhaustion of their lifespan, through the exhaustion of their <s>karma</s>, through the exhaustion of their merit, fall from the <s>Ābhāsvara</s>

body.translated_text: ) divine abode and come here to the human realm of common destiny. Here they exist as form-beings, mind-made, complete, with unimpaired faculties, endowed with all major and minor limbs, beautiful, established in [radiant] complexion, self-luminous, moving through the sky, feeding on joy, nourished by joy, long-lived, abiding for a long duration. At that time, neither the sun nor the moon has appeared in the world; nor have the constellations; nor moments, instants, or hours; nor nights and days; nor months, fortnights, seasons, or years appeared in the world. Neither woman nor man is distinguished — beings are simply designated as 'being.'

children.translated_text: ) They ate that as their food and sustenance, long-lived, abiding for a long duration. Among them, whoever consumed less food became beautiful in complexion; whoever consumed more food became ugly in complexion. Thus, depending on the twofold distinction in food, a twofold distinction in complexion became apparent. When the twofold distinction in complexion existed, one being despised another: 'Ha! Being, I am beautiful in complexion; you are ugly!' Because of those beings who were proud of their complexion, because of their adoption of those very sinful, unwholesome qualities, the earth-essence (<s>pṛthivīrasa</s>) disappeared. When the earth-essence disappeared, those beings, coming together and assembling, grieved, lamented, and wailed. They said thus: 'Alas, the flavor! Alas, the flavor!' Just as nowadays humans, having eaten some delicious, excellent food, recollecting those very old words and syllables, say thus: 'Alas, the flavor! Alas, the flavor!' Just so, those beings, O <s>Gautamas</s>, when the earth-essence disappeared, coming together and assembling, grieved, lamented, and wailed. They said thus: 'Alas, the flavor! Alas, the flavor!' But they do not know the meaning: 'This is the meaning of that saying, this is the meaning of that saying.'

Then a certain being of greedy nature tasted the earth-essence with his fingertip. As he tasted it, he relished it; as he relished it, he consumed it by the method of taking morsels of food. Other beings saw that being tasting the earth-essence with his fingertip — as he tasted it, he relished it; as he relished it, he consumed it by the method of taking morsels. Having seen, those beings too began to taste the earth-essence with their fingertips. As they tasted it, they relished it; as they relished it, they consumed it by the method of taking morsels. When those beings consumed the earth-essence by the method of taking morsels of food, roughness and heaviness descended upon their bodies. Their beautiful radiant complexion disappeared. Darkness appeared in the world. It is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>), O <s>Gautamas</s>, that from the appearance of darkness in the world, the sun and moon appear in the world; the constellations, moments, instants, and hours, nights and days, months, fortnights, seasons, and years appear in the world. body.translated_text: Then the differentiation of faculties appeared among them. Some had the female faculty; some had the male faculty. Those who had the female faculty and those who had the male faculty gazed at each other eye to eye. As they gazed at each other eye to eye, they became attracted; as they became attracted, they became agitated; as they became agitated, they engaged in sexual intercourse. Other beings saw a being engaging in intercourse with another being; having seen, they threw dirt, clods of earth, gravel, and potsherds. They said thus: 'Shame on you, vulgar being, doer of improper deeds! Shame on you, vulgar being, doer of improper deeds! How can you, sir, defile a being?' Just as nowadays, when a bride is being led in marriage, people throw powder, perfume, garlands, and strips of cloth, and say: 'Be happy, bride! Be happy, bride!' — just so, those beings, having seen a being engaging in intercourse with another being, threw dirt, clods of earth, gravel, and potsherds. They said thus: 'Shame on you, vulgar being, <shame on you, vulgar being, doer of improper deeds!> How can you, sir, defile a being?' Thus, O <s>Gautamas</s>, what was formerly considered improper is now considered proper; what was formerly considered undisciplined is now considered disciplined; what was formerly considered blameworthy is now considered praiseworthy. They would banish that one for a day, two, three, or even seven days. And because those beings had become excessively devoted to that sinful, evil practice, they were eager to build houses, [thinking:] 'Here we shall do the improper deed, here we shall do the improper deed.' The designation 'house' (<s>agāra</s>) arose. This, O <s>Gautamas</s>, is the ancient, original (

body.translated_text: ) we are form-beings, mind-made, complete, with unimpaired faculties, endowed with all major and minor limbs, beautiful, established in [radiant] complexion, self-luminous, moving through the sky, feeding on joy, nourished by joy, long-lived, abiding for a long duration. For us, the earth-essence (<s>pṛthivīrasa</s>) appeared, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, endowed with flavor. We consumed the earth-essence by the method of taking morsels of food. Since we consumed the earth-essence by the method of taking morsels of food, roughness and heaviness descended upon our bodies; that beautiful radiant complexion disappeared; darkness appeared in the world. We, feeding on that, nourished by that, long-lived, abide for a long duration. Among us, whoever consumed little food became beautiful in complexion; whoever consumed abundant food became ugly in complexion — thus, from the twofold measure of food, a twofold measure of complexion became apparent. When there was this twofold measure of complexion, being despised being: 'Alas, being! I am beautiful in complexion; you are ugly in complexion!' Because of the pride in complexion among us beings, on account of the adoption of those very evil, unwholesome qualities (<s>dharmas</s>), the earth-essence disappeared. When the earth-essence disappeared, the earth-crust (<s>pṛthivīparpaṭaka</s>) appeared, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, endowed with flavor. Because of the pride in complexion among us beings, on account of the adoption of those very evil, unwholesome qualities, the earth-crust disappeared. When the earth-crust disappeared, a forest creeper (<s>vanalatā</s>) appeared, endowed with color, endowed with fragrance, endowed with flavor. Because of the pride in complexion among us beings, on account of the adoption of those very evil, unwholesome qualities, the forest creeper disappeared. When the forest creeper disappeared, an uncultivated, self-sown rice (<s>śāli</s>) bearing grain appeared — without husk, without chaff, pure, clean, four finger-breadths [tall], wrapped [in its sheath]. Cut in the evening, it would be ripe and regrown by morning — thus, cut and cut again, it would grow back, and appeared as though uncut. We, feeding on that, nourished by that, long-lived, abide for a long duration. Since we consumed the uncultivated, self-sown grain-bearing rice by hoarding and accumulating, therefore its husk and chaff enveloped the grain (

body.translated_text: 'Let us come together and assemble, measure out fields, establish boundaries, and set landmarks — "this is yours, this is mine."' They came together, assembled, and measured out fields; they established boundaries; they set landmarks. This, O <s>Gautamas</s>, is the ancient and primary origin of the activity of setting landmarks in the world. And that was through <s>dharma</s>, not through <s>adharma</s>. Herein, this <s>dharma</s> is the supreme <s>dharma</s> of the <s>Jinendras</s> (conqueror-lords). Then a certain being, while standing at his own rice, took another's rice without it being given. Another being saw that being standing at his own rice, taking another's rice without it being given. Having seen, he said this to that being: 'Why do you, sir, standing at your own rice, take another's rice [without permission]? Go, sir! Do not do this again!' A second and third time, that being, standing at his own rice, took another's rice without it being given. That being saw him, a second and third time, standing at his own rice, taking another's rice without it being given. Having seen, he said this to that being: 'Why do you, sir, standing at your own rice, take another's rice [without permission]?' He seized him, dragged him, and even brought him down into the midst of the assembly: 'This being, sirs, standing at his own rice, takes another's rice without it being given!' Then those beings said to that being: 'Why do you, sir, standing at your own rice, up to three times take another's rice without it being given? Go, sir! Do not do this again!' Then that being said to those beings: 'Sirs, I have been seized, dragged, and even publicly shamed by this being on account of rice!' Then those beings said to the being [who seized him]: 'Why do you, sir, seize a being, drag him, and even bring him down into the midst of the assembly on account of rice? (

body.translated_text: and encourage those who should be encouraged. And from what our fields shall yield, we shall give him a rightful share of the land.' They came together and assembled, and whichever being among them was the most handsome, the most pleasing to look at, the most inspiring of confidence, and the most distinguished — him they established as lord of the fields. And they said thus: 'Come, sir! Restrain those among us who should be restrained; encourage those who should be encouraged. And from what our fields shall yield, we shall give you a rightful share of the land.' He restrained those who should be restrained and encouraged those who should be encouraged. And from what their fields yielded, they gave him a rightful share of the land. Approved (<s>saṃmata</s>) by the great assembly — [thus] the designation <s>Mahāsaṃmata</s> (Great Elect) arose. Lord of the fields, he protects from harm (<s>kṣatāt trāyate</s>) — [thus] the designation <s>Kṣatriya</s> arose. He delights (<s>rañjayati</s>) the people through <s>dharma</s>, through virtuous conduct and behavior, through wise conduct and behavior — [thus] the designation <s>Rājā</s> (King) arose. Of King <s>Mahāsaṃmata</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, human beings received the designation 'beings' (<s>satvā</s>). Of King <s>Mahāsaṃmata</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, <s>Roca</s> was the son. Of King <s>Roca</s>, human beings received the designation <s>Ehikā</s> ('Come here!'). Of <s>Roca</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, <s>Kalyāṇa</s> was the son. Of King <s>Kalyāṇa</s>, human beings received the designation <s>Tilakā</s>. Of <s>Kalyāṇa</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, <s>Varakalyāṇa</s> was the son. Of King <s>Varakalyāṇa</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, human beings received the designation <s>Abhrakaṇṭhā</s>. Of <s>Varakalyāṇa</s>, <s>Upoṣadha</s> was the son. Of King <s>Upoṣadha</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, human beings received the designation <s>Stālajaṅghā</s>. Of King <s>Upoṣadha</s> (

body.translated_text: ) a boil appeared on the crown of his head — soft, very soft, like cotton floss or kapok floss — it never caused any affliction. Through the process of ripening, it burst open. A prince was born — handsome, pleasing to look at, inspiring confidence, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>). Born from the crown — [thus] the designation <s>Mūrdhnāta</s> ('Crown-born') arose. As soon as the prince was born, he was brought into the inner palace. King <s>Upoṣadha</s> had sixty thousand women. The breasts of all of them flowed with milk. Each one said: 'Nurse me! Nurse me!' (<s>māṃ dhāpaya</s>) — [thus] the designation <s>Māndhātā</s> arose. At the time when King <s>Māndhātā</s> exercised sovereignty, at that time human beings were thinkers, evaluators, and examiners. Having thought, evaluated, and examined, they measured out separate craft-stations and work-stations — [thus] they received the designation <s>Manuja</s> ('descendants of Manu'). These, O <s>Gautamas</s>, are the six kings who had immortal lifespans and immeasurable lifespans.

body.translated_text: Of King <s>Māndhātā</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, a boil appeared on his right thigh — soft, very soft, like cotton floss or kapok floss — it caused no affliction. Through the process of ripening, it burst open. A prince was born — handsome, pleasing to look at, inspiring confidence, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>).

body.translated_text: ) it burst open; a prince was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>); born from the left thigh, the name <s>Upacāru</s> arose for him. That prince was of great supernatural power and great might — even now he has exercised sovereign lordship over three continents. O <s>Gautamas</s>, on king <s>Upacāru</s>'s right foot a boil appeared, soft and very soft, like cotton-fluff or kapok-fluff; it caused no affliction whatsoever, and through the course of ripening it burst open; a prince was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man; born from the right foot, the name <s>Cārumān</s> arose for him. That prince was of great supernatural power and great might — even now he has exercised sovereign lordship over two continents. O <s>Gautamas</s>, on king <s>Cārumān</s>'s left foot a boil appeared, soft and very soft, like cotton-fluff or kapok-fluff; it caused no affliction whatsoever, and through the course of ripening it burst open; a prince was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man; born from the left foot, the name <s>Upacārumān</s> arose for him. That prince was of great supernatural power and great might — even now he has exercised sovereign lordship over one continent. Thus indeed, O <s>Gautamas</s>, king <s>Mahāsaṃmata</s>'s son was <s>Roca</s>; <s>Roca</s>'s son was <s>Kalyāṇa</s>; <s>Kalyāṇa</s>'s was <s>Varakalyāṇa</s>; <s>Varakalyāṇa</s>'s was <s>Upoṣadha</s>; <s>Upoṣadha</s>'s was <s>Māndhātā</s>; <s>Māndhātā</s>'s was <s>Cāru</s>; <s>Cāru</s>'s was <s>Upacāru</s>; <s>Upacāru</s>'s was <s>Cārumān</s>; <s>Cārumān</s>'s was <s>Upacārumān</s>; then <s>Ruci</s>, <s>Suruci</s>, <s>Muci</s>, <s>Mucilinda</s>, <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Aṅgīratha</s>, <s>Bhṛṅga</s>, <s>Bhagīratha</s>, <s>Sagara</s>, <s>Sāgara</s>, <s>Mahāsāgara</s>, <s>Śakuni</s>, <s>Mahāśakuni</s>, <s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Upakuśa</s>, <s>Mahākuśa</s>, <s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Mahāsudarśana</s>, <s>Praṇaya</s>, <s>Mahāpraṇaya</s>, <s>Praṇāda</s>, <s>Mahāpraṇāda</s>, <s>Prabhaṅkara</s>, <s>Pratāpavān</s>, <s>Meru</s>, <s>Merumān</s>, <s>Merumanta</s>, <s>Arci</s>, <s>Arciṣmān</s>, <s>Arciṣmanta</s>; O <s>Gautamas</s>, through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Arciṣmān</s>, (

body.translated_text: ) in the city of <s>Potalaka</s> there were ten thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Arindama</s>; because he subdues enemies (<s>arīn damayati</s>), the name <s>Arindama</s> arose for him. O <s>Gautamas</s>, through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Arindama</s>, in <s>Ayodhyā</s> there were fifty-four thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>; because he conquers the unconquered (<s>ajitaṃ jayati</s>), [the name] <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>

body.text: iti saṃjñā udapādi / ajitaṃjayasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā vārāṇasyāṃ triṣaṣṭī rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako duṣprasaho nāma rājābhūt / duṣprasahasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā kiṃpilye nagare caturaśītirājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako brahmadatto nāma rājābhūt / brahmadattasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā hastināpure dvātriṃśad rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako hastidatto nāma rājābhūt / hastidattasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā takṣaśilāyāṃ paṃca rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako kālīśo nāma rājābhūt / kālīśasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā urasāyāṃ nagaryāṃ dvātriṃśad rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako nagnajin nāma rājābhūt / nagnajino gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā ajitaṃjaye nagare dvātriṃśad rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako jayadatto nāma rājābhūt / jayadattasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā kanyakubjāyāṃ nagaryāṃ dvādaśarājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako jayaseno nāma rājābhūt / jayasenasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā caṃpāyāṃ nagaryāṃ aṣṭādaśa rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako nāgadevo nāma rājābhūt / nāgadevasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā tālipye nagare paṃcaviṃśatī (
body.translated_text: — the name arose for him. O <s>Gautamas</s>, through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s>, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there were sixty-three thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Duṣprasaha</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Duṣprasaha</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Kimpilya</s> there were eighty-four thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Brahmadatta</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in <s>Hastināpura</s> there were thirty-two thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Hastidatta</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Hastidatta</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in <s>Takṣaśilā</s> there were five thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Kālīśa</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Kālīśa</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Urasā</s> there were thirty-two thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Nagnajit</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Nagnajit</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Ajitaṃjaya</s> there were thirty-two thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Jayadatta</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Jayadatta</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Kanyakubja</s> there were twelve thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Jayasena</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Jayasena</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Campā</s> there were eighteen thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Nāgadeva</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Nāgadeva</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Tālipya</s> there were twenty-five (

body.text: SBV I 19
body.translated_text: SBV I 19

body.text: ) rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako naradevo nāma rājābhūt / naradevasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā tāmaliptyāṃ nagaryāṃ dvādaśa rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimakaḥ sāgaradevo nāma rājābhūt / sāgaradevasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā dantapuryāṃ nagaryāṃ aṣṭādaśa rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimakaḥ sumatir nāma rājābhūt / sumater gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā rājagṛhe nagare paṃcaviṃsatī rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimakas tamonudo nāma rājābhūt / tamonudasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ ekaśatarājaśatam abhūt; teṣām apaścimako mahendraseno nāma rājābhūt / mahendrasenasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā kuśāvatyāṃ nagaryāṃ caturaśītirājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimakaḥ samudraseno nāma rājābhūt / samudrasenasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api potalake nagare rājasahasram abhūt; teṣām apaścimakas tapaṃcaro nāma rājābhūt /
body.translated_text: ) thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Naradeva</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Naradeva</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Tāmaliptī</s> there were twelve thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Sāgaradeva</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Sāgaradeva</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Dantapurī</s> there were eighteen thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Sumati</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Sumati</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> there were twenty-five thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Tamonuda</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Tamonuda</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, again in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there were ten thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Mahendrasena</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Mahendrasena</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Kuśāvatī</s> there were eighty-four thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Samudrasena</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Samudrasena</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, again in the city of <s>Potalaka</s> there were one thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Tapaṃcara</s>.

body.text: tapaṃcarasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api kuśāvatyāṃ nagaryāṃ caturaśītirājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako mahīmukho nāma rājābhūt / mahīmukhasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ rājaśatasahasram abhūt; teṣām apaścimako mahīpatir nāma rājābhūt / mahīpater gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api ayodhyāyāṃ nagaryāṃ śatasahasram abhūt; teṣām apaścimako mahīdharo nāma rājābhūt / mahīdharasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā mithilāyāṃ nagaryāṃ caturaśītirājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimako mahādevo nāma rājābhūt / mahādevasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api mithilāyāṃ nagaryāṃ (
body.translated_text: Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Tapaṃcara</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, again in the city of <s>Kuśāvatī</s> there were eighty-four thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Mahīmukha</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Mahīmukha</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, again in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there were one hundred thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Mahīpati</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Mahīpati</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, again in the city of <s>Ayodhyā</s> there were one hundred thousand [kings]; the last of them was a king named <s>Mahīdhara</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Mahīdhara</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Mithilā</s> there were eighty-four thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Mahādeva</s>. Through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Mahādeva</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, again in the city of <s>Mithilā</s> (

body.text: SBV I 20
body.translated_text: SBV I 20

body.text: ) caturaśītimahādevasahasrāṇi rājarṣaya brahmacaryam acārṣuḥ; teṣām apaścimako nimir nāma rājābhūt / nimer nimagno dṛḍhanemiḥ khanur upakhanuḥ khanumān khanumantaḥ sudṛśaḥ samadṛśaḥ śrutaseno dharmaseno vidito mahāvidito viditasena aśoko vigataśoko dṛḍhaseno jarāsandha dhundhumāraḥ aruṇo diśāṃpatir eṇḍaḥ saṃkakarakaḥ ānanda ādarśamukho janakaḥ saṃjanako janarṣabhaḥ annapānaḥ pracurānnapānaḥ ajito 'parājitaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ supratiṣṭhitaḥ mahābalo mahābalavāhanaḥ sumatir dṛḍhavāhanaḥ śatadhanuḥ citradhanuḥ navatidhanuḥ vijitadhanur dṛḍhadhanur daśarathaḥ śataratho navatirathaḥ nararṣabhaḥ citraratho vicitraratho dṛḍharathaḥ; dṛḍharathasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā sāṃkāsye nagare saptasaptatī rājasahasrāṇy abhūvan; teṣām apaścimakaḥ ambarīṣo nāma rājābhūt / ambarīṣasya gautamā rājñaḥ nāgasaṃpālaḥ putraḥ; nāgasaṃpālasya gautamā rajñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ ekaśataṃ rājaśatam abhūt; teṣām apaścimako krkir nāma rājābhūt / tena khalu samayena kāśyapo nāma śāstā loke utpannaḥ; tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān; yasya antike bodhisatvo bhagavān āyatyāṃ bodhāya praṇidhāya (
body.translated_text: ) eighty-four thousand <s>Mahādeva</s>s were royal sages (<s>rājarṣi</s>) who practiced celibate conduct (<s>brahmacarya</s>); the last of them was a king named <s>Nimi</s>. From <s>Nimi</s>: <s>Nimagn</s>a, <s>Dṛḍhanemi</s>, <s>Khanu</s>, <s>Upakhanu</s>, <s>Khanumān</s>, <s>Khanumanta</s>, <s>Sudṛśa</s>, <s>Samadṛśa</s>, <s>Śrutasena</s>, <s>Dharmasena</s>, <s>Vidita</s>, <s>Mahāvidita</s>, <s>Viditasena</s>, <s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Vigataśoka</s>, <s>Dṛḍhasena</s>, <s>Jarāsandha</s>, <s>Dhundhumāra</s>, <s>Aruṇa</s>, <s>Diśāṃpati</s>, <s>Eṇḍa</s>, <s>Saṃkakaraka</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, <s>Ādarśamukha</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Saṃjanaka</s>, <s>Janarṣabha</s>, <s>Annapāna</s>, <s>Pracurānnapāna</s>, <s>Ajita</s>, <s>Aparājita</s>, <s>Pratiṣṭhita</s>, <s>Supratiṣṭhita</s>, <s>Mahābala</s>, <s>Mahābalavāhana</s>, <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Dṛḍhavāhana</s>, <s>Śatadhanu</s>, <s>Citradhanu</s>, <s>Navatidhanu</s>, <s>Vijitadhanu</s>, <s>Dṛḍhadhanu</s>, <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Śataratha</s>, <s>Navatiratha</s>, <s>Nararṣabha</s>, <s>Citraratha</s>, <s>Vicitraratha</s>, <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>; through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in the city of <s>Sāṃkāśya</s> there were seventy-seven thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Ambarīṣa</s>. King <s>Ambarīṣa</s>'s son, O <s>Gautamas</s>, was <s>Nāgasaṃpāla</s>; through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Nāgasaṃpāla</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, again in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there were ten thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Kṛki</s>. At that time, a teacher named <s>Kāśyapa</s> had arisen in the world — a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), endowed with knowledge and conduct (<s>vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna</s>), Well-gone (<s>Sugata</s>), Knower of the World (<s>Lokavid</s>), Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Men to be Tamed (<s>Puruṣadamyasārathi</s>), Teacher of Gods and Humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>; in whose presence the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, having made his aspiration for future awakening (<s>Bodhi</s>), (

body.text: SBV I 21
body.translated_text: SBV I 21

body.text: ) brahmacaryaṃ caritvā tuṣite devanikāye upapannaḥ / kṛker gautamā rājñaḥ sujātaḥ putraḥ; sujātasya gautamā rājñaḥ putraprapautṛkayā naptṛpranaptṛkayā punar api potalake nagare ekaśataṃ rājaśatam abhūt; teṣām apaścimako karṇo nāma rājābhūt
body.translated_text: ) having practiced celibate conduct (<s>brahmacarya</s>), was reborn in the <s>Tuṣita</s> divine abode. King <s>Kṛki</s>'s son, O <s>Gautamas</s>, was <s>Sujāta</s>; through the sons and grandsons, nephews and great-nephews of king <s>Sujāta</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, again in the city of <s>Potalaka</s> there were ten thousand kings; the last of them was a king named <s>Karṇa</s>.

body.text: Story of Gautama, the progenitor of Ikṣvāku
body.translated_text: Story of <s>Gautama</s>, the progenitor of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>

body.text: karṇasya gautamā rājño dvau gautamo bharadvājaś ca; tayor gautamo naiṣkarmyābhinandi; bharadvājo rājyābhinandī; sa pitaraṃ paśyati dharmādharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayantaṃ; sa saṃlakṣayati: aham api pitur atyayād rājā bhaviṣyāmy aham api dharmādharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayitvā narakaparāyaṇo bhaviṣyāmi; kim atra prāptakālam agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajiṣye iti viditvā yena karṇo rājā tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya pādayor nipatya vijñāpayati; tātānujānīhi māṃ pravrajāmi śraddhayā agārād anagārikām iti; sa kathayati: putra yasyārthe yajñā ijyante homā hūyante tapāṃsi tapyante tat tava karatalagataṃ rājyaṃ; mamātyayād rājā bhaviṣyasi / kimarthaṃ pravrajasīti / sa kathayati: tāta na śakyaṃ mayā dharmādharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayituṃ; tad anujānīhi pravrajāmīti; tato rājñā avaśyaṃ nirbandhaṃ jñātvā anujñātaḥ / tena khalu samayena anyatamasminn āśramapade kṛṣṇadvaipāyano nāma ṛṣiḥ prativasati; tato gautamaḥ kumāro rājñā samanujñāto hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita udagraprītisaumanasyajāto yena kṛṣṇadvaipāyano riṣis tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya vinīteryāpathapādābhivandanaṃ (
body.translated_text: King <s>Karṇa</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, had two sons: <s>Gautama</s> and <s>Bharadvāja</s>. Of those two, <s>Gautama</s> delighted in renunciation; <s>Bharadvāja</s> delighted in kingship. He saw his father ruling the kingdom by both righteous and unrighteous means. He reflected: 'I too, after my father's passing, will become king; I too, having ruled the kingdom by righteous and unrighteous means, will be destined for hell. What is timely here? I shall go forth from the household life to the homeless life.' Having understood this, he approached king <s>Karṇa</s>. Having approached and fallen at his feet, he petitioned: 'Father, please give me permission — I wish to go forth from the household life to the homeless life out of faith.' He replied: 'Son, that for the sake of which sacrifices are offered, oblations are poured, and austerities (<s>tapas</s>) are practiced — that kingdom is in the palm of your hand; after my passing, you will become king. Why do you wish to go forth?' He replied: 'Father, I am unable to rule the kingdom by righteous and unrighteous means; therefore, please give me permission — I wish to go forth.' Then the king, knowing his firm insistence was unavoidable, gave permission. At that time, in a certain hermitage (<s>āśramapada</s>), a sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>) named <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> was dwelling. Then prince <s>Gautama</s>, having been given permission by the king, joyful, delighted, elated, filled with gladness and happiness, approached the sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s>. Having approached, with humble deportment, having bowed at his feet, (

body.text: SBV I 22
body.translated_text: SBV I 22

body.text: ) kṛtvā kathayati pravrajyārthī pravrajāyasva mām iti / sa tena pravrajitaḥ; kṛṣṇadvaipāyano ṛṣiḥ phalamūlāṃbubhakṣaḥ; tasyāpi gautama ṛṣiḥ gautama ṛṣiḥ iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā / yāvad apareṇa samayena karṇo rājā kālagataḥ; bharadvājakumāro rājyaiśvaryādhipatye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ pitryaṃ rājyaṃ kārayati; yāvad apareṇa samayena gautamo ṛṣir upādhyāyāsya kathayati: upādhyāya na śaknomi āraṇyakābhir oṣadhībhir yāpayituṃ; grāmāntaṃ samavasarāmīti; sa kathayati: putra śobhanaṃ; grāme vā araṇye vā prativasatā riṣiṇā sarvathā indriyāṇi rakṣitavyānīti; gaccha tvaṃ potalasāmantakena śākhāparṇakuṭiṃ kṛtvā vāsaṃ kalpaya; evam upādhyāya ity uktvā gautama riṣiḥ potalakasāmantakena śākhāparṇakuṭiṃ kṛtvā avasthitaḥ; tena khalu samayena potalake nagare bhadrā nāma rūpājīvanī prativasati; mṛṇālaś ca nāmnā dhūrtapuruṣaḥ; tena vastrālaṃkāram anupreṣitaṃ paricāraṇāya; sā tadvastrālaṃkāraṃ prāvṛtya saṃprasthitā; anyatamaś ca puruṣaḥ paṃcakārṣāpaṇaśatāny ādāyopasthitaḥ; bhadre āgaccha paricāraya iti; sā saṃlakṣayati: yadi gamiṣyāmi paṃcakārṣāpaṇaśatāni lapsye; adākṣiṇyaṃ caitad gṛhāgataṃ pratyākhyāyānyatra gamanam iti; tayā preṣyadārikābhihitā: gaccha mṛṇālasya kathaya āryā kathayati na tāvad ahaṃ sajjā paścād āgamiṣyāmīti; tayāpi tasya gatvārocitaṃ; so 'pi puruṣo bahukaraṇīyaḥ; sa
body.translated_text: ) having done so, he speaks to the one desiring ordination: 'Ordain me into the renunciant life.' He was ordained by him. The sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> subsisted on fruits, roots, and water. He too acquired the designation '<s>Gautama</s> the sage, <s>Gautama</s> the sage.' Then at another time, King <s>Karṇa</s> passed away. Prince <s>Bhāradvāja</s> was established in the sovereignty and dominion of the kingdom and administered his ancestral kingdom. Then at another time, the sage <s>Gautama</s> said to his preceptor: 'Preceptor, I am unable to sustain myself on forest herbs; let me go to a village.' He replied: 'Son, very well. Whether dwelling in a village or in the forest, a sage must in every way guard his senses. Go and make a hut of branches near <s>Potalaka</s> and arrange your dwelling there.' Having said 'Yes, preceptor,' the sage <s>Gautama</s> made a hut of branches near <s>Potalaka</s> and settled there. Now at that time, in the city of <s>Potalaka</s>, there lived a courtesan named <s>Bhadrā</s>, and a scoundrel named <s>Mṛṇāla</s>. He had sent clothing and ornaments for her services. She put on those clothes and ornaments and set out. Then a certain man came forward offering five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>: '<s>Bhadrā</s>, come and attend to me.' She thought: 'If I go, I will obtain five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>; but it would be discourteous to refuse one who has come to my house and go elsewhere.' She told her maidservant: 'Go and tell <s>Mṛṇāla</s>: "The lady says she is not yet ready; she will come later."' The girl went and informed him. That man too had many affairs to attend to. He

The girl went and informed <s>Bhadrā</s>. Then she went out to that garden. The scoundrel <s>Mṛṇāla</s> said: 'Is it proper for you to entertain another man with my clothing and ornaments?' She replied: 'Noble sir, indeed the fault is mine. But women are ever-erring; please forgive me.' Then he, filled with anger, drew his sword from its sheath and took her life. Then the maidservant raised a great uproar: 'The lady has been murdered! The lady has been murdered!' Hearing this, people came running from all sides. Now the sage <s>Gautama</s> was dwelling in that very hermitage. Then that scoundrel <s>Mṛṇāla</s>, terrified, concealed the blood-stained sword before the sage <s>Gautama</s> and mingled into the great crowd of people. The crowd, seeing the blood-stained sword, said: 'This renunciant has taken <s>Bhadrā</s>'s life.' Then, surrounding the sage <s>Gautama</s>, they spoke angrily: 'You, renunciant, you bear the banner of a sage yet commit such a deed!' He said: 'What have I done?' They said: 'You consorted with <s>Bhadrā</s> and then took her life.' He said: 'Peace — I am not the doer of this deed.' Though he spoke peacefully, the great crowd bound him tightly with his arms behind his back and brought him before the king: 'Lord, this renunciant consorted with <s>Bhadrā</s> and took her life.' Kings who do not investigate [said]: 'If so, then go — impale him on a stake. This renunciant is abandoned by me.' body.text: sa bāṣpagadgadakaṇṭhaḥ aśruparyākulekṣaṇaḥ karuṇadīnavilaṃbitākṣaraṃ kathayati: hā vatsa kim idaṃ; so 'pi gadgadakaṇṭho marmavedanoparodhajanitaviṣādaḥ kathayaty upādhyāya karmāṇi; kim anyad bhaviṣyatīti / sa kathayati: vatsa nāsi kṣata upahato vā; tāta kṣato 'haṃ kāyena no tu cittena; vatsa kathaṃ jñāyate; upādhyāya satyopayācanaṃ kariṣye śṛṇu yena satyena satyavacanena kṣato 'haṃ kāyena no tu cittena tena satyena satyavacanena yeyam upādhyāyasya kṛṣṇavarṇā cchavir iyaṃ suvarṇavarṇā bhaved; bhāvitādhyāśayo 'sau mahātmā; vacanāvasānasamanantaram eva kṛṣṇadvaipāyanasya ṛṣeḥ kṛṣṇavarṇā cchavir antarhitā; suvarṇavarṇā saṃvṛttā / sāmantakena śabdo visṛtaḥ kṛṣṇadvaipāyanariṣiḥ suvarṇavarṇaḥ saṃvṛtta iti / tasya suvarṇadvaipāyanaḥ suvarṇadvaipāyana iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā; sa paraṃ vismayam upagataḥ; tato 'sau gautamariṣiḥ kathayati: upādhyāya itaś cyutasya me kā gatir bhaviṣyati kā upapattiḥ ko 'bhisaṃparāya iti / sa kathayati: vatsa brāhmaṇāḥ kathayanti: aputrasya gatir nāstīti; asti tvayā kiṃcid apatyam utpāditam; upādhyāya kumāra evāhaṃ; strītantre aprakṛtijñaḥ; pitrā rājyanimittaṃ protsāhyamānaḥ pravrajitaḥ; kuto mamāpatyasamutpattiḥ; vatsa yady evaṃ pūrvopabhuktaviṣayānusmaraṇaṃ kuru; upādhyāya gāḍhavedanābhyāhatasya me idānīṃ chidyamāneṣu marmasu mucyamāneṣu sandhiṣu (
body.translated_text: His throat choked with tears, his eyes overflowing with tears, he spoke with words slow and piteous with grief: 'Alas, my child, what is this?' He too, with choked throat, afflicted by the grief born of the obstruction of bodily agony, said: 'Preceptor, it is <s>karma</s>; what else could it be?' He said: 'Child, are you cut or wounded?' 'Father, I am wounded in body, but not in mind.' 'Child, how is this known?' 'Preceptor, I shall make a truth-declaration (<s>satyopayācana</s>). Listen: By this truth, by this truthful word — that I am wounded in body but not in mind — by this truth, by this truthful word, may the dark complexion of the preceptor <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> become golden.' He was a great being of cultivated aspiration. At the very end of his words, the dark complexion of the sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> disappeared and became golden. The news spread through the surrounding area: 'The sage <s>Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana</s> has become golden-complexioned!' He acquired the designation '<s>Suvarṇadvaipāyana</s>, <s>Suvarṇadvaipāyana</s>.' He was overcome with supreme wonder. Then the sage <s>Gautama</s> said: 'Preceptor, when I die here, what will be my destiny, what my rebirth, what my future state?' He said: 'Child, the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> say: "There is no [good] destiny for one without a son." Have you produced any offspring?' 'Preceptor, I was but a youth, unknowing of the ways of women. My father urged me to renounce for the sake of the kingdom. How could I have produced offspring?' 'Child, if so, then recollect sensory experiences previously enjoyed.' 'Preceptor, I am struck by intense pain; now, as my vital points are being cut and my joints are coming apart, (

body.translated_text: ) with my mind fixed solely on death, how can recollection of previously enjoyed sensory experiences arise?' His preceptor was one who had attained the five supernatural powers (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>). Through his supernatural power, he created a great storm of wind and rain. Drops of rain fell upon his body. Then, from the touch of cool water and wind, the pain was suppressed. He began to recollect previously enjoyed sensory experiences. As he recollected the passion of sexual intercourse, two drops of semen fell mixed with blood. Four things are inconceivable: contemplation of the self, contemplation of the world, contemplation of the <s>karma</s>-fruition of beings, and contemplation of the <s>Buddha</s>-domain of <s>Buddhas</s>. From those two drops of semen, two eggs appeared. At the time of sunrise, ripened by the sun's rays, they split open. Two boys were born. Not far away there was a sugarcane field. They entered there. Then the sun's rays became more intense. The sage <s>Gautama</s>, scorched by the sun's rays, died. Then the sage <s>Suvarṇadvaipāyana</s> came. He saw that he had died. Near the stake he saw that the eggs had split open and the shells remained. Following the trail here and there, he entered the sugarcane field and saw the two boys. He began to reflect: 'Whose sons are these?' He saw: 'They are the sons of the sage <s>Gautama</s>.' Then even greater affection arose in him. He took them to the hermitage, nursed them, nourished them, and raised them.

body.translated_text: He then proceeded to establish their names: 'They were born at the time of sunrise, ripened by the sun's rays; therefore they belong to the solar lineage (<s>sūryagotra</s>).' Thus their first designation '<s>Sūryagotra</s>' was established. 'They are the sons of the sage <s>Gautama</s>, so they are <s>Gautamas</s>.' Thus their second designation '<s>Gautama</s>' was established. 'They issued from his own body, so they are <s>Āṅgīrasas</s>.' Thus their third designation '<s>Āṅgīrasa</s>' was established. 'They were found in a sugarcane field, so they are <s>Ikṣvākus</s>.' Thus their fourth designation '<s>Ikṣvāku</s>' was established. Then at another time, King <s>Bhāradvāja</s> died without a son. The ministers assembled and began to hold a council: 'Sirs, whom shall we now anoint as king?' Others said: 'His brother <s>Gautama</s> has gone forth among the sages. This kingdom belongs to him by hereditary succession. Let us anoint him.' Having deliberated, they approached the sage <s>Suvarṇadvaipāyana</s>. Having approached and fallen at his feet, they said: 'Great sage, where has <s>Gautama</s> gone?' He replied: 'He was killed by you yourselves.' 'Great sage, we do not even remember seeing him. How could we have killed him?' (

body.translated_text: ) 'I shall remind you.' 'Very well.' He then reminded them. They said: 'Great sage, if that is so, let there be no more mention of his name. He was an evildoer, not to be spoken of.' 'What evil did he do?' 'This and that.' 'He was not an evildoer. He was innocent and harmless, yet was killed by you.' 'How so?' Then he narrated in detail what had happened. They became remorseful and said: 'Great sage, if that is so, then we are the evildoers, not he.' While they were speaking thus, the two boys approached the sage. The ministers said: 'Great sage, whose boys are these?' He replied: 'They are the sons of that very man.' 'How were they born, and what are their names?' He then narrated in detail, including their origin. The ministers, having heard, were overcome with supreme wonder. Having taken leave of the sage, they anointed the elder of the two boys with the royal consecration. He too died without a son. Then the second, younger one was anointed. He acquired the designation 'King <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, King <s>Ikṣvāku</s>.' From King <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, through a succession of sons, grandsons, great-grandsons, and great-great-grandsons, in the city of <s>Potalaka</s> there were one hundred and one <s>Ikṣvāku</s> kings.

body.translated_text: The last among them was an <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king named <s>Virūḍhaka</s>. <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Gautama</s> <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, had four sons: <s>Ulkāmukha</s>, <s>Karakarṇī</s>, <s>Hastiniyaṃsa</s>, and <s>Nūpuraka</s>. In the course of time, his chief queen passed away. He sat with his cheek resting on his hand, consumed by worry. The ministers said: 'Why does Your Majesty sit with his cheek on his hand, consumed by worry?' He said: 'My chief queen has passed away. How should I not be consumed by worry?' 'Your Majesty, if so, why is a chief queen not sought for Your Majesty? There are daughters of the neighboring kings' (

body.translated_text: The king said: 'These princes are eager for the kingdom. While they exist as rivals, who will give me his daughter?' 'Let Your Majesty set his mind at ease; we shall search.' Then a certain king's daughter was found — beautiful, lovely, pleasing, and suitable for queenship. Having found her, they went to that king's presence. Through intermediaries, they informed the king. The king gave the command: 'Let them be summoned.' Then they were sent to the king's presence. Falling at his feet, they sat down after exchanging courtesies. Having found an occasion for conversation, they looked directly at the king and said: 'Your Majesty, may there be well-being, well-being!' The king said: 'What do you seek?' '<s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king's chief queen has passed away. We request a maiden for his sake.' The king said: 'Excellent — a fitting bridegroom. However, I give her on a condition: if my daughter bears a son, he shall be established in sovereign royal authority.' 'Your Majesty, let it be so. We shall go and inform Your Majesty [i.e., our king].' Having gone, they reported the full account to <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king. The king said: 'Gentlemen, this is not proper — to pass over the elder princes who are eager for the kingdom and establish the youngest.' 'Your Majesty, this matter is uncertain. Let the queen be brought first. Let Your Majesty enjoy, delight, and sport with her. It is not known whether she will bear a son, or a daughter, or will be barren.' The king said: 'Gentlemen, if so, go ahead. Then let the agreement stand.' They went and accepted her. Then the king married her with great pomp and ceremony. And she became dear to the king. He enjoyed, delighted, and sported with her. As he was enjoying, delighting, and sporting with her, in the course of time the queen became pregnant. At the completion of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, lovely, and pleasing. At his birth, having performed the birth ceremony, a name was established: 'What shall the boy's name be?' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, since even before his birth he (

body.translated_text: )?' They said: 'It is His Majesty's.' The princes began to turn back. The ministers said: 'Princes, enter! Why do you turn back?' They said: 'It is the king's garden. How can we enter?' The ministers said: 'Whether the king sports or the princes sport — what conflict is there?' They entered and began to play. The ministers told the king: 'Your Majesty, the garden has been beautifully prepared. It is time for Your Majesty to see it.' The king set out. He heard the din and noise in the garden. Having heard, he again asked the ministers: 'Gentlemen, a din and noise is heard in the garden. Who is there?' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, it is the princes.' 'If so, the princes are abandoned by me!' The ministers fell at his feet and said: 'Your Majesty, let the princes be forgiven. Let them not be abandoned!' The king said: 'Very well, let it be so.' They began to banish them. Falling at the king's feet they said: 'Your Majesty, if so, please command that whichever retainers wish to go with us shall not be prevented.' The king gave the command. They set out. The people of the realm were devoted to them. Together with them, a great multitude set out. For seven days the city gate of <s>Potalaka</s> stood open as the multitude departed. The ministers reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, if the city gate is not closed, <s>Potalaka</s> will soon be deserted.' 'If so, close the gates.' Then those princes, taking their respective sisters, gradually reached the foothills of the <s>Himālaya</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Bhagīrathī</s>, not far from the hermitage of the sage <s>Kapila</s>. There they built leaf-huts of branches and arranged their dwelling. Hunting and killing deer, they sustained their livelihood. Three times a day they would visit the hermitage of the sage <s>Kapila</s>. Intoxicated by the pride of fresh youth, exceedingly tormented by passion and desire, they became increasingly pale and emaciated

'Is it permissible for us to do so, great sage?' 'It is permissible, gentlemen, as has been done formerly by <s>Kṣatriyas</s> who have lost their kingdoms.' children.translated_text: ) have been born to them.' 'Is it possible, stewards, for the princes to do thus?' 'Your Majesty, it is possible.' Then <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> king, raising his body upright and extending his right arm, made a joyful exclamation: 'The princes are truly capable (<s>śākyā</s>)! The princes are supremely capable (<s>paramaśākyā</s>)!' Since a word was uttered by a being of great authority — 'The princes are truly <s>Śākya</s>! The princes are supremely <s>Śākya</s>!' — the designation <s>Śākya</s> came into being.

The sage <s>Kapila</s>, because of the thorn of noise, could not attain one-pointedness of mind (<s>cittaikāgratā</s>) in his <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations). He said: 'Gentlemen, beware. I shall go elsewhere.' 'Great sage, why?' 'I cannot attain one-pointedness of mind; the <s>dhyānas</s> have the thorn of noise.' 'Great sage, you stay right here. We shall go elsewhere. But please grant us a plot of land.' 'Gentlemen, very well.' The sages, those great souls, fulfill desired wishes. Then, taking a golden pitcher, he marked out a city by pouring streams of water in the shape of a city. Because the sage <s>Kapila</s> gave up the site (<s>vastu</s>) for their dwelling, the name <s>Kapilavastu</s> — '<s>Kapila</s>'s site' — came into being. They prospered there. A great multitude grew. Due to crowding, they could not grow further. The gods, knowing their minds, pointed out another region to them. Going there, they built a second city. The name <s>Devadṛśa</s> — 'Seen-by-the-gods' — came into being. Then they came together, assembled, and began to confer: 'Gentlemen, we were banished because of taking wives of equal [rank]. Therefore none of us shall take a second wife of equal [rank]. One should be content with just one.' So they marry only one wife of equal [rank] and not a second. Then at a later time, King <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, remembering his dear sons, addressed the ministers: 'Ho, stewards! Where are those princes now?' They reported in detail: 'Your Majesty, they were banished on account of a certain matter. Taking their respective sisters, they departed from here. On the foothills of the <s>Himālaya</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Bhagīrathī</s>, not far from the hermitage of the sage <s>Kapila</s>, they have arranged their dwelling. body.translated_text: <s>Rājyābhinandī</s> was anointed to kingship; he too died without a son. <s>Ulkāmukha</s> was established in royal sovereignty and dominion; he too died without a son. <s>Karakarṇī</s> became king; he too died without a son. <s>Hastiniyaṃsa</s> became king; he too died without a son. <s>Nūpuraka</s> became king; his son was <s>Opuraka</s>; <s>Opuraka</s>'s [son was] <s>Gopuraka</s>. Of King <s>Gopuraka</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, through sons and grandsons, through descendants and great-descendants, there were fifty-five thousand kings in the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. The last of them was <s>Daśaratha</s>, <s>Śatarataha</s>, <s>Navatirataha</s>, <s>Citrarataha</s>, <s>Vijitaratha</s>, <s>Dṛḍharatha</s>, <s>Daśadhanu</s>, <s>Śatadhanu</s>, <s>Navatidhanu</s>, <s>Vijitadhanu</s>, <s>Citradhanu</s>, <s>Dṛḍhadhanu</s>. Of <s>Dṛḍhadhanu</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, there were two sons: <s>Siṃhahanu</s> and <s>Siṃhanādī</s>. However many archers there are in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, <s>Siṃhahanu</s> is declared foremost among them. Of <s>Siṃhahanu</s>, O <s>Gautamas</s>, there were four sons: <s>Śuddhodana</s>, <s>Śuklodana</s>, <s>Droṇodana</s>, and <s>Amṛtodana</s>; and four daughters: <s>Śuddhā</s>, <s>Śuklā</s>, <s>Droṇā</s>, and <s>Amṛtikā</s>. <s>Śuddhodana</s> had two sons: the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the Venerable <s>Nanda</s>. Of <s>Śuklodana</s> (

body.text: SBV I 32

) dvau putrau; āyuṣmāṃś ca tiṣyo bhadrakaś ca śākyarājaḥ; droṇodanasya dvau putrau mahānāmā āyuṣmāṃś cāniruddhaḥ; amṛtodanasya dvau putrau āyuṣmān ānando devadattaś ca; śuddhāyāḥ suprabuddhaḥ putraḥ; śuklāyāḥ putro mālī; droṇāyā bhāddālī; amṛtikāyāḥ śaivalaḥ bhagavato rāhulaḥ putra iti gautamā rāhule mahāsaṃmatavaṃśaḥ pratiṣṭhitaḥ; ucchinnā bhavanetrī vikṣīṇo jātisaṃsāro nāstīdānīṃ punarbhavaḥ
body.translated_text: ) there were two sons: the Venerable <s>Tiṣya</s> and <s>Bhadraka</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> king. <s>Droṇodana</s> had two sons: <s>Mahānāma</s> and the Venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>. <s>Amṛtodana</s> had two sons: the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> and <s>Devadatta</s>. <s>Śuddhā</s>'s son was <s>Suprabuddha</s>. <s>Śuklā</s>'s son was <s>Mālī</s>. <s>Droṇā</s>'s [son was] <s>Bhāddālī</s>. <s>Amṛtikā</s>'s [son was] <s>Śaivala</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>'s son is <s>Rāhula</s>. Thus, O <s>Gautamas</s>, in <s>Rāhula</s> the lineage of <s>Mahāsaṃmata</s> is established. The stream of becoming is cut off; the cycle of births is exhausted; there is now no further rebirth.

body.text: Buddha's remarks
body.translated_text: <s>Buddha</s>'s remarks

body.text: atha bhagavān āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya kathāparyavasānaṃ viditvā utthāya niṣaṇṇaḥ; niṣadyāyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate: sādhu sādhu maudgalyāyana sādhu sādhu khalu tvaṃ maudgalyāyana yas tvaṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ purastāc chākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavamśam ārabhya dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kathayasi; punar api tvaṃ maudgalyāyana abhīkṣṇam api tvaṃ śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya dharmyāṃ kathāṃ kathaya; tad eṣāṃ bhaviṣyati dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya; tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: udgṛhṇīta yūyaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya dharmyāṃ kathāṃ dhārayituṃ grāhayituṃ vācayituṃ; tat kasya hetoḥ; arthopasaṃhitā bhikṣavaḥ śākyānāṃ paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya dharmyā kathā; arthopasaṃhitā brahmacaryopasaṃhitā; yuktam eva bhikṣavaḥ śraddhayā pravrajitena kulaputreṇa śākyānāṃ (
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having learned that the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>'s discourse had concluded, rose and sat down. Having sat down, he addressed the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Well done, well done, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>! Well done indeed, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, that you have given a doctrinal discourse to the monks concerning the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>. Furthermore, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, you should frequently give doctrinal discourses concerning the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>; that will be for the long-lasting benefit, welfare, and happiness of these [monks].' There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Learn, O monks, the doctrinal discourse concerning the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>, so as to retain it, master it, and recite it. For what reason? The doctrinal discourse concerning the ancient family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>, O monks, is connected with meaning and connected with the holy life. It is indeed fitting, O monks, for a son of good family who has gone forth out of faith, to retain, master, and recite the doctrinal discourse concerning the ancient (

body.text: SBV I 33
) paurāṇaṃ kulavaṃśam ārabhya dharmyāṃ kathāṃ dhārayituṃ grāhayituṃ vācayitum; atha kāpilavastavāḥ
body.translated_text: ) family-dynasty of the <s>Śākyas</s>.' Then the <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>

body.text: śākyā bhagavato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntāḥ
body.translated_text: having rejoiced in and approved the words of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

body.text: Siṃhahanu's reign
body.translated_text: <s>Siṃhahanu</s>'s reign

body.text: tena khalu samayena kapilavastuni nagare siṃhahanur nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca; devadṛśe nagare suprabuddho rājyaṃ rājā kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca; suprabuddhasya rājño lumbinī nāmāgramahiṣī abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā janapadakalyāṇī; devadṛśe 'nyatamo gṛhapatiḥ prativasaty āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī; tasyārāmaḥ puṣpasaṃpannaḥ phalasaṃpannaḥ śālisaṃpanno nānāvihaganikūjitaḥ; tasyābhirāmatayā rājā kālānukālaṃ tatra gatvā sārdham antaḥpureṇa ratikrīḍāṃ pratyanubhavati; lumbinyās taṃ dṛṣṭvā spṛhā utpannā; sa kathayati: deva mamaitam ārāmam anuprayaccheti; rājā kathayati: gṛhapatisantako 'yam ārāmaḥ; katham anuprayacchāmi; yadi tvam ārāmeṇārthinī anyaṃ tavārthāya śobhanataraṃ kārayāmīti; tato rājñā suprabuddhena lumbinyā arthāya tadviśiṣṭatara ārāmaḥ kāritaḥ; tasya luṃbinīvanaṃ lumbinīvanam iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā; siṃhahanor dīrgharātram ayam āśāsakaḥ: aho bata me kule cakravartī utpadyeta iti; suprabuddhasyāpi rājño dīrgharātram ayam āśāsakaḥ: aho bata me siṃhahanunā sārdhaṃ saṃbandhaḥ syād iti; yāvat tasyāpareṇa samayena devyā sārdhaṃ krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā; sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā; dārikā jātā abhirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetā; (
body.translated_text: At that time, in the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a king named <s>Siṃhahanu</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. In the city of <s>Devadṛśa</s>, King <s>Suprabuddha</s> was ruling his kingdom — prosperous, flourishing, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. King <s>Suprabuddha</s> had a chief queen named <s>Lumbinī</s>, who was beautiful, lovely, graceful, the loveliest in the land. In <s>Devadṛśa</s> there dwelt a certain householder, wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, of vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. He had a garden endowed with flowers, endowed with fruits, endowed with rice, resounding with various birds. Because of its beauty, the king would go there from time to time and enjoy pleasures and amusements with his inner court. <s>Lumbinī</s>, having seen it, felt a longing. She said: 'Lord, please give me this garden.' The king said: 'This garden belongs to the householder; how can I give it? If you desire a garden, I shall have another, more beautiful one made for your sake.' Then King <s>Suprabuddha</s> had a garden superior to that one made for <s>Lumbinī</s>'s sake. It came to be known as '<s>Lumbinīvana</s>' — the grove of <s>Lumbinī</s>. <s>Siṃhahanu</s> had this long-held aspiration: 'Oh, if only a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) would be born in my family!' King <s>Suprabuddha</s> also had this long-held aspiration: 'Oh, if only I could have an alliance with <s>Siṃhahanu</s>!' Then at a later time, while he was playing, enjoying himself, and attending upon the queen, in due course his wife became pregnant. After eight or nine months had passed, she gave birth; a girl was born, beautiful, lovely, graceful, endowed with all major and minor limbs. (

body.text: SBV I 34

) tasyā rūpaśobhayā suprabuddho rājā sāntaḥpuro devadṛśanivāsī janakāyaś ca paraṃ vismayam upagataḥ; sandigdhamanāś ca saṃvṛttaḥ: kim iyaṃ dārikā āhosvid viśvakarmanirmiteyaṃ māyeti; tasyās trīṇi saptakāny ekaviṃśatidivasān vistareṇa jātāyā jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate: kiṃ bhavatu dārikāyā nāmeti; amātyāḥ kathayanti: deva devadṛśanivāsijanakāyā rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu vipravadante; kecit kathayanti: dārikā evāsau pūrvakarmavipākābhiniṣpannā evaṃ varṇarūpaśobheti; apare kathayanti: nāsau dārikā; kiṃtarhi viśvakarmanirmitā sā māyeti tasmād bhavatu dārikāyā māyeti nāma; tasya māyeti nāma kṛtaṃ; māyā dārikā aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradattā pūrvavad yāvan mahatī saṃvṛttā; sā naimittikair vyākṛtā; putraṃ janayiṣyaty anekalakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ; rājā bhaviṣyati balacakravartī; bhūyo 'py asya krīḍato rammāṇasya paricārayataḥ duhitā
body.translated_text: ) By the beauty of her form, King <s>Suprabuddha</s> together with his inner court, the inhabitants of <s>Devadṛśa</s>, and the populace were overcome with the greatest wonder. He became doubtful in mind: 'Is this a [human] girl, or is she an illusion created by <s>Viśvakarman</s>?' On the twenty-first day, having performed the birth-celebration in detail for the newborn, a name was to be established: 'What shall be the girl's name?' The ministers said: 'Lord, the inhabitants and populace of <s>Devadṛśa</s> are debating in the streets, roads, crossroads, and intersections. Some say: "That girl was produced by the ripening of past <s>karma</s> to have such beauty of form and complexion." Others say: "She is not a [human] girl; rather, she is an illusion (<s>māyā</s>) created by <s>Viśvakarman</s>." Therefore, let the girl's name be <s>Māyā</s>.' Her name was made <s>Māyā</s>. The girl <s>Māyā</s> was entrusted to eight nurses, and as before she grew up to be mature. The soothsayers prophesied about her: 'She will give birth to a son endowed with many auspicious marks. He will become a king, a powerful <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).' Furthermore, while he was playing, enjoying himself, and attending upon [his wife], a daughter

body.text: jātā pratirūpā darśanīyā prāsādikā paramayā varṇapuṣkalatayā samanvāgatā; tasyā janmani sarvaṃ tan nagaram udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsitaṃ; na cāsyāḥ śakyate sarvathā rūpaśobhāṃ varṇayituṃ; yathā māyāyās tasyā api vistareṇa jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate; kiṃ bhavatu dārikā nāmeti; amātyāḥ kathayanti: asyā rūpaśobhā yan māyāṃ vyatiricya vartate tasmād bhavatu mahāmāyeti; sāpy unnītā vardhitā mahatī saṃvṛttā; sā naimittikair vyākṛtā; putraṃ janayiṣyati dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtaṃ; sa rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartīti; suprabuddhena rājñā siṃhahanor dūto 'nupreṣitaḥ; dve duhitarau jāte māyā mahāmāyā ca; tatraikā vyākṛtā putraṃ janayiṣyati lakṣaṇasaṃpannaṃ; sa rājā bhaviṣyati balacakravartīti; dvitīyā vyākṛtā putraṃ janayiṣyati dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣanaiḥ (
body.translated_text: was born, beautiful, lovely, graceful, endowed with supreme excellence of complexion. At her birth, that entire city was illuminated with an extraordinary radiance; and the beauty of her form could not in any way be fully described. Just as for <s>Māyā</s>, when the birth-celebration was performed in detail for her newborn, a name was to be established: 'What shall be the girl's name?' The ministers said: 'Her beauty surpasses even <s>Māyā</s>'s; therefore, let her be named <s>Mahāmāyā</s> (Great <s>Māyā</s>).' She too was raised and grew up to maturity. The soothsayers prophesied about her: 'She will give birth to a son adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>). He will become a king, a <s>cakravartin</s>.' King <s>Suprabuddha</s> sent a messenger to <s>Siṃhahanu</s>: 'Two daughters have been born, <s>Māyā</s> and <s>Mahāmāyā</s>. Of these, one has been prophesied to give birth to a son endowed with auspicious marks — he will become a king, a powerful <s>cakravartin</s>. The second has been prophesied to give birth to a son adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person (

body.text: SBV I 35

) samalaṅkṛtaṃ; sa rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartīti; anayor yābhipretā śuddhodanasya kumārasyārthāyānayeti; siṃhahanunā pratisandeśo dattaḥ, dvābhyām api kumārasya prayojanaṃ; kiṃ tu na dve sadṛśe bhārye ekasyopasthāpayitavye iti yaivaṃ vyākṛtā putraṃ janayiṣyati dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtaṃ sa rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartīti, eṣā tāvat pratīṣṭā; dvitīyāyā arthāya gaṇam avalokayiṣyāmīti; tena sā pañcaśataparivārā preṣitā; tena khalu samayena śākyānāṃ pāṇḍavā nāma khaṣāḥ prativiruddhāḥ; śākyāḥ saṃbhūya rājñaḥ siṃhahanoḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntāḥ; deva pāṇḍavaiḥ khaṣair upadrutāḥ sma, sāhāyyaṃ kalpayeti; sa kathayati bhavanto vṛddho 'haṃ na śaknomi taiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃgrāmayituṃ; deva śuddhodanaṃ kumāram anupreṣaya; samayato 'nupreṣayāmi yadi kumārasya yathābhipretaṃ varaṃ prārthayato 'nuprayacchata; te kathayanti: deva evaṃ bhavatu prayacchāmaḥ; rājñā caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ datvā śuddhodanaḥ kumāraḥ preṣitaḥ; tena te khaṣāḥ hataprahatavidhvastāḥ kṛtāḥ; tataḥ śākyāḥ parituṣṭāḥ siṃhahano rājñaḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntāḥ; deva kumāreṇa pāṇḍavā khaṣāḥ hataprahatāḥ vidhvastāḥ kṛtāḥ; parituṣṭā smaḥ; vada kumārasya kaṃ varam anuprayacchāmaḥ; bhavantaḥ śākyaiḥ kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ na kenacid dve sadṛśe bhārye upasthāpayitavye iti; deva kiṃ mucyatāṃ kriyākāraḥ; sa kathayati: sutarāṃ baddhavyo na moktavyaḥ; kiṃ tu kumārasyaikaṃ varam anuprayacchatha, dvitīyāṃ sadṛśīṃ bhāryām upasthāpayituṃ; deva śobhanam; evaṃ kriyatāṃ; tataḥ siṃhahanunā suprabuddhasya lekho 'nupreṣitaḥ avalokito
mayā gaṇaḥ; dvitīyāṃ duhitaram anupreṣayeti; tena sāpi pañcaśataparivārā preṣitā; śuddhodanena kumāreṇa dve api pariṇīte (
body.translated_text: ) — he will become a king, a <s>cakravartin</s>. Whichever of these you prefer, send for her for Prince <s>Śuddhodana</s>.' <s>Siṃhahanu</s> sent a reply: 'The prince has need of both. However, two equal wives should not be provided for one [prince].' The one who was prophesied to give birth to a son adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person, who will become a king, a <s>cakravartin</s> — let her be reserved for now; for the second, I shall look over the assembly [of eligible brides]. He sent her with an entourage of five hundred. At that time, enemies called the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> <s>Khaṣas</s> had risen against the <s>Śākyas</s>. The <s>Śākyas</s>, having assembled, approached King <s>Siṃhahanu</s>: 'Lord, we are threatened by the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> <s>Khaṣas</s>; please arrange assistance.' He said: 'Sirs, I am old; I am unable to wage war against them.' 'Lord, please send Prince <s>Śuddhodana</s>.' 'I shall send him on condition that you grant the prince whatever boon he requests.' They said: 'Lord, so be it; we shall grant it.' The king gave him a fourfold army and sent Prince <s>Śuddhodana</s>. By him those <s>Khaṣas</s> were struck, beaten, and routed. Then the <s>Śākyas</s>, delighted, approached King <s>Siṃhahanu</s>: 'Lord, the prince has struck, beaten, and routed the <s>Pāṇḍava</s> <s>Khaṣas</s>. We are delighted. Tell us — what boon shall we grant the prince?' 'Sirs, the <s>Śākyas</s> have made a covenant that no one shall provide two equal wives [for one man].' 'Lord, let the covenant be annulled.' He said: 'On the contrary, it should be further strengthened, not annulled. But grant the prince one boon: to provide a second equal wife.' 'Lord, excellent; let it be done.' Then <s>Siṃhahanu</s> sent a letter to <s>Suprabuddha</s>: 'I have looked over the assembly. Send the second daughter.' He sent her too with an entourage of five hundred. Prince <s>Śuddhodana</s> married both. (

body.text: SBV I 36
Śuddhodana succeeds Siṃhahanu and the descent of the Buddha
body.translated_text: <s>Śuddhodana</s> succeeds <s>Siṃhahanu</s> and the descent of the <s>Buddha</s>

body.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena siṃhahanū rājā kālagataḥ; kapilavastuni śuddhodano rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ cākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ
body.translated_text: Then at a later time, King <s>Siṃhahanu</s> died. In <s>Kapilavastu</s>, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> ruled his kingdom — prosperous, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people.

body.translated_text: and at a later time, together with Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, he went to the upper terrace of the palace and enjoyed, delighted, and sported with music without men [present]. For it is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that a <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven surveys the world with five examinations (<s>avalokana</s>): examination of birth, examination of region, examination of time, examination of lineage, and examination of the woman. (1) For what reason do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> make the examination of birth? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven thinks: 'In what kind of birth do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> take rebirth?' He sees: in a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family or a <s>Kṣatriya</s> family. Therein, sometimes <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> are considered of high family; sometimes <s>Kṣatriyas</s>. Now, however, <s>Kṣatriyas</s> are considered of high family. 'Let me take rebirth in a <s>Kṣatriya</s> family; let there not be occasion for others to say: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took rebirth in a contemptible birth."' For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has, from beginningless time, performed and accumulated <s>karma</s> that conduces to non-reproach; for the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are teachers of the <s>Dharma</s> whose fruit is never barren. For this reason, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> make the examination of birth. (2) For what reason do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> make the examination of region? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'In what kind of region do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> take rebirth?' He sees the region that is rich in sugarcane, rice, garlands, cows, and buffaloes, teeming with hundreds of mendicants, free from robbers and bandits, inhabited by noble people. He thinks: 'This is the Middle Country (<s>Madhyadeśa</s>), rich in sugarcane, rice, garlands, cows, and buffaloes, teeming with hundreds of mendicants, free from robbers and bandits, inhabited by noble people. Let me take rebirth in the Middle Country. Let there not be occasion for others to say: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> (
