body.translated_text: ) took rebirth in a border region."' For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has, from beginningless time, performed and accumulated <s>karma</s> that conduces to non-reproach; for the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are teachers of the <s>Dharma</s> whose fruit is never barren. For this reason, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> make the examination of region. (3) For what reason do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> make the examination of time? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'At what kind of time do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> take rebirth in <s>Jambudvīpa</s>?' When the lifespan of beings is on the increase, when humans live eighty thousand years or more, they do not take rebirth; when the lifespan is on the decrease, when humans live one hundred years or less, they do not take rebirth. For what reason do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> not take rebirth when humans live eighty thousand years or more? For humans who live eighty thousand years are hard to disturb, hard to make understand — dull, of soft faculties, heedless, abounding in pleasure, and unfit vessels for the truths. And when the lifespan is on the decrease, below one hundred years, the five corruptions (<s>kaṣāya</s>) become dominant — namely, corruption of lifespan (<s>āyuḥkaṣāya</s>), corruption of defilements (<s>kleśakaṣāya</s>), corruption of beings (<s>satvakaṣāya</s>), corruption of views (<s>dṛṣṭikaṣāya</s>), and corruption of the age (<s>kalpakaṣāya</s>). 'Let there not be occasion for others to say: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took rebirth at a time when the five corruptions were dominant."' For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has, from beginningless time, performed and accumulated <s>karma</s> that conduces to non-reproach; and the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are teachers of the <s>Dharma</s> whose fruit is never barren

Let there not be occasion for others to say: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took rebirth in an inferior family."' For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has, from beginningless time, performed and accumulated <s>karma</s> (

anākṣepasaṃvartanīyaṃ karma kṛtam upacitam; <avandhyaphaladharmadeśikāś ca buddhā bhagavantaḥ>; anena kāraṇena bodhisatvāḥ stryavalokanaṃ kurvanti; atha bodhisatvaḥ pañca vyavalokanāni vyavalokya ṣaṭ kāmāvacarān devāṃs trir anuśrāvayati ito 'haṃ mārṣās tuṣitād devanikāyāc cyutvā manuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ grahīṣyāmi rājñaḥ śuddhodanasyāgramahiṣyāḥ kukṣau; tasya putratvam adhigamya amṛtam adhigamiṣyāmi; yo yuṣmākam amṛtenārthī sa manuṣyeṣu pratisandhiṃ gṛhṇātu bhūyo madhyadeśa iti; evam uktās tuṣitakāyikā devā bodhisatvam idam avocan: yat khalu bodhisatva jānīyā etarhi kalikaluṣo lokaḥ krūrasantānaprajā ākulīkṛtaś ca jaṃbūdvipaḥ ṣaḍbhis tārkikaiḥ ṣaḍbhir ānuśravikaiḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ samāpattṛbhiḥ; tatra ṣaṭ tārkikāḥ katame? tadyathā pūraṇaḥ kāśyapaḥ (
body.translated_text: ) that conduces to non-reproach; and the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are teachers of the <s>Dharma</s> whose fruit is never barren. For this reason, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> make the examination of lineage. (5) For what reason do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> make the examination of the woman? The <s>Bodhisattva</s> thinks: 'In the womb of what kind of woman do <s>Bodhisattvas</s> take rebirth?' He sees a woman who is beautiful, virtuous, of good family, well-born, one who increases the family's [honor], and who in the presence of former <s>Buddhas</s> has made the aspiration: 'Oh, may I become the mother of a <s>Buddha</s>!' — one who is able to bear the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in her womb for ten months, and who does not neglect her own welfare. He thinks: 'This <s>Mahāmāyā</s>, for seven generations on both the maternal and paternal side, is of unblemished conduct — beautiful, virtuous, well-born, one who increases the family's [honor]; she is able to bear the <s>Bodhisattva</s> in her womb for ten months and not neglect her own welfare. For <s>Mahāmāyā</s> has, in the presence of former <s>Buddhas</s>, made the weighty aspiration: "Oh, may I become the mother of a <s>Buddha</s>!" Let there not be occasion for others to say: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> took rebirth in the womb of a woman not endowed with the [auspicious] marks."' For the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has, from beginningless time, performed and accumulated <s>karma</s> that conduces to non-reproach; and the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, are teachers of the <s>Dharma</s> whose fruit is never barren. For this reason, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> make the examination of the woman. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having made the five examinations, announced three times to the gods of the six desire-realms (<s>kāmāvacara</s>): 'From this <s>Tuṣita</s> divine abode, sirs, I shall pass away and take rebirth among humans, in the womb of the chief queen of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Having attained sonship to him, I shall attain the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>). Whoever among you desires the deathless, let him take rebirth among humans in the Middle Country.' Thus addressed, the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods said this to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'May the <s>Bodhisattva</s> know that now the world is defiled by the corruption of the dark age (<s>kali</s>), with cruel and harsh beings as progeny, and <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is thrown into confusion by six rationalists (<s>tārkika</s>), six traditionalists (<s>ānuśravika</s>), and six practitioners of meditative attainments (<s>samāpattṛ</s>). Of these, who are the six rationalists? Namely, <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s> (

body.translated_text: , the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Puṣkarasāri</s>, and the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Lohitya</s>. Who are the six practitioners? Namely, <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s>, <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>, <s>Subhadra</s> the wanderer, <s>Sañjayī</s> the young man, the sage <s>Asita</s>, and <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> the matted-hair ascetic. Here, however, for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, a seat is prepared extending twelve <s>yojanas</s> for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. And we think thus: "The <s>Dharma</s> that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven will teach — having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, we shall practice accordingly, such that it will be for our long-lasting welfare, benefit, and happiness."' Thus addressed, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> said this to the <s>Tuṣita</s> gods: 'In that case, sirs, let all musical instruments be sounded!'

'Whoever among you, sirs, desires the deathless, let him take rebirth in the Middle Country, traveling among the six great cities.' <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, thought: 'This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to take rebirth in the womb of Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s>. Let me provide her with nourishment and purify her womb.' Having thus understood, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, provided nourishment to Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s> and purified her womb. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> dwelling in <s>Tuṣita</s> heaven, having made the five examinations and announced three times to the gods of the six desire-realms, in the appearance of an elephant, in the middle watch of the night, descended into the womb of Queen <s>Mahāmāyā</s>. And he said:
He who had vowed to rescue the world,
having bidden farewell to the gods, descended from there. /
He entered the womb of the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage
like the young sun [entering] a twilight bank of clouds. //

The <s>Tuṣita</s> deities sounded all musical instruments. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, having filled a conch, declared: 'Which among these, sirs, is the loudest sound?' 'The conch sound, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'Just as this conch sound, sirs, stands having overpowered all instruments, even so shall I, having descended to <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, overpower the six rationalists, the six traditionalists, and the six practitioners, and attain the deathless. I shall satisfy the world with the deathless. I shall fill the conch of impermanence. I shall beat the drum of emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>). I shall roar the lion's roar of non-self (<s>nairātmya</s>).' Having thus understood, he spoke this verse:
As a single lion scatters many packs of beasts,
as a single thunderbolt cleaves many peaked mountains, /
as a single <s>Śakra</s> conquers many lords of <s>Dānavas</s>,
as a single sun dispels all darkness — // (

children.translated_text: Just as a vast cloud, well-gathered,
full of water, driven by the force of the wind —
so, in like manner, the sage entering the womb,
like the sun approaching a mass of clouds after a long time. //

It is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having fallen from the <s>Tuṣita</s> divine abode, descended into his mother's womb, at that very time there was a great earthquake; and this entire world was suffused with a magnificent radiance; even those world-interstices — dark, gloomy, shrouded in blind darkness — where these two, the sun and moon, so mighty in supernatural power and so great in majesty, do not experience each other's radiance — even those at that time were suffused with a magnificent radiance; the beings reborn there cannot see even their own outstretched arm; but by that radiance, seeing other beings, they recognized: 'Other beings too have been reborn here! Other beings too have been reborn here!'

It is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> descended into his mother's womb, at that time <s>Śakra</s> <s>Devendra</s> stationed four divine sons as guardians of the mother — bearing swords, bearing spears, bearing lances, bearing javelins — [saying:] 'Let no one harm the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, whether human or non-human.' It is the natural law that at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained in his mother's womb, he remained as if enclosed in a sheath, untouched by the impurity of the womb, by the impurity of the afterbirth, by the impurity of blood, or by any other unclean and defiling substance; just as a jewel-gem placed upon <s>Kāśika</s> cloth — neither does the jewel-gem stain the <s>Kāśika</s> cloth, nor does the <s>Kāśika</s> cloth stain the jewel-gem; even so, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained in his mother's womb, he remained as if enclosed in a sheath, untouched by the impurity of the womb, by the impurity of the afterbirth, by the impurity of blood, or by any other unclean and defiling substance — just as a jewel-gem [on Kāśika cloth]. It is the natural law that at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> remained in his mother's womb, at that time the mother saw the entire interior of her womb completely filled [with him]; just as an eight-faceted beryl (<s>vaiḍūrya</s>) gem — pure, well-born, clear, limpid, unclouded — were strung upon a five-colored thread: blue, yellow, red, white, and crimson; a man with eyes, seeing it, would know: 'This is the thread, this is the gem; the gem is strung upon the thread.' Even so, at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> remained in his mother's womb, at that time the mother saw the entire interior of her womb completely filled. It is the natural law that at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> remained in his mother's womb, at that time the mother was neither weary of body nor fatigued of body while bearing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. children.translated_text: ) subsided. Again a pregnancy-craving arose in her: 'Oh, if only all prisoners could be released!' The king released all prisoners, and the pregnancy-craving that had arisen in her subsided. Again a pregnancy-craving arose in her: 'Oh, if only gifts could be given and merit could be performed!' The king gave gifts and performed meritorious deeds, and the pregnancy-craving that had arisen in her subsided. Again a pregnancy-craving arose in her: 'Oh, if only I could see the gardens!' The king showed her the gardens, and the pregnancy-craving that had arisen in her subsided. Again a pregnancy-craving arose in her: 'Oh, if only I could stay in a garden!' King <s>Suprabuddha</s> had a garden named <s>Lumbinī</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> sent word to him: 'Your daughter wishes to go out to the garden; please have the garden cleaned.' He gave orders to his attendants: 'Sirs, clean the garden.' They cleaned the garden. Then she went out accompanied by her attendant-women. Then, while strolling in the <s>Lumbinī</s> grove, she saw a blossoming <s>aśoka</s> tree. Seeing it, she stood there, ready to give birth.

Then <s>Mahāmāyā</s> developed a pregnancy-craving: 'Oh, if only I could drink water from the four great oceans!' She informed King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> reported it to the soothsayers: 'Why has the queen developed such a pregnancy-craving?' The soothsayers explained: 'Your Majesty, the queen will bear a prince; adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>), after going forth he will drink the entire ocean of the knowable.' The king asked: 'If water from the great ocean is not given to her, what would happen?' 'She would bear a deformed son.' The king said: 'For my part, <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s son shall have all limbs intact.' At that time, in <s>Kapilavastu</s>, there lived a wandering ascetic (<s>parivrājaka</s>) named <s>Raktākṣa</s>, skilled in magical illusion (<s>indrajāla</s>). The king had him summoned and informed him. He showed her, who had ascended to the upper terrace of the palace, the four great oceans and gave her water. body.text: devendraḥ saṃlakṣayati: bodhisatvamātā hrīmatī; na śaknoti mahājanaparivṛtā prasavitum; upāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyam iti; tena tumulaṃ vātavarṣaṃ nirmitam; tenāsau mahājanakāyaḥ samantād vidrutaḥ; tataḥ śakro devendraḥ vṛddhadhātrīvarṇam ātmānām abhinirmāya mahāmāyāyāḥ purastād avasthitaḥ sā prasavitum ārabdhā; bodhisatvo nirgacchaṃś chakreṇājinaśāṭikāyāṃ pratigṛhītaḥ; sa garbhavāsapariklāntaḥ; atha bodhisatvasyaitad abhavat: madaprāpto 'yaṃ śakro bhaviṣyati mayā bodhisatvaḥ pratīcchita iti; viditvā vajraśarīram ātmānam adhiṣṭhitaḥ; śakro devendraḥ kaṃpayitum ārabdho bodhisatvenābhihitaḥ; muñca muñca kauśika apaihi purastād iti; (
body.translated_text: <s>Devendra</s> reflected: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mother is modest; she is unable to give birth surrounded by a great crowd of people. A stratagem must be devised.' He created a tumultuous storm of wind and rain. By this, that great crowd of people scattered in all directions. Then <s>Śakra</s> <s>Devendra</s>, having magically created himself in the form of an old midwife, stood before <s>Mahāmāyā</s>. She began to give birth. As the <s>Bodhisattva</s> emerged, <s>Śakra</s> received him in a leather cloth (<s>ajinaśāṭikā</s>). He was wearied from dwelling in the womb. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'This <s>Śakra</s> must be intoxicated with pride [thinking]: "The <s>Bodhisattva</s> has been received by me."' Having realized this, he established his own body as a <s>vajra</s>-body. <s>Śakra</s> <s>Devendra</s> began to tremble. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said to him: 'Release, release, O <s>Kauśika</s>! Step aside from before me!' (

body.translated_text: ) It is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was born, at that time there was a great earthquake; as before, [the world was suffused with radiance] up to: 'Other beings too have been reborn here! Other beings too have been reborn here!' It is the natural law that at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> emerged from his mother's womb, he emerged as if from a sheath, untouched by the impurity of the womb, by the impurity of the afterbirth, by the impurity of blood, or by any other unclean and defiling substance. It is the natural law that at the time when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> emerged from his mother's womb, at that time the mother was neither sitting nor lying down; the <s>Kṣatriya</s> lady gave birth to the <s>Kṣatriya</s> while standing. It is the natural law that the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, just born, walked seven steps, unsupported by anyone; and he surveyed the four directions; and he spoke these words: 'This is the eastern direction — I shall be the foremost for <s>Nirvāṇa</s>. This is the southern direction — I shall be worthy of offerings from the entire world. This is the western direction — this shall be my last birth. This is the northern direction — I shall cross beyond the cycle of existences (<s>bhava-saṃsāra</s>).' The gods held above his head a white parasol with a jeweled handle and a fly-whisk. It is the natural law that for the just-born <s>Bodhisattva</s>, two streams of water appeared from the sky — one cool, one warm — with which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was bathed. It is the natural law that for the just-born <s>Bodhisattva</s>, before his birth-mother, a great well appeared, flowing with water, from which his mother performed the water-rites with water. It is the natural law that for the just-born <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the deities from the sky cast divine blue lotuses (<s>utpala</s>), lotuses (<s>padma</s>), white water-lilies (<s>kumuda</s>), white lotuses (<s>puṇḍarīka</s>), powdered aloe (<s>agaru</s>), powdered <s>tagara</s>, powdered sandalwood, powdered <s>tamālapatra</s>, (

In the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, a son was born to King <s>Mahāpadma</s>. He thought: 'At the birth of my son, the world was illuminated as if by the rising orb of the sun; and he is the son of <s>Bimbā</s>; let his name be <s>Bimbisāra</s>.' King <s>Anantanemin</s> thought: 'At the birth of my son, the world was illuminated as if by a flash of lightning (<s>pradyota</s>); let his name be <s>Pradyota</s>.' But this was not so [from their own merit]; rather, all of that was due to the supernatural power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.

On <s>Kiṣkindha</s> mountain dwelt a sage named <s>Asita</s>, skilled in the knowledge of cosmic contraction and expansion. He had a nephew named <s>Nālada</s>. From time to time he would teach him about cosmic contraction and expansion. He had gone forth in his presence. At the birth of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> (

children.text: asitas tv abravīt tīkṣṇā bhanoḥ śītā tv iyaṃ prabhā /
children.translated_text: <s>Asita</s> replied: 'The sun's rays are hot, but this radiance is cool.

children.text: tad asmin praviśaty ābhir nūnam eṣā muniprabhā //
children.translated_text: Since it enters here with these [qualities], surely this is the radiance of a sage.'
'Surely the <s>Bodhisattva</s> of great splendor is emerging from the womb.
This is the radiance of that great being as he emerges, pure,
golden in appearance, spreading through the three worlds.'

children.text: nāladaḥ kathayati: upādhyāya gacchāmo bodhisatvaṃ paśyāmaḥ; sa kathayati: vatsa idānīṃ bodhisatvo maheśākhyamaheśākhyābhir devatābhir ākīrṇo viharati; sthānam etad vidyate yad vayam avakāśaṃ na lapsyāmahe; yadā bhagavān kapilavastu praveśito bhavati, nāma cāsya vyavasthāpitam, tadā vayaṃ darśanāyopasaṅkramiśyāma iti; yam eva divasaṃ bodhisatvo bhagavān jātaḥ tam eva divasaṃ rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya chandakapramukhāni pañcopasthāyakaśatāni jātāni; cchandikāpramukhāni pañcopasthāyikaśatāni <jātāni>; pañcahastinīśatāni prasūtāni; pañcavaḍavāśatāni pañcabhir nidhiśatair mukhāny upadarśitāni; prātisīmaiś ca koṭṭarājabhiḥ karapratyayā upanibaddhāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nālada</s> said: 'Preceptor, let us go and see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' He replied: 'Child, right now the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is surrounded by great and mighty deities. It is quite possible that we will not find an opportunity. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> has been brought into <s>Kapilavastu</s> and his name has been established, then we shall approach for an audience.' On the very day the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was born, on that very day, five hundred male attendants headed by <s>Chandaka</s> were born to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>; five hundred female attendants headed by <s>Chandikā</s> were born; five hundred she-elephants gave birth; five hundred mares [foaled]; five hundred treasure-troves revealed their openings; and the border kings of vassal states pledged their tributes.

body.text: Names of the bodhisatva
body.translated_text: Names of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>

body.translated_text: The ministers reported the events to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. The king reflected: 'At the birth of my son, all purposes and all enterprises have been fulfilled. Let the prince's name be <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> (All-purposes-accomplished).' There the first name of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was established, namely <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s>. (

body.text: SBV I 48

) iti; kapilavastuni nagare śākyavardhano nāma yakṣo naivāsikaḥ; ācaritaṃ śākyānāṃ, yasya kasyacit chākyasya putro vā jāte duhitā vā sa śākyavardhanasya pādābhivandako nīyate; rājñā pauruṣeyāṇām ājñā dattā: gacchata bhavantaḥ kumāraṃ śākyavardhanasya yakṣasya pādayor nipatya pātayata iti; evaṃ deva ity amātyā rājñāḥ śuddhodanasya pratiśrutya, bodhisatvaṃ catūratnamayāṃ śibikām āropya kapilavastunagaraṃ praveśayitum ārabdhāḥ; kāpilavāstavāḥ śākyāś caṇḍā rabhasāḥ karkaśāḥ sāhasikāś ca; te bodhisatvasya praviśato munaya iva sthitāḥ; rājā śuddhodanaḥ saṃlakṣayati: ime kāpilavāstavāḥ
body.translated_text: ) In the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> there resided a <s>yakṣa</s> (spirit) named <s>Śākyavardhana</s>. It was the custom of the <s>Śākyas</s> that whenever a son or daughter was born to any <s>Śākya</s>, the child was taken to pay respects at the feet of <s>Śākyavardhana</s>. The king ordered his attendants: 'Go, sirs, take the prince and have him bow at the feet of the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Śākyavardhana</s>.' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' the ministers assented to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, placed the <s>Bodhisattva</s> on a palanquin made of four kinds of jewels, and began to bring him into the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. The <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> were fierce, impetuous, harsh, and violent. Yet as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered, they stood like silent sages. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> reflected: 'These <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>

body.text: śākyāś caṇḍā rabhasāḥ karkaśāś ca kumārāsya praviśato munaya ivāvasthitāḥ; bhavatu kumārasya śākyamunir iti nāmeti; tatra bohisatvasya dvitīyaṃ nāma vyavasthāpitaṃ yaduta śākyamunir iti; bodhisatvaḥ śāyavardhanasya yakṣaya bhavanasasmīpaṃ nītaḥ; adrākṣīc chākyavardhano yakṣo bodhisatvaṃ bhavanasamīpam āgataṃ; dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhavanān nirgamya sarvakāyena bodhisatvasya pādayor nipatitaḥ; janakāyena rājñā śuddhodanāya niveditam: deva śākyavardhana eva yakṣo bodhisatvasya pādayor nipatitaḥ iti; śrutvā ca rājā kathayati: bhavanto devā api kumārasya pādayor nipatanti; devānām apy ayaṃ devaḥ; tasmāt bhavatu kumārasya devātideva iti nāma iti; tatra bodhisatvasya tṛtīyaṃ nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ yaduta devātideva iti; sāṃpratajāto bodhisatvaḥ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ dhātryai dattaḥ: ayaṃ te dhātri kumāraḥ kālena kālam udvartayitavyaḥ, kālena kālaṃ snapayitavyaḥ, kālena kālaṃ bhojayitavyaḥ, kālena kālaṃ samyak sukhena parihartavyaḥ iti; tam enaṃ dhātrī āttamanāttamanā ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ pratigṛhya, kālena kālam udvartayati, kālena kālaṃ snapayati, kālena kālaṃ bhojayati, kālena kālam samyak sukhena pariharati; apīdānīṃ ye gandhāḥ sumanojñarūpāḥ tair vilipya, sarvālaṅkārair alaṅkṛtaṃ pituḥ śuddhodanasyānuprayacchati; tam enaṃ rājā śuddhodano gṛhītvā, aṅke niṣādya, punaḥ punaḥ prekṣate harṣajātaḥ (
body.translated_text: who are fierce, impetuous, and harsh — as the prince enters, they stand like silent sages. Let the prince's name be <s>Śākyamuni</s> (Sage of the <s>Śākyas</s>).' There the second name of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was established, namely <s>Śākyamuni</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> was brought near the dwelling of the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Śākyavardhana</s>. The <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Śākyavardhana</s> saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> approaching his dwelling. Having seen, he came out of his dwelling and prostrated his entire body at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The people reported to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'Your Majesty, the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Śākyavardhana</s> himself has prostrated at the feet of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' Having heard, the king said: 'Sirs, even the gods prostrate at the feet of the prince. He is a god even among gods. Therefore, let the prince's name be <s>Devātideva</s> (God above gods).' There the third name of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was established, namely <s>Devātideva</s>. The newborn <s>Bodhisattva</s> was given by his parents to a nurse: 'Nurse, this prince is to be massaged from time to time, bathed from time to time, fed from time to time, and properly cared for with comfort from time to time.' The nurse, overjoyed, received him with both hands, and from time to time massaged him, from time to time bathed him, from time to time fed him, and from time to time properly cared for him with comfort. Furthermore, having anointed him with the most pleasing fragrances, adorned with all ornaments, she would present him to his father <s>Śuddhodana</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having received him, seated him on his lap, and gazed at him again and again, filled with joy. (

Predictions of the naimittikas
body.translated_text: Predictions of the <s>naimittikas</s> (diviners)

body.text: dharmatā khalu sāṃpratajātaṃ bodhisatvaṃ mātāpitarau brāhmaṇānāṃ, naimittikānām, vipañcanakānām copadarśayataḥ: kaccid bhavantaḥ samanvāgataḥ kumāro dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ? yaiḥ samanvāgatasya mahāpuruṣasya
body.translated_text: It is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that the parents show the newborn <s>Bodhisattva</s> to <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, diviners (<s>naimittikas</s>), and soothsayers (<s>vipañcanakas</s>): 'Sirs, is the prince endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>)? When a great person is endowed with these marks,

body.text: ?) dve gatī bhavato, nānyā; saced gṛhī agāram adhyāvasati, rājā bhavati cakravartī, cāturantāṃ vijetā, dhārmiko, dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥ; tasyemāny evaṃrūpāṇi sapta ratnāni bhavanti; tadyathā (1) cakraratnam, (2) hastiratnam, (3) aśvaratnam, (4) maṇiratnam, (5) strīratnam, (6) gṛhapatiratnam, (7) pariṇāyakaratnam eva saptamam; pūrṇaṃ cāsya bhavati sahasraṃ putrāṇāṃ śūrāṇāṃ vīrāṇāṃ varāṅgarūpiṇāṃ parasainyapramardakānām; sa imām eva samudraparyantāṃ mahāpṛthivīm akhilām akaṇṭakām anutpīḍām adaṇḍenāśastreṇa dharmeṇa samenābhinirjityādhyāvatsyati; sacet keśaśmaśrv avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajati tathāgato bhavaty arhan saṃyaksaṃbuddho vighuṣṭaśabdo loka iti; tathyaṃ deva samanvāgataḥ kumāro dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāiḥ; yaiḥ samanvāgatasya mahāpuruṣasya dve gatī bhavato nānyā; sacet gṛhī agāram adhyāvasati, rājā bhavati cakravarti, cāturantāṃ vijetā, dhārmiko dharmarājāḥ pūrvavad yāvat tathāgato bhavaty arhan samyakasṃbuddho vighuṣṭaśabdo loke
body.translated_text: two destinies await him, and no other: if he remains a householder dwelling at home, he becomes a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), a conqueror of the four quarters, righteous, a <s>Dharmarāja</s> (king of righteousness), endowed with the seven treasures. His seven treasures are of this kind: (1) the wheel-treasure, (2) the elephant-treasure, (3) the horse-treasure, (4) the jewel-treasure, (5) the woman-treasure, (6) the householder-treasure, (7) the counselor-treasure as the seventh. He has a full thousand sons — heroes, warriors, of excellent form, crushers of enemy armies. He conquers this entire great earth, bordered by the ocean, undivided, free of thorns, free from oppression, without rod or weapon, by righteousness, by equity, and dwells [as its lord]. But if he shaves off his hair and beard, dons the saffron robes, and goes forth from the household life to homelessness with perfect faith, he becomes a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>), whose fame resounds throughout the world.' 'Truly, Your Majesty, the prince is endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great person. When a great person is endowed with these marks, two destinies await him, and no other: if he remains a householder dwelling at home, he becomes a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>, a conqueror of the four quarters, righteous, a king of righteousness... as before, up to... he becomes a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One, whose fame resounds throughout the world.'

body.text: Lakṣaṇas of a mahāpuruṣa
body.translated_text: The marks (<s>lakṣaṇas</s>) of a great person (<s>mahāpuruṣa</s>)

body.text: katamāni tāni bhavanto dvātriṃśat mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni? yaiḥ samanvāgatasya mahāpuruṣasya dve gatī bhavato nānyā; pūrvavad yāvad vighuṣṭaśabdo loke (
body.translated_text: 'What, sirs, are those thirty-two marks of a great person, being endowed with which a great person has two destinies and no other? As before, up to... whose fame resounds throughout the world.' (

body.text: SBV I 50

) (1) supratiṣṭhitapādo deva kumāraḥ; apīdānīṃ supratiṣṭhitatvāt pādayoḥ samam ākramate mahīm; idaṃ kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam; (2) adhastāc cāsya pādatalayoḥ cakre jāte sahasrāre, sanābhike sanemike, sarvākāraparipūrṇe; idaṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam; (3) dīrghāṅgulir deva kumāraḥ (4) āyatapādpārṣṇir (5) mṛdutaruṇapāṇipādaḥ; mṛdukam asya pāṇipādaṃ tadyathā tūlapicur vā karpāsapicur vā; idaṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam; (6) jālinīpāṇipādo deva kumāraḥ; jāliny asya hastayoś ca pādayoś ca, tadyathā abhijātasya haṃsarājasya; idaṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam; (7) ucchāṅkhacāro deva kumāraḥ; (8) eṇījaṅghaḥ; (9) anavanatakāyaḥ anavanamanena kāyena ubhau jānumaṇḍalāv āmārṣṭi parāmārṣṭi; idaṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣaṇam; (10) kośogatavastiguhyo deva kumāraḥ; kośogatavastiguhyaṃ tadyathā abhijātasya hastyājāneyasya vā aśvājāneyasya vā; ideṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam; (11) nyagrodhaparimaṇḍalo deva kumāraḥ; yāvān kāyena tāvān vyāmena, yāvān vyāmena tāvān kāyena; idaṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam; (12) ūrdhvāṅgaromo deva kumāraḥ; (13) ekaikaromaḥ; ekaikam asya roma kāye jātaṃ nīlam, kuṇḍalajātakāṃ pradakṣiṇāvartam; idaṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam; (14) suvarṇavarṇasaṅkāśo deva kumāraḥ; vyāmaprabhaḥ kāñcanasannibhas tvak; (15) sūkṣmacchaviḥ; apīdānīṃ sūkṣmatvāc cchave rajomalam asya kāye na santiṣṭhate; idaṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣlakṣaṇam; (16) saptotsadakāyo deva kumāraḥ; saptotsadāḥ kāye jātāḥ; dvau hastayor dvau pādayor dvāu aṃsayor ekaṃ grīvāyām; idaṃ deva kumārasya mahāpuruṣasya mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇam; (
body.translated_text: ) '(1) The prince has well-planted feet, Your Majesty. Because his feet are well-planted, he treads evenly upon the ground. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (2) On the soles of his feet, wheels have appeared — with a thousand spokes, with hub and rim, complete in every feature. This, Your Majesty, is a mark of a great person of the prince. (3) The prince has long fingers, Your Majesty. (4) He has extended heels. (5) He has soft and tender hands and feet; his hands and feet are soft, like cotton-down or kapok-down. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (6) The prince has webbed hands and feet, Your Majesty; there is webbing on his hands and feet, like that of a noble king of geese. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (7) The prince has high-ankled gait, Your Majesty. (8) He has antelope-like legs. (9) He has an unbent body — without bending his body, he can touch and rub both kneecaps. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (10) The prince has his male organ enclosed in a sheath, Your Majesty — enclosed in a sheath like that of a noble thoroughbred elephant or thoroughbred horse. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (11) The prince has the proportions of a banyan tree, Your Majesty — his height equals his arm-span, and his arm-span equals his height. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (12) The prince has body-hair growing upward, Your Majesty. (13) He has single hairs in each pore; each hair on his body grows singly, dark blue, curling, turning to the right. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (14) The prince has a complexion like gold, Your Majesty; he radiates light for a fathom, his skin resembling gold. (15) He has fine skin; because of the fineness of his skin, dust and dirt do not cling to his body. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (16) The prince has a body with seven prominences, Your Majesty; seven prominences have appeared on his body — two on the hands, two on the feet, two on the shoulders, and one on the neck. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (

This is a mark of a great person of the prince. (29) The prince has deep blue eyes, Your Majesty. (30) He has eyelashes like a cow's. (31) He has an <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (cranial protuberance) on his head. (32) Between his eyebrows a tuft of hair (<s>ūrṇā</s>) has appeared — white, like a conch shell, curling to the right. This is a mark of a great person of the prince. These,

It is a natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that the mother who gave birth to the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> passed away seven days after his birth; immediately upon passing, she was reborn in the excellent <s>Trayastriṃśat</s> (Thirty-three) divine abode. It is a natural law that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> was handsome, lovely, and pleasing; he had surpassed human complexion but had not yet attained divine complexion. Even now, men and women gazing upon him find no satiation and experience joy — just as a gold coin made of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> gold, polished by a goldsmith, placed upon a fresh white woolen cloth, shines, glows, and radiates exceedingly. Even so, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> was handsome, lovely, and pleasing, having surpassed human complexion but not yet attained divine complexion. children.translated_text: It is a natural law that the newly-born <s>Bodhisattva</s> was unblinking; when looking at forms, he did not blink — just like the <s>Trayastriṃśat</s> gods. It is a natural law that the newly-born <s>Bodhisattva</s> was endowed with the divine eye born of the fruition of past <s>karma</s>, by which he could see swiftly, by day and by night, in all directions for a <s>yojana</s>. It is a natural law that the newly-born <s>Bodhisattva</s> had a sweet voice, a melodious voice, a charming voice — just as the <s>Haimavata</s> (Himalayan) bird has a sweet voice, a melodious voice, a charming voice; even so, the newly-born <s>Bodhisattva</s> had a sweet voice, a melodious voice, a charming voice. It is a natural law that the newly-born <s>Bodhisattva</s> was wise, discerning, intelligent, endowed with analytical and investigative wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>). Even now, sitting down with King <s>Śuddhodana</s> on matters of state, he penetrates with his wisdom the deep meaning, words, and syllables.

body.translated_text: The arrival of <s>Asita</s> and <s>Nālada</s>:

body.text: tato nāladaḥ kathayati: upādhyāya bodhisatvaḥ kapilavastuni praveśitaḥ; nāmatrayaṃ ca vyavasthāpitam; idānīṃ gacchāmo bodhisatvaṃ darśanāya iti; sa kathayati; evaṃ kurmaḥ; tau saṃprasthitau; bodhhisatvānubhāvād ṛddheḥ parihīṇau; padbhyām eva kapilavastunagaraṃ praviśya rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya gṛhadvāraṃ gatau; tata asitariṣir dauvārikaṃ puruṣaṃ āmantrayate: gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa rajñaḥ śuddhodanasya gatvā kathaya, asitariṣir dvāri tiṣṭhati, devaṃ draṣṭukāma iti; tena praviśya (
body.translated_text: Then <s>Nālada</s> said: 'Preceptor, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has been brought into <s>Kapilavastu</s>, and three names have been established. Now let us go to see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' He said: 'Let us do so.' The two set out. By the power of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, they lost their supernatural abilities (<s>ṛddhi</s>). Going on foot, they entered the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> and went to the door of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s residence. Then the sage <s>Asita</s> addressed the doorkeeper: 'Go, good man, go to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> and tell him: "The sage <s>Asita</s> stands at the door, wishing to see His Majesty."' He went in (

body.text: tataḥ sāṃpratajāto bodhisatvo dhātryā aṅke gṛhītvā riṣer upanāmitaḥ; asitena riṣiṇā ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ pratigṛhītaḥ; muhūrtaṃ nirīkṣya kathayati: deva darśitaḥ kumāro brāhmaṇānāṃ naimittikānāṃ vipañcanakānām? rājā kathayati darśitaḥ; kim tair vyākṛtam? rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī, pūrvavad yāvad vighuṣṭaśabdo loke; athāsitariṣir bodhisatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate

After examining him for a moment, he said: 'Your Majesty, has the prince been shown to the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sign-readers and soothsayers?' The king said: 'He has been shown.' 'What did they declare?' 'They declared he will become a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch),' and so forth as before, down to 'whose fame resounds in the world.' body.text: Asita's departure
body.translated_text: <s>Asita</s>'s departure:

body.text: asitarṣiḥ kliṣṭasantānaḥ saṃlakṣayti: ahaṃ bodhiṣatvasyānubhāvād ṛddheḥ parihīṇaḥ; sayadi padbhyāṃ gamiṣyāmi
body.translated_text: The sage <s>Asita</s>, with an afflicted mind, reflected: 'I have lost my supernatural powers by the influence of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. If I go on foot,

body.text: mahājanakāyo māṃ pratarkayiṣyati rājā ca ; iti viditvā kathayati: deva tavāyaṃ dīrgharātram āśāsakaḥ, aho batāsitarṣiḥ, padbhyām eva kapilavastu praviśed iti; so 'haṃ padhbhyām kapilavastu praviṣṭaḥ; idānīṃ padbhyām eva niṣkramiṣyāmi; tvaṃ mārgaśobhāṃ ca kārayeti; rājñā śuddhodanena amātyānām ājñā dattā: gacchata bhavanto nagaraśobhāṃ mārgaśobhāṃ ca kārayata rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇām; asitiriṣiḥ padbhyāṃ kapilavastuno nagarān niṣkrāmati; yad vaḥ kṛtyaṃ vā karaṇīyaṃ vā tat kurudhvam iti; evaṃ devety amātyaiḥ rājñaḥ pratiśrutya kapilavastunagaram apagataśarkarakaṭhallaṃ (
body.translated_text: the great multitude will gossip about me, and so will the king.' Having realized this, he said: 'Your Majesty, this has been a long-cherished wish of yours: "Oh, if only the sage <s>Asita</s> would enter <s>Kapilavastu</s> on foot!" So I entered <s>Kapilavastu</s> on foot. Now I shall also depart on foot. Please have the road decorated.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> gave orders to the ministers: 'Go, sirs, and have the city and the roads decorated. At the streets, lanes, crossroads, and squares, have bell-announcements made: "The sage <s>Asita</s> is departing the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> on foot. Whatever duty or business you have, attend to it."' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' the ministers assented to the king. The city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was cleared of gravel and stones, (

) vyavasthāpitam, candanavāripariṣiktam surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibaddham āmuktapallavadāmakalāpam, ucchritadhvajapatākaṃ; rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakesu ghaṇtāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam: śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ kapilavāstavāḥ śākyāḥ asitarṣiḥ kapilavastuno nagarān niṣkrāmati; yad vaḥ kṛtyaṃ vā karaṇīyaṃ vā tat kurudhvam iti; tato 'sau kliṣṭabuddhiḥ kṛtopacārī rājñā śuddhodanenāmātyagaṇaparivṛtenānekaiś ca kāpilavāstavair brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhir anugamyamāno madhyamadhyena nagarasya parayā vibhūtyā kapilavastuno niṣkrāntaḥ; rājānaṃ nivartya yatheṣṭagatipracāratayā saṃprasthito 'nupūrveṇa kiṣkindhaṃ parvatam anuprāptaḥ; sa tam adhiruhya itaś cāmutaś ca paribhraman yathābhipretasthānasamanveṣaṇayā anyatamasmin pradeśe niṣaṇṇaḥ; tatas tena mārgaśramaṃ prativinodya dhyānāny utpāditāni; ṛddhiś cābhinirhṛtā; yāvad apareṇa samayena asitariṣir glānaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; sa upasthīyate mūlagandhapatrapuṣpaphalabhaiṣajyaiḥ; tathāpy asau hīyata eva; tato 'sya nāladaḥ śarīrāvasthāṃ paricchidya kathayati: upādhyāya yatkiṃcid vayaṃ pravrajitās tat sarvam amṛtārthino mṛtagaveṣiṇaḥ; saced upādhyāyenāmṛtam adhigatam asmākam apu amṛtena saṃvibhāgaṃ karotv iti; sa kathayati: māṇava aham api yatkiṃcit pravrajitaḥ sarvaṃ tad amṛtārthī amṛtagaveṣi; na ca mayāmṛtam adhigatam; api tu ya eṣa śākyānāṃ kumāra utpanna eṣo 'mṛtam adhigamiṣyati; amṛtena jagat santarpayiṣyati; tasyāntike pravraja; pravrajya ca tena <na> jātivādaḥ kartavyo na gotravādo na māṇavakavādaḥ; kevalaṃ tu pravrajya brahmacaryaṃ caritavyam; amṛtādhigame codyogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ; tatas te amṛtaṃ bhaviṣyati; iti viditvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate
body.translated_text: ) sprinkled with sandalwood water, fitted with censers of fragrant incense, adorned with garlands of fresh sprouts, and with raised banners and flags. At the streets, lanes, crossroads, and squares, bell-announcements were made: 'Hear, O <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>! The sage <s>Asita</s> is departing the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Whatever duty or business you have, attend to it.' Then that one of afflicted mind, having been duly honored, accompanied by King <s>Śuddhodana</s> surrounded by his company of ministers and by many <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> and householder citizens of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, departed through the middle of the city with supreme magnificence from <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Having taken leave of the king, proceeding as he wished, he gradually reached Mount <s>Kiṣkindha</s>. Having ascended it, wandering here and there in search of a suitable place, he sat down at a certain spot. There, having recovered from the fatigue of the journey, he generated the <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations) and brought forth his supernatural powers (<s>ṛddhi</s>). Then at a later time, the sage <s>Asita</s> fell ill. He was attended to with medicines of roots, fragrances, leaves, flowers, and fruits. Yet even so, he continued to decline. Then his [disciple] <s>Nālada</s>, perceiving his bodily condition, said: 'Preceptor, for whatever reason we went forth — all of it was in search of the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>), seeking the deathless. If the preceptor has attained the deathless, please share it with us as well.' He said: 'Young man, I too — for whatever reason I went forth — all of it was in search of the deathless, seeking the deathless. I have not attained the deathless. But that prince who has been born among the <s>Śākyas</s> — he will attain the deathless. He will satisfy the world with the deathless. Go forth in his presence. And having gone forth, you should not engage in disputes about birth, lineage, or being a young student. Rather, having gone forth, practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>). And you should make effort toward attaining the deathless. Then the deathless will be yours.' Having understood this, he spoke this verse:

There he taught the <s>Brāhmaṇical</s> <s>mantras</s> to five hundred young students. <s>Nālada</s> was of the <s>Kātyāyana</s> <s>gotra</s> (lineage). He acquired the designation '<s>Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>.' He will approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> after his perfect awakening (<s>abhisaṃbuddhabodhi</s>). The <s>Bhagavān</s> will instruct him with the teaching for <s>Kātyāyana</s>, awaken him, deliver him from the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and establish him in the ultimate, definitive <s>Nirvāṇa</s>, the supreme peace. His designation will become '<s>Mahākātyāyana</s>, <s>Mahākātyāyana</s>.'

children.text: athāpareṇa samayena śākyamunir bodhisatvo dhātryaṃsagataḥ suvarṇapātryāṃ śālimāsaudanaṃ bhuṅkte; sa prabhūtaṃ bhuṅkte; nāvatiṣṭhata iti dhātrī ācchettum ārabdhā; na śaknoty ācchettum; tayā rājñe śuddhodanayā ārocitam; rājā antaḥpurasahīya ācchettum ārabdhaḥ; so 'pi na śaknoti; tato rājñā amātyāḥ kapilavāstavāś ca janakāyāḥ prayukṭāḥ; te 'pi na śaknuvanty ācchettum; tataḥ pañcahastiśatāni yoktritāni; bodhisatvaḥ saṃlakṣayati: mā mameti balaṃ paṃsayiṣyanti; yanv aham kuṭilāṅgulikayā pātrīṃ vidhārayeyam iti; tena kuṭilāṅgulikayā suvarṇapātrī ākṛṣṭā; tāni ca pañcaśatāni pṛṣṭhatomukhāni ākṛṣṭāni, na tu taiḥ suvarṇapātrī ākṛṣṭā; rājā śuddhodanaḥ saṃlakṣayati: bodhisatvena vāmena pāṇinā pañcahastiśatāny ākṛṣṭāni; niyatam ubhābhyāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ nāgasahasram ākrakṣyati; tasmād bhavatu kumārasya nāgasahasrabala iti nāmeti
children.translated_text: Then at another time, <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while sitting on the nurse's lap, was eating rice and bean porridge from a golden bowl. He ate a great deal and would not stop, so the nurse tried to take it away, but she could not. She reported this to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. The king, together with the inner court, tried to take it away, but he too could not. Then the king employed ministers and the people of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, but they too could not take it away. Then five hundred elephants were yoked [to pull]. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'Lest they damage my strength.' So he held the bowl with a crooked finger. With his crooked finger, he pulled the golden bowl; and the five hundred [elephants] were dragged backward, but they could not pull the golden bowl from him. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> reflected: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> has dragged five hundred elephants with his left hand alone. Certainly, with both hands he will drag a thousand elephants. Therefore, let the prince's name be <s>Nāgasahasrabala</s> (Strength-of-a-Thousand-Elephants).'

body.text: dharmatā khalu śākyamunir bodhisatvaḥ pañcaśataparivāraḥ kṛmivarmaṇo lipyācāryasya lipiṃ śikṣaṇāyopanyastaḥ; kṛmivarmaṇā lipyācāryeṇa bodhisatvasya lipir likhitvā dattā; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati jānāmy aham enām iti; tatas tena dvitiyā tṛtīyā; evaṃ yāvat pañcalipiśatāni likhitvā dattāni; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati: etām apy ahaṃ jāne anyāṃ kathayeti; kṛmivarmā kathayati: etāvatyo loke lipayaḥ pracaranti, nāham anyāṃ jāne iti; tato bodhisatvena svayam eva lipir likhitvā kṛmivarmaṇo dattā; uktaś ca kathaya kiṃnāmeyaṃ lipir iti; sa kathayati na jānāmīti; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati: dvayor loke pradurbhāvād iyaṃ lipiḥ prajñāyate, bodhisatvasya cakravartino vā iti; gaganatalasthena brahmaṇābhihitam: evam etat kṛmivarman yathā bodhisatvaḥ kathayati; dvayor eva loke prādurbhāvād iyaṃ lipiḥ prajñāyate, bodhisatvasya cakravartino vā iti; bodhisatveneyaṃ lipir brahmasvareṇa vācitā; brahmaṇā ca gaganatalasthena sākṣyaṃ dattam; brāhmī lipir brāhmī lipir iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā; yadā bodhisatvo lipyāḥ pāraṃ gataḥ bhāddālināma bodhisatvasya mātulas tena hastigrīvāyaṃ śikṣāyāṃ śikṣitaḥ; sahadevo nāma iṣvastrācāryaḥ; tena pañcaśataparivāraḥ cchedyaṃ śikṣayitum ārabdhaḥ; bhāddālinā sahadeva ucyate: bodhisatvaḥ kāruṇikaḥ
body.translated_text: It is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with an entourage of five hundred, was placed under the writing-master <s>Kṛmivarman</s> to learn writing. <s>Kṛmivarman</s> the writing-master wrote out a script and gave it to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I know this one.' Then he gave a second, a third — thus up to five hundred scripts were written out and given. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I know this one too. Tell me another.' <s>Kṛmivarman</s> said: 'This many scripts are current in the world. I do not know another.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> himself wrote out a script and gave it to <s>Kṛmivarman</s>, and said: 'Tell me — what is the name of this script?' He said: 'I do not know.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'This script becomes known in the world through the appearance of two: a <s>Bodhisattva</s> or a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).' <s>Brahmā</s>, standing in the sky, declared: 'It is just so, <s>Kṛmivarman</s>, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> says. Only through the appearance of two in the world does this script become known: a <s>Bodhisattva</s> or a <s>Cakravartin</s>.' Since the <s>Bodhisattva</s> recited this script with the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s> standing in the sky bore witness, the designation '<s>Brāhmī</s> script' came into being. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had reached the far shore of writing, <s>Bhāddālī</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s maternal uncle, trained him in elephant-riding. There was an archery master named <s>Sahadeva</s>. By him, [the <s>Bodhisattva</s>] with an entourage of five hundred was taught the skill of cutting. <s>Bhāddālī</s> told <s>Sahadeva</s>: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is compassionate.

body.text: sarvāś śikṣāś śikṣayitavyaḥ; evam anye kumārāh; ayaṃ devadattaḥ krūrakarmā; asya marmavedho na vyapadeṣṭavyaḥ mā sarvalokaṃ vyāpādayiṣyatīti; yadā bodhisatvaḥ sarvaśikṣāsu śikṣitaḥ, pañcasu sthāneṣu kṛtāvī saṃvṛttaḥ, dūravedhe, śabdavedhe, marmavedhe, akṣūṇavedhe, dṛḍhaprahāritāyāṃ ca, sāmantakena śabdo visṛtaḥ śākyānāṃ kumāra utpannaḥ pūrvavad yāvad vighuṣṭaśabdo loka iti; tena khalu samayena vaiśālair licchavibhir lakṣaṇasaṃpanno hastī labdhaḥ; te saṃlakṣayanti; rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya putro naimittikair vyākṛtaḥ rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartīti; tasyānubhāvād idaṃ hastiratnam (
body.translated_text: He should be taught all skills. The same for the other princes. But this <s>Devadatta</s> is a cruel-doer. The vital-point strike should not be taught to him, lest he destroy all the world.' When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> had been trained in all skills, he became accomplished in five fields: long-distance striking, sound-guided striking, vital-point striking, sure-hitting, and hard-hitting. The report spread throughout the region: 'A prince has been born among the <s>Śākyas</s>' — as before, up to 'the report spread throughout the world.' At that time, the <s>Vaiśālī</s> <s>Licchavis</s> had obtained an elephant endowed with auspicious marks. They deliberated: 'King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s son has been prophesied by the soothsayers to become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>. Through his power this elephant-jewel (

body.translated_text: ) has appeared. Let us go and present it to him.' They adorned that elephant with elephant-ornaments and set out with great splendor, gradually reaching <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Having stationed the elephant at the gate of the royal palace, they stood there. By chance, the cruel-doer <s>Devadatta</s> came out. He saw that elephant-lord, thus adorned and splendid. Great jealousy arose in him. Filled with jealousy and anger, he asked: 'Whose is this elephant-lord?' They told him: 'Prince <s>Śākyamuni</s> has been prophesied by the soothsayers to be a <s>Cakravartin</s>. This elephant-jewel has been sent by the assembly of <s>Vaiśālī</s> [for him].' <s>Devadatta</s>, his anger further inflamed, said: 'Before he becomes a <s>Cakravartin</s>, you have already brought him an elephant-jewel!' Having said this, he killed the elephant with a single palm-strike. Then <s>Nanda</s> happened to pass by that spot. He saw it and asked: 'Sirs, this fine elephant — who killed it?' They told him: '<s>Devadatta</s>.' He reflected: 'Surely <s>Devadatta</s> tested his strength here. <Let me too test my strength here.>' Thinking thus, he grabbed it by the tail and placed it to one side, [thinking:] 'Lest it cause a stench.' Then <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> came out. He saw it and asked: 'Where did this elephant come from?' They told him what had happened. 'Who killed it?' '<s>Devadatta</s>.' 'That is not right. Guests should be honored with hospitality. In what spot was it killed?' 'In this spot.' 'Who brought it here?' '<s>Nanda</s>.' He reflected: 'Surely those two tested their strength here. Let me too test my strength here.' Knowing this, he grabbed it by the tail, threw it over the rampart, and it flew over seven ramparts and seven moats before landing. Where it fell, a pit was formed. The name '<s>Hastigarta</s>' (Elephant Pit) came into being. (

body.translated_text: The princes said: 'Let us go and practice cutting.' They went out. Having heard, <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> went out with an entourage of five hundred to practice cutting. The princes were doing fine cutting — what they cut fell down. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> did thick cutting — what he cut did not fall; it remained standing just as before. The princes said: 'Sirs, <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is said to be strong, accomplished in five fields. Yet he does not even know how to cut. He is not stronger than us. For the trees we cut all fell down, while those he cut remain standing as before.' Now a deity who was devoted to <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'These <s>Śākyas</s>, not knowing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s strength and skill, will disparage and belittle him. A stratagem must be devised.' She released such a wind that all those trees fell crashing down. Seeing this, the <s>Śākyas</s> were overcome with supreme wonder. Then they began to practice piercing. For that, there were iron targets. Seven iron palm-trees, a drum, and a gong were set up. <s>Devadatta</s>, having taken a stance, shot an arrow; one palm-tree was pierced. <s>Nanda</s> [pierced] two. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> shot an arrow; seven palm-trees, the drum, and the gong were pierced. That arrow entered the netherworld. The <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-deities) drew it out. Water appeared — sweet [to taste]. The great multitude began to drink it. Devout <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders established a shrine there. Even today, monks who venerate shrines pay homage to it. (

children.translated_text: The princes, mounted on chariots, entered <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Soothsayers were coming out of the city. They prophesied about Prince <s>Śākyamuni</s> as he was entering on his chariot: 'If this one does not go forth within twelve years, he will certainly become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> heard that the prince had been prophesied by the soothsayers. Having heard, filled with joy and delight, he summoned the <s>Śākyas</s> and said: 'I have heard, sirs, that the prince has been prophesied by the soothsayers — if he does not go forth within twelve years, he will certainly become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>. If the prince does not go forth within twelve years and becomes a <s>Cakravartin</s>, we shall traverse the four continents, roaming through the sky. Let a household be established for him.' The ministers said: 'Lord, the prince has no interest in sensory pleasures.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said: 'Let us show all the maidens to the prince. Whichever he prefers, we shall bring her into the inner court.' Others said: 'Lord, the prince delights in giving. Let ornaments be given to the maidens. Whichever pleases him, we shall bring her into the inner court.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said: 'Let it be done thus.' The ministers assembled a heap of ornaments of various kinds, adorned with jewels. Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having arranged the beauty of the house and the beauty of the city, and having set up a lion-throne on a pavilion at the auspicious constellation, date, and hour, seated Prince <s>Śākyamuni</s> [there]. Near the lion-throne, a heap of various jeweled ornaments was arranged. Ministers and other leading citizens of <s>Kapilavastu</s> were admitted. Then all the maidens were brought in, adorned with attire, ornaments, and equipment befitting the prestige of their families. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with his delight in giving, gave ornaments to them. (

body.translated_text: The <s>Śākya</s> <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> had a daughter named <s>Yaśodharā</s>, who had attained beauty, youth, and the prime of age. The <s>Śākya</s> <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s> said to her: 'Daughter, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> is giving ornaments.' She said: 'Father, do we not have our own jewelers?' 'Daughter, we do. But the one who

body.text: bodhisatvasya kanyābhirucitā tām asau varayati; tāta varayatu vā mā vā; api tu sa eva mama bhartā; putri yady evaṃ sutarāṃ gantavyam; gacchataḥ; yaśodharābhinavavayāḥ; suveṣā, mahājanamanonayanāny ākṣipantī sarvās tāḥ kanyāḥ devakanyā ivāvabhāsamānā praviśya śānteneryāpathena bodhisatvasya purastād avasthitā; bodhisatvena sarvālaṅkārikaṃ dattam; aṅgulīyakam eva samavaśiṣṭam; bodhisatvena tasyās tad upadarśitam; tatas tayā anādikālaprakarṣapraṇayanayā siṃhāsanasopānakam abhiruhya bodhisatvahastāt svayam ākṛṣṭam; amātyāḥ kāpilavāstavaś ca pradhānasaṃmato janakāyaḥ kathayanti: bhavantaḥ sarvakanyānām iyaṃ viśiṣṭā; śaknoty eṣā kumārasya cittagrāhaṃ kartum; eṣā praveśyatām iti; tato rājñā śuddhodanena yaśodharā viṃśatikanyāsahasraparivārā śākyamuṇeḥ kumārasyāntaḥpuraṃ praveśitā
body.translated_text: the maiden favored by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — him she chose. 'Father, whether he chooses [me] or not, he alone is my husband.' 'Daughter, if so, all the more must you go.' They went. <s>Yaśodharā</s>, in the bloom of youth, beautifully adorned, captivating the minds and eyes of the great multitude — all those maidens, shining like divine maidens — entered and stood before the <s>Bodhisattva</s> with calm deportment. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> had given away all the ornaments; only the ring remained. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> showed it to her. Then she, impelled by the affection cultivated over beginningless time, ascended the steps of the lion-throne and herself took it from the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s hand. The ministers and the leading citizens of <s>Kapilavastu</s> said: 'Sirs, of all the maidens, she is the most distinguished. She is able to capture the prince's heart. Let her be admitted [into the inner palace].' Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> admitted <s>Yaśodharā</s>, accompanied by twenty thousand maidens, into the inner palace of prince <s>Śākyamuni</s>.

body.translated_text: It is indeed the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that when <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, arise in the world, a tree named <s>Sārakalyāṇī</s> is born. It grows one hundred arm-lengths per day. As long as the sun has not risen, it can be cut even with a fingernail; but once the sun has risen, it cannot be cut even with a weapon, nor burned by fire. Between <s>Kapilavastu</s> and <s>Devadṛśa</s> (

body.text: ) atrāntarā nadī rohakā nāma, tasyāḥ kūle jātaḥ; kālena kālam udakavṛddhyā tasya mūlaṃ śocitam; vātavaśāt patitaḥ setuvan nadīṃ ruddhvā sthitaḥ; tataḥ suprabuddhasya rājñaḥ anudakena deśo nāśyati; śuddhodanasyāpy udakena; suprabuddhena rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya sandiṣṭam: sārakalyāṇi vṛkṣaḥ patitaḥ; rohakāṃ nadīm avaṣṭabhyāvasthitaḥ; kumārā balavantaḥ śrūyante; tad etān preṣayitum arhasi iti; rājā śuddhodanaḥ kathayati: nāhaṃ kumārāṇām ājñāṃ dadāmīti; chandaḥ kathayati: kevalaṃ devo 'nujānātu; ahaṃ tathā kariṣyāmi yathā na ca kumārāṇām ājñā dīyate, atha ca punaḥ svayam eva gacchantīti; rājñā śuddhodanenādhivāsitaṃ; chandena nadyā rohakāyās tīre pratyekaṃ kumārāṇām udyānāni māpitāni; uktāś ca kumārā gacchāma udyānaṃ; te kathayanti, gacchāmaḥ; te pratyekaṃ ratham abhiruhya udyānaṃ gatāḥ; devadattasyodyānopariṣṭad dhaṃso gacchati; sa devadattena śareṇa viddhaḥ; bodhisatvasyodyāne nipatitaḥ; bodhisatvena gṛhītvā viśalyīkṛtaḥ; upahāraś ca dattaḥ; svastho jātaḥ; devadattena bodhisatvasya sandiṣṭam: mayāyaṃ pūrvaparigṛhīto haṃsaḥ, preṣayainam iti; bodhisatvena sandiṣṭam: yadaiva mayā bodhāya cittam utpāditaṃ, taidaiva mayā sarvasatvāḥ parigṛhītā iti; tatra devadattasya bodhisatvena sārdhaṃ carame bhave tatprathamato vairūkṣyam utpannam; anyabhaveṣu tu bahuśaḥ; suprabuddhena (
body.translated_text: ) in between, there was a river called <s>Rohakā</s>. [The tree] had grown on its bank. In the course of time, due to the rising of the water, its root was undermined. Carried by the force of the wind, it fell and, blocking the river like a bridge, stood [across it]. As a result, King <s>Suprabuddha</s>'s territory was being ruined by lack of water, while <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s [territory was being ruined] by excess water. King <s>Suprabuddha</s> sent word to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>: 'The <s>Sārakalyāṇī</s> tree has fallen and is blocking the river <s>Rohakā</s>. The princes are reputed to be strong; please send them.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> replied: 'I do not command the princes.' <s>Chandaka</s> said: 'Let Your Majesty just grant permission. I shall arrange it so that the princes are not commanded, yet they will go of their own accord.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> consented. <s>Chandaka</s> laid out individual gardens for the princes on the bank of the river <s>Rohakā</s>. The princes were told: 'Let us go to the garden.' They said: 'Let us go.' They each mounted their chariots and went to the garden. A goose was flying above <s>Devadatta</s>'s garden. <s>Devadatta</s> struck it with an arrow. It fell into the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s garden. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> picked it up, removed the arrow, and gave it treatment. It recovered. <s>Devadatta</s> sent word to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'That goose was first captured by me; send it back.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> replied: 'From the very moment I generated the aspiration for <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), I have taken all beings under my protection.' There, in this final existence, <s>Devadatta</s>'s first enmity toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s> arose; but in other existences, [it had arisen] many times. <s>Suprabuddha</s> (

body.text: SBV I 64
body.translated_text: SBV I 64

body.text: ) kumārā udyānabhūmiṃ sārakalyāṇīvṛksasyāpanayanāya nirgatā iti śrutvā mahājanakāyaḥ preṣitaḥ; tatroccaśabdamahāśabdo mahājanakāyasya ca nirghoṣo jātaḥ; bodhisatvaḥ
body.translated_text: ) hearing that the princes had gone out to the garden grounds for the removal of the <s>Sārakalyāṇī</s> tree, sent a great multitude of people. There arose a great clamor, a loud noise from the great multitude. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>

body.text: pṛcchati: bhavantaḥ kim eṣa uccaśabdamahāśabdo mahājanakāyasya ca nirghoṣa iti; chandena yathāvṛttaṃ samākhyātam; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati: yady evaṃ gacchāmo 'panayāmaḥ; bodhisatvaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ sārdhaṃ kumāraiḥ; yāvad vivarād āśīviṣo bodhisatvasyābhimukho nirgataḥ; udāyinā mā bodhisatvaṃ daṅkṣyatīti tīkṣṇena śastreṇa madhye chinnaḥ; tena udāyī śvāsena dagdhaḥ kṛṣṇībhūtaḥ; tasya kālodāyī kālodayīti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā; tataḥ kumārāḥ sārakalyāṇīvṛkṣam apanetuṃ pravṛttāḥ; devadattena parikaraṃ baddhvā īṣaccālitaḥ; nandeneṣad utkṣiptaḥ; bodhisatvena tu sarvam upari vihāyasā kṣipto dvikhaṇḍo jātaḥ; nadyā rohakāyā ekasmiṃs tīre ekakhaṇḍo niparitaḥ, dvitīye dvitīyaḥ; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati: bhavantaḥ ayaṃ sārakalyāṇīvṛkṣaḥ śītavipākaḥ, pittaghnaḥ; gaṇḍagaṇḍaṃ kṛtvā nayata; utpātagaṇḍapiṭakānāṃ pralepaṃ dāsyatha; kumārāḥ svakasvakān rathān abhiruhya udyānabhūmeḥ kapilavastu saṃprasthitāḥ; purapraveśe rathābhirūḍho bodhisatvo naimittikair vyākṛtaḥ; yady eṣa saptadivase na pravrajati, rājā bhavati cakravartīti
body.translated_text: asked: 'Sirs, what is this great clamor, this loud noise of the great multitude?' <s>Chandaka</s> narrated the events as they had occurred. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'If so, let us go and remove it.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> set out together with the princes. Then a venomous serpent emerged from a crevice directly toward the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. <s>Udāyin</s>, [thinking] 'Let it not bite the <s>Bodhisattva</s>!', cut it in half with a sharp weapon. He was burned by its [dying] breath and turned black. Thus the name <s>Kālodāyin</s> ('Dark <s>Udāyin</s>') came into being for him. Then the princes set about removing the <s>Sārakalyāṇī</s> tree. <s>Devadatta</s>, having girded his loins, slightly moved it. <s>Nanda</s> slightly lifted it. But the <s>Bodhisattva</s> hurled the entire thing upward through the sky, and it broke into two pieces. On one bank of the river <s>Rohakā</s> one piece fell, and the second on the other bank. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Sirs, this <s>Sārakalyāṇī</s> tree is cooling in its effects and alleviates bile (<s>pitta</s>). Cut it into pieces and take them. You may use it as a poultice for boils, tumors, and abscesses.' The princes, mounting their respective chariots, set out from the garden grounds toward <s>Kapilavastu</s>. As the <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered the city mounted on his chariot, the soothsayers made a prophecy: 'If he does not go forth within seven days, he will become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).'

body.translated_text: It is indeed the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that when the <s>Bodhisattva</s> wishes to go out to the garden, he addresses the charioteer: 'Come now, charioteer, quickly yoke the fine vehicle, upon which, having mounted, I shall go out to the garden.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> addressed the charioteer: 'Come now, charioteer, quickly yoke the fine vehicle, upon which, having mounted, I shall go to the garden.' 'Yes, my lord,' the charioteer assented to <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, yoked the fine vehicle, and approached <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, he said to <s>Śākyamuni</s> the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'The fine vehicle is yoked, my lord; now let my lord decide the time.' body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> addressed the charioteer: 'Was the prince, charioteer, cheerful and delighted when he went out to the garden? Was he pleased in the garden?' 'No, Your Majesty.' 'For what reason?' 'Your Majesty, the prince, while going out to the garden, saw a man — aged, old, decrepit, bent, crooked like a rafter, leaning on a staff, going forward with a trembling body; and his hair was discolored, not like that of other men. Having seen, he addressed me thus: "Who is this man, charioteer? Aged, old, decrepit, bent, crooked like a rafter, leaning on a staff, going forward with a trembling body; and his hair is discolored, not like that of other men." I said to him: "This, my lord, is what is called old." He said: "What is this old, charioteer?" I said to him: "This man, my lord, will soon have to die. That is what is called old." He said: "Am I too, charioteer, subject to the law of aging? Have I not passed beyond the state of being subject to aging?" I said to him: "My lord too is subject to the law of aging and has not passed beyond the state of being subject to aging." He said: "Then, charioteer, turn back the chariot; go to the inner palace. For I, having gone to the inner palace, shall contemplate this matter: I have not passed beyond aging." That prince, Your Majesty, has gone into the inner palace (

body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had this thought: 'Surely the words of those <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> diviners and soothsayers will come to be true! Surely the prince, having shaved off his hair and beard and donned the saffron robes, will go forth from the household life to the homeless life with perfect faith! Let me provide the prince with ever greater measures of the five strands of sensual pleasure — perhaps, being delighted, he will not go forth.' body.translated_text: Again they raised a voice: 'If the prince does not take us, we shall enter the great ocean.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Enter it as you please.' They entered the great ocean. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> proceeded onward until he saw the farmers — with their heads covered in dust, their hands and feet cracked and split, their bodies powdered with dirt; and the oxen — their bodies wounded by the goad, their backs and hip regions soaked with blood, their breath obstructed by hunger, thirst, and exhaustion, their hearts oppressed by labored breathing, their wounds on the shoulders oozing with pus and blood from the pressure of the yoke, their bodily vitality being devoured by swarms of flies and worms, their feet lacerated by the plough and yoke, their mouths and nostrils streaming with saliva and mucus, covered with gadflies, mosquitoes, and skin parasites. Having seen this, with his mind overwhelmed by the compassion accumulated through beginningless eons of merit, he said this to the farmers: 'Sirs, to whom do you belong?' They said: 'To Your Lordship.' He said: 'Go, sirs — from this day forward you are neither slaves nor servants nor serfs; go wherever you wish and dwell in comfort.' And to the oxen he said: 'Go — you too, from this day forward, eat grass with uncut tips; drink clear, untrampled, and pure water; and may cool breezes blow from the four directions.'

body.translated_text: Then, having made an act of devotion with faith, he lifted the <s>Bodhisattva</s> from his couch, placed him on the chariot, and set out through the middle of the cremation ground toward <s>Kapilavastu</s>. Thus the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s harem consisted of sixty thousand women, headed by <s>Gopikā</s>, <s>Mṛgajā</s>, and <s>Yaśodharā</s>.

children.translated_text: ) have declared that the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, if he does not go forth within seven days, will become a <s>Cakravartin</s>. Therefore the <s>Bodhisattva</s> must be carefully guarded for seven days and nights. Let us have the city well-secured.' Then they surrounded the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> with seven ramparts and seven moats. Iron doors were placed at the city gates. Melodious bells were fastened to the doors, whose sound, when the doors were opened, resounded for a <s>yojana</s> in every direction. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> was stationed on the palace terrace, attended by beautiful and captivating women with dancing, singing, and music. Ministers with cavalry forces were posted at guard stations all around the outer rampart. Patrols were organized. A door to the inner apartments was constructed of the kind that requires five hundred men to open, and when opened, its sound resounded throughout King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s residence. Upon hearing that sound, the people of the inner apartments and those stationed at the city gates remained alert, as did the ministers, citizens, and country-folk stationed outside the city. With that great splendor, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, on the upper terrace of the palace, stood being serenaded by unmanned musical instruments — <s>vīṇā</s>, flute, <s>paṇava</s> drum, <s>sughoṣaka</s>, and the like. At night, outside, <s>Śuddhodana</s> with his fourfold army stood vigilant at the eastern gate; <s>Droṇodana</s> at the southern; <s>Śuklodana</s> at the western; <s>Amṛtodana</s> at the northern. In the middle of the city, a <s>Śākya</s> named <s>Mahānāman</s> was the night-watchman. He went to the eastern gate and called: 'Who is awake? Who is awake?' The king said: 'I am awake.' 'Stay awake, Your Majesty; wakefulness brings you welfare.' Having understood, he spoke this verse:

After six days and nights have passed, the prince will become a <s>Cakravartin</s>. We shall traverse the sky and travel across the four continents.' body.translated_text: Meanwhile, <s>Mahāprajāpatī</s> saw four dreams: the moon swallowed by <s>Rāhu</s>; the sun rising in the east and setting in the same [direction]; a great multitude bowing to herself; and herself laughing. <s>Yaśodharā</s> saw eight dreams: her maternal family line broken; the throne of fortune (<s>śrīparyaṅka</s>) broken; her bracelet-adorned arms broken; her rows of teeth shattered; her braid of hair fallen loose; the goddess of fortune (<s>Śrī</s>) departing from the house; the moon swallowed by <s>Rāhu</s>; the sun rising in the east and setting in the same [direction]. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too saw five dreams: the great earth as his great bed; Mount <s>Sumeru</s>, king of mountains, as his universal pillow; his left arm plunged into the eastern great ocean; his right arm plunged into the western great ocean; both feet plunged into the southern great ocean; a stalk of grass (<s>sthitikā tṛṇajāti</s>) growing from his navel up to the sky and remaining there; all-white birds with black heads falling at his feet and rising up to his kneecaps; birds of various colors coming from the four directions and standing before him as one color; himself walking upon a mountain of filth; having seen, with a joyful mind he reflected: 'Such dreams as I have seen — before long I shall attain the supreme knowledge.' Then <s>Yaśodharā</s> reported her dreams to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'My lord, today I have seen eight dreams.' (

body.translated_text: 'The maternal lineage-staff is broken; the royal couch (<s>śrīparyaṅka</s>) is broken; both bracelet-arms are broken; the string of teeth has scattered; the braid has fallen loose; <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) has left the house; the moon has been seized by <s>Rāhu</s>; the sun rose in the east and set right there.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, consoling <s>Yaśodharā</s>, explained away the dreams: 'You say "my maternal lineage-staff is broken" — is it not still standing? You say "the royal couch is broken" — it too is not broken; see, it is still here. You say "both bracelet-arms are broken" — look for yourself whether they are broken or not. You say "the string of teeth has scattered" — this is for you personally to verify; look whether they have scattered or not. You say "the braid has fallen loose" — this is for you personally to verify; look whether it has fallen loose or not. You say "<s>Śrī</s> has left my house" — a woman's husband is her <s>Śrī</s>; and here I still stand. You say "the moon has been seized by <s>Rāhu</s>" — but here the moon is clearly visible. You say "the sun rose in the east and set right there" — it is now midnight; it has not yet risen; how will it set?' Thus reassured, <s>Yaśodharā</s> fell silent. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflected: 'Given the dreams <s>Yaśodharā</s> has seen, I must certainly depart this very day. Let me tell her partially, by hints.' He told her partially, by hints. <s>Yaśodharā</s> said: 'Lord, wherever you go, you will take me there.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, speaking with <s>Nirvāṇa</s> as his hidden meaning, said: 'So be it. Wherever I go, there I shall take you.' (

The <s>Bodhisattva</s> looked back with his entire body to the right, with the gaze of an elephant (<s>nāgāvalokita</s>). He thought: 'This is my last night in which I share a bed in a house together with women.' Furthermore, he reflected: 'If I leave by the front gate and depart by another gate, the king will think at his final hour: "The prince did not look back at me."' Then he saw King <s>Śuddhodana</s> held fast in deep sleep. Circumambulating him, he said: 'Father, it is not from disrespect, not from lack of devotion that I go.
