) pratisandhir gṛhītaḥ; yadā bodhisatvo 'nuttarāṃ saṃyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate tadā taṃ khaṭuṃkāśvavādena avabodhya saṃsārakāntārād uttāryātyantaniṣṭhe yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratisthāpayiṣyati
children.translated_text: ) When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains the unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment, he will awaken that one through the sound of a donkey-driver's whip, and having ferried him across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, will establish him in the ultimate security of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

Then <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, the king of horses, licked the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet with his tongue. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, stroking him with a palm bearing the marks of wheel, <s>svastika</s>, and <s>nandyāvarta</s>, said: 'Go, <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>. When I have attained awakened enlightenment, I shall be grateful to you.' And he told <s>Chandaka</s>: 'You must not let <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> enter the inner palace.' Thus addressed, <s>Chandaka</s>, his voice choked with tears and his eyes overflowing, took <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> the king of horses and set out, looking back again and again at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The distance they had covered in two watches, they took seven nights to return. <s>Chandaka</s> reflected: 'If we enter at the same time, with the great lamentation I will not be able to hold myself together.' So he stayed in the park and sent <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> ahead. <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> neighed. Hearing that sound, the people of the inner court and other folk rushed out in alarm, but they did not see the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Embracing <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s> by the neck, they began to weep. For it is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that other ordinary animals born in lower realms attain conventional knowledge; how much more so <s>Kaṇṭhaka</s>, the king of horses! Hearing the great crowd's distress, inwardly choked by suppressed tears, he died. Through his merit, he took rebirth in a certain <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> family devoted to the six duties. (

body.text: The taking of the Yellow Robes
body.translated_text: The taking of the yellow robes

body.text: bodhisatvasya kāṣāyaiḥ prayojanam utpannam; anupame nagare 'nyatamo gṛhapatir āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī; tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam; sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati; tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> needed ochre robes (<s>kāṣāya</s>). In the city of <s>Anupama</s>, there was a certain householder — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, of vast and extensive property, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, competing with the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. He brought a wife from a family of equal status. He enjoyed, delighted, and sported with her. As he was enjoying, delighting, and sporting,

body.text: putro jātaḥ; evaṃ yāvad daśaputrā jātāh; sarvaiś ca pravrajya pratyekā bodhiḥ sākṣātkṛtā; teṣāṃ mātā vṛddhā; sā tebhyaḥ śāṇakāni cīvarāṇy anuprayacchati; tair abhihitā: aṃba vayaṃ parinirvāsyāmaḥ; nāsmākam etaiḥ prayojanam; kin tu rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya śākyamunir nāma putraḥ kumāro 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbhotsyate; tasyaitāni dāsyasi; tatas te mahatī phalāvāptir bhaviṣyati; ityuktvā jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtāḥ; tayāpi vṛddhayā tāni cīvarāṇi maraṇakāle duhitur dattāni; yathāvṛttaṃ cārocitam; sāpy asyā duhitā glānā saṃvṛttā; tayāpi maraṇāvasthāṃ paricchidya vṛkṣe sthāpitāni; yā devatā tasmin vṛkṣe 'dhyuṣitā sā āyācitā tvayaitāni rājñaḥ śuddhodanaputrasya dātavyānīti; śakrasya devendrasyādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate; tena tāni gṛhītvā nītāni; tato jarājīrṇalubdhavarṇam ātmānam abhinirmāya tāni prāvṛtya dhanurbāṇavyagrapāṇiḥ bodhisatvasya pratimārge 'vasthitaḥ; bodhisatvaś cānupūrveṇa taṃ mārgaṃ pratipannaḥ paśyati lubdhaṃ dhanurbāṇavyagrapāṇiṃ kāṣāyavastraprāvṛtam; dṛṣṭvā ca punas taṃ puruṣam āmantrayate: bhoḥ puruṣa etāni sāṇakāni vastrāṇi pravrajitānurūpāṇi; imāni kāśikasūkṣmāṇi gṛhāṇa; mamaitaṇy anuprayaccha iti; sa kathayati: kumāra nāham etāny anuprayacchāmi; mā me syur atonidānaṃ pare vaktāraḥ, tvayā rājakumāraṃ jīvitād vyaparopya etāni kāśikasūkṣmāṇi vastrāṇi gṛhītāni <iti>; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati: bhoḥ puruṣa sarvaloko (
body.translated_text: a son was born; thus up to ten sons were born. All of them went forth and realized <s>pratyeka</s> (solitary) enlightenment. Their mother grew old. She would offer hempen robes to them. They told her: 'Mother, we are going to attain final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. We have no need of these. But King <s>Śuddhodana</s> has a prince named <s>Śākyamuni</s> who will attain the unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment. Give these to him; from that a great fruit will arise for you.' Having said this, and having performed the supernatural feats of blazing, heating, raining, and illuminating, they attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the remainderless element of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>). The old woman, at the time of her death, gave those robes to her daughter and told her the whole story. That daughter too fell ill. Knowing that death was near, she placed them in a tree. The deity dwelling in that tree was entreated: 'You must give these to the son of King <s>Śuddhodana</s>.' <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, through whose lower faculty of knowledge and vision all is discerned, took those [robes] and brought them. Then, having created himself in the form of an aged, emaciated hunter, he wrapped himself in them and, with bow and arrows in hand, stood on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s path. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, proceeding gradually along that road, saw the hunter with bow and arrows in hand, wrapped in ochre robes. Having seen, he addressed that man: 'Sir, these hempen garments are suitable for a renunciant. Take these fine <s>Kāśī</s> silks; give me those.' He said: 'Prince, I shall not give these. Others might accuse me, saying: "You killed the prince and took these fine <s>Kāśī</s> silks."' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Sir, the whole world (

body.text: SBV I 93

) māṃ jānīte yāḍṛśo 'haṃ śaktisaṃpannaḥ; kaḥ śaknoti māṃ jīvitād vyaparopayitum; ko vā śraddhatte tvayāhaṃ jīvitād vyaparopita iti; nirviśaṅkaḥ prayaccha iti; tataḥ śakro devendro bodhisatvasya pādayor nipatya śāṇakāny anuprayacchati; kāśikāni gṛhṇāti; bodhisatvasya tāni śāṇakāni vastrāṇi na kāyapramāṇikāṇi; tasyaitad abhavat: aho bata me śāṇakāni cīvarāṇi kāyapramāṇikāni syur iti; vākpravyāhārasamanantaram eva bodhisatvasya tāni śāṇakāni cīvarāṇi kāyapramāṇikāni saṃvṛttāni; yathāpitad bodhisatvasya bodhisatvānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena; bodhisatvaḥ saṃlakṣayati: idānīm ahaṃ pravrajitaḥ, kariṣyāmi jagato 'nugraham iti; tatas tāni bodhisatvakāśikavastrāṇi <pratigṛhya> śakreṇa deveṣu trayastriṃśeṣu kāśikamahaḥ prajñaptaḥ; śrāddhair brāhmaṇagṛhapatibhir tasmin pradeśe kāṣāyapratigrahaṇaṃ nāma caityaṃ pratiṣṭhāpitam adyāpi caityavandakā bhikṣavo vandante; tato bodhisatvo muṇḍaḥ kāṣāyavastraprāvṛtaḥ itaś cāmutās ca paryaṭan bhārgavasya riṣer āśramapadam anuprāptaḥ
body.translated_text: ) knows what manner of being I am, endowed with such power. Who could kill me? Or who would believe that I was killed by you? Give [them] without hesitation.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, fell at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet and gave him the hempen [robes], taking the <s>Kāśī</s> silks. Those hempen garments did not fit the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body. He thought: 'Oh, if only these hempen robes would fit my body!' No sooner had he spoken these words than the hempen robes became fitted to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s body — just as things happen through the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s power and through the power of the deities. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflected: 'Now I am a renunciant. I shall perform a benefit for the world.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, having received the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s <s>Kāśī</s> silks, established among the Thirty-three gods a festival called '<s>Kāśikamaha</s>' (Festival of the <s>Kāśī</s> Silks). Devout <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders established at that spot a shrine called '<s>Kāṣāyapratigrahaṇa</s>' (Reception of the Ochre Robes); even today, monks who venerate shrines pay homage to it. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, shaven-headed and wrapped in ochre robes, wandering here and there, arrived at the hermitage of the sage <s>Bhārgava</s>.

body.translated_text: The sage <s>Bhārgava</s>

body.translated_text: At that time, the sage <s>Bhārgava</s>, resting his cheek on his hand, was absorbed in thought.

body.text: vyavasthitaḥ; sa bodhisatvena tathāvidho dṛṣṭaḥ; uktaś ca: maharṣe kim arthaṃ kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparas tiṣṭhasi iti; sa kathayati: mamāsminn āśramapade tālāḥ sauvarṇaiḥ puṣpaphalair āsan; te yathā paurāṇāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ iti; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati: maharṣe yasyānubhāvād etasminn āśramapade tālāḥ sauvarṇaiḥ puṣpaphalair āsan sa jīrṇāturamṛtasandarśanād udvigno vanaṃ saṃśṛtaḥ; yady asau jīrṇāturamṛtasandarśanād udvignas tapovanaṃ <na> saṃśṛto 'bhaviṣyat tasyaitad udyānam abhaviṣyat; ity evam ukto bhārgavariṣir bodhisatvaṃ nirīkṣitum ārabdhah; tato rūpaśobhāṃ śāntaṃ ca veṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā, ciraṃ nirīkṣya kutūhalajātaḥ kathayati: bhoḥ pravrajita mā haiva tvam eva saḥ; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati: maharṣe vyaktam etat; tato bhārgavena vismayotphulladṛṣṭinā bodhisatvas tatprathamata āsanenopanimantritaḥ puṣpaphalaiś ca; evaṃ pratisaṃmodito muhūrtam āsthāya kathayati: maharṣe kiyad dūram itaḥ kapilavastu nagaram (
body.translated_text: was standing thus; the <s>Bodhisattva</s> saw him in such a state and said: 'O great sage, why do you stand with your cheek resting on your hand, absorbed in worry?' He replied: 'In this hermitage of mine, the palm trees used to bear golden flowers and fruits; now they have become as they were in ancient times.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Great sage, the one by whose power the palm trees in this hermitage bore golden flowers and fruits — he, agitated by the sight of old age, sickness, and death, has taken refuge in the forest. Had he not been agitated by the sight of old age, sickness, and death and taken refuge in the ascetic forest, this would have been his garden.' When thus addressed, the sage <s>Bhārgava</s> began to gaze at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then, seeing his beauty of form and his serene appearance, after gazing for a long time, filled with curiosity, he said: 'O renunciant, could it be that you yourself are he?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Great sage, that is evident.' Then <s>Bhārgava</s>, with eyes wide open in astonishment, invited the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to be seated first and offered him flowers and fruits. Having been thus greeted, after resting for a moment, he said: 'Great sage, how far from here is the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>? (

children.translated_text: I shall proclaim the going forth — how the one with eyes went forth,
how, upon investigation, he resolved upon going forth.
'Crowded is the household life, a dwelling-place of impurities;
going forth is open space' — knowing this, he thus went forth. //

body.translated_text: Having crossed the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, wandering gradually on his journey, he arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being skilled in various crafts and trades, having fashioned a leaf-cup of oleander leaves, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms with a serene deportment. At that time, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> had ascended to the upper terrace of the palace. He saw him going about for alms-food (<s>piṇḍapāta</s>) with a pleasing manner of advancing and withdrawing, of looking ahead and looking aside, of bending and stretching, and of wearing the outer robe (<s>saṅghāṭī</s>), inner robe (<s>cīvara</s>), and carrying the bowl (<s>pātra</s>). Having seen, he thought: 'Of all the renunciants and accomplished ones dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, none has such a deportment as this renunciant.' And here it is said:

children.translated_text: Having gone forth, then with his body he abandoned evil deeds;

Then, having gone to <s>Rājagṛha</s>, the best of cities of the <s>Magadhas</s>,
the protector went about for alms, fully aware and mindful. //

with a pleased mind, having seen, he then said this to his ministers: //

body.translated_text: King <s>Bimbisāra</s> said: 'O renunciant, what do you seek by this vow?' He replied: 'Unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' The king said: 'O renunciant, when you have attained unsurpassed perfect awakening, please remember us as well.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'So be it; I shall remember you.' Having said this, he departed from <s>Rājagṛha</s>.

Considering that path as inadequate, he approached <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>. Having approached, he said this to <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>: 'If it is not burdensome to you, <s>Ārāḍa</s>, I would practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in your presence.' He replied: 'It is not burdensome to me, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>; dwell at ease.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'How many states have you, <s>Ārāḍa</s>, realized?' He replied: 'As far as the sphere of nothingness (<s>ākiñcanyāyatana</s>), Venerable <s>Gautama</s>.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: '<s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s> too has faith, and I too have faith; <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s> too has energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom, and I too have energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s> has directly realized these states as far as the sphere of nothingness. Why should I not directly realize these states?' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the sake of attaining those unattained states, for the sake of realizing those unrealized states, for the sake of directly knowing those not yet directly known, dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute, exerted himself. Dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute, he before long directly realized those states. Having directly realized those states, he again approached <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>. Having approached, he said this to <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>: 'Is it not the case, <s>Ārāḍa</s>, that you have directly realized these states through your own higher knowledge, as far as the sphere of nothingness?' He replied: 'Indeed, <s>Gautama</s>, I have directly realized these states as far as the sphere of nothingness.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I too, Venerable <s>Ārāḍa</s>, have directly realized these states through my own higher knowledge, as far as the sphere of nothingness.' 'Then, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, as far as you [have attained], so far have I; as far as I, so far you. Come, let us both together lead this community.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having understood that this path was not sufficient, approached <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s>. Having approached, he said to <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s>: 'If it is not burdensome to you, <s>Udraka</s>, I would practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in your presence.' 'It is not burdensome to me, venerable <s>Gautama</s>. Dwell at your ease.' 'How many states (<s>dharmas</s>) have you, <s>Udraka</s>, directly realized?' 'Up to the station of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (<s>naivasaṃjñānāsaṃjñāyatana</s>), venerable <s>Gautama</s>.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: '<s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s> has faith; I too have faith. <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s> has energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom; I too have energy, mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom. <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s> has directly realized states up to the station of neither-perception-nor-non-perception. Why should I not directly realize these states?' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, for the attainment of those very states not yet attained, for the realization of those not yet realized, for the direct knowledge of those not yet directly known, dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, with resolute mind, exerted himself. Dwelling alone, secluded, heedful, ardent, with resolute mind, before long he directly realized those states. Having directly realized those states, he again approached <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s>. Having approached, he said to <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s>: 'Have you, <s>Udraka</s>, directly realized these states through your own higher knowledge up to the station of neither-perception-nor-non-perception?' 'Indeed, venerable <s>Gautama</s>, I have directly realized these states up to the station of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I too, venerable <s>Udraka</s>, have directly realized these states through my own higher knowledge up to the station of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.' 'Then, venerable <s>Gautama</s>, what is yours is mine; what is mine is yours. Come, let the two of us together lead this community. In this matter, we two are equal, having attained the same [level].' Then <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s>, though he was the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s former teacher, honored him with the highest honor, venerated him with the highest veneration, and was delighted and pleased with respect to the highest matters concerning him. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'This path too is not sufficient for knowledge, not sufficient for vision, not sufficient for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' body.translated_text: King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, overcome by grief for his son, constantly sent messengers to search for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. He heard that prince <s>Siddhārtha</s>, having dwelt with <s>Udraka Rāmaputra</s>, had departed from <s>Rājagṛha</s> and was wandering without attendants. Having heard, he sent three hundred attendants. In the city of <s>Devadṛśa</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> <s>Suprabuddha</s> likewise heard; he too sent two hundred attendants. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surrounded by five hundred attendants, wandered in the austerity-grove. He reflected: 'The practice of an austerity-grove

body.text: ākīrṇavihāratā ca nālam amṛtādhigamāya; yanv ahaṃ pañcopasthāyakān gṛhītvā pariśiṣṭān preṣayeyam iti; tena mātṛpakṣād dvau gṛhītau, pitṛpakṣāt trayaḥ; te tasyopasthānaṃ kurvanti; atha bodhisatvaḥ pañcabhir upasthāyakaiḥ parivṛto gayādakṣiṇena yenorubilvāsenāyanīgrāmakas tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ; sa itaś cāmutaś ca paribhramann adrākṣīd ramaṇīyaṃ pṛthivīpradeśam, prāsādikaṃ vanaṣaṇḍam, nadīṃ ca nairañjanāṃ śītalasyandanāṃ sasikatāṃ sūpatīrthāṃ haritaśādvalavistīrṇakūlāṃ nānāvṛkṣopaśobhitāṃ ramaṇīyāṃ; dṛṣṭvā ca punar asyaitad abhavat: ramaṇīyo batāyaṃ pṛthivīpradeśaḥ, prāsādikaṃ ca vanaṣaṇḍam, nadī ca nairañjanā śītalasyandanā sasikatā sūpatīrthā haritaśādvalavistīrṇakūlā nānāvṛkṣopaśobhitā ramaṇīyā; aho bata prahāṇārthinā kulaputreṇemaṃ vanaṣaṇḍam niśritya prahāṇaṃ praṇidhātuṃ <yuktam>; ahaṃ ca prahāṇenārthī; yanv aham imaṃ vanaṣaṇḍaṃ niśritya prahāṇaṃ praṇidadhyām iti (
body.translated_text: and the state of dwelling in crowded conditions are not sufficient for attaining the deathless (<s>amṛta</s>). Let me keep five attendants and send the rest away.' He kept two from the mother's side and three from the father's side. They attended upon him. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, surrounded by five attendants, set out on a journey to the south of <s>Gayā</s>, toward the village of <s>Urubilvāsenāyanī</s>. Wandering here and there, he saw a delightful tract of land, a pleasing grove, and the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> — with cool, flowing waters, sandy, with easy fords, with banks spread with green grass, adorned with various trees, delightful. Having seen, he thought: 'How delightful is this tract of land! How pleasing is this grove! And the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> is cool-flowing, sandy, with easy fords, with banks spread with green grass, adorned with various trees, delightful. It would be fitting for a son of good family who seeks striving to rely upon this grove and devote himself to striving. And I too seek striving. Let me rely upon this grove and devote myself to striving.' (

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having entered that grove, sat down at the foot of a certain tree. Pressing teeth against teeth, pressing the tip of the tongue against the palate, he restrained, suppressed, and tormented mind with mind. As he restrained, suppressed, and tormented mind with mind, sweat poured from every pore of his body. Just as a strong man, having seized a weaker man by the upper arms, were to restrain, suppress, and torment him, and sweat would pour from his pores — even so, at that time, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> pressed teeth against teeth, pressed the tip of the tongue against the palate, and restrained, suppressed, and tormented mind with mind, sweat poured from every pore of his body. Yet his energy was aroused and unshrinking; his body was calm and unagitated; his mindfulness was established and unconfused; his mind was concentrated and one-pointed. Though the <s>Bodhisattva</s> experienced such painful, sharp, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable feeling, his mind was not overwhelmed — because his body had been cultivated [through prior practice]. He then thought: 'Let me practice breath-restraining meditation (<s>vyādhmātaka dhyāna</s>) to an even greater degree.' He began to practice breath-restraining meditation to a greater degree. Practicing breath-restraining meditation, he held back the in-breaths and out-breaths through mouth and nose. When the in-breaths and out-breaths through mouth and nose were held back, at that time exceedingly intense headaches arose in his head. Just as a strong man were to tie a tight leather strap around a weaker man's head, exceedingly intense headaches would arise — even so, as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> practiced breath-restraining meditation, exceedingly intense headaches arose in his head. Yet his energy was aroused and unshrinking; his body was calm and unagitated; his mindfulness was established and unconfused; his mind was concentrated and one-pointed. body.text: atha saṃbahulā devatā bodhisatvasya cetasā cittam ājñāya yena bodhisatvas tenopasaṅkrāntāḥ; upasaṅkramya bodhisatvam idam avocan: sacet tvaṃ mārṣa mānuṣyakeṇāhāreṇārttīyase jehrīyasi vitarasi vijugupsase, vayaṃ te sarvaromakūpeṣu divyam ojaḥ kāye upasaṃharāmaḥ; tat tvam āsādaya iti; atha bodhisatvasyaitad abhavat: ahaṃ cen manuṣyāṇām anāhāratāṃ pratijānīyām, devatāś ca me sarvaromakūpeṣu divyam
body.translated_text: Then numerous deities, having understood the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind with their own minds, approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, they said to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'If you, sir, are weary, disgusted, averse, and repulsed by human food, we shall infuse divine nourishment (<s>ojas</s>) into your body through all your pores. Please accept it.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'If I were to profess to humans that I am fasting, yet deities were to infuse divine nourishment into my body through all my pores, and I were to accept that, that would be a falsehood for me. What would be a falsehood would be a wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>) for me. And on account of wrong view, some beings here, at the breaking up of the body after death, are reborn in a state of deprivation, an evil destiny, a downfall, in the hells. Let me completely refuse the words of the deities and take only a little, a small, a scanty, a meager amount of food — whether soup of <s>mudga</s> (mung beans), or soup of <s>kulattha</s> (horse gram), or soup of <s>hareṇukā</s> (a type of pulse).'

body.translated_text: ) remained aroused and unshrinking; his body remained tranquil and unagitated; his mindfulness remained established and unconfused; his mind remained concentrated and one-pointed. Even as the <s>Bodhisattva</s> at that time experienced such self-inflicted painful, intense, harsh, bitter, and disagreeable sensations, his mind did not become overwhelmed. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, eating only a little, scant, meager, slight amount of food, his spine became like a twisted rope; his buttocks became like a camel's hoof. Sometimes, trying to stand up, he fell face-down; sometimes, trying to sit down, he fell on his back. Holding the front of his body, he would steady the back; holding the back of his body, he would steady the front. He rubbed his body with both hands, massaged it; and as he rubbed and massaged his body with both hands, even now his body-hairs, rotted at the roots, fell to the ground. Then this thought occurred to him: 'This path too is not sufficient for knowledge, not sufficient for vision, not sufficient for supreme perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' Then three deities approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The first said: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is dark.' The second said: 'He is not dark, but swarthy.' The third said: 'He is neither dark nor swarthy, but has the complexion of a <s>madgura</s> fish (catfish).' The <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s beautiful, radiant complexion had completely disappeared.

body.text: atha bodhisatvasya tasmin samaye aśrutapūrvās tisra upamāḥ pratibhātāḥ; 1) tadyathā ārdraṃ kāṣṭhaṃ sasnehaṃ jala upanikṣiptaṃ syād ārāt sthalāt; atha puruṣa āgacched agnyarthī agnigaveṣī; sa tatrādharāraṇyām uttarāraṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpya abhimathnan na bhavyo 'gniṃ saṃjanayituṃ, tejaḥ prāviṣkartum; evam eva tad bhavati yathāpitad ārdrāt kāṣṭhāt sasnehāt; evam eva ye kecic chramaṇā vā brāhmaṇā vā kāmeṣu na kāyena cittena vā vyapakṛṣṭā viharanti, teṣāṃ yaḥ kāmeṣu kāmacchandaḥ kāmasnehaḥ kāmapremā kāmālayaḥ kāmaniyantrī kāmādhyavasānaṃ <sa> teṣāṃ cittaṃ paryādāya tiṣṭhati; evam eva tad bhavati yathāpitat kāyena cittena (
body.translated_text: Then at that time, three previously unheard similes occurred to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 1) Suppose a wet, sap-filled piece of wood were placed in water, far from dry land. Then a man should come, seeking fire, searching for fire. If he were to place an upper fire-stick upon a lower fire-stick and rub, he would not be able to generate fire or produce heat — and this is because of the wet, sap-filled wood. Even so, whatever ascetics or <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> do not dwell with body and mind withdrawn from sensual pleasures — their desire for pleasures, attachment to pleasures, love of pleasures, reliance on pleasures, bondage to pleasures, fixation on pleasures — this overwhelms their minds. ) āharati; na tāvad dvitīyaṃ yāvad asya tad ojaḥ kāyān na vigataṃ bhavati; tasyaikaṃ tilam āhāram āharataḥ sutarām aṅgapratyaṅgāni parikṣīṇāni, yathā ekaṃ tilam, ekaṃ taṇḍulam, ekaṃ kolam, ekaṃ kulattham, ekaṃ māṣam, ekaṃ mudgaṃ
body.translated_text: ) — he did not take a second until the nourishment of the first had not yet departed from his body. As he ate a single sesame seed as food, his major and minor limbs became even more emaciated. Similarly with one grain of rice, one jujube, one horse-gram, one black bean, one mung bean.

body.text: Reaction of Śuddhodana and others
body.translated_text: Reaction of <s>Śuddhodana</s> and others:

body.text: tāṃ duṣkaracaryāvasthāṃ śrutvā rājā śuddhodanaḥ ardhatṛtīyāni vārtāvāhakaśatāni preṣayati; suprabuddho 'pi rājā ardhatṛtīyāni; tayoḥ pratidivasaṃ muhur muhur vārtāṃ kathayanti: bodhisatva īdṛśīṃ duṣkaracaryāṃ carati; ekaṃ tilam āhāram āharati; ekaṃ taṇḍulam, ekaṃ kolam, ekaṃ kulattham, ekaṃ māṣam, ekaṃ mudgam; darbhasaṃstare ca śayyāṃ kalpyati; iti śrutvā rājā śuddhodanaḥ putraśokābhibhūto bhūyasyā mātrayā bāṣpopatapyamānahṛdayo 'śruparyākulekṣaṇaḥ santapyate; darbhasaṃstare ca śayyāṃ kalpayati; sārdham antaḥpureṇa yaśodharā devī bhartus tadavasthāṃ pratiśrutya bhartṛśokābhibhūtā bāṣpārdravadanā vinirmuktamālyābharaṇā viṣaṇṇā
body.translated_text: Having heard of his condition during these severe austerities, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> sent two hundred and fifty news-carriers; King <s>Suprabuddha</s> also [sent] two hundred and fifty. They reported news to both repeatedly, day after day: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> is practicing such severe austerities. He eats a single sesame seed as food; a single grain of rice, a single jujube, a single horse-gram, a single black bean, a single mung bean. And he prepares his bed on a spread of <s>darbha</s> grass.' Having heard this, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, overwhelmed by grief for his son, with heart burning all the more with tears, his eyes overflowing with tears, was consumed with anguish. And he prepared his bed on a spread of <s>darbha</s> grass. Together with the inner apartments, Queen <s>Yaśodharā</s>, hearing of her husband's condition, overwhelmed by grief for her husband, with tear-drenched face, having discarded garlands and ornaments, dejected,

body.text: duṣkaraṃ carati; ekaṃ tilam āhāram āharati; ekaṃ taṇḍulam, ekaṃ kolam, ekaṃ kulattham, ekaṃ mudgam; tṛṇasaṃstare ca śayyāṃ kalpayati; tasyāḥ sa garbho layaṃ gataḥ; rājñā śuddhodanena śrutam; sa saṃlakṣayati: yadi yaśodharā pratidivasaṃ bodhisatvasya vārtāṃ śṛṇoti sthānam etad vidyate yad bhartṛśokābhyāhatā anayā duṣkaracaryayā garbhaṃ na dhārayiṣyati; prāṇair vā viyokṣyate; tad upāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartvayaṃ yena yaśodharāyā bodhisatvavārtāṃ na kaścit kathayati iti viditvā rājñā śuddhodanena sarvāntaḥpurajanaḥ kriyākāraṃ kārito na kenacit bodhisatvavārtā yaśodharāyā arocayitavyā <iti>; vārtāsaṃcārakāś ca samanuśiṣṭāḥ, māṃ muktvā na kasyacid bodhisatvavārtā nivedayitavyeti; śrutvāpi svayaṃ vārtāṃ yaśodharāpekṣayā antarnigūḍhasantāpo 'nyathāntaḥpurajanaṃ vipralaṃbhayati, yaṃ śrutvā yaśodharā devī prāṇān sandhārayati (
body.translated_text: practiced severe austerities. She ate a single sesame seed as food; a single grain of rice, a single jujube, a single horse-gram, a single mung bean. And she prepared her bed on a spread of grass. Her embryo was absorbed [i.e., the pregnancy was suspended]. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> heard of this. He reflected: 'If <s>Yaśodharā</s> hears the news of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> daily, it is quite possible that, stricken with grief for her husband, she will not be able to carry the embryo through these severe austerities, or she will lose her life. A stratagem must be devised so that no one tells <s>Yaśodharā</s> the news of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>.' Having decided thus, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> made all the people of the inner apartments take a solemn oath: 'No one shall report the news of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> to <s>Yaśodharā</s>.' And he instructed the news-carriers: 'Except to me, the news of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> shall not be conveyed to anyone.' Even after hearing the news himself, out of concern for <s>Yaśodharā</s>, concealing his inner anguish, he deceived the people of the inner apartments with contrary reports, so that Queen <s>Yaśodharā</s> might sustain her life. (

children.translated_text: Unpalatable food:

children.text: atha bodhisatvasyaitad abhavat: ayam api mārgo nālaṃ jñānāya, nālaṃ darśanāya, nālam anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye; yanv ahaṃ paramavikṛtam āhāram āhareyam iti; sa paramavikṛtabhojanam āhāram āharati; tatredaṃ paramavikṛtabhojanam; ye te vatsakā acirajātakā mātus stanyena yāpayanti teṣām uccāraprasrāvaḥ; tāvac ca na dvitīyam āhāram āharati, yāvad asya tad ojaḥ kāyān na vigataṃ bhavati; dvitīye tu <vigate> dvitīyam āhāram āharati; mahāśmaśānaṃ ca gatvā mṛtakaḍebaraṃ śirasy upanidhāya dakṣiṇena pārśvena śayyāṃ kalpayati pāde pādam ādhāyālokasaṃjñī smṛtaḥ saṃprajānan utthānasaṃjñām eva manasi kurvānaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'This path too is not sufficient for knowledge, not sufficient for vision, not sufficient for unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>). Let me take extremely repulsive food.' He began taking extremely repulsive food. And this was the extremely repulsive food: those calves that are just born and subsist on their mother's milk — their urine and excrement [constituted his food]. He would not take a second meal until the nourishment from the first had been completely exhausted from his body; only when the second [portion of nourishment] was exhausted would he take a second meal. Going to the great charnel ground, placing a dead corpse at his head, he arranged his bed on the right side, placing foot upon foot, mindful with the perception of light, clearly comprehending, directing his mind to the perception of rising.

body.text: Village girls and boys
body.translated_text: Village girls and boys

body.text: apīdānīm grāmakumārakā grāmakumārikāś cāgamyāsyobhayoḥ karṇasrotasos tūlikā āsārayanty api prasārayanty api; ubhayoḥ karṇasrotasor evaṃ cāhuḥ, pāṃsupiśācakaṃ bata paśyāmaḥ, pāṃsupiśācakaṃ bata paśyāmaḥ iti; apīdānīṃ pāṃsum api kṣipanti, loṣṭam api, śarkarām api; nābhijānāti bodhisatvas teṣāṃ grāmakumārakāṇāṃ grāmakumārikāṇāṃ vā antike praduṣṭaṃ cittam utpādayituṃ, pāpikāṃ vā vācaṃ niścārayitum; evaṃrūpāṇi bodhisatvasya duṣkarāṇi carataḥ etad abhavat: ye kecid duḥkhaprahāṇayogam anuyuktā viharanti sarve te etāvan nāta uttareṇa; ato bhūyas so 'pi mārgo nālaṃ jñānāya, nālaṃ darśanāya, nālam anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye iti; ārabdhaṃ cāsya vīryaṃ bhavaty asaṃlīnam; prasrabdhaḥ kāyo bhavaty asaṃrabdhaḥ; upasthitā smṛtir bhavaty asaṃmūḍhā; samāhitaṃ cittaṃ bhavaty ekāgram; tasyaitad abhavat: katamo 'sau mārgaḥ alaṃ jñānāya, alaṃ darśanāya, alam anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhaye iti; tasyaitad abhavat: abhijānāmy ahaṃ pituḥ śuddhodanasya niveśane karmāntān anusaṅgamya jambūcchāyāyāṃ niṣadya
body.translated_text: Then village boys and village girls would come and insert sticks into both his ear canals, and pull them out again; into both his ear canals they would speak thus: 'Just look — a dust-demon! Just look — a dust-demon!' They would throw dust at him, clods of earth, and pebbles. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> could not bring himself to generate an angry thought toward those village boys and village girls, nor to utter a harsh word. While the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was practicing such difficult austerities, he thought: 'Whoever dwells devoted to the practice of eliminating suffering — all of them [do] this much and no further. Moreover, this path too is not sufficient for knowledge, not sufficient for vision, not sufficient for unsurpassed perfect awakening.' Yet his energy was aroused and unshrinking; his body was calm and unagitated; his mindfulness was established and unconfused; his mind was concentrated and one-pointed. He then thought: 'What, then, is the path that is sufficient for knowledge, sufficient for vision, sufficient for unsurpassed perfect awakening?' He thought: 'I remember that in my father <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s house, having gone out to observe the field-work, sitting in the shade of a <s>jambu</s> tree,

body.text: viviktaṃ kāmair viviktaṃ pāpakair akuśalair dharmaiḥ savitarkaṃ savicāraṃ vivekajaṃ prītisukhaṃ (
body.translated_text: secluded from sensual desires, secluded from unwholesome states, accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, born of seclusion, with joy and happiness, (

body.text: SBV I 108

) prathamaṃ dhyānam upasaṃpadya vihartum; syāt sa mārgaḥ, syāt pratipad alaṃ jñānāya, alaṃ darśanāya, alam anuttarāyai samyaksaṃbodhye; sa tu mayā na sukaram utpādayituṃ yathāpitat kṛśena durbalenāplasthāmena; yanv ahaṃ yathāsukham āśvasyāṃ yathāsukhaṃ praśvasyāṃ, yathāsukham audāram āhāram āhareyam odanakulmāṣān; sarpistailābhyāṃ gātrāṇi mrakṣayeyam; sukhodakena ca kāyaṃ pariṣiñceyam iti; sa yathāsukham āśvasiti, yathāsukhaṃ praśvasiti; audārikam āhāram āharaty odanakulmāṣān; sarpistailābhyāṃ gātrāṇi mrakṣayati; sukhodakena ca kāyaṃ pariṣiñcati
body.translated_text: ) I had entered and dwelt in the first <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). Could that be the path, could that be the practice sufficient for knowledge, sufficient for vision, sufficient for unsurpassed perfect awakening? But that cannot easily be generated by me while I am this emaciated, feeble, and lacking in strength. Let me breathe in comfortably, breathe out comfortably, and take substantial food — rice and barley gruel. Let me anoint my limbs with ghee and oil, and bathe my body with warm water.' He breathed in comfortably, breathed out comfortably; he took substantial food — rice and barley gruel; he anointed his limbs with ghee and oil; and he bathed his body with warm water.

children.translated_text: The five attendants desert

children.text: atha teṣāṃ pañcānām upasthāyakānām etad abhavat: ayaṃ bhavantaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ śaithilikaḥ saṃvṛtto, bāhuliko bahulājīvaḥ, prahāṇavibhrānto ya eṣa idānīm audārikam āhāram āharaty odanakulmāṣān; sarpistailābhyāṃ gātrāṇi mrakṣayati; sukhodakena kāyaṃ pariṣiñcati; na śakyam anenādhunā kiṃcid adhigantum; iti viditvā bodhisatvam apahāya prakrāntāḥ, anupūrveṇa vārāṇasīṃ gatvā ye loke arhantas tān uddiśya pravrajitāḥ; te pañca samagrāḥ sahitāḥ saṃmodamānā avivadamānā ṛṣivadane viharanti mṛgadāve iti pañcakāḥ pañcakā iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā
children.translated_text: Then those five attendants thought: 'Sirs, this ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has become lax, given to excess, living a life of abundance, fallen from striving. He now takes substantial food — rice and barley gruel; anoints his limbs with ghee and oil; bathes his body with warm water. He cannot now attain anything.' Knowing this, they abandoned the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and departed. Gradually reaching <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, they went forth, having gone forth in honor of the <s>Arhats</s> in the world. The five of them, harmonious, in concord, rejoicing together, not quarreling, dwelt at the Deer Park (<s>Mṛgadāva</s>) in <s>Ṛṣivadana</s>. They acquired the designation 'the group of five' (<s>pañcakāḥ</s>).

body.text: Nandā and Nandabalā
body.translated_text: <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>

body.text: bodhisatvo 'py anupūrveṇa kāyasya sthāmaṃ ca balaṃ ca viryaṃ ca saṃjanayya anupūrveṇa senāyanīgrāmaṃ gataḥ; tatra seno nāma grāmikaḥ; tasya dve duhitarau nandā ca nandabalā ca; tābhyāṃ śrutam: śākyānāṃ kumāra utpanno 'nuhimavatpārśve nadyā bhāgīrathyās tīre kapilasya ṛṣer āśramapadasya nātidūre: sa brāhmaṇair naimittikair vipañcanakair vyāktṛaḥ rājā bhaviṣyati cakravartī; sa cābhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvalakṣaṇasaṃpannaḥ sarvajanamanoharaḥ; yā nārī dvādaśavarṣāṇi idam evaṃrūpaṃ vrataṃ samādāya vartate tasyā (
body.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, having gradually regained the strength, power, and energy of his body, gradually went to the village of <s>Senāyanī</s>. There lived a village headman named <s>Sena</s>. He had two daughters, <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>. They had heard: 'A prince has been born among the <s>Śākyas</s>, at the base of the <s>Himālaya</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Bhāgīrathī</s>, not far from the hermitage of the sage <s>Kapila</s>. He has been prophesied by <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> diviners and soothsayers to become a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>. He is handsome, lovely, and pleasing, endowed with all the marks, captivating the minds of all people. Whatever woman observes a vow of this kind for twelve years — he will be her husband.' (

body.text: SBV I 109

) asau bhartā bhavati iti; puruṣābhiprāyo mātṛgrāmaḥ; tābhyāṃ dvādaśavārṣikaṃ vrataṃ taptam; tasya samāptau ṣoḍaśaguṇitaṃ madhupāyasaṃ tapaḥparikhinnāya ṛṣaye pratipādyate āgantukāya iti śrutvā ca punas tābhyāṃ gosahasraṃ dohayitvā tad eva gosahasraṃ pāyitam; tatas tad eva gosahasraṃ dohayitvā pañcaśatāni pāyitāni; tatas tāni pañcaśatāni dohayitvā tāny eva <pañcaśatāni> pāyitāni; <tataḥ tāni> pañcaśatāni dohayitvā ardhatṛtīyāni śatāni pāyitāni; tatas tāny ardhatṛtīyāni śatāni dohayitvā <tāny evārdhatṛtīyāni śatāni pāyitani; tatas tāny ardhatṛtīyāni śātāni dohayitvā> pañcaviṃśatyuttaram śataṃ pāyitam; tatas tat pañcaviṃṣatyuttaraṃ śataṃ dohayitvā <tad eva pañcaviṃśatyuttaraṃ śataṃ pāyitam; tataḥ tat pañcaviṃśatyuttaraṃ śataṃ dohayitvā> triṣaṣṭiḥ pāyitā; tatas tāṃ triṣaṣṭiṃ dohayitvā saiva triṣaṣṭiḥ pāyitā; tatas tāṃ triṣaṣṭiṃ dohayitvā dvātriṃśat pāyitā; tatas tā dvātriṃśat dohayitvā tā eva dvātriṃśat pāyitāḥ; tatas tā dvātriṃśat dohayitvā ṣoḍaśa pāyitāḥ; tatas tāḥ ṣoḍaśa dohayitvā tā eva ṣoḍaśa
body.translated_text: ) Women are inclined toward men. The two of them observed the twelve-year vow. At its completion, a milk-rice (<s>madhupāyasa</s>) concentrated sixteen-fold was to be offered to a weary sage who comes as a guest. Having heard this, the two of them had a thousand cows milked and fed that [milk] to that very thousand cows. Then having milked that thousand cows, they fed five hundred. Then having milked those five hundred, they fed those very five hundred. Then having milked those five hundred, they fed two hundred and fifty. Then having milked those two hundred and fifty, they fed those very two hundred and fifty. Then having milked those two hundred and fifty, they fed one hundred and twenty-five. Then having milked that one hundred and twenty-five, they fed that very one hundred and twenty-five. Then having milked that one hundred and twenty-five, they fed sixty-three. Then having milked those sixty-three, they fed those very sixty-three. Then having milked those sixty-three, they fed thirty-two. Then having milked those thirty-two, they fed those very thirty-two. Then having milked those thirty-two, they fed sixteen. Then having milked those sixteen, they fed those very sixteen.

body.text: pāyitāḥ; tatas tāḥ ṣodaśa dohayitvā aṣṭau pāyitāḥ; tatas tā aṣṭau dohayitvā tā evāṣṭau pāyitāḥ; tatas tā aṣṭau dohayitvā sphaṭikamayyāṃ sthālyāṃ ṣoḍaśaguṇitaṃ madhupāyasaṃ sādhayitum ārabdhāḥ; śuddhāvāsakāyikā devāḥ saṃlakṣayanti; bodhisatvaḥ idaṃ pāyasaṃ bhuktvā adyaivānuttaraṃ jñānam adhigamiṣyati; tatas tejaupasaṃhāraḥ kartavya iti taiḥ sadyobalā oṣadhayaḥ prakṣiptāḥ; tatra ca kṣīre saṃparivartamāne cakrasvastikanandyāvartāni cihnāni dṛśyante; tatra ca upago nāmājīvakaḥ paribhramaṃs taṃ pradeṣam anuprāptaḥ; tena tat pāyasaṃ dṛṣṭam; sa saṃlakṣayati: ya etat pāyasaṃ bhuṅkte so 'nuttaraṃ jñānam adhigamiṣyati; yanv aham etat prārthayeyam iti; sa muhūrtam ekānte prakramya sthito yāvad avatāritam iti; sa upasaṅkramya kathayati: kṣuttarṣaśramapīḍito 'smi; mamaitat prayaccha iti; te kathayataḥ: nānuprayacchāma iti; sa tūṣṇīṃ prakrāntaḥ; tatas tābhyāṃ sphaṭikamayyāṃ sthālyāṃ ratnamayyāṃ pātryāṃ prakṣiptam; śakrasya devendrasyādhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: tasyām avasthāyāṃ brāhmaṇaveṣam abhinirmāya tayoḥ purato 'vasthitaḥ; brahmāpy avatīrya tasyādūre avasthitaḥ; te śakrāya dātum ārabdhe; sa kathayati: kiṃ mamānuprayacchatha āhosvid yo mamāntikād viśiṣṭataraḥ? yas tavāntikād viśiṣṭataraḥ tasyānuprayacchāvaḥ; ayaṃ brahmā mamāntikāt prativiśiṣṭaḥ; tad asyānuprayacchatam; te tasmai dātum ārabdhe; (
body.translated_text: Then having milked those sixteen, they fed eight. Then having milked those eight, they fed those very eight. Then having milked those eight, they began to prepare the sixteen-fold concentrated milk-rice (<s>madhupāyasa</s>) in a crystal vessel. The gods of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> (Pure Abodes) reflected: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having eaten this milk-rice, will this very day attain the unsurpassed knowledge. Therefore, a concentration of vital essence must be effected.' They cast in herbs of immediate potency. As the milk churned therein, the signs of wheel, <s>svastika</s>, and auspicious spiral appeared. Then a certain <s>Ājīvaka</s> ascetic named <s>Upaga</s>, wandering about, arrived at that spot. He saw that milk-rice. He reflected: 'Whoever eats this milk-rice will attain the unsurpassed knowledge. Let me request it.' He stepped aside for a moment and waited until it was taken off [the fire]. He approached and said: 'I am afflicted by hunger, thirst, and fatigue. Give this to me.' They said: 'We shall not give it.' He departed in silence. Then the two placed it from the crystal vessel into a jeweled bowl. <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, through whose lower faculty of knowledge and vision all is discerned, in that situation, having created himself in the form of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, stood before them. <s>Brahmā</s> too descended and stood not far away. They began to give it to <s>Śakra</s>. He said: 'Do you give it to me, or to one who is more distinguished than I?' 'We give it to one more distinguished than you.' 'This <s>Brahmā</s> is more distinguished than I. Give it to him.' They began to give it to him. (

body.text: SBV I 110

) sa kathayati: kiṃ mamānuprayacchatha āhosvid yo mamāntikāt prativiśiṣṭatamaḥ; yas tavāntikāt prativiśiṣṭatamaḥ; amī śuddhāvāsakāyikā devāḥ; ebhyo 'nuprayacchatam; te tebhyo dātum ārabdhe; te kathayanti: kiṃ asmākam anuprayacchatha āhosvid yo 'smadviśiṣṭatamaḥ? yo yuṣmadviśiṣṭatamaḥ; te kathayanti: ayaṃ bodhisatvo bhagavān nairañjanām abhyavagāhya gātrāṇi pariṣicya alpasthāmavatvān na śaknoti pratyuttartum; eṣo 'smadviśiṣṭatamaḥ; asmāy anuprayacchatam; te tasya sakāśam saṃprasthite; tadā devatābhir arjunaśākhāvanāmitā yām avalaṃbya bodhisatvo nadīṃ nairañjanām uttīrya cīvarakāṇi prāvṛtya nadyā nairañjanāyās tīre niṣaṇṇaḥ; tatas tābhyāṃ satkṛtya tīvreṇāśayena tan madhupāyasaṃ tasmai pratipāditam; bodhisatvenāpi tayor anugrahārthaṃ pratisaṅgṛhītam; pratigṛhya kathayati: kim eṣāpi pātrī parityaktā? te kathayataḥ: bhagavann eṣāpi parityaktā; tato boshisatvena madhupāyasaṃ paribhujya sā pātrī prakṣālya nadyāṃ nairañjanāyāṃ prakṣiptā; nāgaiḥ pratigṛhītā; devānām adhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate; śakreṇa devānām indreṇa garuḍaveṣam abhinirmāya nadīṃ nairañjanāṃ kṣobhayitvā, nāgān vitrāsya, tāṃ pātrīm apahṛtya, deveṣu trayastriṃśeṣu pātrīmahaḥ prajñaptaḥ; tato nandā nandabalā bodhisatvenokte: anena dānena kiṃ prārthayatha iti; te kathayataḥ: bhagavan yo 'sau śākyānāṃ kumāra utpanno 'nuhimavatpārśve
body.translated_text: ) He said: 'Do you give it to me, or to one who is the most distinguished of all?' 'To one who is the most distinguished of all.' 'These are the gods of the <s>Śuddhāvāsa</s> heaven. Give it to them.' They began to give it to them. They said: 'Do you give it to us, or to one more distinguished than us?' 'To one more distinguished than you.' They said: 'This <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, having plunged into the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> to bathe his limbs, because of his lack of strength cannot climb out. He is the most distinguished of all. Give it to him.' They set out toward his presence. Then the deities bent down a branch of an <s>arjuna</s> tree, grasping which the <s>Bodhisattva</s> crossed the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>. Having put on his robes, he sat down on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>. Then those two, with devoted reverence and intense aspiration, offered that milk-rice to him. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, for the purpose of benefiting them, accepted it. Having accepted, he said: 'Is this bowl also given up?' They said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, this too is given up.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having eaten the milk-rice, washed the bowl and cast it into the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>. The <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-deities) caught it. Through the lower faculty of knowledge and vision of the gods, <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, having created himself in the form of a <s>Garuḍa</s>, agitated the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, terrified the <s>Nāgas</s>, seized the bowl, and among the Thirty-three gods a festival called '<s>Pātrīmaha</s>' (Bowl Festival) was established. Then <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s> were addressed by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: 'What do you wish for by this gift?' They said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, that prince who was born among the <s>Śākyas</s>, at the base of the <s>Himālaya</s>,

children.translated_text: ) On the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, sitting here and there, he searched for a [suitable] place. He saw a great rocky mountain furnished with various flowers and fruits. Having ascended it, he sat down cross-legged in a secluded, open place on the earth. Immediately after sitting down, that mountain crumbled. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflected: 'Surely I have committed unwholesome deeds, since this mountain has crumbled.' The deities, knowing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind with their own minds, said: 'Lord, you have not committed unwholesome deeds. Rather, this is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>): the entire earth cannot support two — one whose wholesome roots have been cut off, and one whose wholesome roots have been fully ripened. You are one whose wholesome roots have been fully ripened. This, Lord, is not the place for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Rather, cross the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> and go to that place — the <s>Vajrāsana</s> (Diamond Seat). There, all <s>Bodhisattvas</s> of the past, future, and present, having sat down, have attained — and will attain — the unsurpassed knowledge.' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> set out by the path indicated by the deities. At each step of his foot, a lotus appeared; from the four great oceans, water came forth; lotus ponds appeared; at the fall of his foot, this great earth, being pressed, began to resound like a bronze vessel. Blue jays and deer circumambulated the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The divine sons of wind-clouds began to blow gently; the divine sons of rain-clouds began to rain lightly. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflected: 'Given the signs that are appearing for me, surely today I shall attain the unsurpassed knowledge.'

body.translated_text: Having said 'So be it,' the <s>Bodhisattva</s> ate the milk-rice. Fully nourished, he attained the strength, power, and energy of the six faculties. (

tato bodhisatvaḥ kālikanāgarājena saṃstūyamāno vajrāsanābhimukhaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ; sa saṃlakṣayati: tṛṇasaṃstare niṣadyāṃ kalpayāmīti; tasya tṛṇaiḥ prayojanam iti śakro devānām indro bodhisatvasya cetasā cittam ājñaya gandhamādanāt parvatāt tūlasaṃsparśānāṃ tṛṃānāṃ bhāram ādāya svastikayāvasikavarṇam ātmānam abhinirmāya bodhisatvasya purastād avasthitaḥ; bodhisatvaḥ kathayati: bhadramukha dīyantāṃ mamaitāni tṛṇānīti; śakreṇa devendreṇa bodhisatvasya pādayor nipatya sagauraveṇa dattāni; tato bodhisatvaḥ svastikasya yāvasikasyāntikāt tṛṇāny ādāya devatopadiṣṭena mārgeṇa yena bodhimūlaṃ tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya anākulam asaṅkulaṃ tṛṇasaṃstarakaṃ prajñapayitum ārabdhaḥ; tatas tāni tṛṇāni pradakṣiṇāni patitum ārabdhāni; bodhisatvaḥ saṃlakṣayati: yathaitāni tṛṇāni pradakṣiṇaṃ patanti, niyataṃ mayādyānuttaraṃ jñānam adhigantavyam; iti viditvā vajrāsanam abhiruhya suptoragarājabhogaparipiṇḍīkṛtaṃ paryaṅkaṃ baddhvā niṣaṇṇaḥ; ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhāṃ smṛtim upasthāpya cittam utpādayati; vācaṃ ca bhāṣate:
  na tāvad bhetsyāmi paryaṅkaṃ yāvad aprāpta āsravakṣayaḥ
body.translated_text:
Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, being praised by <s>Kālika</s> the <s>Nāgarāja</s>, set out toward the <s>Vajrāsana</s>. He reflected: 'I shall arrange my seat upon a bed of grass.' <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, knowing the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s mind with his own mind, took a bundle of grass soft to the touch from Mount <s>Gandhamādana</s>, and having created himself in the form of a grass-cutter named <s>Svastika</s>, stood before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'Good sir, please give me that grass.' <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, falling at the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s feet, respectfully gave it. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having taken the grass from <s>Svastika</s> the grass-cutter, proceeded by the path indicated by the deities to the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree. Having approached, he began to arrange a grass-seat, undisturbed and unconfused. Then that grass began to fall turning to the right. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflected: 'As this grass falls turning to the right, surely today I must attain the unsurpassed knowledge.' Knowing this, he ascended the <s>Vajrāsana</s>, and having assumed the cross-legged posture with legs coiled like the coils of a sleeping serpent-king, he sat down. Setting his body upright, establishing mindfulness before him, he generated the resolution and spoke these words:
'I shall not break this cross-legged posture until I have attained the destruction of the defilements (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>).'

body.text: sa na tāvat bhindati paryaṅkaṃ yāvad aprāpta āsravakṣayaḥ
body.translated_text: He did not break his cross-legged posture until he had attained the destruction of the defilements.

) <s>Māra</s> the Evil One reflected: 'Since this banner trembles, surely some misfortune is about to occur.' He began to investigate and saw the <s>Bodhisattva</s> seated on the <s>Vajrāsana</s>. He thought: 'This son of <s>Śuddhodana</s> is seated on the <s>Vajrāsana</s>. Before he encroaches upon my domain, I must create an obstruction for him.' Knowing this, with hair standing on end, wearing a hempen cloth, having created himself in the form of a letter-carrier, he approached the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Having approached, he said in haste: 'Why do you sit here doing nothing? The city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> has been seized by <s>Devadatta</s>; the inner palace has been destroyed; the <s>Śākyas</s> have been slaughtered!' Thereupon three unwholesome, evil thoughts arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — namely, a thought of sensual desire, a thought of ill-will, and a thought of harm. Regarding <s>Yaśodharā</s>, <s>Mṛgajā</s>, and <s>Gopikā</s>, there was a thought of sensual desire; regarding <s>Devadatta</s>, a thought of ill-will; regarding the <s>Śākyas</s> who followed him, a thought of harm. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thought: 'Why have these three unwholesome, evil thoughts arisen in me?' He looked and saw: '<s>Māra</s> the Evil One has approached with the purpose of creating disturbance.' Then three wholesome thoughts arose in the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — namely, a thought of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>), a thought of non-ill-will, and a thought of non-harm.
Again <s>Māra</s> said: 'Why are you seated at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'I shall attain the unsurpassed knowledge.' <s>Māra</s> said: 'Prince, how can you attain the unsurpassed knowledge?' The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'You, Evil One, having performed a single sacrifice, attained sovereignty over the realm of desire. How much more so I, who have performed countless billions of sacrifices over three incalculable aeons! And for the benefit of beings, I have given away my head, hands, feet, eyes, flesh, blood, sons, wife, gold, and treasure for the attainment of the unsurpassed knowledge. Shall I not attain the unsurpassed knowledge? How could that be?' Thus addressed, <s>Māra</s> said: 'Regarding you — you yourself are the witness that you performed a single sacrifice and attained sovereignty over the realm of desire. But who is your witness that over three incalculable aeons you performed countless billions of sacrifices and gave away your head, hands, feet, eyes, flesh, blood, sons, wife, gold, and treasure for the attainment of the unsurpassed knowledge?' body.translated_text:
in three incalculable eons (<s>kalpāsaṅkhyeya</s>), many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of sacrifices have been performed; and for the sake of beings, head, hands, feet, eyes, flesh, blood, sons, wives, gold, and other [possessions] have been given up.' Then the earth-deity, having broken through the earth, with palms joined, raised her voice: 'It is so, O Evil One, as the <s>Bhagavān</s> declares!' When this was said, <s>Māra</s> the Evil One became silent, dejected, his shoulders slumped, face downcast, without inspiration, absorbed in brooding.
Distressed and disheartened, he reflected: 'Even doing all this, I cannot find an opening against the <s>Śākya</s>, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>. Let me create an even greater obstruction for him.' Having said this, he departed. Then he sent his three daughters — <s>Tṛṣṇā</s> (Craving), <s>Ratā</s> (Delight), and <s>Rati</s> (Pleasure). They, intoxicated by the pride of beauty and youth, adorned with divine garments and ornaments, began to display feminine wiles before the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, through his skill in means (<s>upāyakauśalya</s>), transformed them so that they became old women. They approached <s>Māra</s>. <s>Māra</s>, seeing them in such a state, was despondent. Resting his cheek on his hand, consumed by anxiety, he stood pondering: 'What stratagem could there be by which I might obstruct the austerities of the <s>Śākya</s>, the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>?' Taking the chief forces of thirty-six billion spirits (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>), in the forms of elephants, horses, camels, deer, buffaloes, boars, dogs, owls, mongooses, monkeys, and other creatures, with swords, lances, iron clubs, discuses, darts, bows, nooses, axes, clubs, and other weapons, and himself having drawn his bow to the ear, he surrounded the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and stood ready. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, seeing them in their many forms bearing various weapons, reflected: 'Even one who engages in conflict with an ordinary man deploys a counter-force; how much more so this lord of the desire-realm! Let me deploy a counter-force.' Having understood this, he began to contemplate the means for their pacification. <s>Māra</s>, together with his thirty-six billion spirits, began to hurl darts, discuses, lances, iron clubs, and arrows upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> entered the attainment of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>). And those weapons became divine blue lotuses (<s>utpala</s>), lotuses (<s>padma</s>), white water-lilies (<s>kumuda</s>), and white lotuses (<s>puṇḍarīka</s>), and began to fall all around the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. Then <s>Māra</s>, rising into the sky above, began to rain down a shower of dust; that too (

Even the rain of stones combined with the poisonous wind did nothing to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>. <s>Māra</s> reflected: 'How long must I stand here surrounding him? Its leaves will constantly make noise, and thus he will not attain one-pointedness of mind.' children.translated_text: ) the <s>Brahma</s>-world. Again <s>Māra</s> reflected: 'Meditations have sound as their thorn. Let me make a sound from afar.' He, surrounded by his retinue of thirty-six billion spirits, produced a great, terrifying, fearful sound. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> too, to ward it off, created a banana-forest extending twelve <s>yojanas</s>, by which that sound was deflected and heard [only as an echo]. The <s>Bodhisattva</s> reflected: 'Let me direct my mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge of the divine ear (<s>divyaśrotrajñāna</s>), by which I may hear whatever sounds I wish to hear — divine as well as human.' Having understood this, he directed his mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge of the divine ear. With the divine ear, purified and surpassing the human, he heard both kinds of sounds — human and non-human, both those far away and those nearby.

There the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Urubilvā</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, at the root of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, devoted to continuous, constant practice of the meditative cultivation of the qualities conducive to awakening (<s>saṃbodhipakṣa dharma</s>). In the first watch of the night, he directed his mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge of the domain of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiviṣayajñāna</s>). He experienced many kinds of supernatural power: having been one, he became many; having been many, he became one. He experienced the knowledge of appearing and disappearing. He passed with unobstructed body through walls, through mountains, through ramparts, as if through space. He dived into and emerged from the earth as if it were water. He walked on water without breaking the surface, as if on earth. He traveled cross-legged through the sky like a bird. body.text: ) nava daśa, viṃśatiṃ, triṃśataṃ, catvāriṃśataṃ, pañcāśataṃ, jātisahasram api, jātiśatāny anekāny api, jātishasrāṇy anekāny api, jātiśatasahasrāṇi, saṃvartakalpam api, vivartakalpam api, saṃvartavivartakaplam api, anekān api saṃvartakalpān, anekān api vivartakalpān, anekān api saṃvartavivartakaplān samanusmarati; amī nāma te bhavantaḥ satvāḥ yatrāham āsam evaṃnāmā, evaṃjātyaḥ, evaṃgotraḥ, evamāhāraḥ, evaṃ sukhaduḥkhaṃ pratisaṃvedī, evaṃdīrghāyuḥ, evaṃcirasthitikaḥ, evamāyuḥparyantaḥ; so 'haṃ tasmāt sthānāc cyutaḥ amutropapannaḥ tasmād api cyutaḥ amutropapannaḥ; tasmād api cyuta ihopapanna iti; sākāraṃ soddeśam anekavidhaṃ pūrvanivāsaṃ samanusmarati; tasyaitad abhavat: eṣāṃ mārakiṃkarāṇāṃ ke apāyagāminaḥ, ke neti; katham etaj jñāyate? tasyaitad abhavat: cyutyupapādajñānasākṣātkriyāyām abhijñayeti; sa rātryā madhyame yāme cyutyupapādajñānasākṣātkriyāyām abhijñāyāṃ cittam abhinirṇamayati; sa divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣyakeṇa satvān paśyati, cyavamānān api upapadyamānān api, suvarṇān api, durvarṇān api, hīnān api, praṇītān api, sugatim api gacchato, durgatim api gacchato; yathākarmopagān satvān yathābhūtān prajānāti; amī nāma te bhavantaḥ satvāḥ kāyaduścaritena samanvāgatā vāṅmanoduścaritena samanvāgatā āryāṇām apavādakā mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ; mithyādṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetoḥ taddhetutatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇād apāyadurgativinipātaṃ narakeṣu prapadyante; amī vā punar bhavantaḥ satvāḥ kāyasucaritena samanvāgatā vāṅmanassucaritena samanvāgatās āryāṇām anapavādakāḥ samyagdṛṣṭayaḥ; samyagdṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetos taddhetutatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇāt sugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyante; tasyaitad abhavat: amī bhavantaḥ satvāḥ kāmāśraveṇa bhavāśraveṇāvidyāśravena
body.translated_text: ), nine, ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, a thousand births, many hundreds of births, many thousands of births, many hundreds of thousands of births, an eon of contraction, an eon of expansion, an eon of contraction-and-expansion, many eons of contraction, many eons of expansion, many eons of contraction-and-expansion, [recollecting]: 'Those beings were there where I was — of such a name, such a birth, such a clan, such food, experiencing such pleasure and pain, of such a lifespan, such a duration of life, such a limit of life. Having passed away from that state, I was reborn there; having passed away from there, I was reborn here.' Thus with its aspects, with its details, he recollected many kinds of previous existences. He thought: 'Among these servants of <s>Māra</s>, who are destined for the lower realms, and who are not? How can this be known?' He thought: 'Through the direct realization of the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth [of beings] (<s>cyutyupapādajñāna</s>).' In the middle watch of the night, he directed his mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth [of beings]. With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he saw beings passing away and being reborn — beautiful and ugly, inferior and superior, going to good destinies and going to evil destinies. He knew beings as they truly are according to their <s>karma</s>: 'These beings, endowed with bad conduct of body, endowed with bad conduct of speech and mind, revilers of the noble ones, holders of wrong views — on account of the adoption of the <s>dharma</s> of wrong-view <s>karma</s>, through that cause and that condition, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in a state of deprivation, an evil destiny, a downfall, in the hells. But these other beings, endowed with good conduct of body, endowed with good conduct of speech and mind, not revilers of the noble ones, holders of right views — on account of the adoption of the <s>dharma</s> of right-view <s>karma</s>, through that cause and that condition, at the breaking up of the body after death, they are reborn in a good destiny, in the heavenly world, among the gods.' He thought: 'These beings wander in <s>saṃsāra</s> through the outflow of desire (<s>kāmāśrava</s>), the outflow of existence (<s>bhavāśrava</s>), and the outflow of ignorance (<s>avidyāśrava</s>)

body.text: ) paśyataḥ kāmāśravāc cittaṃ vimucyate; bhavāśravād cittaṃ vimucyate; <avidyāśravāc cittaṃ vimucyate>; vimuktasya vimuktam eva jñānadarśanaṃ bhavati, kṣīnā me jātir, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ, kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmīti; iti tatrābhisaṃbuddhabodhir bhagavān kṛtakṛtyaḥ, kṛtakaraṇīyaḥ, tejodhātuṃ samāpannaḥ
body.translated_text: ) as he thus saw, his mind was liberated from the taint of sensual desire (<s>kāmāśrava</s>); his mind was liberated from the taint of existence (<s>bhavāśrava</s>); his mind was liberated from the taint of ignorance (<s>avidyāśrava</s>). Being liberated, there arose the knowledge and vision of liberation itself: 'Destroyed is my birth; the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) has been lived; what was to be done has been done; I know there is no further becoming beyond this.' Thus the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having attained awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) there, his task accomplished, his duty fulfilled, entered the element of radiance (<s>tejodhātu samāpatti</s>).

children.translated_text: <s>Māra</s>'s defeat, and mischievous rumor

children.text: yadā bodhisatvena ṣaṭtriṃśādbhūtakoṭiparivāraṃ māraṃ maitreṇāstreṇābhinirjitya anuttaraṃ jñānam adhigataṃ, tadā mārasya pāpīyaso hastād dhanuḥ srasto, dhvajaḥ patitaḥ, bhavanaṃ ca kampitam; tato māraḥ pāpīyān ṣaṭtriṃśadbhūtakoṭiparivāro duḥkhī, durmanā, vipratīsārī, tatraivāntarhitaḥ; mārakāyikābhir devatābhiḥ kapilavastunagare ārocitam: śākyamunir bodhisatvo duṣkaracaryāṃ caritvā vajrāsanam abhiruhya tṛṇasaṃstare kālagataḥ iti; yat śrutvā rājā śuddhodanaḥ antaḥpurakumārāmātyagaṇasahīyo mahatā duḥkhadaurmanasyena santaptaḥ, kapilavāstavaś ca janakāyaḥ; gopikā mṛgajā yaśodharā ca bodhisatvaguṇānusmaraṇāt mūrchitāḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatitāḥ; jalāvasekapratyāgataprāṇās tā antaḥpurajanena sāntvyamānā aśruparyākulekṣaṇā muhur bāṣparodhagadgadasvarā vipralapantyo 'vasthitāḥ; tāṃ vipratipattiṃ dṛṣṭvā buddhābhiprasannābhir devatābhir ārocitam: na śākyamunir bodhisatvaḥ kālagataḥ, api tu tenānuttaraṃ jñānam adhigatam iti
children.translated_text: When the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having conquered <s>Māra</s> together with his retinue of thirty-six <s>koṭis</s> (tens of millions) of demons with the weapon of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>), attained the unsurpassed knowledge, at that time the bow fell from the hand of <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, his banner fell, and his abode trembled. Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, together with his retinue of thirty-six <s>koṭis</s> of demons, miserable, dejected, and remorseful, vanished right there. The deities of <s>Māra</s>'s host announced in the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s>, having practiced severe austerities, ascended the diamond seat (<s>vajrāsana</s>) and died upon a bed of grass.' Hearing this, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, together with the inner apartments, the princes, and the assembly of ministers, was scorched with great suffering and grief, as was the populace of <s>Kapilavastu</s>. <s>Gopikā</s>, <s>Mṛgajā</s>, and <s>Yaśodharā</s>, from recollecting the virtues of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, fainted and fell to the ground. Their vital breath was restored by sprinkling water, and as they were being consoled by the people of the inner apartments, with eyes filled with tears, their voices repeatedly choked and faltering with suppressed sobs, they stood there lamenting. Seeing this confusion, the deities who were devoted to the <s>Buddha</s> announced: 'The <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> has not died; rather, he has attained the unsurpassed knowledge.'

body.text: Rāhula and Ānanda
body.translated_text: <s>Rāhula</s> and <s>Ānanda</s>

body.text: yat śrutvā rājā śuddhodanaḥ saparivāraḥ kapilavāstavaś ca janakāyaḥ paraṃ harṣam upāgatāḥ; anuttarajñānādhigame ca bhagavataḥ yaśodharāyaḥ putro jātaḥ; amṛtodanasya ca putro jātaḥ; rāhuṇā candro grastaḥ; atha rājā śuddhodanaḥ tāṃ saṃpattiṃ dṛṣṭvā hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita udagraprītisaumanasyajātaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; tena kapilavastunagaram apagatapāṣaṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitam, candanavāripariṣiktaṃ surabhidhūpasphaṭikopanibaddham āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpam ucchṛtadhvajapatākaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ ramaṇīyam; (
body.translated_text: Hearing this, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> with his retinue, and the populace of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, attained supreme joy. And at the time of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s attainment of the unsurpassed knowledge, a son was born to <s>Yaśodharā</s>; and a son was born to <s>Amṛtodana</s>; and the moon was eclipsed by <s>Rāhu</s>. Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, seeing this auspicious conjunction, became joyful, delighted, elated, filled with gladness and happiness. He had the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> prepared — cleared of stones, gravel, and rubbish, sprinkled with sandalwood water, fitted with censers of fragrant incense, hung with garlands and silk-banner clusters, with raised flags and pennants, strewn with various flowers, and made delightful. (

body.text: ) caturṣu nagaradvāreṣu dānaśālā māpitā madhye ca śṛṇgāṭakasya; tataḥ pūrvanagaradvāre śramaṇabrāhmaṇacarakaparivrājakādīnavānāthakṛpaṇavanīpakayācanakebhyo dānāni dattāni; dakṣiṇe paścime uttare madhye śṛṅgāṭakasya
body.translated_text: ) At the four city gates alms-halls were built, and in the middle of the crossroads. At the eastern city gate, gifts were given to ascetics, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, wanderers, mendicants, and to the poor, destitute, wretched, vagrants, and beggars. At the southern, western, and northern gates and in the middle of the crossroads

body.text:
dānāni dīyante; puṇyāṇi kriyante; yaśodharāyāḥ putrasya nāma vyavasthāpyate; antaḥpurajanaḥ kathayati: asya janmani rāhuṇā candro grastaḥ; tasmād bhavatu dārakasya rāhula iti nāmeti; amṛtodanasyāpi tathaiva dānāni datvā puṇyāni kṛtvā putrasya nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate; kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti: jñātaya ūcuḥ: yasmād asya janmani sarvaṃ nagaram ānanditaṃ, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya ānanda iti nāmeti; rājā śuddhodanaḥ kathayati: yo 'yaṃ yaśodharāyāḥ putro jātaḥ naiṣa śākyamuneḥ putraḥ; iti śrutvā yaśodharā vyathitā; tatas tayā bodhisatvasya vyāyāmaśilāyām āropya krīḍāpuṣkariṇyās tīre sthitayā satyopayācanaṃ kṛtam: yady ayaṃ bodhisatvena jātas tathāsyāṃ puṣkariṇyāṃ saha śilayā plaveta; no cen nimajjeta; ityuktvā udake prakṣiptaḥ; sa tūlapicuvat saha śilayā plavitum ārabdhaḥ; rājā śuddhodanas tad atyadbhutaṃ <śrutvā> mahājanakāyaparivṛto bodhisatvasya kriḍāpuṣkariṇīgato yāvat paśyati rāhulabhadraṃ bodhisatvasya śilāyāṃ niṣaṇṇaṃ tūlapicuvad udake plavamānam; dṛṣṭvā ca punaḥ hṛṣṭatuṣṭapramudita udagraprītisaumanasyajātaḥ sahasā puṣkariṇīm avatīrya rāhulabradraṃ kumāram aṃśenādāya vyutthitaḥ
  yadā bhagavatā ṣaṭtriṃśadbhūtakoṭiparivāraṃ māraṃ maitreṇāstreṇābhinirjitya anuttaraṃ jñānam adhigatam, atyarthaṃ tasmin samaye mahāpṛthivīcālo 'bhūt; sarvaś cāyaṃ loka udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭo 'bhūt; yā api tā lokasya lokāntarikā andhās tamaso 'ndhakāratamisrā yatremau sūryācandramasāv evaṃmahardhikāv evaṃmahānubhāvāv ābhayā ābhāṃ na pratyanubhavataḥ, tā api tasmin samaye udāreṇāvabhāsena sphuṭā abhūvan; tatra ye satvā upapannās <te svakam api bāhuṃ pragṛhītaṃ na paśyanti>; te tayā ābhayā (
body.translated_text:
gifts were given; merit was performed. A name was established for <s>Yaśodharā</s>'s son. The people of the inner apartments said: 'At his birth, the moon was eclipsed by <s>Rāhu</s>; therefore let the boy's name be <s>Rāhula</s>.' For <s>Amṛtodana</s>'s [son] likewise, having given gifts and performed merit, a name was established for his son: 'What shall the boy's name be?' The kinsmen said: 'Since at his birth the entire city was delighted, let the boy's name be <s>Ānanda</s>.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said: 'This son born to <s>Yaśodharā</s> — he is not the son of <s>Śākyamuni</s>.' Hearing this, <s>Yaśodharā</s> was distressed. Then she, having placed [the child] upon the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s exercise-stone and standing at the bank of the pleasure-pool, made a truth-declaration (<s>satyopayācana</s>): 'If this child was fathered by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, then let him float in that pool together with the stone; if not, let him sink.' Having said this, she cast him into the water. He began to float together with the stone, like cotton-fluff. King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having heard of this extraordinary [event], surrounded by a great crowd of people, went to the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s pleasure-pool and saw young <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> seated on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s stone, floating in the water like cotton-fluff. Having seen, joyful, delighted, elated, filled with gladness and happiness, he hastily descended into the pool, took the young prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> upon his shoulder, and emerged.
When the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having conquered <s>Māra</s> together with his retinue of thirty-six <s>koṭis</s> of demons with the weapon of loving-kindness, attained the unsurpassed knowledge, at that very time there was a great earthquake; and this entire world was suffused with a magnificent radiance; even those world-interstices — dark, gloomy, shrouded in blind darkness — where these two, the sun and moon, so mighty in supernatural power and so great in majesty, do not experience each other's radiance — even those at that time were suffused with a magnificent radiance; the beings reborn there could not see even their own outstretched arm; but by that radiance, (

body.text: Two Devatas
body.translated_text: Two <s>Devatās</s> (deities)

body.text:
atha dvayor brahmakāyikayor devatayor <brahmaloke nivāsinor> etad abhavat: ayaṃ buddho bhagavān urubilvāyāṃ viharati; nadyā nairañjanāyās tīre bodhimūle acirābhisaṃbuddhabodhis tejodhātusamāpannaḥ saptāham ekaparyaṅkena atināmayati; na cainaṃ kaścit piṇḍakena pratipādayati; yan nu vayam enaṃ gatvā pratyekapratyekaṃ gāthābhir abhiṣṭuyāma iti; atha dve brahmakāyike devate tadyathā balavān puruṣaḥ saṃmiñjitaṃ vā bāhuṃ prasārayet, prasāritaṃ vā saṃmiñjayet, evam eva dve brahmakāyike devate brahmaloke antarhite bhagavataḥ purataḥ pratyaṣṭhātām; ekāntasthite dve brahmakāyike devate; ekā gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
  uttiṣṭha vijitasaṃgrāma
  sārthavāhānigha vicara loke /
  deśaya sugata varadharmaṃ
  bhaviṣyanti
body.translated_text:
Then two deities of the <s>Brahmakāyika</s> [heaven], dwelling in the <s>Brahma</s>-world, had this thought: 'This <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> is dwelling at <s>Urubilvā</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, having recently attained awakening, having entered the attainment of the element of radiance (<s>tejodhātu</s>), passing seven days in a single cross-legged posture. And no one provides him with alms-food. Let us go and praise him, each with a verse.' Then the two <s>Brahmakāyika</s> deities — just as a strong man might extend a bent arm or bend an extended arm — in that very instant, vanishing from the <s>Brahma</s>-world, appeared before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Standing to one side, the two <s>Brahmakāyika</s> deities — the first one spoke a verse:
'Arise, O victor of the battle!
Caravan leader, wander free from affliction in the world!
Teach, O <s>Sugata</s>, the excellent <s>Dharma</s> —
there will be

body.text: dharmaratnasyājñātāraḥ //
body.translated_text: those who will understand the jewel of the <s>Dharma</s>!' //

body.text:
dvitiyā gāthaṃ bhāṣate
  uttiṣṭha vijitasaṅgrāma
  parṇalopānigha vicara loke /
  cittaṃ hi te suviśuddhaṃ
  pañcadaśyāṃ śaśīva paripūrṇaḥ // (
