children.translated_text: Having said this, they vanished right there. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having emerged from that <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), at that moment spoke a verse:

children.text: yac ca kāmasukhaṃ loke yac cāpi divijaṃ sukham /
children.translated_text: Whatever pleasure of desire there is in the world, and whatever divine pleasure —
these do not equal even a sixteenth part of the happiness of the destruction of craving (<s>tṛṣṇākṣaya</s>). //

body.translated_text:
The second one spoke a verse:
'Arise, O victor of the battle!
Wanderer free from debt, go about in the world!
For your mind is well-purified —
like the moon on the fifteenth day, full and complete.' // (

children.text: nikṣipya hi guruṃ bhāraṃ nādadīta paraṃ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having set down a heavy burden, one should not take up another again.
Painful is the taking up of a burden; the laying down of a burden is happiness. //
Having abandoned all craving, through the exhaustion of all conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>),
through the complete understanding of all states of existence, one does not go to another birth. //

body.text: Trapuṣa and Bhallika
body.translated_text: <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>

body.text: vimuktiprītisukhasaṃvedī buddho bhagavān saptāham ekaparyaṅkena atināmayati; na cainaṃ kaścit piṇḍakena pratipādayati; tena khalu samayena trapuṣabhallikau vaṇijau pañcamātraiḥ śakaṭaśataiḥ sārdham anuvyavaharamāṇau, tasminn eva mārge adhvapratipannāv abhūtām; atha trapuṣabhallikayor vaṇijor anyatamāyāḥ purāṇamitrāmātyajñātisālohitāyāḥ devatāyāḥ etad abhavat: ayaṃ buddho bhagavān urubilvāyāṃ viharati nadyā nairañjanāyās tīre bodhimūle acirābhisaṃbuddho vimuktiprītisukhapratisaṃvedī saptāham ekaparyaṅkenātināmayati; na cainaṃ kaśit piṇḍakena pratipādayati; taṃ trapuṣabhallikau vaṇijau tatprathamataḥ pratipādayetām; tat syāt trapuṣabhallikayor vaṇijor dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya; yanv ahaṃ svayam evautsukyam āpadayeya yaduta bhagavataḥ piṇḍapātapradānasya hetor iti; atha sā devatā sarvaṃ karvaṭakam udāreṇāvabhāsena sphāritvā trapuṣabhallikau vaṇijāv idam avocat: vaṇijau vaṇijau ayaṃ buddho bhagavān uribilvāyāṃ viharati nadyā nairañjanāyās tīre bodhimūle acirābhisaṃbuddho vimuktiprītisukhapratisaṃvedī; saptāham ekaparyaṅkenātināmayati; nainaṃ kaścit piṇḍakena pratipādayati; taṃ yuvāṃ tatprathamataḥ piṇḍakena pratipādayatam; tad yuvayor bhaviṣyati dīrgharātram arthāya hitāya sukhāya; ityuktvā sā devatā tatraivāntarhitā; (

children.translated_text: SBV I 123

children.text: ) atha trapuṣabhallikayor vaṇijor etad abhavat: na batāvaro buddho bhaviṣyati; nāvaraṃ dharmākhyānam; yatredānīṃ devatā api tasya bhagavata autsukyam āpadyante yaduta piṇḍapātapratipādanahetoḥ; iti viditvā prabhūtaṃ madhu ca manthāś ca ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntau; upasaṅkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte 'sthātām; ekāntasthitau trapuṣabhallikau vaṇijāv idam avocatām: ihāvābhyāṃ bhadanta bhagavantam uddiśya prabhūtaṃ madhu ca manthāś ca ānītāḥ; tān bhagavān pratigṛhṇātv anukampām upādāya iti; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ pāṇau piṇḍapātaṃ pratigṛhṇīyāṃ, tadyathā anyatīrthikaḥ; yanv ahaṃ samanvāhareyam kutra pūrvakaiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ piṇḍapātaḥ pratigṛhīto hitāya prāṇinām iti; devatā bhagavata ārocayanti: pātre bhadanta pūrvakaiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ piṇḍapātaḥ pratigṛhīto hitāya prāṇinām iti; bhagavato 'pi samanvāhṛtya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate pātre pūrvakaiḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaiḥ piṇḍapātaḥ pratigṛhīto hitāya prāṇinām iti; tatra bhagavataḥ pātreṇa pātrakāryam utpannam; atha catvāro mahārājā bhagavataḥ pātreṇa pātrakāryam utpannam iti viditvā anyatamasmāt pāṣāṇaparvatāc catvāri śailamayāni pātrāṇy amanuṣyakṛtāny amanuṣyaniṣṭhitāny acchāni śucīni niṣpratigandhāny ādāya, yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntāḥ; upasaṅkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte tasthuḥ; ekāntasthitāś catvāro mahārājā bhagavantam idam avocan: iha asmābhir bhadanta bhagavataḥ pātreṇa pātrakāryam utpannaṃ viditvā anyatamamāt pāṣāṇaparvatāc catvāri śailamayāni pātrāṇy amanuṣyakṛtāny amanuṣyaniṣṭhitāni acchāni śucīni niṣpratigandhāni ānītāni; tāni bhagavān pratigṛhṇātv anukampām upādāya iti; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: saced aham ekasya mahārājasyāntikād ekaṃ pātraṃ pratigrahīṣyāmi, trayāṇāṃ bhaviṣyati cetaso 'nyathātvam; saced dvayor, dvayor bhaviṣyati cetaso 'nyathātvam; sacet trayāṇām ekasya bhaviṣyati cetaso (
children.translated_text: ) Then the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s> thought: 'The <s>Buddha</s> must indeed be no ordinary one; no ordinary one is the proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s> — since even now the deities themselves are eager regarding the <s>Bhagavān</s>, namely for the purpose of providing alms-food.' Having understood this, taking an abundance of honey and parched grain, they approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s> said this: 'Here, Venerable Sir, we have brought an abundance of honey and parched grain for the <s>Bhagavān</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept them out of compassion.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'It would not be fitting for me to accept alms-food in my hand, like a follower of another sect. Let me consider: in what vessel did the previous Perfectly Awakened Ones (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddhas</s>) accept alms-food for the benefit of beings?' The deities informed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable Sir, the previous Perfectly Awakened Ones accepted alms-food in a bowl, for the benefit of beings.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> too, having reflected, his knowledge and vision confirmed: 'The previous Perfectly Awakened Ones accepted alms-food in a bowl, for the benefit of beings.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> had need of a bowl. Then the Four Great Kings, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had need of a bowl, from a certain rocky mountain brought four stone bowls — made by non-human beings, fashioned by non-human beings, clear, pure, and odorless — and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Four Great Kings said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Here, Venerable Sir, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had need of a bowl, we have brought from a certain rocky mountain four stone bowls — made by non-human beings, fashioned by non-human beings, clear, pure, and odorless. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept them out of compassion.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'If I accept one bowl from one Great King, three will be displeased. If from two, two will be displeased. body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, experiencing the happiness of the bliss of liberation (<s>vimuktiprītisukha</s>), passed seven days in a single cross-legged posture. And no one provided him with alms-food. At that time, the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>, traveling with approximately five hundred carts, were proceeding along that very road on a trade-journey. Then a certain deity — an old friend, minister, relative, or kinsman of the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s> — had this thought: 'This <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> is dwelling at <s>Urubilvā</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, having recently attained awakening, experiencing the happiness of the bliss of liberation, passing seven days in a single cross-legged posture. And no one provides him with alms-food. Let <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s> the merchants be the first to provide him with alms-food. That would be for their long-lasting benefit, welfare, and happiness. Let me myself generate eagerness [in them] for the purpose of offering alms-food to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then that deity, having suffused the entire caravan-halt with a magnificent radiance, said this to the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>: 'Merchants, merchants! This <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> is dwelling at <s>Urubilvā</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>, at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree, having recently attained awakening, experiencing the happiness of the bliss of liberation. He has been passing seven days in a single cross-legged posture. No one provides him with alms-food. Be the first to provide him with alms-food. That will be for your long-lasting benefit, welfare, and happiness.' Having said this, that deity vanished right there. (

children.text: atha bhagavān trapuṣabhallikayor vaṇijor antikāt piṇḍapātam ādāya yena nadī nairañjanā tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya nadyā nairañjanāyās tire niṣadya bhaktakṛtyam akārṣīt; tatra madhv api vātikaṃ, manthā api vātikāḥ, tena bhagavato vātābādhikaṃ glānyam utpannam; atha māraḥ pāpīyān bhagavato vātābādhikaṃ glānyam utpannaṃ viditvā, yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya bhagavantam idam avocat: parinirvātu bhagavān, parinirvāṇakālasamaya iti; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: māro batāyaṃ pāpīyān upasaṅkrānto yaduta vyākṣepakarmaṇi; iti viditvā māraṃ pāpīyāṃsam idam avocat: na tāvat pāpīyan parinirvāsyāmi, yāvan na me śrāvakāḥ paṇḍitā bhaviṣyanti vyaktā medhāvinaḥ, alam utpannotpannānāṃ parapravādakānāṃ saha dharmeṇa nigrahītāraḥ alaṃ svasya vādasya paryavadāpayitāraḥ bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇyaḥ upāsakā upāsikāḥ, vaistārikaṃ ca me brahmacaryaṃ bhaviṣyati bāhujanyaṃ pṛthubhūtaṃ yāvad devamanuṣyebhaḥ samyaksuprakāśitam iti; atha mārasya pāpīyasa etad abhavat: na parinirvāsyati bata śramaṇo gautamaḥ; iti viditvā duḥkhī durmanā vipratīsārī tatraivāntarhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having received alms-food from the merchants <s>Trapuṣa</s> and <s>Bhallika</s>, approached the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>. Having approached, he sat down on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s> and performed his meal. Now the honey was wind-producing, and the parched grain was also wind-producing; therefore a wind-related ailment arose in the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One, knowing that a wind-related ailment had arisen in the <s>Bhagavān</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>; it is the time for <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'This is <s>Māra</s> the Evil One who has approached, namely for the purpose of causing distraction.' Having understood, he said this to <s>Māra</s> the Evil One: 'I shall not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, Evil One, until my disciples become wise, discerning, and intelligent — capable of refuting opponents who arise with opposing doctrines in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>, capable of establishing their own doctrine — monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen. And until my holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) becomes widespread, extensive, well-known, reaching even gods and humans, and well-proclaimed.' Then <s>Māra</s> the Evil One thought: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> will indeed not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>.' Having understood, unhappy, displeased, and regretful, he vanished right there.

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having dwelt as long as he wished at the abode of <s>Mucilinda</s> the <s>Nāgarāja</s>, approached the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree. Having approached, he sat down on a prepared grass seat, cross-legged, with body erect, having established mindfulness before him. He passed seven days in a single sitting, contemplating in forward and reverse order the twelve-limbed <s>pratītyasamutpāda</s> (dependent origination), namely: when this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this, that arises. That is: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s> arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> (six sense-bases); conditioned by the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging); conditioned by <s>upādāna</s> arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); conditioned by <s>bhava</s> arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); conditioned by <s>jāti</s> arise <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death), sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair. Thus arises this entire mass of suffering. That is: when this does not exist, that does not come to be; from the cessation of this, that ceases. That is: from the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s> cease; from the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s>, <s>nāmarūpa</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s>, the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> cease; from the cessation of the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s>, <s>sparśa</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>sparśa</s>, <s>vedanā</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>vedanā</s>, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, <s>upādāna</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>upādāna</s>, <s>bhava</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>bhava</s>, <s>jāti</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>jāti</s>, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair cease. Thus ceases this entire mass of suffering.
Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at the end of that very week, having emerged from that <s>samādhi</s>, at that moment spoke this verse:

Then <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s>, just as a strong man might extend a bent arm or bend an extended arm, vanished from the <s>Brahma</s>-world and appeared before the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s>, at that moment, spoke this verse:
'Formerly in <s>Magadha</s> there appeared

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'The <s>Dharma</s> I have realized is profound, of profound appearance, difficult to see, difficult to comprehend, beyond reasoning, beyond the scope of reasoning, subtle, to be understood by the wise, the learned, and the discerning. If I were to declare it to others, and they were not to understand it, that would be a weariness for me, a vexation, a mere arising of displeasure in mind. Let me rather dwell alone in the forest, inclined toward the practice of abiding happily in the present <s>Dharma</s>.' There the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s mind inclined toward dwelling with little concern, not toward teaching the <s>Dharma</s>. Then <s>Brahmā Sahāmpati</s> thought: 'Alas, this world is perishing! Alas, this world is being destroyed! For at long last, on rare occasion, <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones (

For those ensnared by passion for existence, this <s>Dharma</s> is not easily awakened to.' //
'The path going against the stream, profound, extremely difficult to see —

body.text: Brahma's request for Dharmadeśanā
body.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>'s request for the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmadeśanā</s>)

body.text: santi bhadanta satvā loke jātā, loke vṛddhās tīkṣṇendriyā api, madhyendriyā api, mṛdvindriyā api, svākārāḥ, suvineyā, alparajaso 'lparajaskajātīyā, ye 'śravaṇāt saddharmasya parihīyante; tadyathā bhadanta utpalāni vā, padmāni vā kumudāni vā, puṇḍarīkāṇi vā udake jātāny, udake vṛddhāny, ekatyāni udakād abhyudgatāni tiṣṭhanti; ekatyāni samodakāni; ekatyāni udakanimagnakośāni tiṣṭhanti; evam eva santi bhadanta satvā loke jātā, loke vṛddhās tīkṣṇendriyā api, madhyendriyā api, mṛdvindriyā api, svākārāḥ, suvineyāḥ, alparajaso 'lparajaskajātīyā ye 'śravaṇāt saddharmasya parihīyante; deśayatu bhagavān dharmam; deśayatu sugato dharmam; bhaviṣyanti dharmatatnasyājñātāraḥ; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: yac cāham svayam eva buddhacakṣuṣā (
body.translated_text: 'Venerable Sir, there are beings born in the world, grown in the world — some with keen faculties, some with middling faculties, some with dull faculties — of good disposition, easily guided, with little dust [in their eyes], of the class with little dust, who are declining from not hearing the true <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Saddharma</s>). Just as, Venerable Sir, among lotuses — blue lotuses, red lotuses, white night-lotuses, or white day-lotuses — born in the water, grown in the water, some have risen above the water and stand [dry]; some stand level with the water; some stand submerged in the water with their buds [below]. Even so, Venerable Sir, there are beings born in the world, grown in the world — some with keen faculties, some with middling faculties, some with dull faculties — of good disposition, easily guided, with little dust, of the class with little dust, who are declining from not hearing the true <s>Dharma</s>. Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s>! Let the <s>Sugata</s> teach the <s>Dharma</s>! There will be those who understand the <s>Dharma</s>.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'Let me myself survey the world with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye.' (

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'Let me first teach the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>Ārāḍa Kālāma</s>, who, though he was my former teacher, honored me with the highest honor, venerated me with the highest veneration, and was delighted and pleased regarding the highest matters.' The <s>Buddha</s> sets out for <s>Vārāṇasī</s>

children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'To whom shall I first teach the <s>Dharma</s>?' He thought: 'Let me first teach the <s>Dharma</s> to the group of five monks (<s>pañcaka bhikṣus</s>), who formerly attended upon me with devotion, love, and reverence while I was engaged in the practice of eliminating suffering.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'Where are the group of five monks now dwelling?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> saw with the divine eye — purified, surpassing the human — the group of five monks dwelling at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at the Deer Park (<s>Mṛgadāva</s>) in <s>Ṛṣivadana</s>. Having seen, after dwelling at the foot of the <s>Bodhi</s> tree for as long as he wished, he set out on a journey toward <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the market-town of the <s>Kāśis</s>.

body.translated_text: The five <s>Bhikṣus</s>

body.text: atha bhagavān kāśiṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran vārāṇasīm anuprāptaḥ; tena khalu samayena pañcakā bhikṣavo vārāṇasyāṃ viharanti ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve; adrākṣuḥ pañcakā bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ dūrata eva; dṛṣṭvā ca punar anyonyaṃ saṃpratasthuḥ; kriyākāraṃ cākārṣuḥ; ayaṃ sa bhavantaḥ śramaṃo gautama āgacchati śaithiliko bāhuliko bahulājīvaḥ prahāṇavibhrāntaḥ; sa etarhy audārikam āhāram āharati odanakulmāṣān; sarpistailābhyāṃ gātrāṇi mrakṣayati; sukhodakena ca kāyaṃ pariṣiñcati; so 'smābhir upasaṅkrānto nābhivādyaḥ, na vanditavyo, na pratyutthātavyo, notthāyāsanenopanimantrayitavyo nānyatra prāg evāsanāni prajñapya; idaṃ syād vacanīyaḥ; saṃvidyante āyuṣman gautama āsanāni; saced ākāṅkṣasi niṣīda iti; yathā yathā bhagavān pañcakān bhikṣūn darśanāyopasaṅkrāmati tathā tathā pañcakā bhikṣavo bhagavatas tejaś ca śriyaṃ ca gauravaṃ ca asahamānā utthāyāsanād eke bhagavato 'rthe āsanaṃ prajñapayanti; eke pādodakaṃ, pādādhiṣṭhānaṃ caikānte upanikṣipanti; eke pratyudgamya cīvarakāṇi pratigṛhṇanti; evaṃ cāhuḥ: etu bhavān gautama; svāgataṃ bhavate gautamāya; niṣīdatu bhavān gautama prajñapta evāsane; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: cyutā bateme nohapuruṣā svasmāt kriyākārād; iti viditvā prajñapta eva āsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; tatrasvit pañcakā bhikṣavo bhagavantam atyarthaṃ nāmavādena gotravādena āyuṣmadvādena samudācaranti; tatra bhagavān pañcakān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: mā yūyaṃ bhikṣavas tathāgatam
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering on his journey through the <s>Kāśī</s> country, arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. At that time, the group of five monks was dwelling at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in the Deer Park at <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> (the Sages' Resort). The group of five monks saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar. Having seen him, they conferred with one another and made an agreement: 'This, sirs, is the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> coming — the slackened one, the indulgent one, one living abundantly, one who has strayed from striving. Now he eats coarse food — rice and bean-porridge. He anoints his limbs with ghee and oil; he bathes his body with pleasant water. When he approaches us, he is not to be greeted, not to be honored, not to be risen for, not to be invited with a seat. Rather, having previously arranged seats, he should be told thus: "There are seats here, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>; sit down if you wish."' But as the <s>Bhagavān</s> drew closer and closer to the five monks for an audience, the five monks, unable to endure the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s majesty, glory, and gravity, rose from their seats. Some prepared a seat for the <s>Bhagavān</s>; some set out foot-washing water and a footstool to one side; some came forward and received his robes. They said: 'Come, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>! Welcome to Venerable <s>Gautama</s>! Let Venerable <s>Gautama</s> sit on the seat that has been prepared.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'These foolish men have indeed fallen away from their own agreement.' Knowing this, he sat on the seat that had been prepared. Thereupon, the five monks addressed the <s>Bhagavān</s> excessively by his personal name, by his clan name, and as 'Venerable.' body.translated_text: ) 'By your former manner, conduct, and practice of severe austerities, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, did you attain anything beyond the human state — any noble distinction, any knowledge, any vision, any attainment of a dwelling in [meditative] peace? How much less so now, when you are slackened, living abundantly, strayed from striving, eating coarse food — rice and bean-porridge — anointing your limbs with ghee and oil, and bathing your body with pleasant water!' 'Do you not, monks, see the serenity of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s face now compared to before, and the difference in his faculties?' They said: 'Indeed so, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>.'

The middle course of conduct
There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the five monks: 'These two extremes, O monks, should not be pursued, should not be practiced, should not be frequented by one who has gone forth. Which two? That which is the pursuit of sensual happiness in sensory pleasures — low, vulgar, common, ignoble; and that which is the pursuit of self-mortification — painful, ignoble, not connected with the goal. Not approaching either of these two extremes, there is a middle way (<s>madhyamā pratipad</s>) that produces vision, produces knowledge, leads to calm, leads to direct knowledge, to awakening, to <s>nirvāṇa</s>. What is the middle way? It is the Noble Eightfold Path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>): right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right intention (<s>samyaksaṅkalpa</s>), right speech (<s>samyagvāk</s>), right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>), right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>).' body.translated_text: ) O monks, my knowledge and vision regarding these four noble truths with their three turnings and twelve aspects had not arisen — had not the vision, knowledge, understanding, and wisdom arisen — so long, O monks, I did not declare to this world — with its gods, with <s>Māra</s>, with <s>Brahmā</s>, among the host of ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, with its gods and humans — that I was free, released, detached, liberated, with a mind rid of distortion, nor did I frequently declare: 'I am the one who has awakened to the unsurpassed, perfect, complete enlightenment (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>).' children.text: asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe āyuṣmata ājñātākauṇḍinyasya virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur utpannam, aśīteś ca devatāsahasrāṇām; tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ kauṇḍinyam āmantrayate sma: ājñātas te kauṇḍinya dharmaḥ? ājñātaḥ bhagavann ājñātaḥ; ājñātas te kauṇḍinya dharmaḥ? ājñātaḥ sugata ājñāta; <ājñāto> āyuṣmatā kauṇḍinyena dharma iti tasmād āyuṣmataḥ kauṇḍinyasya ājñātakauṇḍinya ity adhivacanam; ājñāta āyuṣmatā kauṇḍinyena dharma iti
children.translated_text: While this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, in the Venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s> there arose the dustless, stainless <s>Dharma</s>-eye regarding phenomena, and in eighty thousand deities as well. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>: 'Have you understood the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>?' 'I have understood, <s>Bhagavān</s>; I have understood.' 'Have you understood the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>?' 'I have understood, <s>Sugata</s>; I have understood.' Since the Venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> understood the <s>Dharma</s>, the Venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> received the designation '<s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>' (Kauṇḍinya-who-understood). The Venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> understood the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: The Budda explains the four Noble Truths
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> explains the four Noble Truths

body.text: tatra bhagavān dvir api pañcakān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: catvārīmāni bhikṣava āryasatyāni; katamāni catvāri? duḥkham āryasatyaṃ, duḥkhasamudayo duḥkhanirodho duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad āryasatyam; 1) duḥkham āryasatyaṃ katamat? jātir duḥkhaṃ, jarā duḥkhaṃ, vyādhir duḥkhaṃ, maraṇaṃ duḥkham, priyaviprayogo duḥkham, apriyasaṃprayogo duḥkham, yad apīcchan paryeṣamāṇo na labhate tad api duḥkham; saṅkṣepataḥ pañca ime upādānaskandhā duḥkham; tasya parijñāyai āryāṣṭaṅgo mārgo bhāvayitavyaḥ; 2) duḥkhasamudayam āryasatyaṃ katamat? tṛṣṇā paunarbhavikī nandīrāgasahagatā tatra tatrābhinandinī; tasyāḥ prahāṇāya āryāṣṭāṅgo mārgo bhāvayitavyaḥ; 3) duḥkhanirodham āryāsatyaṃ katamat? yad asyā eva tṛṣṇāyāḥ paunarbhavikyāḥ nandīrāgasahagatāyās tatra tatrābhinandinyā aśeṣaprahāṇaṃ pratinisargo vāntībhāvaḥ kṣayo virāgo nirodho (
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the group of five monks a second time: 'There are, monks, four noble truths (<s>āryasatya</s>). What four? The noble truth of suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), the noble truth of the origin of suffering (<s>duḥkhasamudaya</s>), [the noble truth of] the cessation of suffering (<s>duḥkhanirodha</s>), and the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering (<s>duḥkhanirodhagāminī pratipad</s>). (1) What is the noble truth of suffering? Birth is suffering, aging is suffering, sickness is suffering, death is suffering, separation from the beloved is suffering, association with the unloved is suffering, not obtaining what one seeks and desires — that too is suffering. In brief, the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) are suffering. For its full understanding, the noble eightfold path (<s>āryāṣṭāṅga mārga</s>) must be cultivated. (2) What is the noble truth of the origin of suffering? It is craving (<s>tṛṣṇā</s>) — that which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, delighting here and there. For its abandonment, the noble eightfold path must be cultivated. (3) What is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering? It is the complete abandonment of that very craving — that which leads to renewed existence, accompanied by delight and passion, delighting here and there — its relinquishment, its being vomited up, its exhaustion, its fading away, its cessation (

  asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe āyuṣmata ājñātakauṇḍinyasyānupādāyāśravebhyaś cittaṃ vimuktam; avaśiṣṭānāṃ tu pañcakānāṃ bhikṣūṇāṃ virajo vigatamalaṃ dharmeṣu dharmacakṣur utpannam; tena khalu samayena eko <loke> arhan bhagavāṃś ca dvitīyaḥ; tatra bhagavān avaśiṣṭān pañcakān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: rūpaṃ bhikṣavo nātmā; rūpaṃ ced bhikṣava ātmā syān na rūpam ābādhāya duḥkhāya saṃvarteta; labhyeta ca rūpasyaivaṃ me rūpaṃ bhavatu, evaṃ mā bhūd iti; yasmāt tarhi bhikṣavo rūpam anātmā tasmād rūpam ābādhāya duḥkhāya saṃvartate; na ca labhyate rūpasyaivaṃ me bhavatu, evaṃ mā bhūd iti; vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñanaṃ bhikṣavo nātmā; vijñānaṃ cet bhikṣavaḥ ātmā syān na vijñānam ābādhāya <duḥkhāya> saṃvarteta; labhyeta ca vijñānasyaivaṃ me vijñānaṃ bhavatu, evaṃ mā bhūd iti; yasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ vijñānam anātmā, tasmād vijñānam ābādhāya
body.translated_text:
), its pacification, its disappearance. For its direct realization, the noble eightfold path must be cultivated. (4) What is the noble truth of the path leading to the cessation of suffering? It is the noble eightfold path — namely: right view (<s>samyagdṛṣṭi</s>), right intention (<s>samyaksaṅkalpa</s>), right speech (<s>samyagvāk</s>), right action (<s>samyakkarmānta</s>), right livelihood (<s>samyagājīva</s>), right effort (<s>samyagvyāyāma</s>), right mindfulness (<s>samyaksmṛti</s>), and right concentration (<s>samyaksamādhi</s>). This too must be cultivated.
When this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, the mind of Venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s> was liberated from the outflows (<s>āśrava</s>) without clinging. For the remaining monks of the group of five, there arose the pure, stainless <s>Dharma</s>-eye with regard to all phenomena (<s>dharma</s>). At that time, there was one <s>Arhat</s> in the world, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> was the second. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the remaining monks of the group of five: 'Form (<s>rūpa</s>), monks, is not the self (<s>ātman</s>). If, monks, form were the self, form would not tend toward affliction and suffering; and one could obtain of form: "Let my form be thus; let it not be thus." But since, monks, form is not-self (<s>anātman</s>), therefore form tends toward affliction and suffering; and one cannot obtain of form: "Let it be thus for me; let it not be thus." Feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), monks, are not the self. If, monks, consciousness were the self, consciousness would not tend toward affliction and suffering; and one could obtain of consciousness: "Let my consciousness be thus; let it not be thus." But since, monks, consciousness is not-self, therefore consciousness tends toward affliction

What do you think, monks — is form permanent or impermanent? 'It is impermanent, Venerable Sir.' And that which is impermanent — is it suffering or not suffering? 'It is suffering, Venerable Sir.' And that which is impermanent, suffering, subject to the law of change — would a learned noble disciple regard it as: "This is mine, this I am, this is my self"? 'No, Venerable Sir.' What do you think, monks — are feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness permanent or impermanent? 'They are impermanent, Venerable Sir.' And that which is impermanent — is it suffering or not suffering? 'It is suffering, Venerable Sir.' body.translated_text: ) Therefore, monks, whatever form — past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; whether far or near — all that is: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' Thus it should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom. Whatever feeling, whatever perception, whatever formations, whatever consciousness — past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; whether far or near — all that is: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' Thus it should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom. And when, monks, a learned noble disciple sees these five aggregates of clinging as neither self nor belonging to self, seeing thus, he does not cling to anything in the world. Not clinging, he is not distressed. Not being distressed, he individually attains <s>parinirvāṇa</s>: 'Exhausted is my birth; the holy life has been lived; what had to be done has been done; I know no further existence beyond this.' When this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, the minds of the remaining monks of the group of five were liberated from the outflows without clinging. At that time, there were five <s>Arhats</s> in the world, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> was the sixth.

body.translated_text: At that time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, on the bank of the river <s>Vārakā</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> created such magical transformations that the householder <s>Agrakulika</s>, seated on that very seat, did not see the young man <s>Yaśas</s>. Then the householder <s>Agrakulika</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Has the <s>Bhagavān</s> perhaps seen the young man <s>Yaśas</s>?' 'In that case, householder, sit down. There is a possibility that, seated on this very seat, you will see the young man <s>Yaśas</s>.' Then the householder <s>Agrakulika</s> thought: 'Surely the <s>Bhagavān</s> must have seen the young man <s>Yaśas</s>; for the <s>Bhagavān</s> speaks thus: "In that case, householder, sit down. There is a possibility that, seated on this very seat, you will see the young man <s>Yaśas</s>."' Having understood this, joyful, delighted, elated, filled with gladness and happiness, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. To the householder <s>Agrakulika</s> seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> — that discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> which is the preliminary task of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, namely: a talk on generosity (<s>dāna</s>), a talk on moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), a talk on heaven (<s>svarga</s>), [expounding] in detail the <s>dharmas</s> that pertain to the disadvantages, defilement, purification, renunciation, and seclusion regarding the enjoyment of sensual pleasures; and when the <s>Bhagavān</s> saw that his mind was receptive, cheerful, joyful, free from the hindrances, and fit and capable of understanding the exalted teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, then [he expounded] that exalted teaching which is the special teaching of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, namely: the Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāry āryasatyāni</s>) — suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), origin (<s>samudaya</s>), cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and path (<s>mārga</s>) — in detail. Just as a clean cloth, free from stains, fit for dyeing, when placed in dye, takes the dye perfectly, (

body.translated_text: At that time there were six <s>Arhats</s> in the world, and the <s>Bhagavān</s> was the seventh. The householder <s>Agrakulika</s> saw the young man <s>Yaśas</s> seated on that very seat. Having seen, he said this to the young man <s>Yaśas</s>: 'Come, young man, let us go home. Your mother is weary and fatigued from lamenting.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said this to the householder <s>Agrakulika</s>: 'What do you think, householder? One who, through the supramundane knowledge and supramundane vision (<s>aśaikṣa jñāna-darśana</s>), has comprehended the Four Noble Truths — suffering, origin, cessation, and path — would such a one return again to the household life? Would he enjoy sensual pleasures through the use of stored provisions?' 'No, Venerable Sir.' 'Just as you, householder, have comprehended the Four Noble Truths through the learner's knowledge and learner's vision (<s>śaikṣa jñāna-darśana</s>) — suffering, origin, cessation, and path — even so the young man has comprehended the Four Noble Truths through the supramundane knowledge and supramundane vision — suffering, origin, cessation, and path.' 'It is a gain, Venerable Sir, a great gain for the young man <s>Yaśas</s>, that he has comprehended the Four Noble Truths through the supramundane knowledge and supramundane vision — suffering, origin, cessation, and path. Excellent, <s>Bhagavān</s>! May the young man <s>Yaśas</s>, together with his attendant-ascetic, visit the householder <s>Agrakulika</s>, out of compassion.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the householder <s>Agrakulika</s> by his silence. Then the householder <s>Agrakulika</s>, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through his silence, (

  bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchanti: kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā yaśasā karma kṛtaṃ yasya karmaṇo vipākena antaḥpuramadhyagatasya svasminn antaḥpure śmaśānasaṃjñā utpannā; sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitena ca bhagavato 'ntike arhatvaṃ ca sākṣātkṛtam; yaśasā evaṃ bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni;

) having crossed beyond doubt, having transcended uncertainty, having attained confidence independent of others in the Teacher's teaching with respect to the <s>Dharma</s>, rising from their seats, arranging their upper garments over one shoulder, joining their palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We are overpowered, Venerable Sir, overpowered! We go to the <s>Bhagavān</s> for refuge, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks (<s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s>). May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept us as female lay-disciples (<s>upāsikā</s>) from this day forward, for as long as we live, having taken refuge, devoted. Therefore, Venerable Sir, let the meal be prepared right here.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to the Venerable <s>Yaśas</s>'s mother and former wife by his silence. Then the Venerable <s>Yaśas</s>'s mother and former wife, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through his silence, with their own hands satisfied and served the <s>Bhagavān</s> with pure, choice hard and soft food in many ways. Knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had eaten and was satisfied, with his hands washed and his bowl set aside, they took a lower seat and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted the Venerable <s>Yaśas</s>'s mother and former wife with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed, and approached his own dwelling. Having approached, he sat down on a prepared seat.
The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did the Venerable <s>Yaśas</s> perform, by the ripening of which <s>karma</s> the perception of a charnel ground arose for him while in his own inner apartments, and adorned with all ornaments, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> (<s>arhatva</s>) in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence?' '<s>Yaśas</s>, O monks, himself performed and accumulated these <s>karmas</s>; when the requisite conditions have matured and the causes have ripened, they stand ready like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition.

body.translated_text:
The <s>karmas</s> accumulated by <s>Yaśas</s> — who else would experience their fruition? O monks, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen externally in the element of earth, nor in the element of water, nor in the element of fire, nor in the element of wind; rather, <s>karmas</s> performed ripen precisely in the appropriated aggregates (<s>skandha</s>), elements (<s>dhātu</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatana</s>) — both wholesome and unwholesome.
<s>Karmas</s> do not perish even after hundreds of eons.
When the conditions come together and the time is right, they bear fruit for embodied beings. // (

  kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ? yo 'sau riṣir eṣa evāsau yaśāḥ kumāraḥ tena kālena tena samayena; yad anena tatra vairāgyam utpāditam tenaitarhi antaḥpuramadhyagatasya pratyayo dattaḥ; iti hi bhikṣavasḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ; ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklo vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ; tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇi apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ; ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text:
In the past, monks, not far from the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there dwelt a sage whose nature was loving-kindness, who was compassionate, devoted to the welfare of all beings. As he entered [the city] for alms-food, he saw a dead corpse. With his mind as if unattached, he entered for alms-food. Having wandered for alms-food, he returned. Then he saw that dead corpse had become decomposed and bloated. Right before him it had burst open. Then and there he generated dispassion. Thus in this case a condition was given [for understanding] within the inner apartments.
What do you think, monks? That sage was none other than the youth <s>Yaśas</s> at that time, in that era. Because he generated dispassion there, therefore now, while in the midst of the inner apartments, a condition was given [for his awakening]. Thus indeed, monks, for deeds that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for deeds that are entirely bright, the result is entirely bright; for mixed deeds, the result is mixed. Therefore, monks, having abandoned entirely dark and mixed deeds, effort should be made in entirely bright deeds alone. Thus should you train, monks.

body.translated_text: In <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the second, third, fourth, and fifth sons of prominent families — <s>Pūrṇa</s>, <s>Vimala</s>, <s>Gavāṃpati</s>, and <s>Subāhu</s> — heard: '<s>Yaśas</s>, the son of a prominent family, having shaved his hair and beard, donning ochre robes, with perfect faith has gone forth from the household life to the homeless life.' Then the sixty <s>Bhadravargīya</s> youths, having bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, sat down to one side. To the sixty <s>Bhadravargīya</s> youths seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> showed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> — the kind of <s>Dharma</s>-discourse that <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, [give as] preliminary instruction: a discourse on generosity (<s>dāna</s>), a discourse on morality (<s>śīla</s>), a discourse on heaven (<s>svarga</s>); he explained in detail the <s>dharmas</s> on the side of purification — the enjoyment, danger, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefits of renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>), seclusion, and purification. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> saw that they were of courageous mind, joyful mind, ready mind, with minds free from the hindrances, capable and ready to understand the exalted teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, then he explained in detail the exalted <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> — namely, the Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāry āryasatyāni</s>): suffering (<s>duḥkha</s>), its origin (<s>samudaya</s>), its cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), and the path (<s>mārga</s>). Just as a clean cloth, free from stains, when placed in dye, takes the dye perfectly — even so, the sixty <s>Bhadravargīya</s> youths, seated on those very seats, realized the Four Noble Truths through direct comprehension (<s>abhisamaya</s>): suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Then the sixty <s>Bhadravargīya</s> youths, having seen the <s>Dharma</s>, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, having understood the <s>Dharma</s>, having penetrated the <s>Dharma</s>, having crossed beyond doubt, having crossed beyond uncertainty, not dependent on another, (

body.translated_text: ) not led by another, having attained confidence in the <s>Dharma</s> within the Teacher's teaching, rose from their seats, arranged their upper robe over one shoulder, and with palms joined in the direction of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We are overcome, Venerable Sir, we are overcome! We go to the <s>Bhagavān</s> for refuge, and to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks (<s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s>). May you accept us as lay followers (<s>upāsakas</s>) from this day forward, for as long as we live, possessed of breath, who have gone for refuge, who are devoted.' Then the sixty <s>Bhadravargīya</s> youths, having rejoiced in and approved of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, having bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

body.text: Conversion of the brahmin Deva
body.translated_text: Conversion of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s>

body.text: tena khalu samayena kapilavastuni devo nāma brāhmaṇaḥ prativasaty āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo bhagavataḥ purāṇo gṛhapatis sakhā: asau pareṇa samayena jñātikṣayaṃ <dhanakṣayam ṛddhikṣayaṃ gataḥ; yadā bhagavatā> ṣaṭtriṃśadbhūtakoṭiparivāraṃ māraṃ vidrāvya anuttaraṃ jñānam adhigataṃ, tadā devo brāhmaṇaḥ patnyā sārdhaṃ senāyanīgrāmakam anuprāptaḥ; devena brāhmaṇena śrutaṃ bhagavatā anuttaraṃ jñānam adhigatam; śrutvā ca tasyaitad abhavat: kathaṃ punar ahaṃ bhagavantaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādayeyam iti; sa patnīm āmantrayate: bhadre bhagavatā anuttaram jñānam adhigatam; sa ca bhagavāṃś cakravartikule jātaḥ; sa idānīṃ senāyanīgrāmakaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ <carati> ............................................................ sā kathayati:
body.translated_text: At that time, in <s>Kapilavastu</s>, there lived a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Deva</s> — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions — an old friend and householder of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. At a later time, he experienced the loss of kinsmen, loss of wealth, and loss of prosperity. When the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having routed <s>Māra</s> surrounded by thirty-six billion [of his hosts], had attained the unsurpassed knowledge, the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s> together with his wife arrived at the village of <s>Senāyanī</s>. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s> heard that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had attained the unsurpassed knowledge. Having heard, he thought: 'How might I provide the <s>Bhagavān</s> with an alms-offering?' He said to his wife: 'Dear one, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has attained the unsurpassed knowledge. The <s>Bhagavān</s> was born in the family of a <s>Cakravartin</s>. Now he walks for alms in the village of <s>Senāyanī</s> ............................................................ ' She said: '

The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s>, having borrowed ornaments from a householder, gave them to his wife. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s>, together with his wife, having prepared pure, excellent hard and soft food, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept a meal at my house tomorrow.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s>'s [invitation] by his silence. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> approached the dwelling of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s>. (

) tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat; atha devo brāhmaṇaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ bhagavantaṃ viditvā sapatnī kaḥ śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ tarpayataḥ saṃpravārayataḥ; anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayitvā saṃpravārayitvā bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastaṃ apanītapātraṃ nīcataram āsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇau dharmaśravaṇāya; atha bhagavān devasya brāhmanasya daksiṇādeśanāṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ iti; devo brāhmaṇas tac chrutvā duḥkhī durmanāḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; aṭavīṃ saṃprasthitaḥ kuto 'ham alaṅkāraṃ dāsyāmīti; nānyatrātmānam ..................................................... tadā paśyati tam alaṅkāram; sa taṃ gṛhītvā gṛham āgataḥ; deva paśyāmīti <patnī> duḥkhadaurmanasyāhatā gṛhaṃ viśodhayati suvarṇakalaśaṃ dīptimantaṃ paśyati yathāpitad buddhasya buddhānubhāvena devatānāṃ ca devatānubhāvena; devas tāṃ pṛcchati: bhadre kim etad? iti; sā kathayati: āryaputra mayā suvarṇakalaśo dṛṣṭaḥ; so 'pi kathayati: bhadre, mayāpi so 'laṃkāro dṛṣṭaḥ; tāv atyarthaṃ bhagavati prasādajātau tathā cābhiprasannau; tato bhagavatā tādṛśī caturāyasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmedeśanā kṛtā; yathā devena brāhmaṇena sapatnīkena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ dṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā śrotraāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam
body.translated_text: ) Having approached, he sat upon the seat that had been prepared. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s>, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s> was comfortably seated, together with his wife, with pure, excellent hard and soft food, with their own hands fed and satisfied [the <s>Bhagavān</s>]. Having with pure, excellent hard and soft food, with their own hands fed and satisfied the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had eaten, that his hands were washed and the bowl removed, they took a lower seat and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having given the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s> the thanksgiving-teaching (<s>dakṣiṇādeśanā</s>), departed. The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s>, having heard this, became sorrowful and distressed. He set out for the wilderness [thinking:] 'How shall I repay the ornaments?' [He saw] no way other than to [sacrifice] himself ..................................................... Then he saw those ornaments. Taking them, he returned home. '<s>Deva</s>, I see...' His wife, stricken with sorrow and distress, was cleaning the house [when] she saw a golden vessel, resplendent — as things happen through the <s>Buddha</s>'s power and through the power of the deities. <s>Deva</s> asked her: 'Dear one, what is this?' She said: 'Noble husband, I saw a golden vessel.' He too said: 'Dear one, I too saw those ornaments.' Those two, having developed intense faith and devotion toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, were thus deeply devoted. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that penetrates the Four Noble Truths, by which the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Deva</s> together with his wife, having shattered the mountain of [wrong] views risen to twenty peaks with the thunderbolt of knowledge, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotaāpattiphala</s>).

body.text: Conversion of Nandā and Nandabalā
body.translated_text: Conversion of <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasyā eva rātryā atyayāt pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya senāyanīgrāmakaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: kasya nv ahaṃ senāyanīgrāmake tatprathamato dharmaṃ deśayeyam; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: yanv ahaṃ nandāyāś ca nandabalāyāś ca

Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'To whom in the village of <s>Senāyanī</s> shall I first teach the <s>Dharma</s>?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'Let me first teach the <s>Dharma</s> to <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>,

) bhagavantaṃ dūrata eva; dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhagavato 'rthāyāsanaṃ prajñapayataḥ evaṃ cāhatuḥ: niṣīdatu bhagavān prajnāpta evāsane; nyaṣīdad bhagavān prajñāpta evāsane; atha nandā ca nandabalā ca grāmikaduhitarau bhagavatpādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇe; ekāntaniṣaṇṇe nandāṃ ca nandabalāṃ ca grāmikaduhitarau bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati yāsau buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūrvakālakaraṇīyā dharmī kathā tadyathā dānakathā śīlakathā svargakathā kāmānām āsvādādīnavasaṃkleśavyavadānanaiṣkramyapraviveke anuśaṃsavyavadānapakṣyān dharmān vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati; yadaite bhagavān adrākṣīd dhṛṣṭacitte kalyacitte muditacitte vinivaraṇacitte bhavye pratibale sāmutkarṣikīṃ dharmadeśanām ājñātuṃ tadā yāsau buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sāmutkarṣikī dharmadeśanā tadyathā duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodho mārgaś catvāry āryasatyāni vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati; tadyathā śuddhaṃ vastram apagatakālakaṃ rañjanopagaṃ raṅge prakṣiptaṃ samyag eva raṅgaṃ pratigṛhṇāti, evam eva nandā ca nandabalā ca tasminn evāsane niṣaṇṇe catvary āryasatyāni abhisamayatas tadyathā duḥkhaṃ samudayaṃ nirodhaṃ mārgam; atha nandā ca nandabalā ca grāmikaduhitarau dṛṣṭadharme prāptadharme paryavagādhadharme tīrṇakāṃkṣe tīrṇavicikitse 'parapratyaye 'nanyaneye śāstuḥ śāsane dharmeṣu vaiśāradyaprāpte; utthāyāsanād ekāṃśam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam idam avocatām: abhikrānte āvāṃ bhadantābhikrānte; ete āvāṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāvo dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca; upāsike cāvāṃ dhārayādyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopete śaraṇagate 'bhiprasanne; atha nandā ca nandabalā ca grāmikaduhitarau bhagavantam idam avocatām; tena hi bhadanta ihaiva bhaktakṛtyaṃ kriyatām; adhivāsayati bhagavān nandāyāś ca nandabalāyāś ca grāmikaduhitroḥ tūṣnīṃbhāvena; atha nandā ca nandabalā ca grāmikaduhitarau bhagavatas tūṣṇīmbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ bhagavantaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayataḥ saṃpravārayataḥ; śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayitvā saṃpravārayitvā bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastaṃ apanītapātraṃ nīcatarakam āsanaṃ gṛhītvā bhagavataḥ pūrato niṣaṇṇe dharmaśravaṇāya (
body.translated_text: ) the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar. Having seen, they prepared a seat for the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said: 'Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> sit on the seat that has been prepared.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> sat on the seat that had been prepared. Then <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, the village headman's daughters, bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat to one side. To <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, the village headman's daughters, seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> showed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> — the kind of <s>Dharma</s>-discourse that serves as the preliminary task of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>: a discourse on generosity, a discourse on morality, a discourse on heaven; he explained in detail the <s>dharmas</s> on the side of purification — the enjoyment, danger, and defilement of sensual pleasures, and the benefits of renunciation, seclusion, and purification. When the <s>Bhagavān</s> saw that they were of courageous mind, joyful mind, ready mind, with minds free from the hindrances, capable and ready to understand the exalted teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, then he explained in detail the exalted <s>Dharma</s>-teaching of the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> — namely, the Four Noble Truths: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Just as a clean cloth, free from stains, when placed in dye, takes the dye perfectly — even so, <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, seated on those very seats, realized the Four Noble Truths through direct comprehension: suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. Then <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, the village headman's daughters, having seen the <s>Dharma</s>, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, having penetrated the <s>Dharma</s>, having crossed beyond doubt, having crossed beyond uncertainty, not dependent on another, not led by another, having attained confidence in the <s>Dharma</s> within the Teacher's teaching — they rose from their seats, arranged their upper robe over one shoulder, and with palms joined in the direction of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We are overcome, Venerable Sir, we are overcome! We go to the <s>Bhagavān</s> for refuge, and to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks. May you accept us as female lay followers (<s>upāsikās</s>) from this day forward, for as long as we live, possessed of breath, who have gone for refuge, who are devoted.' Then <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, the village headman's daughters, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Then, Venerable Sir, please let the meal be taken right here.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, the village headman's daughters', [invitation] by his silence. Then <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, the village headman's daughters, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s acceptance through his silence, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s> was comfortably seated, with pure, excellent hard and soft food, with their own hands fed and satisfied [the <s>Bhagavān</s>]. Having with pure, excellent hard and soft food, with their own hands fed and satisfied the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had eaten, that his hands were washed and the bowl removed, they took a lower seat and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> for the purpose of hearing the <s>Dharma</s>. body.text: yaiḥ sārdhaṃ tvayā sāmavāyikāni karmāṇi kṛtāni teṣāṃ ye kecit sannipatitāḥ kecid adyatvepi janapadair amuṣmin karmāntān kārayantas tiṣṭhanto tān śabdayeti; rājñā taddeśanivāsino janakāyās sarve āhūtāḥ; tato rājā biṃbisāro dvādaśabhī rathasahasrair aṣṭādaśabhiś ca peṭakāśvasahasrair anekaiś ca māgadhakair brāhmaṇagṛhapatiśatasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ rājagṛhān niryāti bhagavato 'ntikaṃ bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṅkramituṃ paryupāsanāyai; tasya yāvatī yānasya bhūmis tāvad yānena gatvā yānād avatīrya padbhyām evārāmaṃ prāvikṣat; yad antarā rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhagavantam adrākṣīt tadantarāt pañcakakudāny apanīya uṣṇīṣaṃ, chatraṃ, khaḍgaṃ, maṇibālavyajanaṃ citre copānahau yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tena añjaliṃ praṇamayya trir ātmano nāmadheyam anuśrāvayati: rājāham asmi bhadanta māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ; rājāham asmi bhadanta māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ; evam etan mahārāja, evam etat; rājā tvaṃ mahārāja māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ; rājā tvaṃ mahārāja māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ; niṣīda tvaṃ mahārāja yathāsvake āsane; atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ; eke māgadhakā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ; eke bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ (
body.translated_text: 'Those with whom you have performed collective deeds — whoever among them has assembled, and whoever is even now carrying out various tasks in the provinces — summon them.' The king summoned all the people dwelling in that region. Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, with twelve thousand chariots, eighteen thousand cavalry horses, and many hundreds of thousands of <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders, went forth from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence, to see and attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having gone as far as the ground was suitable for vehicles, he dismounted from his vehicle and entered the grove on foot. When the King of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>, saw the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he removed the five emblems of royalty — the turban, the parasol, the sword, the jeweled yak-tail fan, and the ornamental sandals — and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he announced his own name three times: 'I am the king, Venerable Sir — the <s>Māgadha</s> <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>. I am the king, Venerable Sir — the <s>Māgadha</s> <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>.' 'Just so, Great King, just so. You are the king, Great King, the <s>Māgadha</s> <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>. You are the king, Great King, the <s>Māgadha</s> <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>. Sit down, Great King, on your own seat.' Then the King of <s>Magadha</s>, <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. Some <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. ) vyatisārya ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ; eke yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ; eke bhagavantaṃ dūrād eva dṛṣṭvā tuṣṇīm ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ
body.translated_text: ) sat down to one side. Some, joining their palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, sat down to one side. Some, having merely seen the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar, sat down silently to one side.

body.text: Urubilvākāśyapa and the Buddha confront
body.translated_text: <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> and the <s>Buddha</s> confront

body.text: tena khalu samayena āyuṣmān urubilvākāśyapas tasyām eva parṣadi sanniṣaṇṇaḥ sannipatitaḥ; atha māgadhakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnām etad abhavat: kiṃ nu mahāśramaṇa urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ caraty āhosvid urubilvākāśyapa eva jaṭilo mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ carati? atha bhagavān māgadhakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ cetasā cittam ājñāya āyuṣmantam urubilvākāśyapaṃ gāthābhir gītena praśnaṃ pṛcchati sma:

children.translated_text: Having seen what, O dweller of <s>Urubilvā</s>,
did you abandon the fire-sacrifice and the sage's vow? /
Explain this matter to me, <s>Kāśyapa</s> —
how was your fire-sacrifice (<s>agnihotra</s>) relinquished? //

body.translated_text: At that time, the Venerable <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> was seated and assembled in that very assembly. Then the <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders thought: 'Does the Great Ascetic practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) under the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, or does the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the minds of the <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders with his own mind, questioned the Venerable <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> with verses and song:

children.translated_text: Foods, drinks, and flavors,
pleasures, and women — some speak of these. /
Seeing these very defilements in the substrata [of existence],

children.text: tasmān na iṣṭe na hute rato 'ham //
children.translated_text: therefore I delight neither in sacrifice nor in oblation. //

children.text: na te 'tra kāmeṣu mano rataṃ ced
children.translated_text: If your mind takes no pleasure in those —
in foods, drinks, and flavors — /
then in what, in the world of gods and humans,
does your mind take pleasure, <s>Kāśyapa</s>? Tell, since you are asked. //
Having seen the state without substrata — peaceful, supreme,
non-possessing, unattached to all states of existence, /
unchanging, not to be led elsewhere —

children.text: tasmān na iṣṭe na hute rato 'ham //
children.translated_text: therefore I delight neither in sacrifice nor in oblation. //

body.text:
yajñair vratair agnibhiś cāpi mokṣaḥ
  ity apy abhūn me manaso vitarkaḥ /
  andho 'smi jātimaraṇānusārī (
body.translated_text:
'Through sacrifices, vows, and fire-worship comes liberation' —
this too was a thought of my mind. /
Blind was I, following the course of birth and death, (

body.text: SBV I 156

)
  anīkṣmāno 'cyutam uttamaṃ padam //
body.translated_text:
)
not perceiving the supreme, imperishable state. //

children.translated_text: Now I see that unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) state,
well taught by the foremost of <s>Nāgas</s>, the Protector. /
For the sake of the great multitude, the Sage, the Guide,
you, O <s>Gautama</s>, of true valor, have arisen! //
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: svāgataṃ te vyavasitaṃ naitad duścintitaṃ tvayā /
children.translated_text: Welcome to you; well-resolved! This was not wrongly conceived by you. /

children.text: pravibhakteṣu dharmeṣu yac chreṣṭhaṃ tad upāgama //
children.translated_text: Among the <s>dharmas</s> that have been analyzed, you have approached the highest. //

body.text: saṃvejaya kāśyapa parṣadam iti /
body.translated_text: Inspire the assembly, <s>Kāśyapa</s>!

children.translated_text: The twin miracle of <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>

children.text: atha āyuṣmān urubilvākāśyapo bhagavatā kṛtāvakāśas takrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno, yathā <svasminn āsane 'ntarhitaḥ> samāhite citte pūrvasyāṃ diśi samabhyudgamya caturvidham īryāpathaṃ kalpayati; tadyathā, caṅkrāmyate, niṣīdati, tiṣṭhati śayyāṃ kalpayati; tejodhātum api samāpadyate; tejodhātusamāpannasya āyuṣmata urubilvākāśyapasya vividhāny arcīṃṣi kāyān niścaranti; tadyathā nīlāni, pītāni, lohitāny, avadātāni, māñjiṣṭhāni, sphaṭikavarṇāni; yamakāny api prātihāryāṇi vidarśayati; adhaḥkāyaḥ prajvalati; uparimāt kāyāc chītalā vāridhārā syandate; uparimaḥ kāyaḥ prajvalati; adhaḥkāyāc chītalā vāridhārā syandate; yathā pūrvasyāṃ diśy evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ, paścimāyām, uttarasyāṃ diśi; iti caturdiśaṃ caturvidham ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśya tān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān pratiprasrabhya yena bhagavāṃs tena añjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat; śāstā me bhagavān śrāvako 'haṃ bhagavataḥ; śastā me bhagavān śrāvako 'haṃ bhagavataḥ; evam etat kāśyapa, <evam etat kāśyapa>, śrāvakas tvaṃ mama śāstā te 'haṃ kāśyapa; śrāvakas tvaṃ mama; niṣīda tvaṃ (

) kāśyapa yathāsvake āsane; athāyuṣmān urubilvākāśyapo bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ; atha māgadhakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnām etad abhavat: na haiva mahāśramaṇa urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ carati; api tu urubilvākāśyapa eva jaṭilo mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ caratīti
children.translated_text: ) <s>Kāśyapa</s>, on your own seat.' Then the Venerable <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. Then the <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders thought: 'The Great Ascetic does not practice the holy life under the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>. Rather, the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> practices the holy life under the Great Ascetic.'

Then the Venerable <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, having been given the opportunity by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, entered the <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) called '<s>takrūpa</s>,' by which, having vanished from his own seat, he emerged in the eastern direction in the sky and displayed the four modes of deportment — namely, walking, sitting, standing, and lying down. He also entered the element of fire (<s>tejodhātu samāpatti</s>). When the Venerable <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> had entered the fire-element, various rays issued from his body — blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored. He also displayed the twin miracle (<s>yamaka prātihārya</s>): his lower body blazed while from his upper body a cool stream of water flowed; his upper body blazed while from his lower body a cool stream of water flowed. Just as in the eastern direction, so in the southern, western, and northern directions he displayed the fourfold supernatural feat in all four directions. Having displayed this, having ceased those supernatural creations, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and joining his palms, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> is my teacher; I am the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s disciple. The <s>Bhagavān</s> is my teacher; I am the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s disciple.' 'Just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, just so, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. You are my disciple; I am your teacher, <s>Kāśyapa</s>. You are my disciple. Sit down, (

body.text: The sermon of the Buddha on the production and passing away by dependence
body.translated_text: The sermon of the <s>Buddha</s> on the production and passing away by dependence

body.text: tatra bhagavān rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāram āmantrayate: rūpaṃ mahārāja utpadyate 'pi; vyayate 'pi; tasyotpādo 'pi veditavyaḥ, vyayo 'pi; vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñānaṃ mahārāja utpadyate 'pi; vyayate 'pi; tasyotpādo 'pi veditvyaḥ, vyayo 'pi; rūpasya mahārāja kulaputra utpādavyayadharmatāṃ viditvā tad rūpaṃ parijānāti; vedanāyāḥ saṃjñāyāḥ saṃskārāṇāṃ vijñānasya mahārāja kulaputra utpādavyayadharmatāṃ viditvā tad vijñānaṃ parijānāti; rūpaṃ mahārāja
body.translated_text: There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>: 'Form (<s>rūpa</s>), Great King, arises and also passes away. Its arising should be understood, and its passing away as well. Feeling (<s>vedanā</s>), perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>), volitional formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>), consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>), Great King — [each] arises and also passes away. Its arising should be understood, and its passing away as well. A son of good family, Great King, having known the nature of arising and passing away of form, fully comprehends that form. A son of good family, Great King, having known the nature of arising and passing away of feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, fully comprehends that consciousness. A son of good family, Great King,

body.text: kulaputra parijānan nopaiti, nopādatte, nādhitiṣṭhati, nābhiniviśati ātmā me iti; vedanāṃ saṃjñāṃ saṃskārān vijñānaṃ mahārāja kulaputra parijānan nopaiti, nopādatte, nādhitiṣṭhati, nābhiniviśati ātmā me iti; rūpaṃ mahārāja kulaputra anupāyantam anupādadānam anadhitiṣṭhantam anabhiniviśantam anātmamamāyamānam aprameyam asaṅkhyeyaṃ nirvṛtam iti vadāmi; vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārān vijñānaṃ mahārāja kulaputra anupāyantam anupādadānam anadhitiṣṭhantam anabhiniviśamānam anātmamamāyamānam aprameyam asaṅkhyeyaṃ nirvṛtam iti vadāmi; atha māgadhakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnām etad abhavat: sati khalu rūpam anātmā, vedanā saṃjñā saṃskārā vijñānam anātmā; atha ko nv asau bhaviṣyaty ātmā vā satvo jīvo vā jantur vā poṣo vā pudgalo vā manujo vā mānavo vā kartā vā kārako vā janako vā saṃjanako vā utthāpako vā samutthāpako (
body.translated_text: fully comprehending form, does not approach it, does not grasp it, does not hold to it, does not cling to it [thinking] 'This is my self.' Fully comprehending feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness, a son of good family, Great King, does not approach it, does not grasp it, does not hold to it, does not cling to it [thinking] 'This is my self.' Of a son of good family, Great King, who does not approach, does not grasp, does not hold to, does not cling, does not conceive 'my self' with respect to form — I declare him to be immeasurable, incalculable, and at peace (<s>nirvṛta</s>). Of a son of good family, Great King, who does not approach, does not grasp, does not hold to, does not cling, does not conceive 'my self' with respect to feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness — I declare him to be immeasurable, incalculable, and at peace.' Then the <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders thought: 'If form is without self, if feeling, perception, volitional formations, and consciousness are without self, then who will be that self, or being, or life-principle, or creature, or person, or individual, or human, or man, or agent, or doer, or producer, or generator, or instigator, or one who instigates, or speaker, or experiencer, (

body.text: SBV I 158

) vā vadako vā vedako vā <pratisaṃvedako vā>, yo na jantur nābhūn, na bhaviṣyati; nāpy etarhi vidyate; yas tatra kṛtākṛtānāṃ kalyāṇapāpakānāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayate; ya imāṃś ca skandhān nikṣipaty anyāṃś ca skandhān pratisaṃdadhāti
body.translated_text: ) or one who experiences — [that being] who neither existed, nor will exist, nor exists now — who experiences the fruition of deeds done and not done, both wholesome and unwholesome, who lays down these aggregates and takes up other aggregates?'

body.text: The sermon of the Buddha on the unreality of the Self
body.translated_text: The sermon of the <s>Buddha</s> on the unreality of the Self

body.text: atha bhagavān māgadhakānāṃ brāhmaṇagṛhapatīnāṃ cetasā cittam ājñāya bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma; ātmā ātmeti bhikṣavo bālo 'śrutavān pṛthagjanaḥ prajñaptim anupatito na cātrāsty ātmā nātmīyaṃ vā; duḥkham idaṃ bhikṣavaḥ utpadyamānam utpadyate; duḥkham idam niruddhyamānaṃ niruddhyate; saṃskārā utpadyamānā utpadyante; niruddhyamānā niruddhyante; tān hetūṃs tān pratyayān pratītya satvānāṃ saṃskārasantatiḥ pravartate; saṃskārasantatipratisandhiṃ khalu bhikṣavas tathāgato viditvā satvānāṃ cyutyupapādaṃ prajñāpayati; paśyāmy ahaṃ bhikṣavo divyena cakṣuṣā viśuddhenātikrāntamānuṣeṇa satvān; paśyāmi cyavamānān apy upapadyamānān api suvarṇān api, durvarṇān api, hīnān api, praṇītān api, sugatim api gacchato, durgatim api gacchataḥ; yathākarmopagān satvān yathābhūtān prajānāmi; amī bhavantaḥ satvāḥ kāyaduścaritena samanvāgatā vāṅmanoduścaritena samanvāgatā āryāṇām apavādakāḥ, mithyādṛṣṭayaḥ mithyādṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetos taddhetutatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt paraṃ maraṇād apāyadurgativinipātaṃ narakeṣūpapadyante; amī vā punar bhavantaḥ satvāḥ kāyasucaritena
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the minds of the <s>Māgadhaka</s> <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householders with his own mind, addressed the monks: 'Self! Self! — monks, the foolish, unlearned worldling, caught up in mere designation — but therein there is no self nor anything belonging to a self. This suffering, monks, arises when arising; this suffering ceases when ceasing. Conditioned formations (<s>saṃskāra</s>) arise when arising and cease when ceasing. Dependent on those causes and those conditions, the continuity of conditioned formations of beings proceeds. Having known this continuity and connection of conditioned formations, monks, the <s>Tathāgata</s> designates the passing away and rebirth of beings. I see, monks, with the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, beings passing away and being reborn — beautiful and ugly, inferior and superior, going to good destinies and going to evil destinies. I know beings as they truly are according to their <s>karma</s>: these beings, endowed with bad conduct of body, speech, and mind, revilers of the noble ones, holders of wrong views — on account of adopting the <s>dharma</s> of wrong-view <s>karma</s>, through that cause and that condition, at the breaking up of the body after death, are reborn in a state of deprivation, in an evil destiny, in a downfall, in the hells. But these other beings, endowed with good conduct of body,

body.text: samanvāgatā vāṅmanassucaritena samanvāgatā āryāṇām anapavādakāḥ samyagdṛṣṭayaḥ samyagdṛṣṭikarmadharmasamādānahetos taddhetutatpratyayaṃ kāyasya bhedāt sugatau svargaloke deveṣūpapadyante; evaṃ cāhaṃ bhikṣavo jānāmy evaṃ paśyāmi; na cāham evaṃ vadāmy ayaṃ me ātmā vā satvo vā jīvo vā jantur vā poṣo vā pudgalo vā manujo vā mānavo vā kartā vā kārako vā janako vā saṃjanako vā utthāpako vā samutthāpako vā vadako vā vedako vā pratisaṃvedako vā, yo na jantur nābhūn na bhaviṣyati, nāpy etarhi vidyate; yas tatra kṛtākṛtānāṃ kalyāṇāpāpakānāṃ karmaṇāṃ vipākaṃ pratisaṃvedayate; imāṃś ca skandhān nikṣipaty anyāṃś ca skandhān pratisandadhāti, nānyatra dharmasaṅketāt; tatrāyaṃ dharmasaṅketo yadutāsmin satīdaṃ bhavati; (
body.translated_text: speech, and mind, not revilers of the noble ones, holders of right views — on account of adopting the <s>dharma</s> of right-view <s>karma</s>, through that cause and that condition, at the breaking up of the body after death, are reborn in a good destiny, in the heavenly world, among the gods. Thus I know, monks, thus I see. Yet I do not say: 'This is my self, or a being, or a life-principle, or a creature, or a person, or an individual, or a human, or a man, or an agent, or a doer, or a producer, or a generator, or an instigator, or one who instigates, or a speaker, or an experiencer, or one who experiences — [a being] who neither existed, nor will exist, nor exists now — who experiences the fruition of deeds done and not done, both wholesome and unwholesome, who lays down these aggregates and takes up other aggregates.' There is nothing apart from the conventional designation of <s>dharmas</s>. And this is the conventional designation of <s>dharmas</s>: 'When this exists, that comes to be.' (

body.text: SBV I 159

) asyotpādād idam utpadyate; yadutāvidyāpratyayāḥ saṃskārāḥ; saṃskārapratyayaṃ vijñānam; vijñānapratyayaṃ nāmarūpam; nāmarūpapratyayaṃ ṣaḍāyatanam; ṣaḍāyatanapratyayaḥ sparśaḥ; sparśapratyayā vedanā; vedanāpratyayā tṛṣṇā; tṛṣṇāpratyayam upādānam; upādānapratyayo bhavaḥ; bhavapratyayā jātiḥ; jātipratyayā jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsāḥ saṃbhavanti; evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati; yadutāsmin satīdaṃ bhavati; asya nirodhād idaṃ niruddhyate; yadutāvidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ; saṃskāranirodhād vijñānanirodhaḥ; vijñānanirodhān nāmarūpanirodhaḥ; nāmarūpanirodhāt ṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ; ṣaḍāyatananirodhāt sparśanirodhaḥ; sparśanirodhād vedanānirodhaḥ; vedanārirodhāt tṛṣṇānirodhaḥ; tṛṣṇānirodhād upādānanirodhaḥ; upādānanirodhād bhavanirodhaḥ; bhavanirodhāj jātinirodhaḥ; jātinirodhāj jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā niruddhyante; evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati; iti hi bhikṣavo duḥkhāḥ saṃskārāḥ; śāntaṃ nirvāṇām; hetusamudayād duḥkhasamudayaḥ; hetunirodhād duḥkhanirodhaḥ; chinnaṃ vartma na pravartate; apratisandhi niruddhyate; eṣa evānto duḥkhasya; tatra bhikṣavaḥ kaḥ parinirvṛto nānyatra duḥkhaṃ, tan niruddhaṃ; tad vyupaśāntaṃ,
body.translated_text: ) from the arising of this, that arises. That is: conditioned by <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance) arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); conditioned by <s>saṃskāras</s> arises <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); conditioned by <s>vijñāna</s> arises <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); conditioned by <s>nāmarūpa</s> arise the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> (six sense-bases); conditioned by the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> arises <s>sparśa</s> (contact); conditioned by <s>sparśa</s> arises <s>vedanā</s> (feeling); conditioned by <s>vedanā</s> arises <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); conditioned by <s>tṛṣṇā</s> arises <s>upādāna</s> (clinging); conditioned by <s>upādāna</s> arises <s>bhava</s> (becoming); conditioned by <s>bhava</s> arises <s>jāti</s> (birth); conditioned by <s>jāti</s> arise <s>jarāmaraṇa</s> (aging-and-death), sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair. Thus arises this entire mass of suffering. That is: when this does not exist, that does not come to be; from the cessation of this, that ceases. That is: from the cessation of <s>avidyā</s>, <s>saṃskāras</s> cease; from the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s>, <s>vijñāna</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s>, <s>nāmarūpa</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s>, the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s> cease; from the cessation of the <s>ṣaḍāyatanas</s>, <s>sparśa</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>sparśa</s>, <s>vedanā</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>vedanā</s>, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>tṛṣṇā</s>, <s>upādāna</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>upādāna</s>, <s>bhava</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>bhava</s>, <s>jāti</s> ceases; from the cessation of <s>jāti</s>, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair cease. Thus ceases this entire mass of suffering. Indeed, monks, formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>) are suffering; <s>nirvāṇa</s> is peace. From the arising of the cause, suffering arises; from the cessation of the cause, suffering ceases. The path is cut and does not continue; without reconnection, [suffering] ceases. This indeed is the end of suffering. Therein, monks, who has attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s>? None other than suffering — that has ceased; that has been pacified

body.text: tac chītībhūtam; śāntam idaṃ bhikṣavaḥ padaṃ yaduta sarvopadhipratiniḥsargaḥ, tṛṣṇākṣayo virāgo nirodho nirvāṇam
body.translated_text: ; that has become cool. This, monks, is the peaceful state (<s>pada</s>) — namely, the relinquishment of all bases of attachment (<s>sarvopadhipratiniḥsarga</s>), the destruction of craving (<s>tṛṣṇākṣaya</s>), dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), cessation (<s>nirodha</s>), <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

'Therefore, Great King, whatever form — past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; whether far or near — all that is: "This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self." Thus it should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom. Therefore, Great King, whatever feeling, perception, formations, whatever consciousness — past, future, or present; internal or external; gross or subtle; inferior or superior; whether far or near — all that is: "This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self." Thus it should be seen as it truly is with right wisdom. Seeing thus, Great King, a learned noble disciple becomes disenchanted with form; becomes disenchanted with feeling, perception, formations, and consciousness. Being disenchanted, he becomes dispassionate. Being dispassionate, he is liberated. Being liberated, the knowledge and vision of liberation arise: "Exhausted is my birth; the holy life has been lived; what had to be done has been done; I know no further existence beyond this."
When this discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> was being spoken, there arose in King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> the dust-free, stain-free eye of the <s>Dharma</s> regarding all phenomena; and in eighty thousand deities; and in many hundreds of thousands of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders. I go to the <s>Bhagavān</s> for refuge, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks (<s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s>). May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept me as a lay-follower (<s>upāsaka</s>), from this day forward, for as long as I live, one who has taken refuge, one of settled faith.
