body.text: The story of the king Kṛki
body.translated_text: The story of King <s>Kṛki</s>

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣava atīte 'dhvani aranābhī nāma śāstā loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamayasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān; sa sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtaḥ; tasya mahājanakāyena śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā viviktāvakāśe pṛthivīpradeśe mahān stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ; tena khalu samayena kṛkir nāma rājā cakravartī aṣṭādaśabhir bhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhir upari vihāyasā anusaṃyān tasya stūpasya samīpam anuprāptaḥ; buddhābhiprasannābhir devatābhis tasya cakraratnaṃ vidhāritam; kṛkī rājā saṃlakṣayati: yathaitac cakraratnam avasthitaṃ, māhaiva me puṇyaparikṣayaḥ syād iti; tasya devatābhir ārocitam: mahārāja na te puṇyaparikṣayaḥ; kintv aranābheḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya etasmin pradeśe stūpam; tenedaṃ cakraratnam avasthitam; na tasyopariṣṭād gacchatīti; tataḥ kṛkī rājā aṣṭādaśabhir bhaṭabalāgrakoṭibhiḥ sahāvatīrṇo yāvat paśyati stūpam asaṃmṛṣṭam; tena saparivāreṇa saṃmṛjya gandhair mālyair dhūpaiś cūrṇair vādyaiḥ pūjāṃ kṛtvā pādayor nipatya saparivāreṇa praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam: yan mayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣinīye kārāḥ kṛtāḥ, anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena evaṃvidhānām guṇānāṃ lābhī syām; evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyam, mā virāgayeyam iti; kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena, tena
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in a former age, a teacher named <s>Aranābhi</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct (<s>vidyācaraṇasaṃpanna</s>), Well-gone (<s>Sugata</s>), Knower of the World (<s>Lokavid</s>), Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Men to be Tamed (<s>Puruṣadamayasārathi</s>), Teacher of Gods and Humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having completed the entire work of a <s>Buddha</s>, he attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder of the aggregates (<s>nirupadhiśeṣa nirvāṇadhātu</s>). A great multitude of people, having performed the veneration of relics upon his body, established a great <s>stūpa</s> in a secluded, open tract of land. At that time, a king named <s>Kṛki</s>, a universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>), traveling through the sky with eighteen billion elite warrior-forces, arrived near that <s>stūpa</s>. The deities devoted to the <s>Buddha</s> stopped his wheel-treasure. King <s>Kṛki</s> reflected: 'Given how the wheel-treasure has halted, surely my merit is not exhausted!' The deities informed him: 'Great King, your merit is not exhausted. But this is the <s>stūpa</s> of the Perfectly Enlightened One <s>Aranābhi</s> in this place. Therefore the wheel-treasure has halted; it does not pass over it.' Then King <s>Kṛki</s>, together with his eighteen billion elite warrior-forces, descended. He saw that the <s>stūpa</s> was unswept. Together with his retinue, having swept it, having worshiped with fragrances, garlands, incense, powders, and music, having prostrated at its feet, together with his retinue he made this aspiration: 'By the wholesome roots of the offerings I have made to such a true and worthy recipient, may I obtain such qualities as these. May I please such a teacher as this and not displease him.' What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the universal monarch (<s>cakravartin</s>) named <s>Kṛki</s> together with his retinue — this is none other than King <s>Bimbisāra</s> at that time, in that era. Because he

), by the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, for many hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of eons, he experienced distinguished divine and human happiness. By the aspiration he made — 'May I obtain such qualities as these' — he, together with his retinue, saw the truth in my presence. By the aspiration he made — 'May I please such a teacher as this and not displease him' — I, monks, am that very teacher: equal to, of the same speed as, of the same strength as, of the same weight as, of the same attainment as the Perfectly Enlightened One <s>Aranābhi</s> — the teacher who has been pleased, not displeased. Thus, monks, for <s>karmas</s> that are entirely dark, the result is entirely dark; for those entirely bright, the result is entirely bright; and for those mixed, the result is mixed. Therefore, monks, having abandoned entirely dark <s>karmas</s> and mixed ones, you should apply yourselves to entirely bright <s>karmas</s> alone. Thus, monks, should you train.
The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'What <s>karma</s>, Venerable Sir, did the Venerable <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> perform, that he was converted through five hundred miracles, while <s>Nadīkāśyapa</s> and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s> were converted with little difficulty?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'By these very ones, monks, <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated, with their requisite conditions gathered — as before, up to: they bear fruit for embodied beings.'

He was attended to with medicines of roots, fragrances, leaves, flowers, and fruits. But the illness did not subside. He was joined with the law of death. Then those sons, having decorated a palanquin with blue, yellow, red, and white cloths,

body.text: śibikām alaṅkṛtya śmaśānaṃ nītvā dhyāpitaḥ; śokavinodanaṃ kṛtvā pituś ca pitṛkāryāṇi dravyavibhāgasañjalpaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ; jyeṣṭho bhrātā kathayati: dravyaṃ vibhajāma iti; tau kanīyāṃsau bhrātarau necchataḥ; sa nirbandhaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ; tau kathayataḥ: yady evaṃ pāralaukikaṃ pathyadanaṃ gṛhṇīmaḥ; paścād vibhāgaṃ kariṣyāma iti; sa kathayati: kiṃ kurmaḥ? tau kathayataḥ: kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pūjām iti; sa duḥśraddadhānaḥ; tena kṛcchreṇa pratijñātam; tatas te kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhaysa pūjāṃ kṛtvā praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ; dvābhyām evaṃ praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam: anena kuśalamūlena yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksaṃbuddhena uttaro nāma māṇavo vyākṛtaḥ bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha iti, tasyāvāṃ śāsane pravrajeva viśesaṃ cādhigacchāva iti; tayoḥ praṇidhānaṃ śrutvā sa jyeṣṭho bhrātā pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ; ahaṃ khatuṃko duḥśraddadhānaś ca; anena kuślamūlena mamāpy asau śākyamuniḥ pañcabhiḥ prātihāryaśataiḥ vinīyāt, pravrājayet; prarajitaś ca viśeṣam adhigaccheyam iti; kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ yo 'sau jyeṣṭho bhrātā khaṭuṃkaḥ duḥśraddadhānaḥ eṣa evāsau urubilvākāśyapaḥ; yau tau kanīyāṃsau bhrātarau etāv etau nadīgayākāśyapau; tatpraṇidhānavaśād urubilvākāśyapaḥ pañcabhiḥ prātihāryaśatair vinītaḥ nadīgayākāśyapau tu alpakṛcchreṇa vinītau
body.translated_text: carried him to the cremation ground and cremated him. Having performed the grief-consolation rites and the funeral ceremonies for their father, they began to hold a council about dividing the property. The eldest brother said: 'Let us divide the property.' The two younger brothers refused. He began to press the matter. They said: 'If so, let us first take care of the other-worldly duty. Afterwards we will make the division.' He said: 'What shall we do?' They said: 'Let us make a worship offering to the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>.' He was lacking in faith. Only with difficulty did he consent. Then, having made a worship offering to the Perfectly Awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s>, they began to make aspirations. The two made this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may we, in the dispensation of that <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> who was prophesied by the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Perfectly Awakened One, to the young man <s>Uttara</s>, saying: "You, young man, in the age when the human lifespan is one hundred years, will become a <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One named <s>Śākyamuni</s>" — may we go forth in his dispensation and attain distinction.' Having heard their aspiration, the eldest brother fell at their feet and began to make his aspiration: 'I am stubborn and lacking in faith. By this root of merit, may that <s>Śākyamuni</s> discipline me with five hundred supernatural transformations (<s>prātihārya</s>), ordain me, and may I, having been ordained, attain distinction.' What do you think, monks? That eldest brother who was stubborn and lacking in faith — he was none other than <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s>. Those two younger brothers — they were none other than <s>Nadī Kāśyapa</s> and <s>Gayā Kāśyapa</s>. By the force of that aspiration, <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s> was disciplined with five hundred supernatural transformations, while <s>Nadī</s> and <s>Gayā Kāśyapa</s> were disciplined with little difficulty.

body.text: The story of Kalandakanivāpa
body.translated_text: The story of <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>:

body.text: yadā rājā bimbisāraḥ kumāro bhavati, tadā rājagṛhe 'nyatamo gṛhapatiḥ; tasyārāmaḥ puṣpaphalasalilasaṃpannaḥ; sa tatrātyartham (
body.translated_text: When King <s>Bimbisāra</s> was [still] a prince, there was a certain householder in <s>Rājagṛha</s>. He had a garden abounding in flowers, fruits, and water. He was exceedingly (

body.text: SBV I 164

) adhyavasitaḥ; yāvad bimbisāreṇa bahirnirgatena tad udyānaṃ dṛṣṭam; so 'tyartham adhyavasitaḥ kathayati: gṛhapate prayaccha mamaitad udyānam iti; sa nānuprayacchati; punar apy upapradānenābhihitaḥ; sa kathayati: kumāra, kāmam ahaṃ deśaparityāgaṃ kuryāṃ, na codyānaṃ dadyām iti; bimbisāraḥ kumāraḥ kathayati: gṛhapate smartavyaṃ te vākyam; yadā ahaṃ rājā bhaviṣyāmi, tadā svayam eva grahīṣyāmīti; sa kathayati: yadā tvaṃ rājā bhaviṣyasi, tadā ahaṃ rājagṛhāt prakramiṣyāmīti; bimbisāraḥ kumāro hum iti kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ; yāvad apareṇa samayena mahāpadmo rājā kālagataḥ; bimbisāraḥ kumāro rājye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ tena tad udyānaṃ haṭhāt gṛhītam; sa gṛhapatir hṛdrogaṃ patitaḥ, tasminn udyāne atyartham adhyavasitaḥ, kālagataḥ; sa tatraiva āśīviṣa utpannaḥ; sa rājño 'bhīkṣṇaṃ randhrānveṣaṇatatparo 'vatiṣṭhate; yāvad rājā bimbisāraḥ saṃprāpte vasantakālasamaye puṣpiteṣu pādapeṣv antaḥpurasahīyas tad udyānaṃ nirgataḥ; sa tatra niṣpuruṣeṇa antaḥpurajanena sārdhaṃ ratikrīḍāṃ pratyanubhūya middham avakrāntaḥ; puṣpaphalalolupo mātṛgrāmaḥ samantāt paryaṭitum ārabdhaḥ; ekā strī khaḍgaṃ rājña ārakṣikā sthāpitā .....................................................
body.translated_text: ) attached to it. Once, when <s>Bimbisāra</s> had gone outside, he saw that garden. Being exceedingly attached, he said: 'Householder, give me this garden.' He refused to give it. He was again addressed with an offer of compensation. He said: 'Prince, I would sooner abandon the country than give up my garden.' Prince <s>Bimbisāra</s> said: 'Householder, remember your words. When I become king, I shall take it myself.' He said: 'When you become king, I shall depart from <s>Rājagṛha</s>.' Prince <s>Bimbisāra</s> said 'Hmm!' and departed. Then at a later time, King <s>Mahāpadma</s> passed away. Prince <s>Bimbisāra</s> was established on the throne. He seized that garden by force. That householder, having been exceedingly attached to the garden, fell into a heart disease and died. He was reborn right there as a venomous serpent. He constantly remained intent on seeking an opportunity against the king. Then, when the spring season arrived and the trees were in bloom, King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, together with the women of his inner apartments, went out to that garden. There, having enjoyed romantic play with the women of his inner apartments, without any guards, he was overcome by torpor. The womenfolk, eager for flowers and fruits, began wandering about in all directions. One woman was posted as a guard with the king's sword. .....................................................

body.text: rājñaḥ puṇyānubhāvāt kalandakā nāma pakṣiṇaḥ; tais tam āśīviṣaṃ parivārya kalakalāśabdaḥ kṛtaḥ; yaṃ śrutvā asidhāriṇyā striyā khadgena jīvitād vyaparopitaḥ; santrastayā ca mahān śabdaḥ kṛtaḥ; tato rājā santrasto vibuddhaḥ kathayati, kim etad iti; tayā striyābhihitam: deva eṣa āśīviṣaḥ devaṃ daṣṭum abisaṃprasthitaḥ kalandakaiḥ pakṣibhiḥ kolāhalaśabdaḥ kṛtaḥ mayā jīvitād vyaparopita iti; rājñas tām avasthāṃ pratiśrutya kumārabhaṭabalāgraḥ rājagṛhanivāsī janakāyaḥ sannipatitaḥ; antar bahis tad udyānaṃ mahatā kolahalaśabdena kṣobhitum ārabdham; prajāvatsalo (
body.translated_text: By the king's merit, there were birds called <s>kalandakas</s>. They surrounded that venomous serpent and raised a clamor. Hearing that, the woman with the sword killed [the serpent]. Frightened, she raised a great cry. Then the king, startled, woke up and said: 'What is this?' The woman said: 'Your Majesty, this venomous serpent had set out to bite Your Majesty. The <s>kalandaka</s> birds raised a clamor. I killed it.' When the king's attendants heard of that situation — the army of young warriors and the people dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s> — they gathered. Inside and outside, the garden began to be shaken with a great commotion. The king was (

body.text: SBV I 165

) rājā; bhūyasā antaḥpurajanakāyo 'śruparyākulekṣaṇo vyavasthitaḥ; tato rājā kathayati: bhavanto yo rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ jīvitenācchādayati, kas tasya vara iti; janakāyaḥ kathayati: upārdhaṃ rājyasyeti; rājā kathayati: bhavantaḥ kalandakaiḥ pakṣibhir mama jīvitaṃ dattam; tad ebhyo dattam upārdhaṃ rājyasya iti; amātyāḥ kathayanti: deva pakṣiṇa ete tiryagyonigatāḥ; kim eṣām upārdharājyena; yasminn ete veṇuvane prativasanti tatraiṣāṃ nivāpaḥ prajñapyatām iti; rājā kathayati: evaṃ kriyatām iti; tad udyānaṃ veṇuvanapariveṣṭitam; amātyais teṣāṃ veṇuvanasāmantake nivāpaḥ prajñaptaḥ; tasya veṇuvanaṃ kalandakanivāpa iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā; rājño bimbisārasya mātula ājīvikānāṃ madhye pravrajitaḥ; tena tad udyānaṃ tasmai nivāsāya dattaṃ
body.translated_text: ) fond of his subjects. For the most part, the people of the inner apartments stood with eyes overflowing with tears. Then the king said: 'Sirs, he who protects the life of a king, an anointed <s>Kṣatriya</s> — what reward [should be given] to him?' The people said: 'Half the kingdom.' The king said: 'Sirs, the <s>kalandaka</s> birds saved my life. Therefore, half the kingdom is given to them.' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, these are birds, animals. What use is half the kingdom to them? In whichever bamboo grove they dwell, let a feeding ground be established for them there.' The king said: 'Let it be so.' That garden was enclosed within a bamboo grove. The ministers established a feeding ground for them near the bamboo grove. That bamboo grove acquired the name '<s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>' (the <s>Kalandaka</s> Birds' Feeding Ground). King <s>Bimbisāra</s>'s maternal uncle had gone forth among the <s>Ājīvikas</s>. He gave that garden to him as a dwelling.

body.text: Bimbisāra presents Veṇuvana to the Buddha
body.translated_text: <s>Bimbisāra</s> presents <s>Veṇuvana</s> to the <s>Buddha</s>:

body.text: yāvad bhagavān magadheṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran rājagṛham anuprāpto 'nyatamasmin vṛkṣamūle 'vasthitaḥ; aśrauśīd rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ, bhagavān māgadhesu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran rājagṛham anuprāpto 'nyatamasmin vṛkṣamūle 'vatiṣṭhatīti; śrutvā ca punar mahatyā rājaṛddhyā, mahatā rājānubhāvena, rājagṛhān niṣkramya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ; ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ śreṇyaṃ bimbisāraṃ bhagavān ramyayā kathayā sandarśayati, samādāpayati, samuttejayati, saṃpraharṣayati; anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā sandarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm; atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāra <utthāyāsanād ekāṃśam uttarāsangaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat: adhivāsayatu me bhagavāṃś śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena: adhivāsayati bhagavān rājño māgadhasya śreṇyasya bimbisārasya tūṣṇimbhāvena;> atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāro bhagavatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā, bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ; rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāras tām eva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kalyam evotthāyāsanāni prajñapya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālam ārocayati: samayo (
body.translated_text: When the <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering through the <s>Magadha</s> territories, reached <s>Rājagṛha</s> and was staying at the foot of a certain tree, King <s>Māgadha Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> heard: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s>, wandering through the <s>Magadha</s> territories, has reached <s>Rājagṛha</s> and is staying at the foot of a certain tree.' Having heard, with great royal splendor and great royal power, he departed from <s>Rājagṛha</s> and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. To the king <s>Māgadha Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted him with a delightful discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then king <s>Māgadha Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> <rose from his seat, arranged his upper garment over one shoulder, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to a meal tomorrow in my residence, together with the community of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to King <s>Māgadha Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> by his silence.> Then King <s>Māgadha Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through his silence, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, rose from his seat, and departed. King <s>Māgadha Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>, that very night, having prepared pure, choice hard and soft food, and early in the morning having arranged seats and set out water-pitchers, announced the time to the <s>Bhagavān</s> through a messenger: 'It is time, (

body.text: SBV I 166
) bhadanta; sajjaṃ bhaktam yasyedānīṃ kālaṃ manyate iti; atha
body.translated_text: ) Venerable Sir. The meal is ready; may the <s>Bhagavān</s> come now when he deems it time.' Then

body.text: bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya, pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṅghapuraskṛto yena rājño māgadhasya śreṇyasya bimbisārasya nivāsas tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṅghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayati, saṃpravārayati; anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpya saṃpravārya, bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ sauvarṇaṃ bhṛṅgāraṃ gṛhītvā tad udyānaṃ bhagavate niryātayati: idaṃ bhadanta veṇuvanaṃ, kalandakanivāpam; atra bhagavān viharatu yathāsukham iti; tathā sthavirair api sūtrānteṣūpanibaddhaṃ, bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpa iti
body.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken up his bowl and robe, accompanied by the community of monks and preceded by the assembly of monks, approached the residence of King <s>Māgadha Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>. Having approached, he sat down on a seat prepared at the head of the community of monks. Then King <s>Māgadha Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s>, knowing that the <s>Buddha</s>-led community of monks was comfortably seated, with his own hands satisfied and served them with pure, choice hard and soft food. Having in many ways satisfied and served them with pure, choice hard and soft food with his own hands, knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had eaten, with his hands washed and his bowl set aside, he took a golden pitcher and formally offered that garden to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This, Venerable Sir, is the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> dwell here at his ease.' Thus the elders too have recorded in the <s>sūtras</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s>, at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>.'

body.text: Anāthapiṇḍada meets the Buddha
body.translated_text: <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> meets the <s>Buddha</s>:

body.text: tena khalu samayena bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe; rājagṛhe 'nyatamo gṛhapatiḥ; tena bhagavān gṛhe upanimantritaḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena; tasmiṃś ca samaye anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ rājagṛham anuprāptaḥ kenacid eva karaṇīyena; sa tasya gṛhapater niveśane rātriṃ vāsam upagataḥ; atha sa gṛhapatiḥ sarātram evotthāyāntarjanam āmantrayate: uttiṣṭhata āryā uttiṣṭhata bhadramukhāḥ; kaṣṭhāni pāṭayata; samidhaṃ prajvālayata; bhaktaṃ pacata; sūpikaṃ pacata; khādyakāny ullāḍayata; pratijāgṛta maṇḍalavāṭam iti; athānāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater etad abhavat: kiṃ punar asya gṛhapater āvāho vā bhaviṣyati, vivāho vā, rāṣṭraṃ vā, śreṇī vā, pūgā vā parṣado vā rājā <vā> anena māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena nimantrito bhaviṣyati; iti viditvā taṃ gṛhapatim idam avocat: kiṃ punas te gṛhapate āvāho vā bhaviṣyati vivāho vā rāṣṭraṃ vā śreṇī vā pūgā vā parṣado vā rājā vā te māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ? na me gṛhapate āvāho, na vivāho, na rāṣṭraṃ, na śreṇī, na pūgā, nāpi parṣado, nāpi rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ; api tu buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṅgho 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ; (
body.translated_text: At that time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the Bamboo Grove (<s>Veṇuvana</s>), at the Squirrels' Feeding Ground (<s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>). In <s>Rājagṛha</s> there was a certain householder. He had invited the <s>Bhagavān</s> to his house together with the community of monks for a meal. At that time the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> had arrived at <s>Rājagṛha</s> on some business. He had taken up lodging for the night at that householder's dwelling. Then that householder, having risen while it was still night, addressed the household servants: 'Arise, noble ones! Arise, good people! Split the wood; kindle the fire; cook the rice; cook the curry; prepare the confections; and keep watch over the ceremonial ground.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> thought: 'Is there going to be a wedding or a marriage at this householder's [residence]? Or a national festival, a guild-gathering, an assembly, or a banquet? Or has the king, <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, been invited to a meal in his home tomorrow?' Having thought this, he said to that householder: 'Is there going to be a wedding or a marriage at your [residence], householder? Or a national festival, a guild-gathering, an assembly, or a banquet? Or has the king, <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, been invited to a meal in your home tomorrow?' 'There is no wedding for me, householder, no marriage, no national festival, no guild-gathering, no assembly, no banquet, nor has the king, <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, been invited to a meal in my home tomorrow. Rather, the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> has been invited to a meal in my home.' (

body.text: SBV I 167
body.translated_text: SBV I 167

body.text: ) anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapater buddha ity aśrutapūrvaṃ ghoṣaṃ śrutvā sarvaromakūpāny āhṛṣṭāni; sa āhṛṣṭaromakūpas taṃ gṛhapatim idam avocat: ka eṣa gṛhapate buddho nāma; asti gṛhapate śramaṇo gautamaḥ śākyaputraḥ śākyakulāt keśaśmaśrv avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajitaḥ; so 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim
body.translated_text: ) When the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> heard the word '<s>Buddha</s>' — a sound never heard before — the hair on his entire body stood on end. With his hair standing on end, he said to that householder: 'Who is this one called "<s>Buddha</s>," householder?' 'There is, householder, an ascetic named <s>Gautama</s>, a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>, who, from the <s>Śākya</s> family, having shaved his hair and beard, having put on ochre robes, with perfect faith went forth from the household life to the homeless life. He has attained unsurpassed perfect awakening

body.text: abhisaṃbuddhaḥ; sa eṣa gṛhapate buddho nāma; ka eṣa gṛhapate saṅgho nāma; santi gṛhapate kṣatriyakulād api kulaputrāḥ keśaśmaśrv avatārya kāṣāyāṇy <vastrāṇy> ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā <agārād anāgarikāṃ> tam eva bhagavantaṃ pravrajitam anupravrajitāḥ; brāhmaṇakulād api vaiśyakulād api śūdrakulād api kulaputrāḥ keśaśmaśrv avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā <agārād anāgārikāṃ> tam eva bhagavantaṃ pravrajitam anupravrajitāḥ; sa eṣa gṛhapate saṅgho nāma; śvaḥ sa mayā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṅgho 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ; kutra gṛhapate sa bhagavān etarhi viharati? asminn eva rājagṛhe śītavane śmaśāne; labhyaṃ gṛhapate so 'smābhir bhagavān draṣṭum; tena hi gṛhapate āgamaya tāvat tvam; sthānam etad vidyate yad ihāgataṃ śvo drakṣyasi; anāthapiṇdado gṛhapatis tāṃ rātriṃ buddhālambanayā smṛtyā middham avakrāntaḥ; so 'prabhāte prabhātasaṃjñī yena śivikādvāraṃ tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; tena khalu samayena śivikādvāraṃ rātryā dvau yāmau vivṛtaṃ tiṣṭhati, pūrvakaṃ paścimakaṃ ca, māhaiva āgantukānāṃ gamikānāṃ ca dūtānāṃ vighāto bhaviṣyatīti; yāvat paśyati śivikādvāraṃ vivṛtaṃ tiṣṭhati; sālokena ca sphuṭam; tasyaitad abhavat: nūnaṃ prabhātā rajanī; tathāhi śivikādvāraṃ vivṛtaṃ tiṣṭhati; iti viditvā tenaiva ālokena nagarān niṣkrāntaḥ; samanantaraniṣkrāntasya cāsya ya ālokaḥ so 'ntarhitaḥ; andhakāraṃ prādurbhūtam; tasyābhūd bhayam; abhūc chambhitatvam; abhūd romaharṣaḥ; māhaiva kaścid viheṭhayen manuṣyo vā amanuṣyo vā dhūrtako vā asaṃprāptaṃ vā svāt prabhūtam kulaśulkam iti; viditvā pratinivartitukāmo madhuskandhasya devaputrasya sthaṇḍilaṃ pradakṣiṇīkaroti, namaskaroti ca; atha madhuskandhadevaputrasya etad abhavat: adyaivānāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā satyadarśanaṃ kartavyam; adyaivāyaṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantam apāsya anyadevatā namaskāraṃ kariṣyati; iti viditvā yāvac ca śivikādvāraṃ yāvac ca śītavanaṃ śmaśānam atrāntarād udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatim idam avocat: abhikrama gṛhapate, mā pratikrama; abhikramatas te śreyo bhavati, na pratikramataḥ; tat kasya hetoḥ
body.translated_text: . He, householder, is the one called "<s>Buddha</s>."' 'Who is this, householder, called "<s>Saṅgha</s>"?' 'There are, householder, sons of good family from the <s>Kṣatriya</s> class who, having shaved their hair and beards, having put on ochre robes, with perfect faith, have gone forth following that very <s>Bhagavān</s> who went forth. From the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> class too, from the <s>Vaiśya</s> class too, from the <s>Śūdra</s> class too, sons of good family, having shaved their hair and beards, having put on ochre robes, with perfect faith, have gone forth following that very <s>Bhagavān</s> who went forth. That, householder, is what is called "<s>Saṅgha</s>." Tomorrow I have invited the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> to a meal in my home.' 'Where, householder, does that <s>Bhagavān</s> now dwell?' 'Right here in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the Cool Grove (<s>Śītavana</s>) charnel ground.' 'Is it possible, householder, for us to see that <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 'In that case, householder, wait for now. There is a possibility that you will see him when he comes here tomorrow.' The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> fell asleep that night with his mindfulness established on the <s>Buddha</s> as its object. While it was still dark, thinking it was dawn, he approached the <s>Śivikā</s> gate. At that time, the <s>Śivikā</s> gate stood open for two watches of the night — the first and the last — [thinking:] 'Let there be no obstruction for travelers, wayfarers, and messengers.' When he saw the <s>Śivikā</s> gate standing open, suffused with light, he thought: 'Surely the night has dawned; for the <s>Śivikā</s> gate stands open.' Having realized this, he went out of the city by that very light. But as soon as he went out, the light that had been there vanished. Darkness appeared. Fear arose in him; trembling arose; his hair stood on end. [He thought:] 'Let not someone harm me — whether a human, a non-human, or a scoundrel — and let not my great family wealth, not yet acquired, be lost.' Having thought this, wishing to turn back, he circumambulated and paid homage to the shrine of the divine son <s>Madhuskandha</s>. Then the divine son <s>Madhuskandha</s> thought: 'This very day the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> is to see the truth. This very day he is about to turn away from the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> and pay homage to another deity.' Having realized this, he suffused with a magnificent radiance the entire area between the <s>Śivikā</s> gate and the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground, and said this to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: 'Go forward, householder, do not turn back! Going forward is better for you, not turning back.' For what reason?

children.translated_text: ) 'Who are you, good sir?' 'I am, householder, a youth named <s>Madhuskandha</s>, a former household-companion of yours. Having generated a serene mind (<s>cittaprasāda</s>) toward the monks <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, I died and was reborn among the <s>Cāturmahārājika</s> (Four Great Kings') gods. I dwell right here at this <s>Śivikā</s> gate as its resident deity. Therefore I say thus: "Go forward, householder, do not turn back! Going forward is better for you, not turning back."' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> thought: 'The <s>Buddha</s> must indeed be no ordinary one; no ordinary one is the proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s> — since even now the deities themselves are eager for the sight of that <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Having realized this, he approached the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground. At that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s> was walking back and forth on the walking-path in the open outside his dwelling, for the most part awaiting the arrival of the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar. Having seen, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, the householder greeted the <s>Bhagavān</s> with a greeting: 'Has the <s>Bhagavān</s> slept well?' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> at that moment spoke verses:

body.text: atha bhagavān anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatim ādāya vihāraṃ praviśya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; anāthapiṇdado gṛhapatir bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaṇ; ekānte niṣaṇṇam anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatiṃ bhagavān dharmyayā kathayā sandarśayati samādāpayati <samuttejyati>, saṃpraharṣayati; yāsau buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ pūrvakālakaraṇīyā dharmyā kathā, tadyathā dānakathā śīlakathā svargakathā kāmānām aśvādādīnavasaṅkleśavyavadānanaiṣkramyapraviveke anuśaṃsavyavadānapakṣyān dharmān vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati; yadā cainaṃ bhagavān adrākṣīt hṛṣṭacittam kalyacittaṃ muditacittaṃ vinivaraṇacittaṃ bhavyaṃ pratibalaṃ sāmutkarṣikīṃ dharmadeśanām ājñātum, tadā yāsau buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ sāmutkarṣikī dharmadeśanā tadyathā duḥkhaṃ samudayo nirodho mārgaś catvāry āryasatyāni vistareṇa saṃprakāśayati; athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatis tasminn evāsane niṣaṇṇaś catvāry āryasatyāny abhisameti; tadyathā (
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, taking the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> with him, entered the dwelling and sat down on a prepared seat. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and sat down to one side. To the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> — that discourse on the <s>Dharma</s> which is the preliminary task of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, namely: a talk on generosity (<s>dāna</s>), a talk on moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), a talk on heaven (<s>svarga</s>), [expounding] in detail the <s>dharmas</s> pertaining to the disadvantages, defilement, purification, renunciation, and seclusion regarding the enjoyment of sensual pleasures; and when the <s>Bhagavān</s> saw that his mind was receptive, cheerful, joyful, free from the hindrances, and fit and capable of understanding the exalted teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, then [he expounded] that exalted teaching which is the special teaching of <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, namely: the Four Noble Truths (<s>catvāry āryasatyāni</s>) — suffering, origin, cessation, and path — in detail. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, seated on that very seat, comprehended the Four Noble Truths — (

The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>,

body.text: gṛhapatir dṛṣṭadharmā prāptadharmā viditadharmā paryavagāḍhadharmā tīrṇakāṅkṣo tīrṇavicikitsaḥ aparapratyayo 'nanyaneyaḥ śāstuś śāsane dharmeṣu vaiśāradyaprāptaḥ utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā, yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat: abhikrānto 'haṃ bhadantābhikrāntaḥ; eṣo 'haṃ bhagavantaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṅghaṃ ca; upāsakaṃ māṃ ca dhāraya adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetaṃ śaraṇāgatam abhiprasannam; atha bhagavān anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatim idam avocat; kinnāmā tvaṃ gṛhapate? aham asmi bhadanta sudatto nāmnā; api tv anāthebhyaḥ piṇḍakam anuprayacchāmi; tato mām anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir iti janaḥ sañjānīte; kutobhūmakas tvaṃ gṛhapate? asti bhadanta prācīneṣu janapadeṣu śrāvastī nāma kosalānāṃ nigamaḥ; tatrāhaṃ prativasāmi
body.translated_text: having seen the <s>Dharma</s>, having attained the <s>Dharma</s>, having understood the <s>Dharma</s>, having penetrated the <s>Dharma</s>, having crossed beyond doubt, having transcended uncertainty, having attained confidence independent of others in the Teacher's teaching with respect to the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat, arranged his upper garment over one shoulder, joined his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I am overpowered, Venerable Sir, overpowered! I go to the <s>Bhagavān</s> for refuge, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks (<s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s>). May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept me as a male lay-disciple (<s>upāsaka</s>) from this day forward, for as long as I live, having taken refuge, devoted.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: 'What is your name, householder?' 'Venerable Sir, my name is <s>Sudatta</s>. But since I give morsels of food to the destitute, therefore people know me as "the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> (Giver-of-food-to-the-helpless)."' 'Where are you from, householder?' 'Venerable Sir, in the eastern districts there is a town of the <s>Kosalas</s> named <s>Śrāvastī</s>. There I dwell.'

Then, having completed and accomplished whatever business or affairs he had in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Please assign me, <s>Bhagavān</s>, a monk as companion, with whose help I may have a monastery built for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'Which monk would be one whom the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> together with his retinue and the people of <s>Śrāvastī</s> would follow?' He saw: the monk <s>Śāriputra</s>. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Attend to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> together with his retinue and the people dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>.' The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> accepted by his silence. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.

'Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> come to <s>Śrāvastī</s>. I shall attend upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> for as long as I live with robes, alms-food, medicines for the sick, and requisites, together with the community of monks (<s>Bhikṣusaṅgha</s>).' 'Householder, are there monasteries (<s>vihāras</s>) in <s>Śrāvastī</s>?' 'No, Venerable Sir.' 'Householder, where there are monasteries, monks consider it worthwhile to come, to go, and to dwell.' 'Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> come; I shall act in such a way that there will be monasteries in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and monks will consider it worthwhile to come, to go, and to dwell.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>'s [invitation] by his silence. body.text: athāyuṣmāṃś chāriputras tasyā eva rātrer atyayāt pūrvāhāṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣat; rājagṛhaṃ piṇḍāya caritvā kṛtabhaktakṛtyaḥ paścādbhaktapiṇḍapātapratikrānto yathāparibhuktaṃ śayanāsanaṃ pratiśamayya, samādāya pātracīvaraṃ, yena śrāvastī tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ; athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ prabhūtaṃ śambalam ādāya ekaikarātrinivāsena śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ sa praviśann eva śrāvastīm ārāmeṇārāmam
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, after the passing of that night, in the morning, having dressed and taken his bowl and robe, entered <s>Rājagṛha</s> for alms. Having walked for alms in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, having completed his meal, returning from his alms-round after eating, he put away his sleeping arrangements as they had been used, took his bowl and robe, and set out on a journey toward <s>Śrāvastī</s>. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having taken abundant provisions, by single-night stages, arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. While entering <s>Śrāvastī</s>, he walked from park to park,

body.text: udyānenodyānam upavanenopavanaṃ caṅkramam anucaṅkramyamāṇo suvicarann evam āha: kataraḥ sa pṛthivīpradeśo bhaviṣyati śrāvastyā nātidūre nātyāsanne divā alpākīrṇo 'lpavilāpo rātrāv alpaśabdo 'lpanirghoṣaḥ alpadaṃśamaśakavātātapasarīsṛpasaṃsparśaḥ, yatrāhaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayiṣyāmīti; adrākṣīd anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir jetasya kumarasyārāmaṃ śrāvastyā nātidūre nātyāsanne divā alpākirṇam alpavilāpaṃ rātrāv alpaśabdam alpanirghoṣam alpadaṃśamaśakavātātapasarīsṛpasparśam; dṛṣṭvā ca punar asyaitad abhavat: atrāhaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayiṣyāmīti; sa praviṣann eva svaṃ niveśanaṃ yena jetaḥ kumāras tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya jetaṃ kumāram idam avocat: anuprayaccha me kumāra ārāmam; (
body.translated_text: from garden to garden, from grove to grove, walking up and down, carefully surveying, and said: 'Which tract of land will there be — not too far from <s>Śrāvastī</s> and not too near, uncrowded by day, quiet by day, with little noise and commotion by night, with few biting insects, gnats, wind, heat, and creeping things — where I may have a monastery built for the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> saw the park of Prince <s>Jeta</s> — not too far from <s>Śrāvastī</s> and not too near, uncrowded by day, quiet by day, with little noise and commotion by night, with few biting insects, gnats, wind, heat, and creeping things. Having seen, he thought: 'Here I shall have a monastery built for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Even as he entered his own dwelling, he approached Prince <s>Jeta</s>. Having approached, he said to Prince <s>Jeta</s>: 'Give me, Prince, your park. (

) ahaṃ tatra bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ kārayāmi iti; sa kathayati:na me gṛhapate sa ārāmaḥ; kintu udyānaṃ tan memeti; dvir api trir apy anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir jetaṃ kumāram idam avocat: anuprayaccha me kumāra ārāmam; ahaṃ tatra bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayāmīti; aparityakto <gṛhapate> me ārāmaḥ koṭisaṃstareṇāpi; punar apy anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir jetaṃ kumāram idam avocat: kṛtārgho 'si kumāra ārāmasya; pratīccha hiraṇyasuvarṇam; mamārāmaḥ; kaḥ kṛtārghaḥ? tvaṃ kṛtārghaḥ; tau kṛtārgho na kṛtārgha iti vivādam āpannau, yena vyāvahārikapuruṣās tena saṃprasthitāḥ; atrāntare caturṇāṃ lokapālānām etad abhavat: ayam anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir udyukto bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayitum; sāhāyyam asyānuṣṭheyam iti; tato vyāvahārikapuruṣam ātmānam abhinirmāya arthādhikaraṇe niṣaṇṇāḥ; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir jetaś ca kumāro vyāvahārikasakāśam upasaṅkrāntau; athānāthapiṇḍako gṛhapatir vyāvahārikapuruṣāṇām etam arthaṃ vistareṇa nivedayati; te kathayanti: kṛtārgho 'si kumāra ārāmasya: pratīccha suvarṇam: gṛhapater ārāma iti; sa tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ śakatair bhāraiḥ mūṭaiḥ piṭakair uṣṭrair gobhir gardbhaiḥ prabhūtaṃ suvarṇam abhinirhṛtya, sarvaṃ jetavanaṃ saṃstartum ārabdhaḥ; na parisamāpyate; tiṣṭhate evānāstīrṇaḥ kaścit pṛthivīpradeśaḥ; tataḥ anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir etam arthaṃ cintayan muhūrtasṃ tūṣṇīm asthāt: katarat tan nidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati? nātistokaṃ, nātiprabhūtaṃ yena ayam anāstīrṇaḥ pṛthivīpradeśaḥ āstariṣyati; na ca punar gopayitavyo bhaviṣyatīti; jetaḥ kumāraḥ saṃlakṣayati: nūnam anāthapiṇḍadsya gṛhapater vipratisāraḥ, kasmād ārāmakāraṇād iyantaṃ mahāntaṃ dhanaskandhaṃ parityajāmi; iti viditvā anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatim idam avocat: sacet te ha gṛhapate vipratisāraḥ pratīccha suvarṇam; mamaivārāmaḥ; na me kumāra vipratisāraḥ; api tv aham etam evārtham anucintayan muhūrtaṃ tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ; katarat tan nidhānaṃ bhaviṣyati? nātistokaṃ nātiprabhūtaṃ, yenāyam anāstīrṇaḥ pṛthivīpradeśaḥ āstariṣyati; na ca prnar gopayitavyo bhaviṣyatīti; atha jetasya kumārasya etad abhavat:na batāvaro
body.translated_text: ) I shall have a monastery built there for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' He said: 'Householder, that is not my park [for sale]; rather, it is my pleasure-garden.' Again and again the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said to Prince <s>Jeta</s>: 'Give me, Prince, your park. I shall have a monastery built there for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'Householder, my park is not given up even at the price of covering [it with coins] by the <s>koṭi</s> (ten million).' Again the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said to Prince <s>Jeta</s>: 'Prince, you have named the price of the park. Accept the gold; the park is mine.' 'Who named the price?' 'You named the price.' The two, [arguing] 'the price was named' versus 'the price was not named,' fell into a dispute. They set out toward the legal arbitrators. Meanwhile, the Four Great Kings (<s>Lokapālas</s>) thought: 'This householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> is eager to have a monastery built for the <s>Bhagavān</s>. He should be given support.' Then, having created themselves in the form of legal arbitrators, they sat at the tribunal for the property dispute. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> and Prince <s>Jeta</s> approached the arbitrators. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> explained the matter in detail to the legal arbitrators. They said: 'You have named the price, Prince, for the park. Accept the gold; the park belongs to the householder.' He fell silent. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, bringing abundant gold by carts, loads, bundles, baskets, camels, oxen, and donkeys, began to cover the entire <s>Jetavana</s>. It was not completed; there remained one tract of land uncovered. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, reflecting on this matter, stood silent for a moment: 'Which treasury will it be? Not too little, not too much — by which this uncovered tract of land will be covered, and yet [the treasury] will not need to be guarded.' Prince <s>Jeta</s> reflected: 'Surely the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> is having second thoughts: "Why, for the sake of a park, do I give up such a great mass of wealth?"' Knowing this, he said to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: 'If you are having second thoughts, householder, take back the gold. The park remains mine.' 'Prince, I am not having second thoughts. Rather, I stood silent for a moment reflecting on this very matter: "Which treasury will it be? Not too little, not too much, by which this uncovered tract of land will be covered, and yet will not need to be guarded."' Then Prince <s>Jeta</s> thought: 'The <s>Buddha</s> must not be

body.translated_text: an ordinary [being]; nor is the proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s> ordinary — since this householder, for the sake of a park, gives up such a great (

) mahāntaṃ dhanaskandhaṃ parityajati; iti viditvā anāthapiṇḍadaṃ gṛhapatim idam avocat: anuprayaccha me gṛhapate anāstīrṇaṃ pṛthivīpradeśam; atrāhaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya dvārakoṣṭhakaṃ māpayāmi; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir jetasya kumārasya anāstīrṇaṃ pṛthivīpradeśam anuprayacchati: yatra jetaḥ kumāro bhagavato 'rthāya dvārakoṣṭhakaṃ māpayati
body.translated_text: ) mass of wealth.' Knowing this, he said to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>: 'Give me, householder, the uncovered tract of land. There I shall have a gatehouse built for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> gave Prince <s>Jeta</s> the uncovered tract of land, where Prince <s>Jeta</s> had a gatehouse built for the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: Obstruction by the Tīrthyas
body.translated_text: Obstruction by the <s>Tīrthyas</s> (non-Buddhist sectarians)

body.text: athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir bhagavato 'rthāya vihāraṃ māpayitum ārabdha iti tīvradveṣaparyākulīkṛtamanasas tīrthyās te saṃbhūya yenānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatis tenopasaṅkrāntāḥ; upasaṅkramya kathayanti: mā tvaṃ gṛhapate śramaṇasya gautamasya arthāyātra vihāraṃ kāraya; kiṃ kāraṇam? asmābhir nagarāṇi bhājitāni; śramaṇasya gautamasya rājagṛham; asmākaṃ śrāvastī; sa kathayati: bhājitāni yuṣmābhir nagarāṇi, na tu madīyaṃ svāpateyam; yasyābhipretaṃ tasya dharmaskandhaṃ kārayāmīti; te rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatāḥ; tatrāpy anāthapiṇḍadena parājitāḥ; dhvāṅkṣās tīrthyā avikṛtavadanāḥ kathayanti: gṛhapate na te kāmakāram anuprayacchāmaḥ; śramaṇasya gautamasyāgraśrāvakaḥ āgataḥ; ca yady asmān vādena parājayate kāraya vihāram iti; sa kathayati: obnanam; āryaśāriputraṃ tāvad avalokayāmīti; athānāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir yenāyuṣmān śāriputraḥ tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramyāyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ; ekāntaniṣaṇṇo 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir āyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram idam avocat: tīrthyā bhadante śāriputra evam āhuḥ: gṛhapate na te kāmakāram anuprayacchāmaḥ; śramaṇasya gautamasya agraśrāvaka āgataḥ; sa yady asmān vādena parājayate, kāraya vihāram iti; katham atra pratipattavyam iti; āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ saṃlakṣayati: kim eṣāṃ santi kānicit kuśalamūlāni uta na santīti; paśyati, santi; kasyāntike pratibaddhāni; mamaiva; punaḥ saṃlakṣayati: kim etāvanta eva mama pratibaddhā vineyā āhosvid anye 'pi vādena vineyāḥ santīti; paśyati, santi; kiyaccireṇa sannipatiṣyanti; paśyati, saptāhasyātyayād iti; samanvāhṛtya kathayati: gṛhapate evaṃ bhavatu; kiṃ tu saptame divase; tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ prītiprāmodyajāto yena tīrthyās tena upasaṅkrāntah; upasaṅkramya (
body.translated_text: Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> began to have a monastery built for the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Tīrthyas</s>, their minds agitated by intense hatred, assembled and approached the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. Having approached, they said: 'Householder, do not have a monastery built here for the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. For what reason? We have divided the cities among ourselves: <s>Rājagṛha</s> belongs to the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>; <s>Śrāvastī</s> belongs to us.' He said: 'You have divided the cities among yourselves, but not my personal property. I shall have a <s>Dharma</s>-hall built for whomever I please.' They went to the king's presence. There too they were defeated by <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. The crow-like <s>Tīrthyas</s>, with unchanged faces, said: 'Householder, we do not grant you permission freely. The chief disciple of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has come. If he defeats us in debate, then build the monastery.' He said: 'Very well. Let me first consult with the noble <s>Śāriputra</s>.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> approached the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said to the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Tīrthyas</s> say thus: "Householder, we do not grant you permission freely. The chief disciple of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has come. If he defeats us in debate, then build the monastery." How should this be handled?' The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: 'Do these [<s>Tīrthyas</s>] have any roots of wholesome merit, or not?' He saw that they did. 'In whose charge are they bound?' 'In mine.' He further reflected: 'Are only these many bound to me as those to be guided, or are there others to be guided through debate as well?' He saw that there were. 'How long until they gather?' He saw: after seven days. Having reflected, he said: 'Householder, let it be so. But on the seventh day.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, filled with joy and delight, approached the <s>Tīrthyas</s>. Having approached, (

body.text: SBV I 174

) tīrthyān idam avocat: bhadanta āryaśāriputraḥ kathayati: śobhanam, evaṃ bhavatu; kiṃ tu spatame divase iti; te saṃlakṣayanti; dvābhyām atra kāraṇābhyāṃ bhavitavyam; athavāsau niṣpalāyitukāmaḥ; athavā pakṣaṃ samanveṣṭukāmaḥ; kim atra prāptakālaṃ; vayam api pakṣaṃ samanveṣāmaha iti; te pakṣaṃ samanveṣṭum ārabdhāḥ; taiḥ pakṣaṃ samanveṣamānai raktākṣo nāma parivrājako dṛṣṭaḥ; sa tair uktaḥ: tvam asmākaṃ sabrahmacārī; śramaṇasya gautamasyāgraśrāvako 'smābhir vādenāhūtaḥ;
body.translated_text: ) he said to the <s>Tīrthyas</s>: 'Venerable sirs, the noble <s>Śāriputra</s> says: "Very well, let it be so. But on the seventh day."' They reflected: 'There must be one of two reasons for this: either he wants to flee, or he wants to seek allies. What is the right thing to do? Let us too seek allies.' They began to seek allies. While seeking allies, they found a wandering ascetic named <s>Raktākṣa</s> (Red-Eye). They said to him: 'You are our fellow practitioner. The chief disciple of the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> has been challenged by us to a debate.

body.text: sa pakṣaṃ samanveṣate; tvam asmākaṃ sāhāyyaṃ kalpaya; kiyatā kālena? itaḥ saptame divase; śobhanam, evaṃ bhavatu; yadā yuṣmākaṃ sannipāto bhavati tadā mamārocayitavyam; tīrthyāḥ śaṅkitodvignamanaso divasānudivasaṃ pakṣaṃ samanveṣayante; divasāṃś ca gaṇayanti
body.translated_text: He is seeking allies. You, give us your support.' 'In how much time?' 'Seven days from now.' 'Very well, let it be so. When your assembly takes place, inform me.' The <s>Tīrthyas</s>, with minds anxious and agitated, day after day sought allies and counted the days.

children.translated_text: The <s>Tīrthyas</s> and <s>Śāriputra</s> contest

children.text: yāvat saptame divase anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā vistīrṇāvakāśe pṛthivīpradeśe āsanaprajñaptiḥ kāritā; āyuṣmataś ca śāriputrasyārthāya siṃhāsanaṃ prajñaptam; nānādeśanivāsinas tīrthyāḥ sannipatitāḥ; śrāvastīnivāsī janakāyaḥ anekāni ca tatsāmantanivāsīni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi, kānicir kutūhalajātāni, kānicit pūrvakaiḥ kuśalamūlaiḥ saṃcodyamānāni; tata āyuṣmān śāriputro 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā saparivāreṇa saṃpuraskṛto vādimaṇḍalaṃ praviśya vineyajanam abhisamīkṣya smitapūrvaṃ samaśānteryāpathena siṃhāsanam abhiruhya niṣaṇṇaḥ; sarvaiva sā parṣad avahitacetaskā āyuṣmantam śāriputram abhisamīkṣamāṇā niṣaṇṇā
children.translated_text: On the seventh day, the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> had seating arrangements prepared in a spacious, open place. A lion-throne was prepared for the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. Heretics dwelling in various regions assembled. The people dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s> [came], along with many hundreds of thousands of living beings from the neighboring regions — some driven by curiosity, some impelled by previous roots of merit. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, accompanied and honored by the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> with his retinue, entered the debating arena. Having surveyed those to be disciplined, with a smile and with calm, composed deportment, he ascended the lion-throne and sat down. That entire assembly sat with attentive minds, gazing at the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.

body.text: Defeat of the Tīrthyas
body.translated_text: Defeat of the <s>Tīrthyas</s> (heretics)

body.text: tata āyuṣmān śāriputras tīrthyān āmantrayāmāsa: bhavantaḥ kiṃ tāvat kariṣyatha? āhosivd vikariṣyatha? te kathayanti: vayaṃ kurmaḥ; tvāṃ vikuru; āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ saṃlakṣayati: yady ahaṃ kariṣyāmi; sadevako 'pi loko na śakṣyati vikartum; prāg eva raktākṣaḥ parivrājakaḥ; iti viditvā raktākṣaṃ parivrājakam idam avocat: tvaṃ kuru, ahaṃ vikariṣyāmīti; sa indrajāle kṛtāvī; tena supuṣpitaḥ (
body.translated_text: Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> addressed the heretics: 'Sirs, will you perform first, or will you counter?' They said: 'We shall perform; you counter.' The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: 'If I perform, even the whole world with its gods would not be able to counter it, let alone the red-eyed wanderer (<s>Raktākṣa parivrājaka</s>).' Knowing this, he said to <s>Raktākṣa</s> the wanderer: 'You perform; I shall counter.' He was skilled in magical illusion (<s>indrajāla</s>). He created a fully blossoming (

body.text: SBV I 175

) sahakārapādapo nirmitaḥ; āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa tumulo vātavarṣa utsṛṣṭaḥ; yenāsau samūla utpāṭya itaś cāmutaś ca vikīrṇo yogijanānām apy aviṣayībhūtaḥ; tatas tena padminī nirmitā; āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa kalabhahastī nirmitaḥ; tena sā samantān marditā; tena saptaśīrṣo nāgo nirmitaḥ; āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa garuḍo nirmitaḥ yenāsāv apahṛtaḥ; tena vetāḍo nirmitaḥ; āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa mantraiḥ kīlitaḥ; kuprayukto vetādā ātmavadhāya cetayate; sa tasyaivopari pradhāvitaḥ; tato 'sau bhītas trastaḥ saṃvigna āhṛṣṭaromakūpaḥ āyuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya pādayor nipatitaḥ: ārya śāriputra trāyasva śaraṇāgato 'smīti; tata āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa mantrā utkīlitāḥ; sa vetāḍo vyupaśāntaḥ; tasyāyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa dharmo deśitaḥ; sa prasādajātaḥ kathayati: labheyāham āryaśāriputra svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam; careyam aham āryaśāriputrasyāntike brahmacaryam iti; āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa sa pravrājitaḥ upasaṃpāditaḥ; avavādo dattaḥ; tenodyacchamena ghaṭamānena vyāyacchamānena sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣākṛtam; arhan saṃvṛttaḥ; traidhātukavītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo
body.translated_text: ) mango tree. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> released a violent storm of wind and rain, by which that tree was uprooted entirely and scattered here and there, disappearing even from the perception of yogic adepts. Then he created a lotus pond. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> created a baby elephant, which trampled it on all sides. Then he created a seven-headed serpent. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> created a <s>Garuḍa</s> bird, which carried it away. Then he created a <s>Vetāḍa</s> (zombie-spirit). The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> bound it with mantras. Wrongly directed, the <s>Vetāḍa</s> turned to destroy its own master and charged directly at him. Then he, frightened, terrified, alarmed, with hair standing on end, fell at the feet of the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, save me! I have come for refuge!' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> released the mantras, and the <s>Vetāḍa</s> was pacified. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. He, having generated faith, said: 'May I, Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, obtain ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>), full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), and monkhood (<s>bhikṣubhāva</s>) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>. I would practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) under Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>.' The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> ordained and fully ordained him. He gave him instruction. By striving, exerting, and making effort, through the abandonment of all defilements, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. He became an <s>Arhat</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding clods and gold equally, with a mind as equanimous as the sky and the palm of the hand, like sandalwood and an axe, with the shell of his egg split open by knowledge,

body.text: vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhaparāṅmukhaḥ, sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ; tataḥ sā parṣad vismayotphullalocanā saṃvṛttā; āyuṣmati śāriputre 'bhiprasannā kathayati: mahān āryaśāriputreṇa vādivṛṣabho nigṛhītaḥ; iti viditvā ayuṣmataḥ śāriputrasya mukhe 'valokikāḥ saṃvṛttāḥ; tata āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa tasyāḥ parṣadaḥ āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā; yāṃ śrutvā anekaiḥ satvasahasraiḥ mahān viśeṣa āgataḥ; kaiścic chrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni; kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bodhau; kaiśid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau; kaiścic charaṇagamanaśikṣāpadāni gṛhītāni; kaiścit srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam; kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam; kaiścid anāgāmiphalam; kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśasaṃprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam; yadbhūyasā sā parṣad buddhanimnā, dharmapravaṇā, saṅghaprāgbhārā, (
body.translated_text: having attained knowledge, supernatural powers, and analytical insight, turned away from becoming, gain, greed, and honor, worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>. Then that assembly, with eyes wide open in amazement, was filled with devotion toward the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, and said: 'The noble <s>Śāriputra</s> has subdued a great bull among debaters!' Knowing this, they turned their faces toward the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, having known the inclinations, latent tendencies, nature, and character of that assembly, gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> as penetrates the Four Noble Truths. Having heard it, many thousands of beings attained great distinction. Some generated the aspiration for the <s>Śrāvaka</s> awakening; some for the solitary (<s>Pratyeka</s>) awakening; some for the unsurpassed perfect awakening. Some took up the going for refuge and the training-precepts. Some directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpatti</s>); some the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmi</s>); some the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmi</s>); some, having gone forth, through the complete abandonment of all defilements, directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. For the most part, that assembly (

body.text: SBV I 176

) vyavasthāpitā; tīrthyāḥ saṃlakṣayanti: na śakyam asmābhir ayaṃ vāde nigrahītum; upāyasaṃvidhānaṃ kartavyam; atraiva bhṛtikayā karma kurmaḥ; tataś chidraṃ labdhvā baiṣkeṇainaṃ praghātayāma iti; te sarve saṃbhūya anāthapiṇḍadasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā kathayanti: gṛhapate tvayāsmākaṃ sarvāṇi vṛttipadāni samucchinnāni; tad anukampāṃ kuru; tvadīyavihāre bhṛtikayā karma kurmaḥ; ciraṃ vayam atra avasthitāḥ; mā deśaparityāgaṃ kurma iti; anāthapiṇḍadaḥ kathayati: āryaśāriputraṃ tāvad avalokayāmi; sa yenāyuṣmān śāriputras tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram idam avocat: <ārya>, tīrthyāḥ kathayanti, asmākaṃ tvayā sarvāṇi vṛttipadāni samucchinnāni; tad anukampāṃ kuru; tvadīye vihāre bhṛtikayā karma kurmaḥ; ciraṃ vayam atrāvasthitāḥ; mā deśaparityāgaṃ kurma iti; āyuṣmāṃś chāriputraḥ samanvāhartuṃ pravṛttaḥ: kiṃ teṣāṃ santi kānicit kuśalamūlāni āhosvin na santi iti; paśyati, santi; kasyāntike pratibaddhāni; mamaiveti; samanvāhṛtya kathayati: gṛhapate evaṃ bhavatu, ko 'tra virodha iti; te tasmin vihāre bhṛtikayā karma kartum ārabdhāḥ; āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa latāvārikaḥ puruṣo raudro nirmitaḥ; sa tat karma kārayitum ārabdhaḥ; āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ teṣāṃ vinayakālaṃ jñātvā tatsamīpe vṛkṣamūlasyādhastāc caṅkramyamāṇas tiṣṭhati; sa tair
dṛṣṭaḥ; te saṃlakṣayanti, ayam asya kāla praghātayituṃ pravivikte tiṣṭhatīti; te tasya sakāśaṃ upasaṅkramya parivārya avasthitāḥ; āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ saṃlakṣayati: kīdṛśena cittena ete matsakāśam upasaṅkrāntā iti; yāvat paśyati vadhakacittena; tenāsau latāvāriko nirmita utsṛṣṭaḥ; tena te 'bhidrutā gacchata karma kuruteti; te kathayanti: ārya śāriputra paritrāyasva; sa kathayati: āyuṣman gaccha; viśrāmyantu tāvad iti; te saṃlakṣayanti: īdṛśo 'sty ayaṃ mahātmā; vayam asya vadhakacittāḥ; eṣo 'smākaṃ maitracittaḥ iti viditvā abhiprasannāḥ; tata āyuṣmatā (
body.translated_text: ) was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, tending toward the <s>Dharma</s>, and leaning toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>. The heretics deliberated: 'We cannot defeat him in debate. A stratagem must be devised. Let us work right here for hire. Then, finding an opportunity, we shall kill him by poison.' They all assembled and went to the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> and said: 'Householder, you have cut off all our means of livelihood. Show compassion. Let us work for hire in your monastery. We have dwelt here a long time; let us not be forced to abandon the region.' <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said: 'Let me first consult Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>.' He approached the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and said: 'Noble Sir, the heretics say: "You have cut off all our means of livelihood. Show compassion. Let us work for hire in your monastery. We have dwelt here a long time; let us not be forced to abandon the region."' The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> began to investigate: 'Do they have any roots of merit or not?' He saw: 'They do.' 'With whom are they connected?' 'With me.' Having investigated, he said: 'Householder, let it be so. What conflict is there?' They began to work for hire in that monastery. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> created a fierce man as an overseer. That one began to supervise the work. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, knowing the right time for their conversion, stood nearby walking back and forth at the foot of a tree. They saw him. They deliberated: 'This is the time to kill him — he stands in a secluded spot.' They approached him and surrounded him. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> reflected: 'With what intention have they approached me?' He saw: with murderous intent. Then he released that created overseer. He charged at them: 'Go! Do your work!' They said: 'Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, save us!' He said: 'Sir, go! Let them rest for now.' They deliberated: 'Such is this great-souled one. We had murderous intent; yet he has loving-kindness toward us.' Knowing this, they were filled with devotion. Then the Venerable (

children.translated_text: Conversion of the <s>Tīrthyas</s>

children.text: te dṛṣṭasatyāḥ kathayanti: labhemahi vayaṃ śāriputra svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam; carema vayaṃ bhadantaśāriputrasyāntike brahmacaryam iti; te āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa pravrājitā upasaṃpāditāḥ; avavādo dattaḥ; tair yujyamānair, ghaṭamānair, vyāyacchamānair idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatīḥ śatanapatanavikiraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaparahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam ity arhantaḥ saṃvṛttāḥ; traidhātukavītarāgāḥ samaloṣṭakāñcanā ākāśapāṇitalasamacittā vāsīcandanakalpā vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośā vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāptā bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhāḥ sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyā mānyā abhivādyāś ca saṃvṛttāḥ
children.translated_text: Having seen the truth, they said: 'May we, <s>Śāriputra</s>, obtain ordination, full ordination, and monkhood in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>. We would practice the holy life under the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>.' They were ordained and fully ordained by the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>. He gave them instruction. By striving, exerting, and making effort, having known the wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> with its five defects to be unsteady and unstable, having struck down all the courses of conditioned existence by their nature of crumbling, falling, scattering, and destruction, through the complete abandonment of all defilements, they directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. They became <s>Arhats</s> — free from passion in the three realms, regarding clods and gold equally, with minds as equanimous as the sky and the palm of the hand, like sandalwood and an axe, with the shells of their eggs split open by knowledge, having attained knowledge, supernatural powers, and analytical insight, turned away from becoming, gain, greed, and honor, worthy of worship, respect, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.
Construction of <s>Vihāras</s> (monasteries)

children.text: tatra āyuṣmatā śariputreṇa vihārasūtram ekānte gṛhītam; anāthapiṇḍadenāpi gṛhapatinā ekānte gṛhītam; āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkartum ārabdhaḥ; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ kathayati: nāhetvapratyayam āryaśāriputra tathāgatā vā tathāgataśrāvakā vā smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti; kaḥ āryaśāriputra hetuḥ? kaḥ pratyayaḥ smitasya prāviṣkaraṇāya? evam etad gṛhapate, evam etat; nāhetvapratyayaṃ tathāgatā vā tathāgataśrāvakā vā smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti; tvayā ceha sūtraṃ gṛhītam; tuṣite devanikāye sauvarṇaṃ bhavanam abhinirvṛttam; tato 'nāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir vismayotphullalocanaḥ kathayati: āryaśāriputra yady evaṃ, tena hi punaḥ sūtraṃ prasāraya bhūyasyā mātrayā; cittam abhiprasādayāmīti; āyuṣmatā śāriputreṇa tat sūtram gṛhītam; anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā bhūyasyā mātrayā tīvreṇa prasādavagena cittam abhiprasāditam; yena prasādajātena samanantaram eva tat sauvarṇaṃ bhavanaṃ catūratnamayaṃ saṃvṛttam; āyuṣmatā cāsya śāriputreṇa niveditam; tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā uttarottarapravṛddhapuṇyasantatinā (

) ṣoḍaśamahallikā vihārā māpitāḥ; ṣaṣṭiś ca kuṭikāvastūni; ṣoḍaśamahallikān vihārān māpayitvā ṣaṣṭiṃ ca kuṭikāvastūni sarvopakaraṇaiḥ pūrayitvā yenāyuṣmān śāriputras tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramyāyuṣmantaṃ śāriputram idam avocat: kiyatpramāṇair āryaśāriputra prayāṇakair bhagavān adhvānaṃ gacchati; tadyathā gṛhapate rājā cakravartī; kiyatpramāṇai rājā cakravartī; daśakrośakair gṛhapate rājā cakravartī prayāṇakair adhvānaṃ gacchati; tato 'nāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā yāvac ca śrāvastī yāvac ca rājagṛham atrāntarād vāsakān parisaṅkhyāya parikramaṇakā māpitāḥ; dānaśalā kāritā; kālārocakaḥ puruṣaḥ sthāpitaḥ; chatradhvajapatākāśobhitāś candanavāripariṣiktāḥ surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibaddhās toraṇāḥ kāritāḥ; kālikāni yāmikāni ca bhaiṣajyāny upasthāpitāni
children.translated_text: ) had sixteen large monasteries (<s>mahallikā vihāra</s>) built, and sixty dwelling-sites (<s>kuṭikāvastu</s>). Having built the sixteen large monasteries and sixty dwelling-sites and having furnished them with all requisites, he approached the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and said: 'How many halting-places (<s>prayāṇaka</s>), Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, does the <s>Bhagavān</s> travel on a journey?' 'Like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), householder.' 'How many [halting-places] for a <s>Cakravartin</s>?' 'A <s>Cakravartin</s>, householder, travels the road with halting-places of ten <s>krośas</s>.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, having calculated the number of rest-stops between <s>Śrāvastī</s> and <s>Rājagṛha</s>, had rest-houses built. He had alms-halls constructed. He stationed a man to announce the time. He had gateways built, adorned with parasols, banners, and flags, sprinkled with sandalwood water, fitted with censers of fragrant incense. He had medicines prepared both seasonal and timely.

There the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> took a measuring cord to one side. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> also took a measuring cord to one side. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> began to smile. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> said: 'Not without cause and reason, Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, do <s>Tathāgatas</s> or disciples of <s>Tathāgatas</s> smile. What, Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the cause? What is the reason for the smile?' 'Just so, householder, just so. Not without cause and reason do <s>Tathāgatas</s> or disciples of <s>Tathāgatas</s> smile. You have taken the measuring cord here, and a golden mansion has been produced in the <s>Tuṣita</s> divine assembly.' Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, with eyes wide with wonder, said: 'Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, if that is so, then stretch the cord further! Let me generate even more faith!' The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> took that cord, and the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, with an even greater surge of faith, generated an even more intense faith. Through that faith thus generated, immediately that golden mansion became one made of four kinds of jewels. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> informed him of this. Then the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, with a continuum of merit ever increasing, (

Standing to one side, that man said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, Venerable Sir, bows his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>; as before, up to: and comfortable dwelling.' I shall serve the <s>Bhagavān</s> for as long as I live with robes, alms-food, lodgings, and medicines and provisions for the sick, together with the community of monks."'
