body.text: The Buddha arrives at Śrāvastī
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> arrives at <s>Śrāvastī</s>

body.text: tato bhagavān dānto dāntaparivāraḥ, śānto śāntaparivāraḥ, mukto muktaparivāraḥ, āśvasta āśvastaparivāraḥ, vinīto vinītaparivāraḥ, arhann arhatparivāraḥ, vītarāgo vītarāgaparivāraḥ, prāsādikaḥ prāsādikaparivāraḥ, ṛṣabha iva gogaṇaparivṛtaḥ, gaja iva kalabhaparivṛtaḥ, siṃha iva daṃṣṭrigaṇaparivṛtaḥ, haṃsa iva haṃsagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, suparṇīva pakṣigaṇaparivṛto, vipra iva śiṣyagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, suvaidya ivāturagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, śūra iva yodhagaṇaparivṛto, daiśika ivādhva gagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, sārthavāha iva vaṇiggaṇaparivṛtaḥ, śreṣṭhīva parijanaparivṛtaḥ, koṭṭarāja iva mantrigaṇaparivṛtaḥ, cakravartīva putrasahasraparivṛtaḥ, candra iva nakṣatragaṇaparivṛtaḥ, sūrya iva raśmisahasraparivṛtaḥ, dhṛtarāṣṭra iva gandharvagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, virūḍhaka iva kumbhāṇḍagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, virūpakṣa iva nāgagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, dhanada iva yakṣagaṇaparivātaḥ, vemacitrīva asuragaṇaparivṛtaḥ, śakra iva tridaśagaṇaparivṛtaḥ, brahmeva brahmakāyikaparivṛtaḥ, stimita iva jalanidhiḥ, sajala iva jaladharaḥ, vimada iva gajapatiḥ, sudāntair indriyair asaṃkṣobhiteryāpathapracāraḥ, dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtaḥ, aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraḥ, vyāmaprabhālaṅkṛtamūrtiḥ, sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ, jaṅgama iva ratnaparvataḥ, samantatobhadrako, daśabhir balaiś, caturbhir vaiśāradyais, tribhir āveṇikaiḥ smṛtyupasthānair mahākaruṇayā ca samanvāgataḥ, mahatā bhikṣusaṅghena, anāthapiṇḍadena gṛhapatinā śrāvastīnivāsinā ca mahājanakāyena, anekaiś ca devatāśatasahasrair anugamyamānaḥ,
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> — tamed, with a tamed retinue; peaceful, with a peaceful retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; reassured, with a reassured retinue; disciplined, with a disciplined retinue; an <s>Arhat</s>, with an <s>Arhat</s> retinue; free from passion, with a passion-free retinue; inspiring confidence, with a confidence-inspiring retinue; like a bull surrounded by a herd of cattle; like an elephant surrounded by young elephants; like a lion surrounded by a pack of fanged beasts; like a royal goose surrounded by a flock of geese; like a <s>Suparṇa</s> (Garuḍa) surrounded by a flock of birds; like a learned teacher surrounded by a group of students; like a skilled physician surrounded by a group of patients; like a hero surrounded by a band of warriors; like a guide surrounded by a group of travelers; like a caravan-leader surrounded by a group of merchants; like a guild-master surrounded by his dependents; like a fortress-king surrounded by a group of ministers; like a universal monarch surrounded by a thousand sons; like the moon surrounded by a host of stars; like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays; like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Gandharvas</s>; like <s>Virūḍhaka</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>; like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Nāgas</s>; like <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>) surrounded by a host of <s>Yakṣas</s>; like <s>Vemacitri</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Asuras</s>; like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by the host of the Thirty-three; like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by <s>Brahmakāyika</s> deities; like a calm ocean; like a water-laden cloud; like a maddened elephant-lord; with well-tamed senses, his conduct and deportment unagitated; adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>); his body resplendent with eighty secondary characteristics; his form adorned with a fathom-wide radiance; his brilliance surpassing a thousand suns; like a walking jeweled mountain, auspicious on all sides; endowed with the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>), the four confidences (<s>catuḥvaiśāradya</s>), the three special mindfulnesses (<s>trīṇi āveṇikāni smṛtyupasthānāni</s>), and great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>); accompanied by a great community of monks, by the householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s> and a great multitude of residents of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, and followed by many hundreds of thousands of deities

body.text: śrāvastīnagarīm anuprāptaḥ; yadā ca bhagavatā śrāvastīṃ nagarīṃ (
body.translated_text: , he arrived at the city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>. And when the <s>Bhagavān</s>, entering the city of <s>Śrāvastī</s> (

body.text: SBV I 180
body.translated_text: SBV I 180

body.text: ) praviśatā sābhisaṃskāraṃ nagarendrakīle dakṣiṇaḥ pādo nyastaḥ tadā ṣaḍvikāraḥ pṛthivīkampo jātaḥ; iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī calati, saṃcalati, saṃpracalati; vyathate, pravyathate, saṃpravyathate; pūrvo digbhāga unnamati; paścimo 'vanamati; paścima unnamati; pūrvo 'vanamati; dakṣina unnamati; uttaro 'vanamati; uttara unnamati; dakṣiṇo 'vanamati; anta unnamati; madhyo 'vanamati; madhya unnamati; anto 'vanamati; sarvaś cāyaṃ loka udāreṇa avabhāsena sphuṭaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ sārdhaṃ lokāntarikābhiḥ; antarīkṣe ca devadundubhayas tāditāḥ; gaganatalasthā devatā <bhagavata> upariṣṭād divyāny utpalāni kṣeptum ārabdhāḥ; padmāni, kumudāni, puṇḍarīkāṇy, agarucūrṇāni, tagarucūrṇāni, candanacūrṇāni, kuṅkumacūrṇāni, tamālapatrāni, divyāni ca māndārakāṇi puṣpāṇi <kṣipanti> cailavikṣepāṃś cākārṣuḥ
body.translated_text: ), intentionally placed his right foot on the city threshold, a great earthquake of six kinds occurred. This great earth trembles, shakes, and quakes violently; it shudders, heaves, and jolts. The eastern quarter rises and the western sinks; the western rises and the eastern sinks; the southern rises and the northern sinks; the northern rises and the southern sinks; the edges rise and the center sinks; the center rises and the edges sink. And this entire world was suffused with a magnificent radiance, including the inter-cosmic voids. In the sky, divine kettledrums were struck. The deities standing in the vault of the sky began to scatter divine blue lotuses (<s>utpala</s>) upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> from above — lotuses (<s>padma</s>), white water-lilies (<s>kumuda</s>), white lotuses (<s>puṇḍarīka</s>), powdered aloe (<s>agaru</s>), powdered <s>tagara</s>, powdered sandalwood, powdered saffron (<s>kuṅkuma</s>), and <s>tamālapatra</s>; and they cast divine <s>māndāraka</s> flowers and waved cloths.

children.translated_text: Effects felt following the <s>Buddha</s>'s arrival

children.text: bhagavataḥ purapraveśe imāny evaṃvidhāścaryāṇy abhūvan; aparāṇi ca; saṃkṣiptāni viśālībhavanti; nīcāny uccāni bhavanti; uccāni samāni bhavanti; hastinaḥ krauñcanti; aśvā heṣante; ṛṣabhā nardanti; gṛhagatāni vividhāni vāditrabhāṇḍāni svayam nadanti; andhāś cakṣuṃṣi pratilabhante; badhirāḥ śrotram; mūkāḥ pravyāharaṇasamarthā bhavanti; pariśiṣṭendriyavikalā indriyāṇi pratilabhante; madyamadākṣiptā vimadībhavanti; viṣapāyitā nirviṣībhavanti; anyonyavairiṇo maitrīṃ pratilabhante; gurviṇyaḥ svastinā prasūyante; bandhanabaddhā mucyante; adhanā dhanāni prailabhante; imāni cānyāni ca bhagavataḥ purapraveśe adbhutaśatasahasrāṇi prādurbhavanti
children.translated_text: At the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s entry into the city, these and other such wonders occurred: narrow things became spacious; low things became high; high things became level; elephants trumpeted; horses neighed; bulls bellowed; various musical instruments in the houses sounded of their own accord; the blind gained sight; the deaf gained hearing; the mute became able to speak; those with impaired faculties regained their faculties; those intoxicated by drink became sober; those who had drunk poison became free from poison; mutual enemies gained friendliness toward each other; pregnant women gave birth safely; those bound in prison were released; the poor obtained wealth. These and hundreds of thousands of other marvels appeared at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s entry into the city.

body.text: The Jetavana
body.translated_text: The <s>Jetavana</s>

body.text: tato bhagavān evaṃvidhena mahatā satkāreṇa śrāvastīṃ praviṣṭaḥ; praviśya purastād bhikṣusaṅghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatiḥ suhṛtsaṃbandhibāndhavajanaparivṛtaḥ sauvarṇaṃ (
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having entered <s>Śrāvastī</s> with such great honor, sat down on a prepared seat before the community of monks. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, surrounded by friends, relatives, and kinsmen, holding a golden (

body.text: SBV I 181
body.translated_text: SBV I 181

body.text: ) bhṛṅgāram ādāya vāridhārāṃ pātayitum ārabdhaḥ; sā na prapatati; anāthapiṇḍado gṛhapatir durmanāḥ saṃlakṣayati: mā mayā kānicit sāpakṣālāni karmāṇi kṛtāni syur iti; bhagavān āha: na tvayā gṛhapate kānicit sāpakṣālāṇi karmāṇi kṛtāni; api tv etasmin pradeśe sthitena tvayā pūrvakāṇāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānām ayam eva pradeśo niryātitaḥ; anyasmin pradeśe sthitvā <pātaya; tenānyasmin pradeśe sthitvā> pātitā; bhagavān pañcāṅgopetena svareṇa svayam eva jetavanam udghoṣayati; udghoṣyamāṇe jetavane jetaḥ kumāraḥ saṃlakṣayati: aho bata bhagavān mamāpi tatprathamato nāmodgrahaṇaṃ kuryād iti; bhagavatā jetasya kumārasya cetasā cittam ājñāya tatprathamato nāmodgrahanaṃ kṛtam: idaṃ bhikṣavo jetavanam anāthapiṇḍadadasyārāmaḥ; iti śrutvā jetaḥ kumāro 'tīva prasannaḥ mama bhagavatā tatprathamato nāmodgrahaṇaṃ kṛtam iti; tatprītiprāmodyajātena tad dravyajātaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya catūratnamayaṃ dvārakoṣṭhakaṃ kāritam; tathā saṅgītikārair api sthavirais sūtrānta upanibaddham:
body.translated_text: ) water-pitcher, began to pour a stream of water. But it did not fall. The householder <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>, disheartened, reflected: 'Perhaps I have committed some defiling <s>karmas</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'You have not committed any defiling <s>karmas</s>, householder. But standing in this spot, you have dedicated this very spot to the former Perfectly Awakened Ones. Pour it standing in another spot.' He then poured it standing in another spot. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, with his voice endowed with five qualities, himself proclaimed the <s>Jetavana</s>. As the <s>Jetavana</s> was being proclaimed, Prince <s>Jeta</s> reflected: 'Oh, if only the <s>Bhagavān</s> would mention my name first!' The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having read Prince <s>Jeta</s>'s mind with his own mind, mentioned his name first: 'This, monks, is the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.' Hearing this, Prince <s>Jeta</s> was exceedingly pleased: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has mentioned my name first!' Born of that joy and delight, he commissioned a gatehouse made of four kinds of jewels for the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s benefit. Likewise, the elders who compiled the canon included it in the <s>sūtrānta</s>:

body.text: bhagavān śrāvastyāṃ viharati jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme iti
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.'

children.translated_text: King <s>Prasenajit</s> meets the <s>Buddha</s>

children.text: aśrauṣīd rājā prasenajit kauśalaḥ śramaṇo gautamaḥ kauśaleṣu janapadeṣu cārikāṃ caran śrāvastīm anuprāptaḥ; śravastyāṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍadasyārāme; sa khalu bhagavān gautamo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddho 'smīty ātmānaṃ pratijānīta iti; śrutvā ca punar yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmukhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisārya ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ; ekāntaniṣaṇṇo rājā prasenajit kauśalo bhagavantam idam avocat: śrutaṃ me bho gautama bhavān gautamo 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddho 'smīty ātmānaṃ pratijānīta iti; ye te bho gautama evam āhuḥ kaccit te evaṃ vyākurvāṇā, no ca bhavantaṃ gautamam abhyācakṣate, nātisaranti; uktavādināś ca te bhavato gautamasya <dharmavādinaś ca dharmasya> cānudharmaṃ vyākurvanti? na ca teṣāṃ kaścid āgacchet parataḥ sahadharmeṇa vādānuvādaṃ garhāsthānīyo dharmaḥ; ye te mahārāja evam (

children.translated_text: SBV I 182

children.text: ) āhus tathyata evaṃ vyākurvāṇā no ca mām abhyācakṣate, nātisaranti; uktavādinaś ca te dharmavādinaś ca dharmasya cānudharmaṃ vyākurvanti; na ca teṣāṃ kaścid āgacchet parataḥ sahadharmeṇa vādānuvādaṃ garhāsthānīyo dharmaḥ; tat kasya hetor? aham asmi mahārāja anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ; kiṃ cāpi bhavān gautama evam āha; api tu nāhaṃ bhavato gautamasya śraddhādeyo gacchāmi; tat kasya hetor? ye tāvad ime, bho gautama, vṛddhavṛddhāḥ, śramaṇabrāhmaṇāḥ, tadyathā pūraṇaḥ kāśyapo, maskarī gośalīputraḥ, sañjayī vairaḍīputraḥ, ajitaḥ keśakambalaḥ, kakudaḥ kātyayano, nirgrantho jñātiputraḥ, te tāvan nānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhā sma ity ātmānaṃ pratijānate? kutaḥ punar bhavān gautamo dahraś ca jātyā, navakāś ca pravrajyayā?
children.translated_text: ) are correctly representing [me]; they do not misrepresent me, they do not go too far. They are speakers of the truth, speakers of the <s>Dharma</s>, and explain in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>. And no one would come from another side with a legitimate counter-argument in criticism of the doctrine. Why? Because I, Great King, have awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening.' 'Even though Venerable <s>Gautama</s> says this, yet I do not accept Venerable <s>Gautama</s> on trust. Why? These, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, are the very old and senior ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — namely, <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Maskarī Gośālīputra</s>, <s>Sañjayī Vairaḍīputra</s>, <s>Ajita Keśakambala</s>, <s>Kakuda Kātyāyana</s>, <s>Nirgrantha Jñātiputra</s> — even they do not declare of themselves: "We have awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening." How then Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, who is young in birth and junior in ordination?'

King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> heard: 'The ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, traveling on a journey through the <s>Kośala</s> territories, has arrived at <s>Śrāvastī</s>. He is dwelling at <s>Śrāvastī</s>, in the <s>Jetavana</s>, the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>. That <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Gautama</s> declares of himself: "I have awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>)."' Having heard, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, having exchanged face-to-face various pleasant and delightful conversation with the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, King <s>Prasenajit</s> of <s>Kośala</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I have heard, Venerable <s>Gautama</s>, that Venerable <s>Gautama</s> declares of himself: "I have awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening." Those who say this of Venerable <s>Gautama</s> — are they correctly representing [you]? Do they not misrepresent Venerable <s>Gautama</s>? Do they not go too far? Are they speaking in accordance with the <s>Dharma</s>? And would no one come from another side with a legitimate counter-argument in criticism of the doctrine?' 'Those, Great King, who say thus (

body.text: The four small ones
body.translated_text: The four small ones

children.text: bhagavān āha: catvāra ime mahārāja dahrā nāvamantavyāḥ; na paribhavitavyāḥ; katame catvāraḥ? kṣatriyo, mahārāja, dahro nāvamantavyaḥ, <dahro> na paribhavitavyaḥ; uraga, mahārāja, dahro nāvamantavyaḥ, dahro na paribhavitavyaḥ; agnir, mahārāja, stoko nāvamantavyaḥ, stoko na paribhavitavyaḥ; bhikṣur, mahārāja, dahro nāvamantavyaḥ, dahro na paribhavitavyaḥ; tat kasya hetor? dharaś cāpi bhikṣur bhavati arhan mahardhiko; mahānubhāvaḥ; idam avocat bhagavān; idam uktvā sugato by athāparam etad uvāca śāstā:
children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'There are, Great King, four small things that should not be scorned, not be despised. What four? A <s>Kṣatriya</s> prince, Great King, [though] young, should not be scorned, should not be despised. A serpent (<s>uraga</s>), Great King, [though] small, should not be scorned, should not be despised. A fire, Great King, [though] small, should not be scorned, should not be despised. A monk (<s>bhikṣu</s>), Great King, [though] young, should not be scorned, should not be despised. Why? Even a young monk may be an <s>Arhat</s>, of great supernatural power and great might.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said this. Having said this, the <s>Sugata</s>, the Teacher, further said:
A <s>Kṣatriya</s> endowed with [royal] marks, of noble birth and great fame — /

Having heard, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> sent a messenger. That one went forth right there [as a monk]. A second messenger was sent. He too went forth right there. Because the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> was so well-proclaimed, whichever messenger he sent would go forth right there. The king, resting his cheek on his hand, sat consumed with worry: 'Whichever messenger I send goes forth right there, because the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> is so well-proclaimed.'

body.translated_text: Instructions to <s>Udāyin</s>:

body.text: bhagavān āha: udāyin gaccha; na te sahasaiva rājakulaṃ praveṣṭavyam; dvāre sthitvā vaktavyam, śākyabhikṣur āgata iti; yadi kathayanti praviśeti, praveṣṭavyam; praviṣṭasya yadi kathayanti, santy anye 'pi śākyabhikṣava iti, vaktavyaṃ santīti; yadi kathayanti sarvārthasiddhasyāpi kumārasya evaṃvidha eva veṣa iti, vaktavyam evaṃvidha eveti; na ca te rājakule vastavyam; yadi kathayanti sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro rājakule vāsaṃ na kalpayatīti; vaktavyaḥ, na kalpayatīti; yadi pṛcchanti kutra vāsaṃ kalpayatīti, vaktavyam araṇye vihāre vā; yadi pṛcchanti ka evaṃvidho vihāra iti, jetavanākāreṇa likhitvā darśayitavyam; yadi pṛcchanti, āgamiṣyati sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāra iti, vaktavyam
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: '<s>Udāyin</s>, go. You should not enter the royal palace abruptly. Standing at the door, you should say: "A <s>Śākya</s> monk has arrived." If they say "Enter," you should enter. When you have entered, if they say "Are there other <s>Śākya</s> monks too?" you should say "There are." If they say "Does <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> the prince also have such an appearance?" you should say "He has such an appearance." And you should not stay in the royal palace. If they say "<s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> the prince does not arrange his dwelling in the royal palace" — you should say "He does not." If they ask "Where does he arrange his dwelling?" you should say "In the wilderness, or in a monastery (<s>vihāra</s>)." If they ask "What kind of monastery?" you should draw and show them one in the style of <s>Jetavana</s>. If they ask "Will <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> the prince come?" you should say

body.text: āgamiṣyati; kiyaccireṇa? saptāhasyātyayad iti
body.translated_text: "He will come." "How soon?" "After seven days."

'Did you not say, "I will return"? How is this?' <s>Udāyin</s> replied: 'Your Majesty, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said that <s>Buddha</s>-messengers should not be like this. As for me, because the <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s> is well-proclaimed, I have gone forth — I have gone forth through my own faith.' The king embraced him with all his limbs and seated him on a prepared seat. Water was strained for him; roots and fruits were prepared; he was fed with pure food. The Venerable <s>Udāyin</s>, endowed with supreme tranquility, self-restraint, and composure, ate according to the proper procedure of instruction. The king, observing him, was struck with wonder and said: 'Does the prince too have such tranquility?' <s>Udāyin</s> replied: 'Your Majesty, my tranquility is but a trifle. How so? Like [comparing] Mount <s>Sumeru</s> with a mustard seed, the ocean with a cow's hoof-print, the sun with a firefly, the sky with a hole.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said: '<s>Udāyin</s>, does prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> too have such an appearance?' 'Such indeed.' Hearing this, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> fainted and fell to the ground. His vital breath was restored by a great sprinkling of water. He said: '<s>Udāyin</s>, will prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> come?' <s>Udāyin</s> replied: 'He will come.' 'How soon?' 'After seven days.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> addressed the ministers: 'Sirs, clean the royal palace and the inner apartments. Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> will come.' <s>Udāyin</s> said: 'Your Majesty, the <s>Bhagavān</s> does not arrange his lodging in the inner palace.' The king said: 'Where does he arrange his lodging?' <s>Udāyin</s> replied: 'In a forest or in a monastery (<s>vihāra</s>).' The king said: 'What sort of monastery?' The Venerable <s>Udāyin</s> drew a sketch in the style of <s>Jetavana</s> and showed it to him. Then the king addressed the ministers: 'Sirs, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park, build sixteen large monasteries in the style of <s>Jetavana</s>, and sixty hut-sites.' 'Yes, Your Majesty,' the ministers assented to the king and built sixteen large monasteries in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park in the style of <s>Jetavana</s>, and sixty hut-sites.

Whichever of you is eager to witness the reunion of father and son, let him take up his robes.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> — tamed, with a tamed retinue; peaceful, with a peaceful retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; assured, with an assured retinue; disciplined, with a disciplined retinue; an <s>Arhat</s>, with an <s>Arhat</s>-retinue; free from passion, with a retinue free from passion; inspiring confidence, with a retinue inspiring confidence — like a bull surrounded by a herd of cattle, like an elephant surrounded by young elephants, like a lion surrounded by a host of fanged beasts, like a royal goose surrounded by a flock of geese, like a <s>Suparṇī</s> (great eagle) surrounded by a host of birds, like a learned <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> surrounded by a host of students, like a good physician surrounded by a host of patients, like a hero surrounded by a host of warriors, like a guide surrounded by a company of travelers, like a caravan-leader surrounded by a company of merchants, like a guild-master surrounded by his entourage, like a fortress-king surrounded by a host of counselors, like a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch) surrounded by a thousand sons, like the moon surrounded by a host of stars, like the sun surrounded by a thousand rays, like <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Gandharvas</s>, like <s>Virūḍhaka</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, like <s>Virūpākṣa</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Nāgas</s>, like <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) surrounded by a host of <s>Yakṣas</s>, like <s>Vemacitrin</s> surrounded by a host of <s>Asuras</s>, like <s>Śakra</s> surrounded by the host of the Thirty-three gods, like <s>Brahmā</s> surrounded by the <s>Brahmakāyikas</s>, calm like the ocean, like a water-bearing cloud, like a lordly elephant free from intoxication, with well-tamed senses, with unperturbed deportment, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body radiant with the eighty minor characteristics, his form adorned with the radiance of a fathom, his splendor surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious in every way, endowed with the ten powers, four fearlessnesses, three special mindfulness-applications, and great compassion — together with a great community of monks, arrived at the river <s>Rohakā</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> heard that prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> had arrived at the river <s>Rohakā</s>. Having heard, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> prepared — cleared of stones, gravel, and rubbish, sprinkled with sandalwood water, adorned with various censers of fragrant incense, hung with garlands and silk-banner clusters. From the river <s>Rohakā</s> all the way to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park, a magnificent road-decoration was arranged. In a broad, open area of ground, various seat-arrangements were prepared. There, at the river <s>Rohakā</s>, some monks were washing their hands; some were discarding their tooth-sticks; some were bathing. The <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s> heard: 'Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> has arrived.' Having heard, they all went out to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park. Some were urged by their previous roots of merit; some were curious, thinking: 'We shall see whether the father bows at the feet of the son, or the son at the father's.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'If I enter <s>Kapilavastu</s> on foot, the proud <s>Śākyas</s> will be displeased [thinking]: "Much has prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> accomplished by going to the austerity-grove! He who, followed by hundreds of thousands of deities, went forth above through the sky, and after all this time, having practiced hundreds of thousands of austerities and attained the deathless, now enters on foot!"'

There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Go, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, announce to the monks: the <s>Bhagavān</s> has set out for <s>Kapilavastu</s>. body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) that, with concentrated mind, rising up into the sky in the eastern direction, he displayed the four modes of deportment: walking, standing, sitting, and reclining. He also entered the element of radiance (<s>tejodhātu</s>). As the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s> entered the element of radiance, various rays issued from his body — blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored. He also displayed the twin miracle (<s>yamaka prātihārya</s>): the lower part of his body blazed with fire while cool streams of water flowed from the upper part; the upper part blazed with fire while cool streams of water flowed from the lower part. how does fear not enter you, O Wise One?' //
King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said:
The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied:
'O <s>Gautama</s>, the root of all fear —
those defilements with their latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>) have been abandoned by me. //

children.text:
so 'haṃ viśoko hy abhayaṃ vasāmi
  na me bhayaṃ svalpam apīha kiṃcit //
children.translated_text:
I dwell free from grief, in fearlessness;
not even the slightest fear is mine here.' //
'Formerly you always bathed in a beautiful bathhouse,
with the finest and most distinguished bathing [unguents].
Now that you are alone, devoted to forest-dwelling,
who bathes you today, O lord of sages?' //
King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said:
'The <s>Dharma</s> is the lake, O <s>Gautama</s>, moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) is the bathing-ford,
clear, praised even by the good.
Having bathed therein, people endowed with knowledge
cross to the far shore with bodies unwetted.' //
The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied: (
'Having bathed with golden and silver pitchers
in your own home, O hero,
how do you now bathe in waters
that are heated and turbid?' //
King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said:
'Pure is the river, O <s>Gautama</s>, with a sacred ford of merit,
clear, praised even by the good.
Having bathed therein, people endowed with knowledge
cross to the far shore with bodies unwetted.' //
The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied:
King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said:
'Your body anointed with yellow sandalwood, wrapped in the finest <s>Kāśī</s> cloth,

children.text: śobhase tvaṃ purā vīra tair viyukto na śobhase //
children.translated_text: you shone formerly, O hero. Deprived of those, you do not shine.' //
The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied:

children.text: śīlam ābharaṇaṃ hy agryaṃ śīlam ivānulepanam /
children.translated_text: 'Moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>) is the supreme ornament; moral conduct is the ointment.
What need have I of gold, jewels, and earrings that cause intoxication?' //
King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said:

children.text: kutaḥ paribhavo jātaḥ kutaś ca bhavabhīrutā /
children.translated_text: 'Whence has this sense of humiliation arisen? Whence this fear of existence?

children.text: nirvedo vā yato jātaḥ pṛṣṭa ācakṣva tan mama //
children.translated_text: Whence has this disenchantment arisen? When asked, tell me this.' //
The <s>Bhagavān</s> replied:

children.text: yataḥ paribhavo mahyaṃ yataś ca bhavabhīratā /
children.translated_text: 'That from which humiliation arose in me, and that from which fear of existence arose,

children.text: nirvedo vā yato jātaḥ śṛṇu tvaṃ kathayāmi te //
children.translated_text: and that from which disenchantment arose — listen, I shall tell you. //

children.text: jarā vyādhiś ca mṛtyuś ca yadi na syād idaṃ trayam /
children.translated_text: Old age, sickness, and death — if these three did not exist,
I too would delight in the most pleasing sensory pleasures.' //
'Excellent, O hero! You are well-born, the delight of the <s>Śākya</s> clan.

children.text: aṣṭābhir lokadarmais tvaṃ yad evaṃ nopalipyase //
children.translated_text: By the eight worldly conditions (<s>lokadharmāḥ</s>) you are indeed undefiled.' //
King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said: (
Then, joyful, his faith blossoming,
having circumambulated the <s>Saṅgha</s> and the Sage,
having bowed his head at the feet of the lord of sages,
he stood gazing at the <s>Sugata</s> from all sides. //

children.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya etad abhavat: lābhā me sulabdhā yasya me putreṇa evaṃvidhā guṇagaṇā adhigatāḥ
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thought: 'It is a gain for me, well-gained, that my son has attained such a host of virtues.'

body.text: Conversion of the Śākyas
body.translated_text: Conversion of the <s>Śākyas</s>

body.text: tato bhagavatā nyagrodhārāme tasyāḥ parṣadaḥ āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca ñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā śuddhodanapramukhaiḥ saptasaptatyā śākyasahasraiḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ sthāpayitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ; devadattaḥ pāpeccho manābhimānī; tena satyadarśanaṃ na kṛtam; sa krodhaparyavasthitaḥ kathayati: yanv aham apīdṛśīm anvāvartanīṃ māyāṃ jānīyām; aham api sarvaṃ lokam anvāvartayeyam iti; sa kṛtapraṇayasaumukhyaiḥ śākyair abhihitaḥ, alaṃ devadatta mā maivaṃ vocaḥ; mahardhiko bhagavān mahānubhāva iti; sa tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ; brahmāvarte udyāne tathāvidho dharmo deśitaḥ yaṃ śrutvā droṇodanapramukhaiḥ ṣaṭsaptatyā śākyasahasraiḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ sthāpayitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ; devadattas tathaiva paribhāṣate; rohītake udyāne tathāvidho dharmo deśito yaṃ śrutvā amṛtodanapramukhaiḥ pañcasaptatyā śākyasahasraiḥ srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ sthāpayitvā rājānaṃ śuddhodanaṃ; devadattas tathaiva paribhāṣate; avaśiṣṭāyāḥ parṣadaḥ kaiścic chrāvakabodhau cittāny utpāditāni; kaiścit pratyekāyāṃ bokhau, kaiścid anuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau; kaiścit srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam; kaiścit sakṛdāgāmiphalam; kaiścid anāgāmiphalam; kaiścit pravrajya sarvakleśaprahāṇād (
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, at the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park, having known the dispositions, latent tendencies, temperaments, and natures of that assembly, gave such a teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> that upon hearing it, seventy-seven thousand <s>Śākyas</s> headed by <s>Śuddhodana</s> directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotaāpattiphala</s>) — except for King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. <s>Devadatta</s>, of evil desires and filled with arrogance, did not gain the vision of truth. Overcome by anger, he said: 'If only I too could learn such mesmerizing magic! I too would make the entire world turn after me.' The <s>Śākyas</s>, who had become well-disposed and kindly, said to him: 'Enough, <s>Devadatta</s>! Do not speak thus. The <s>Bhagavān</s> is of great supernatural power, of great majesty.' He fell silent. At the <s>Brahmāvarta</s> garden, a similar teaching was given, hearing which seventy-six thousand <s>Śākyas</s> headed by <s>Droṇodana</s> directly realized the fruit of stream-entry — except for King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. <s>Devadatta</s> spoke disparagingly in the same manner. At the <s>Rohītaka</s> garden, a similar teaching was given, hearing which seventy-five thousand <s>Śākyas</s> headed by <s>Amṛtodana</s> directly realized the fruit of stream-entry — except for King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. <s>Devadatta</s> spoke disparagingly in the same manner. As for the remaining assembly — some generated the aspiration for the awakening of a disciple (<s>śrāvaka</s>); some for solitary awakening (<s>pratyekabodhi</s>); some for the unsurpassed perfect awakening; some directly realized the fruit of stream-entry; some the fruit of once-returning (<s>sakṛdāgāmin</s>); some the fruit of non-returning (<s>anāgāmin</s>); some, having gone forth and abandoned all defilements, (

body.text: SBV I 195
) arhatvaṃ
body.translated_text: ) directly realized <s>arhatship</s>.

body.text: sākṣātkṛtam; kecid buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gatāḥ; kecid dharmam; kecit saṅgham; yadbhūyasā sā pariṣad buddhanimnā dharmapravaṇā saṅghaprāgbhārā vyavasthāpitā
body.translated_text: Some went to the <s>Buddha</s> for refuge; some to the <s>Dharma</s>; some to the <s>Saṅgha</s>. For the most part, that assembly was established as inclined toward the <s>Buddha</s>, flowing toward the <s>Dharma</s>, leaning toward the <s>Saṅgha</s>.

body.text: The pride of Śuddhodana
body.translated_text: The pride of <s>Śuddhodana</s>

body.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya etad abhavat; pūrvaṃ bhagavān sasurāsurasya jagataḥ pūjyaś cābhūn mānyaś cābhūd abhivādyaś ca; idānīṃ manuṣyapūjito na devapūjita iti; athānyatamaḥ śākyakumāro gāthāṃ bhāṣate:

children.translated_text: 'This multitude has been satisfied, O great sage,
by the rain of the true <s>Dharma</s>, O best of speakers.
Lifted from the dreadful path of downfall,
this world is now set upon the path of liberation.' //

children.text:
rājā śuddhodanaḥ atiharṣāt satyāni na paśyati, mamaiva ekasya putra evaṃmahardhiko mahānubhāva iti; bhagavān saṃlakṣayati: kiṃ kāraṇaṃ rājā śuddhodanaḥ satyāni na paśyati; tasyaitad abhavat; atiharṣeṇa mamaivaikasya putra evaṃmahardhika evaṃmahānubhāva iti; sarvathā madāpanayo 'sya kartavya iti; dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ satyāni na dṛśyante atilīnatayā audbilyena ca; tad asya līnaṃ cittam audbilyaṃ ca; yanv aham asya līnāṃ santatim apanayeyam audbilyaṃ ceti; tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate: samanvāhara maudgalyāyana rājānaṃ śuddhodanam; evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yena rājā śuddhodanas tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; adrākṣīd rājā śuddhodanaḥ āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam dūrād eva; dṛṣṭvā ca punar āyuṣmantam mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat: etu bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana, svāgataṃ bhavate mahāmaudgalyāyanāya; niṣīdatu bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ prajñapta evāsane; niṣaṇṇaḥ āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ prajñapta evāsane
  athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte sve āsane 'ntarhitaḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśy upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya caturvidham īryāpathaṃ kalpayati; tadyathā cāṅkramyate, tiṣṭhati, niṣīdati, śayyāṃ kalpayati; tejodhātum api samāpadyate; (
children.translated_text:
King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, due to excessive joy, did not see the truths, [thinking:] 'Only my son alone is of such great supernatural power and majesty.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'For what reason does King <s>Śuddhodana</s> not see the truths?' He thought: 'Due to excessive joy — "Only my son alone is of such great supernatural power and majesty." His pride must be removed by all means.' The truths are not seen for two reasons: excessive depression and excessive elation. His mind is depressed and elated. 'Let me remove his depressed mental stream and his elation.' There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Attend to King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> saw the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> from afar. Having seen, he said to the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Come, Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>! Welcome to the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>! Let the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> sit on the seat that has been prepared.' The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> sat on the seat that had been prepared.
Then the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> that, with his mind concentrated, he vanished from his own seat. In the eastern direction, rising up into the sky, he displayed the four modes of deportment — walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. He also entered the fire-element concentration (<s>tejodhātu samāpatti</s>). (

children.text: ) tejodhātusamāpannasya āyuṣmato mahāmaudgalyāyanasya vividhāny arcīṃṣi kāyān niścaranti; tadyathā nīlāni pītāni lohitāny avadātāni māñjiṣṭhāni sphaṭikavarṇāni; yamakāny api prātihāryāṇi vidarśayati; adhaḥ kāyaḥ prajvalati; uparimāt kāyāc chītalā vāridhārā syandante; uparimaḥ kāyaḥ prajvalati; adhaḥkāyāc chītalā vāridhārā syandante; yathā pūrvasyāṃ diśy evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ paścimāyām uttarasyāṃ diśīti caturdiśaṃ caturvidham ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśya tān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān pratiprasrabhya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ
children.translated_text: ) When the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> had entered the fire-element, various rays issued from his body — blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored. He also displayed the twin miracle (<s>yamaka prātihārya</s>): his lower body blazed while from his upper body cool streams of water flowed; his upper body blazed while from his lower body cool streams of water flowed. Just as in the eastern direction, so in the southern, western, and northern directions — he displayed the fourfold supernatural feat in all four directions. Having displayed these, he ceased those supernatural creations and sat on the seat that had been prepared.

children.text: atha rājā śuddhodanaḥ āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam idam avocat: santi mahāmaudgalyāyana anye 'pi bhagavataḥ śrāvakā evaṃmahardhikā evaṃmahānubhāvā iti; santi mahārāja; gāthāṃ ca bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said to the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Are there, <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, other disciples of the <s>Bhagavān</s> of such great supernatural power and majesty?' 'There are, Great King.' And he spoke this verse:
'Of great majesty, possessing the three knowledges, skilled in reading others' minds,
with defilements destroyed, likewise <s>Arhats</s> — many are the disciples of the Sage.' //

body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thought: 'Formerly the <s>Bhagavān</s> was worshipped, honored, and saluted by the world including the gods and <s>Asuras</s>. But now he is worshipped only by humans, not by gods.' Then a certain <s>Śākya</s> prince spoke this verse:

body.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya etad abhavat: na khalu mamaiva ekasya putra evaṃmahardhika evaṃmahānubhāvaḥ; api tu santy anye 'pi pravrajitā evaṃmahardhikā
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thought: 'It is not the case that my son alone is of such great supernatural power and majesty. Rather, there are other renunciants too of such great supernatural power

body.text: evaṃmahānubhāvā iti; tasya yad audbilyam abhūt tat prativigatam; atrāntare bhagavatā laukikaṃ cittam utpāditam: aho bata śakrabrahmādayo devā āgaccheyuḥ; śuddhāyāṃ devaparṣadi dharmaṃ deśayeyam iti; dharmatā khalu yasmin samaye buddhā bhagavanto laukikaṃ cittam utpādayanti tadā kuntapipīlakā api prāṇinas tasmin samaye bhagavataś cetasā cittam ājānanti; prāg eva śakrabrahmādayo devāḥ; yasmiṃs tu samaye lokottaraṃ cittam utpādayanti tasmin samaye mahāśrāvakā api bhagavataś cetasā cittaṃ nājānanti; kaḥ punar vādaḥ śakrabrahmādayo devāḥ; kuta eva kuntapipīlikā api prāṇinaḥ
body.translated_text: of such great supernatural power!' His distress was dispelled. Meanwhile, the <s>Bhagavān</s> had generated a worldly thought: 'Oh, if only <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods would come! I would teach the <s>Dharma</s> in a pure divine assembly.' It is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that whenever <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> generate a worldly thought, at that time even the tiniest ant-like creatures know the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s mind with their minds, to say nothing of <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods. But whenever they generate a supramundane thought, at that time even the great disciples cannot know the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s mind with their minds, let alone <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the other gods — and how much less the tiniest ant-like creatures!

body.text: The Buddha teaches to the Gods
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> teaches to the gods

body.text: atha śakrasya devendrasya etad abhavat: kimarthaṃ thagavatā laukikaṃ cittam utpāditam iti; tasyaitad abhavat: śuddhāyāṃ devaparṣadi dharmaṃ deśayitukāma iti; tena viśvakarmaṇo devaputrasya ājñā dattā; nirmiṇu viśvakarman nayagrodhārāme catūratnamayaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ, vicitrāṃ cāsanaprajñaptim; bhagavān śuddhāyaṃ devaparṣadi dharmaṃ deśayitukāma iti; paraṃ bhadraṃ bata kauśika iti; viśvakarmā devaputraḥ śakrasya devendrasya pratiśrutya nyagrodhārāme catūratnamayaṃ kūṭāgāraṃ nirmiṇoti, vicitrāṃ cāsanaprajñaptim; tatra catvāro mahārājāś caturṣu dvāreṣv avasthitāḥ, dhṛtarāṣṭro, virūḍhakaḥ, virūpākṣaḥ, kuberaś ca; pūrvasmin dvāre dhṛtarāṣṭra (
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, thought: 'For what purpose has the <s>Bhagavān</s> generated a worldly thought?' He realized: 'He wishes to teach the <s>Dharma</s> in a pure divine assembly.' He gave the command to the divine son <s>Viśvakarman</s>: 'Create, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s>, a pavilion made of four kinds of jewels, and arrange a variety of seats. The <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to teach the <s>Dharma</s> in a pure divine assembly.' 'Very well, <s>Kauśika</s>!' The divine son <s>Viśvakarman</s>, having assented to <s>Śakra</s> lord of the gods, created in the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s> a pavilion made of four kinds of jewels and arranged a variety of seats. The Four Great Kings were stationed at the four gates — <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, and <s>Kubera</s>. At the eastern gate, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, (

body.text: SBV I 197

) aṅgadakuṇḍalavicitramālyābharaṇavibhūṣitaḥ, dakṣiṇe virūḍhako divyālaṅkāravibhūṣitaḥ, paścime ca virūpākṣo nānāratnavibhūṣitaḥ, uttare kuberaḥ sarvālaṅkāravibhūṣitaḥ; tataḥ śakro devendro nyagrodhārāme mahatīṃ vibhūtiṃ kārayitvā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya bhagavata etam arthaṃ vistareṇārocayati; tato bhagavān śakrādibhir anekair devatāśatasahasraiṛ parivṛtaḥ kūṭāgāraṃ praviśya mahatyā devaparṣadaḥ purastān nānāratnavibhūṣite siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; atha āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano rājānaṃ śuddhodanam ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramyāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ praviṣṭaḥ; rājā śuddhodano dhṛtarāṣṭreṇa devarājena nivāritaḥ, tiṣṭha <tiṣṭha> mahārāja mā pravikṣaḥ; kiṃ kāraṇam? bhagavān śuddhāyāṃ devaparṣadi dharmaṃ deśayati; nātra mānuṣamātrasya praveśo 'stīti; atha rājā śuddhodanaḥ dakṣiṇaṃ dvāraṃ gataḥ; virūḍhakena devarājena dṛṣṭvābhihitaḥ: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha mahārāja mā pravikṣaḥ; rājā śuddhodanaḥ kathayati: kas tvaṃ bhadramukha; aham asmi mahārāja virūḍhakaḥ; bhagavān śuddhāyāṃ devaparṣadi dharmaṃ deśayati; nātra manuṣyapraveśo 'stīti; atha rājā śuddhodanaḥ paścimaṃ dvāraṃ gataḥ; virūpākṣeṇa devarājena dṛṣṭvābhihitaḥ: tiṣṭha tiṣṭha mahārāja, mā pravikṣaḥ; rājā śuddhodanaḥ kathayati, kas tvaṃ bhadramukha; virūpākṣaḥ kathayati; aham asmi mahārāja virūpākṣaḥ; bhagavān śuddhāyāṃ devaparṣadi dharmaṃ deśayati; yatra manuṣyabhūtasya na praveśo labhyate; atha rājā śuddhodana uttaraṃ dvāraṃ gataḥ; vaiśravaṇena mahārājena dṛṣṭvā abhihitaḥ, tiṣṭha tiṣṭha mahārāja mā pravikṣaḥ; rājā śuddhodanaḥ kathayati, kas tvaṃ bhadramukha;
body.translated_text: ) adorned with armlets, earrings, garlands, and various ornaments; at the southern, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>, adorned with divine ornaments; at the western, <s>Virūpākṣa</s>, adorned with various jewels; at the northern, <s>Kubera</s>, adorned with all ornaments. Then <s>Śakra</s> lord of the gods, having arranged great magnificence in the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and reported the matter in detail. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by <s>Śakra</s> and others and many hundreds of thousands of deities, entered the pavilion and sat upon a lion-throne adorned with various jewels, before the great divine assembly. Then the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, bringing King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> entered. But King <s>Śuddhodana</s> was stopped by <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> the divine king: 'Stop, stop, Great King! Do not enter.' 'For what reason?' 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> is teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in a pure divine assembly. There is no entry here for a mere human.' Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> went to the southern gate. The divine king <s>Virūḍhaka</s> saw him and said: 'Stop, stop, Great King! Do not enter.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said: 'Who are you, good sir?' 'I am, Great King, <s>Virūḍhaka</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> is teaching the <s>Dharma</s> in a pure divine assembly. There is no entry here for humans.' Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> went to the western gate. The divine king <s>Virūpākṣa</s> saw him and said: 'Stop, stop, Great King! Do not enter.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> said: 'Who are you, good sir?'

body.text: The Buddha teaches to Śuddhodana
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> teaches <s>Śuddhodana</s>

children.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśīṃ caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikīṃ dharmadeśanāṃ kṛtavān, yāṃ śrutvā rājñā śuddhodanena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣāktkṛtam; sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtam; na pitrā, na rājñā, na devatābhiḥ, na pūrvapretaiḥ, na śramaṇabrāhmaṇaiḥ, nānyena svajanabandhuvargeṇa, yad bhagavatā asmākaṃ kṛtam; ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ; laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ; pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi; vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi; pratiṣṭhāpitā devamanuṣyeṣu; āha ca:
children.translated_text: Then, having known King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s inclinations, latent tendencies, nature, and character, the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> as penetrates the Four Noble Truths. Having heard it, King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, having shattered the mountain of the view of self-identity (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) with its twenty peaks by the diamond of knowledge, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truth, he uttered a joyful exclamation (<s>udāna</s>) three times: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother; not by our father; not by a king; not by the gods; not by deceased ancestors; not by ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; not by any other relative or kinsman — what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us! The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up; the mountains of bones have been crossed over; the doors to the lower realms have been shut; the doors to heaven and liberation have been opened; we have been established among gods and humans.' And he spoke [verses]:
What should be done by a good son who repays his debt to his father — /

children.text: tat tvayā kṛtam asmākaṃ cittaṃ mokṣaparāyaṇam //
children.translated_text: that you have done for us: our minds are set on liberation. //

children.text: durgatibhyaḥ samuddṛtya svarge mokṣe ca te vayam /
children.translated_text: Having rescued us from the evil destinies and by your good effort, /

children.text: sthāpitā suprayatnena sādhu te duṣkaraṃ kṛtam //
children.translated_text: established us in heaven and liberation — well done! You have accomplished a difficult deed. //

children.translated_text: Like merchants through greed, through the lure of heaven, /
you have attracted us, O Protector, through affection — we who desired the pleasures of existence. //

body.text: atha rājā śuddhodanaḥ utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena, sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghena; adhivāsayati bhagavān rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvena; atha rājā śuddhodano bhagavatas tūṣṇīṃbhāvena adhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrānto yena śuklodanas tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya śuklodanam idam avocat: kumāra rājyābhiṣekas te prāptaḥ; pratīccha rājyam; kasyārthe? yato bhagavataḥ sakāśāt satyāni dṛṣṭāni; katarasmin divase? adyaiva; (
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, rising from his seat, arranging his upper garment over one shoulder, joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to a meal tomorrow in my inner palace, together with the community of monks.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> consented to King <s>Śuddhodana</s> by his silence. Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, knowing the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through his silence, bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. He approached <s>Śuklodana</s> and said: 'Prince, the royal consecration has come to you. Accept the kingdom.' 'On whose behalf?' 'Because I have seen the truths from the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'On which day?' 'This very day. (

body.text: SBV I 199

) mayā yam eva divasaṃ bhagavatā nyagrodhārāme dharmo deśitas tam eva divasaṃ saptasaptatyā śākyasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ satyāni dṛṣṭānīti; evaṃ droṇodano rājyaṃ pratīcchety uktaḥ; sa kathayati: yadā bhagavatā brahmāvarte udyāne dharmo deśitas tadā ṣaṭsaptatyā śākyasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ satyāni dṛṣṭānīti; evam amṛtodano rājyaṃ pratīcchety uktaḥ sa kathayati, mayāpi yadā bhagavatā rohītake udyāne dharmo deśitas tadā pañcasaptatyā śākyasahasraiḥ sārdhaṃ satyāni dṛṣṭāni; yady evam idānīṃ kaṃ rājye pratiṣṭhāpayāmaḥ;
body.translated_text: ) On the very day when the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s>, on that very day seventy-seven thousand <s>Śākyas</s> together with me saw the truths.' Likewise, <s>Droṇodana</s> was told: 'Accept the kingdom.' He said: 'When the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>Brahmāvarta</s> garden, at that time seventy-six thousand <s>Śākyas</s> together with me saw the truths.' Likewise, <s>Amṛtodana</s> was told: 'Accept the kingdom.' He said: 'I too, when the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>Rohītaka</s> garden, at that time seventy-five thousand <s>Śākyas</s> together with me saw the truths.' 'If so, whom shall we now establish on the throne?'

body.text: te kathayanti; bhadrikaṃ śākyarājam iti; taiḥ saṃbhūya bhadrikaḥ śākyarājo rājyaiśvaryādhipatye abhiṣiktaḥ
body.translated_text: They said: '<s>Bhadrika</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> prince.' Then, having assembled, they anointed <s>Bhadrika</s> the <s>Śākya</s> prince in the sovereign royal authority.

children.translated_text: Dedication of <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s>

children.text: atha rājā śuddhodanas tām eva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kalyam evotthāya āsanakāni prajñāpya udakamaṇīn pratiṣṭhāpya bhagavato dūtena kālam ārocayati: samayo bhadanta; sajjaṃ bhaktam; yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate iti; atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṅghapuraskṛto yena rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya bhaktābhisāras tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya purastād bhikṣusaṅghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; atha rājā śuddhodanaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṅghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpayati, saṃpravārayati; anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ santarpya saṃpravārya bhagavantaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ sauvarṇaṃ bhṛṅgāraṃ gṛhītvā bhagavate nyagrodhārāmaṃ niryātitavān; bhagavatā ca pañcāṅgopetena svareṇa dakṣiṇā ādiṣṭā:
children.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, that very night, having prepared pure, choice hard and soft food, and having risen early in the morning, arranged seats and set out water-pitchers, and announced the time to the <s>Bhagavān</s> through a messenger: 'It is time, Venerable Sir. The meal is ready. Let the <s>Bhagavān</s> come now when he deems it time.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, in the forenoon, having dressed and taken up his bowl and robe, surrounded by the assembly of monks and preceded by the community of monks, approached King <s>Śuddhodana</s>'s meal-invitation. Having approached, he sat down on a seat prepared at the head of the community of monks. Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s>, knowing that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with his own hands satisfied and served them with pure, choice hard and soft food. Having in many ways satisfied and served them with pure, choice hard and soft food with his own hands, and knowing that the <s>Bhagavān</s> had eaten, with his hands washed and his bowl set aside, he took a golden pitcher and formally dedicated the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s> to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. And the <s>Bhagavān</s>, with a voice possessing five qualities, pronounced the dedicatory blessing (<s>dakṣiṇā</s>):

The <s>Śākyas</s> follow the <s>Buddha</s>

children.text: rājñā śuddhodanena jaṭilā pravrajitāḥ bhikṣavo dṛṣṭāḥ; śānteryāpathatvāc cittaprāsādikā no tu kāyaprāsādikāḥ kaṣṭais tapovrataviśeṣaiḥ karśitaśarīrāḥ; dṛṣṭvā ca punar asyaitad abhavat: kiṃ vāpīme jaṭilāḥ śānteryāpathatvāc cittaprāsādikāḥ no tu kāyaprāsādikāḥ; kathaṃrūpeṇa parivāreṇa bhagavān śobheta; saṃlakṣayati, śākyaparivāreṇaiti; tataḥ sarvaśākyān sannipātya kathayati; bhavanto yadi sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro na pravrajito 'bhaviṣyat, ko 'bhaviṣyad? rājā cakravartī; yūyaṃ ke 'bhaviṣyata? anuyātrikāḥ; idānīṃ sarvārthasiddhaḥ kumāro 'nuttaro dharmarājaḥ; kasmān nānuyātrikā bhavatha; deva kiṃ pravrajāmaḥ? pravrajata; kiṃ sarva eva? kulaikikayā; evaṃ kurmaḥ; rājñā śuddhodanena kapilavastunagare ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam; rājā evaṃ samājñāpayati mama viṣayanivāsibhiḥ śākyaiḥ kulaikikayā pravrajitavyam iti
children.translated_text: King <s>Śuddhodana</s> saw the formerly matted-hair ascetics who had gone forth as monks — serene in their deportment, thus pleasing to the mind, though not pleasing to the eye, their bodies emaciated by their special austerity-vows. Having seen, he thought: 'These matted-hair ascetics, though pleasing to the mind because of their serene deportment, are not pleasing to the eye. With what kind of retinue would the <s>Bhagavān</s> look resplendent?' He reflected: 'With a retinue of <s>Śākyas</s>.' Then, having summoned all the <s>Śākyas</s>, he said: 'Sirs, if Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> had not gone forth, what would he have been?' 'A <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).' 'And you, what would you have been?' 'His retinue.' 'Now Prince <s>Sarvārthasiddha</s> is the unsurpassed <s>Dharma</s>-king. Why do you not become his retinue?' 'Lord, shall we go forth?' 'Go forth!' 'All of us?' 'One from each family.' 'We shall do so.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had a proclamation made in the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> by the ringing of a bell: 'The king commands thus: the <s>Śākyas</s> dwelling in my realm are to go forth, one from each family.'

body.text: Aniruddha and Mahānāman
body.translated_text: <s>Aniruddha</s> and <s>Mahānāman</s>

body.text: droṇodanasya dvau putrau aniruddho mahānāmā ca; tayor mahānāmā kṛṣikarmāntānuṣṭhāne atyartham abhiyuktaḥ; aniruddhas tu upariprāsādatalagato niṣpuruṣeṇa tūryeṇa krīḍati ramate paricārayati; mahānāmā mātrā abhihitaḥ: putra rājñā ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritaṃ śākyaiḥ kulaikikayā pravrajitavyam iti; sa tvaṃ pravraja; sa kathayati, nāhaṃ pravrajāmi; yas te priyaḥ putraḥ sukhāsīnas tiṣṭhati taṃ pravrājaya; putra puṇyamaheśākhyo
body.translated_text: <s>Droṇodana</s> had two sons: <s>Aniruddha</s> and <s>Mahānāman</s>. Of these two, <s>Mahānāman</s> was exceedingly devoted to agricultural work. <s>Aniruddha</s>, however, on the upper terrace of the palace, enjoyed, delighted, and sported with unmanned musical instruments. <s>Mahānāman</s> was told by his mother: 'Son, the king has had a bell-proclamation made: "From each <s>Śākya</s> family, one person shall go forth." You should go forth.' He said: 'I will not go forth. That son of yours who sits at ease enjoying himself — make him go forth.' 'Son, that being

body.text: 'sau satvo; mā tena saha spardhāṃ kuru; amba tvaṃ tasyābhiprasannā yenāsau puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ; adya tasyāmba mā kiṃcit preṣaya; jñāsyāmi kiṃ puṇyamaheśākhyo na veti; putra evaṃ bhavatu; pratyakṣīkaromi; tayā riktapiṭharikābhi <ḥ> peṭakaṃ pūrayitvā śuklena vastreṇa ācchādya mudrālakṣitaṃ kṛtvā preṣyadārikāyā haste preṣitaḥ; sandiṣṭā, yadi pṛcchet kim atreti, vaktavyaṃ na kiṃcid iti; sā tam ādāya saṃprasthitā; (
body.translated_text: is one of great accumulated merit. Do not compete with him.' 'Mother, you are partial to him because he is one of great merit. Today, Mother, do not send him anything. I shall find out whether he truly is of great merit or not.' 'Son, let it be so. I shall demonstrate.' She filled a basket with empty vessels, covered it with white cloth, sealed it, and sent it in the hands of a maidservant. She instructed her: 'If he asks "What is in here?" say "Nothing."' She took it and set out. (

) śakrasya devendrasya adhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate; sa saṃlakṣayati: yena nāma upāriṣṭaḥ pratyekabuddhaḥ piṇḍakena pratipāditaḥ; tasyādya kathaṃ bhojanena vighāto bhaviṣyatīti; bhojanopasaṃhāro 'sya kartavya iti; tenāsau peṭako nānāsūpikarasavyañjanopetasyāhārasya pūritaḥ; yāvad asau dārikā tam ādāya aniruddhasya sakāśaṃ gatā; tadā tenoktā dārikā, kim atreti; sā kathayati, kumāra na kiṃcid iti; aniruddhaḥ saṃlakṣayati: priyo 'haṃ mātuḥ; kim asau riktaṃ preṣayiṣyatīti; nūnam atra nāma nakiṃcid bhojanaṃ prakṣiptam; paśyāmi tāvad iti samudghāṭitam; sarvaṃ tad udyānam anekopakaraṇasurabhigandhasaṃpūrṇaṃ vyavasthitam; ghrātvā aniruddhaḥ paraṃ vismayam upagataḥ; mātṛbhakto 'sau; tena mātur agrapiṇḍapātaḥ preṣitaḥ; sandiṣṭaṃ ca amba pratidivasam īdṛśaṃ nakiṃcinnāma bhojanaṃ preṣayitum arhasīti; sāpi dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam upagatā; tayā mahānāmno darśitam; putra dṛṣṭaṃ te? amba dṛṣṭam; tan na tvaṃ mayā pūrvam evoktaḥ puṇyamaheśākhyas sa satvamanuṣyasubhagaḥ; mā tena saha spardhāṃ kuruṣveti; sa kathayati: amba puṇyamaheśākhyo vā bhavatu mā vā; nāhaṃ pravrajāmīti; yataś ca mahānāmā sarvāvasthaṃ nādhivāsitavān pravrajyāṃ, tatas tayā aniruddho 'bhihitaḥ: putra rājñā ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam: śākyaiḥ kulaikikayā pravrajitavyam iti; sa tvaṃ kiṃ pravrajasi, āhosvid gṛhe tiṣṭhasīti; sa kathayati: amba pravrajyāyāṃ ko 'nuśaṃasaḥ? ka ādīnavaḥ? gṛhāvāse ko 'nuśaṃsaḥ? ka ādīnavaḥ? putra pravrajyā saṃpadyamānā nirvāṇāvāhikā bhavati; vipadyamānā devamanuṣyāvāhikā bhavati; gṛhāvāsaḥ samyakpratipālyamāno devamanuṣyāvāhakaḥ; apratipālyamāno narakatiryakpretāvāhakaḥ; amba yaḥ pravrajyāyām ādīnavaḥ, sa gṛhāvāse anuśaṃsaḥ; tasmād alaṃ gṛhāvāsena; anujānīhi; pravrajāmīti; sā kathayati: putra śobhanam, evaṃ kuru; aniruddhasya bhadrikaḥ śākyarājo vayasyakaḥ; sa tasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ; tena khalu samayena bhadrikaḥ śākyarājo vīṇāṃ sārayati; tasya vīṇāṃ sārayataḥ tantrī cchinnā; svaraḥ svarāntaraṃ gataḥ; aniruddho vīṇāyāṃ kṛtāvī; tena yathānusvaraṃ nimittam udgṛhītam; sa dvāre sthitvā dauvārikaṃ puruṣam āmantrayate: gaccha bhoḥ puruṣa, bhadrikasya rājño nivedaya aniruddho dvāre tiṣṭhati devaṃ draṣṭukāma iti; dauvārikeṇa (
body.translated_text: ) <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the Gods (<s>Devendra</s>), possesses downward-directed knowledge and vision. He reflected: 'This one, by whom the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> <s>Upariṣṭa</s> was sustained with a morsel of food — how can he today be deprived of a meal? His food must be provided.' He filled that basket with food endowed with various soups, flavors, and seasonings. Then that girl took it and went to <s>Aniruddha</s>. He then asked the girl: 'What is in here?' She said: 'Prince, nothing.' <s>Aniruddha</s> reflected: 'I am dear to my mother. Would she send me something empty? Surely the food in here is called "nothing." Let me see.' He opened it. The entire garden was suffused with the fragrance of various provisions. Having smelled it, <s>Aniruddha</s> was overcome with supreme wonder. He was devoted to his mother. He sent the first portion of food to his mother. And he instructed her: 'Mother, please send me such "nothing" food every day.' She too, having seen, was overcome with supreme wonder. She showed it to <s>Mahānāman</s>. 'Son, have you seen?' 'Mother, I have seen.' 'Did I not tell you before? That being is one of great merit, blessed with human good fortune. Do not compete with him.' He said: 'Mother, whether he is of great merit or not, I will not go forth.' Since <s>Mahānāman</s> would not in any circumstance consent to ordination, she said to <s>Aniruddha</s>: 'Son, the king has had a bell-proclamation made: "From each <s>Śākya</s> family, one person shall go forth." Will you go forth, or will you remain at home?' He said: 'Mother, what is the benefit of going forth? What is the disadvantage? What is the benefit of household life? What is the disadvantage?' 'Son, going forth, when successful, leads to <s>nirvāṇa</s>; when unsuccessful, it leads to the worlds of gods and humans. Household life, when properly maintained, leads to the worlds of gods and humans; when not maintained, it leads to hell, animal realms, and the realm of hungry ghosts.' 'Mother, the disadvantage of going forth is the advantage of household life. Therefore, enough of household life. Please give permission. I shall go forth.' She said: 'Son, very well, do so.' <s>Aniruddha</s> had a friend, the <s>Śākya</s> king <s>Bhadrika</s>. He went to him. At that time, the <s>Śākya</s> king <s>Bhadrika</s> was tuning a <s>vīṇā</s>. As he was tuning the <s>vīṇā</s>, a string broke. One note passed into another. <s>Aniruddha</s> was skilled in the <s>vīṇā</s>. He recognized the sign by the interval of the notes. Standing at the door, he addressed the doorkeeper: 'Go, good man, inform King <s>Bhadrika</s> — <s>Aniruddha</s> stands at the door, wishing to see His Majesty.' The doorkeeper (

body.text: SBV I 202
) gatvā bhadrikasya śākyarājasya niveditam: deva aniruddho dvāre tiṣṭhati
body.translated_text: ) went and informed the <s>Śākya</s> king <s>Bhadrika</s>: 'Your Majesty, <s>Aniruddha</s> stands at the door,

body.text:
devaṃ draṣṭukāma iti; sa kathayati: praviśatu bhavān aniruddhaḥ; ko bhavantam aniruddhaṃ vārayati; sa praviṣṭaḥ; rājñā pariṣvajya niṣāditaḥ; uktaś ca kiyac ciraṃ tavāgatasyeti; sa kathayati; yadā tava vīṇāṃ sārayatas tantrī chinnā; svaro svarāntaraṃ gata iti; sa paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ kathayati: vīṇāyāṃ bhavān kṛtāvī; bhadrikaḥ śākyarājaḥ kathayati: kumāra kim āgamanaprayojanam; aniruddhaḥ kathayati: deva rājñā śuddhodanena ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam: śākyaiḥ kulaikikayā pravrajitavyam iti; tad avalokito bhava; pravrajāmiti; rājā kathayati, yady evam aham api pravrajāmīti; saṃpradhārayāveti; adya tvam ihaiva vāsam <upagaccha; sa ihaiva vāsam> upagataḥ: śayyākarmāntikena śāyyāyāṃ jvaragandhikāni vastrāṇy ācchāditāni; puṣpāṇi cāvakīrṇāni; aniruddhaḥ śayyāniṣaṇṇaḥ; tasya mallikāvṛntam adhastād avasthitam; sa sparśapratisaṃvedī
kathayati: kim atrādhastāc chilāputrakas tiṣṭhatīti; te pratyavekṣitum ārabdhāḥ; mallikāvṛntaṃ <dṛṣṭvā> te paraṃ vismayam āpannāḥ; aniruddho rātrau duḥkhaṃ suptaḥ; prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ rājñābhihitam: kaccid aniruddhaḥ sukhaṃ supta iti; sa kathayati: deva na sukhaṃ supta iti; rājñābhihitam, kimartham; aniruddhaḥ kathayati; deva jvaragandhāni vastrāṇi prajñaptāni; puṣpāṇi cāvakīrṇāni; puṣpavṛntaiḥ kāyo drūyate; rājñā śayyākarmāntika āhūyoktaḥ: kimartham tvayā jvaragandhāni vastrāṇi prajñaptāni; śayyākarmāntikenābhihitam: mama bhāṇḍāgārikena anupradattāni; rājñā bhāṇḍāgārika āhūyoktaḥ: kimarthaṃ tvayā jvaragandhikāni vastrāṇy anupradattāni; sa kathayati; deva mama tantuvāyenānupradattāni; rājñā tantuvāya āhūyoktaḥ; kimarthaṃ tvayā jvaragandhikāni vastrāṇy anupradattāni? tantuvāyaḥ kathayati: deva vastre ūyamāne kiṃcic cheṣam; tan mayā jvaritena utam; rājā kathayati: kumāra kathaṃ tvayā vijñātam; sa kathayati, uṣṇasparśapratisaṃvedanāt; jvaragandhena ca; rājā paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ kathayati: (
body.translated_text: wishing to see Your Majesty.' He said: 'Let the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s> enter. Who would prevent the venerable <s>Aniruddha</s>?' He entered. The king embraced him and seated him. He asked: 'How long since you arrived?' He said: 'Since the time your <s>vīṇā</s> string broke while you were tuning it and one note passed into another.' He was overcome with wonder and said: 'You are skilled in the <s>vīṇā</s>!' The <s>Śākya</s> king <s>Bhadrika</s> said: 'Prince, what is the purpose of your visit?' <s>Aniruddha</s> said: 'Your Majesty, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> has had a bell-proclamation made: "From each <s>Śākya</s> family, one person shall go forth." Please consider this. I am going forth.' The king said: 'If so, I too shall go forth.' 'Let us deliberate.' 'Today you stay here.' He stayed there. The bedding attendant had covered the bed with cloths that had a fever-smell. And flowers had been strewn. <s>Aniruddha</s> sat on the bed. Beneath him there was a jasmine stem. Being sensitive to touch, he said: 'Is there a stone fragment beneath here?' They began to examine. Having seen the jasmine stem, they were overcome with supreme wonder. <s>Aniruddha</s> slept poorly that night. At dawn, the king asked: 'Did <s>Aniruddha</s> sleep well?' He said: 'Your Majesty, I did not sleep well.' The king asked: 'Why?' <s>Aniruddha</s> said: 'Your Majesty, cloths with a fever-smell were spread. And flowers were strewn. The flower stems irritated my body.' The king summoned the bedding attendant and asked: 'Why did you spread cloths with a fever-smell?' The bedding attendant said: 'They were provided to me by the storekeeper.' The king summoned the storekeeper and asked: 'Why did you provide cloths with a fever-smell?' He said: 'Your Majesty, they were provided to me by the weaver.' The king summoned the weaver and asked: 'Why did you provide cloths with a fever-smell?' The weaver said: 'Your Majesty, while the cloth was being woven, there was a slight remainder. That I wove while feverish.' The king said: 'Prince, how did you detect it?' He said: 'By the sensation of heat to the touch, and by the smell of fever.' The king, overcome with supreme wonder, said: '(

body.text: SBV I 203

) bhavanta aniruddho bhavati śākyasubhagaḥ; tato bhadrikena śākyarājenābhihitaḥ: yady ahaṃ pravrajāmi, devadattaḥ śākyānāṃ rājā bhaviṣyati; sa śākyānām anarthaṃ kariṣyati; yannu vayaṃ sarve saṃbhūya devadattaṃ protsāhayāma iti
body.translated_text: ) Sirs, <s>Aniruddha</s> is truly blessed among the <s>Śākyas</s>!' Then the <s>Śākya</s> king <s>Bhadrika</s> said: 'If I go forth, <s>Devadatta</s> will become the king of the <s>Śākyas</s>. He will bring harm to the <s>Śākyas</s>. Let us all join together and persuade <s>Devadatta</s> [to go forth too].'

body.text: Devadatta entrapped
body.translated_text: <s>Devadatta</s> entrapped:

body.text: sa bhadrikena śākyarājenāhūtaḥ; tataḥ sarvaiḥ sambhūyābhihitaḥ: devadatta vayaṃ sarve pravrajāmaḥ; tvaṃ kiṃ kariṣyasi; devadattaḥ saṃlakṣayati: yadi vakṣyāmi na pravrajāmīti bhadrikaḥ śākyarājo na pravrajiṣyati; tad upāyasaṃvidhānena enān vipralambhayāmi; api nu mayā yam eva divasaṃ bhagavatā nyagrodhārāme ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśitaṃ tadaiva me buddhir utpannā, yathaivānena anvāvartinyā māyayā mahājanakāyo 'nvāvartitaḥ, tathaiva mayā anvāvartitavyaḥ; iti viditvā kathayati: deva yūyaṃ pravrajatha;
body.translated_text: He was summoned by the <s>Śākya</s> king <s>Bhadrika</s>. Then all of them together said: '<s>Devadatta</s>, we are all going forth. What will you do?' <s>Devadatta</s> reflected: 'If I say "I will not go forth," <s>Bhadrika</s> the <s>Śākya</s> king will not go forth. Let me deceive them with a stratagem. Indeed, on the very day when the <s>Bhagavān</s> displayed a supernatural feat at the <s>Nyagrodha</s> park, the thought arose in me: "Just as he has led the great multitude around with his compelling magic, so too I should lead them around."' Having decided thus, he said: 'Your Majesty, you go forth;

body.text: ahaṃ kimarthaṃ tiṣṭhāmīti; bhadrikaḥ śākyarājaḥ saṃlakṣayati: mṛṣāvādiko 'yam; pratijñāyāṃ sthāpayitvā mahājanakāyaḥ pratisaṃviditaḥ kartavya iti; tato rājñā tasya tad vacanaṃ patrābhilikhitaṃ kṛtvā kapilavastuni nagare ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritam: śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ kapilavastunivāsinaḥ paurā, bhadrikarevatāniruddhadevadattapramukhāni pañcaśākyaśatāni pravrajiṣyanti; śrutvā bhavadbhiḥ prāmodyam utpādayitavyam iti; śrutvā devadattasya mahad duḥkhadaurmanasyam utpannam; yadi mayā vijñātam abhaviṣyat bhadrikaḥ śākyarājo niścayena pravrajed iti, na mayā pratijñātam abhaviṣyat; idānīṃ yadi na pravrajiṣyāmi, mṛṣāvādika iti kṛtvā rājyam api na lapsye; sarvathā kim atra prāptakālam; pravrajāmi; pravrajita eva rājyam kārayiṣyāmīti
body.translated_text: why should I remain?' The <s>Śākya</s> king <s>Bhadrika</s> reflected: 'This one is a liar. Having established him in a pledge, the great multitude should be made to witness it.' Then the king had his words written down on a document and had a bell-proclamation made in the city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>: 'Hear, citizens of <s>Kapilavastu</s>! Five hundred <s>Śākyas</s> headed by <s>Bhadrika</s>, <s>Revatā</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, and <s>Devadatta</s> will go forth. Having heard, you should generate joy.' Having heard, great sorrow and dejection arose in <s>Devadatta</s>: 'If I had known that <s>Bhadrika</s> the <s>Śākya</s> king would definitely go forth, I would not have made the pledge. Now if I do not go forth, being called a liar, I will not even obtain the kingdom. In any case, what is timely here? I shall go forth. Even after going forth, I shall exercise royal power.'

body.text: Ordination of five hundred Śākyas
body.translated_text: Ordination of five hundred <s>Śākyas</s>:

body.text: atha rājñaḥ śuddhodanasya etad abhavat: apaścimāṃ śākyānāṃ vibhūtiṃ paśyāmīti; tena tan nagaram apagatapāṣāṇāśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ, candanavāripariṣiktam ucchritadhvajapatākam āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpaṃ surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibaddhaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ ramaṇīyam; tataḥ anekaśākyaśatasahasraparivāraḥ nagaradvāre siṃhāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; śākyastriyaḥ śākyakumāryāś ca kutūhalajātā gavākṣavātāyanavedikāsv avasthitāḥ, śākyānām vibhūtiṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ (
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śuddhodana</s> thought: 'I am seeing the <s>Śākyas</s>' splendor for the last time.' He had the city cleared of gravel and stones, sprinkled with sandalwood water, with raised banners and flags, adorned with silk garlands, fitted with censers of fragrant incense, strewn with various flowers, and made delightful. Then, surrounded by hundreds of thousands of <s>Śākyas</s>, he sat on a lion-throne at the city gate. The <s>Śākya</s> women and <s>Śākya</s> maidens, filled with curiosity, positioned themselves at the windows, ventilation openings, and balconies, wishing to see the <s>Śākyas</s>' splendor. (

body.text: SBV I 204

) nānādeśabhyāgataś ca janakāyaḥ rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu; naimittikā brāhamaṇā vipañcanakā āhūtāḥ śākyaparīkṣāṃ prati, ko 'trārādhakaḥ ko na veti; atha śākyā mātāpitrāv avalokya hārakaṭakakeyūrādyalaṅkāravibhūṣitāḥ pratyekapratyekaṃ ratheṣv abhiruhya nirgantum ārabdhāḥ; pūrvaṃ bhadrikaḥ śākyarājo nirgataḥ; naimittikair dṛṣṭaḥ; te kathayanti: eṣa tāvad ārādhako bhaviṣyatīti; evaṃ revatāniruddhaprabhṛtayo nirgatāḥ; te 'pi naimittikair vyākṛtāḥ; tato devadatto nirgataḥ; tasya nirgacchataḥ śyenakena śakunakena cūḍāmaṇir apahṛtaḥ; naimittikair dṛṣṭaḥ; te kathayanti: yādṛśam asya nimittaṃ niyatam ayaṃ śāstari prahṛtya narakaparāyaṇo bhavatīti; kokālikakhaṇḍadravyakaṭamorakatiṣyasamudradattānāṃ nirgacchatāṃ khareṇa vāśitam; te 'pi naimittikair vyākṛtāḥ: ete 'pi mahāśrāvakeṣu vāgduścaritaṃ kṛtvā narakaparāyaṇā bhaviṣyanti iti; upanandasya hastiskandhābhirūḍhasya itaś cāmutaś ca vyavalokayato muktāhāraḥ patitaḥ; sa hastiskandhād avatīrya gṛhītaḥ; so 'pi vyākṛtaḥ: anenātyantalobhān narakeṣūpapattavyam iti; tatas teṣāṃ śākyānāṃ bhadrikāniruddhadevadattapramukhāni pañcaśākyaśatāni udyānayātrāpratispardhayā śobhayā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntāni; bhagavān saṃlakṣayati: saced ahaṃ śākyān ehibhikṣukayā pravrājayiṣyāmi kecid ārādhakā bhaviṣyanti, kecid anārādhakāḥ; ye anārādhakās teṣāṃ bhaviṣyaty anyathātvam; sarvaś caihibhikṣuś caramabhavikaḥ; yanv ahaṃ sarvān eva bhikṣūn
body.translated_text: ) and a great multitude of people from various regions [gathered] in the streets, lanes, squares, and crossroads. <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> diviners and soothsayers were summoned to examine the <s>Śākyas</s> — who among them would succeed [in the religious life] and who would not. Then the <s>Śākyas</s>, looking toward their parents, adorned with necklaces, bracelets, armlets, and other ornaments, each mounted their chariots and began to go forth. First, <s>Bhadrika</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> king, went forth. He was observed by the diviners. They declared: 'This one will certainly succeed.' Likewise <s>Revata</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, and the others went forth. They too were declared upon by the diviners. Then <s>Devadatta</s> went forth. As he was going forth, a hawk snatched away his crest-jewel. The diviners observed this. They declared: 'Given this omen, this one will certainly strike against the Teacher and be destined for hell.' When <s>Kokālika</s>, <s>Khaṇḍadravya</s>, <s>Kaṭamoraka</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, and <s>Samudradatta</s> went forth, a she-donkey brayed. They too were declared upon by the diviners: 'These too, having committed verbal misconduct against the great disciples, will be destined for hell.' When <s>Upananda</s>, mounted on the shoulder of an elephant, was looking about here and there, his pearl necklace fell. He descended from the elephant's shoulder and picked it up. He too was declared upon: 'This one, due to extreme greed, will be reborn in the hells.' Then those five hundred <s>Śākyas</s>, headed by <s>Bhadrika</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, and <s>Devadatta</s>, with the splendor rivaling a garden excursion, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'If I ordain the <s>Śākyas</s> with the "Come, monk" (<s>ehibhikṣuka</s>) formula, some will succeed and some will not. Those who do not succeed will undergo a change [for the worse]. And every "Come, monk" ordainee must be one in his final existence. Let me instead ordain all monks

body.text: jñapticaturthena karmaṇā pravrājayeyam upasaṃpādayeyam; iti viditvā bhikṣūn āmantrayate: pravrājayata bhikṣavaḥ kāpilavāstavān śākyān, upasaṃpādayata jñapticaturthena karmaṇā iti; evaṃ bhadanteti te bhikṣavo bhagavataḥ pratyaśrauṣuḥ
body.translated_text: with the formal act of the fourth motion (<s>jñapticaturtha karma</s>).' Having understood this, he addressed the monks: 'Ordain the <s>Śākyas</s> of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, monks; confer the full ordination (<s>upasaṃpadā</s>) upon them with the formal act of the fourth motion.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' those monks assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: Upālin, the barber
body.translated_text: <s>Upālin</s>, the barber

body.text: śākyānām upālī nāma kalpakaḥ rājñā śuddodanena teṣāṃ pravrajatāṃ keśāvaropakaḥ preṣitaḥ; bhadrikasya śākyarājasya keśān avatārayan so 'śrudurdinavadano bāṣpoparuddhyamānahṛdayo muhur (
body.translated_text: The <s>Śākyas</s> had a barber named <s>Upālin</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> had sent him to shave the heads of those who were going forth. As he shaved the hair of <s>Bhadrika</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> king, with a tear-dampened face, his heart choked with sobs, repeatedly (

body.text: SBV I 205
body.translated_text: SBV I 205

body.text:
) niśvāsaparāyaṇaḥ keśān avatārayati; bhadrikaḥ śākyarājaḥ kathayati: upālin kimarthaṃ rodiṣi? sa karuṇadīnavilambitair akṣaraiḥ kathayati: deva mayā jambūdvīpapradhānānāṃ puruṣāṇām upasthānaṃ kṛtvā, idānīṃ prākṛtapuruṣāṇām upasthānaṃ kartavyaṃ bhaviṣyati; kāmaṃ prāṇaviyogaḥ, na yuṣmābhiḥ parityaktasya jīvitam iti; bhadrikaḥ śākyarājaḥ kathayati: alam upālin darśitas tvayā svāmibhaktyanurāgaḥ; niyaccha śokam; ahaṃ tathā kariṣyāmi yathā prākṛtapuruṣāṇām upasthānaṃ na kariṣyasi; iti viditvā tenaikasmin pradeśe paṭakaḥ prasāritaḥ, śākyakumārāś ca abhihitāḥ: śṛṇvantu bhavantaḥ kumārā eṣo 'smākam upālī kalpakaḥ kṛtopasthānaḥ; tad asya jīvikānimittam alaṅkāraṃ paṭe sthāpayata; nāsmābhiḥ punar agāre vastavyam iti; tair hārārdhahārakaṭakakeyūrakuṇḍalānāṃ nānāratnapratyuptānām alaṅkāraviśeṣāṇāṃ paṭake mahān rāśiḥ kṛtaḥ; upālinā teṣām anupūrveṇa keśāvaropaṇaṃ kṛtam; te snātuṃ gatāḥ; sa saṃlakṣayati: ime tāvat kumārāḥ kulavibhavayauvanopetāḥ sphītāny antaḥpurāṇi, sphītāni kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇy apāsya pravrajitāḥ; aham asminn alaṅkāramātre sakto 'nayena vyasanam āpatsye; yady ahaṃ na nīcakulotpannaḥ syām, aham api svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyodyujyeyaṃ, ghaṭeyaṃ, vyāyaccheyam, oghānām uttaraṇāya, yogānāṃ samatikramaṇāyeti
  dharmatā hy eṣā yathā buddhā bhagavantas trī rātreḥ, trir divasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokayanti, evaṃ mahāśrāvakā api; adrākṣīd āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ upālinaṃ kalpakam atīva saṃvignam; dṛṣṭvā ca punar yenopālī kalpakas tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya upālinaṃ kalpakam idam avocat: kasmāt tvam upālin atīva saṃvignaḥ kare kapolaṃ datvā cintāparas tiṣṭhasīti; sa kathayati: katham ahaṃ bhadanta śāriputra na cintāparo bhavāmi yatredānīm amī kumārāḥ kulavibhavayauvanopetāḥ sphītāny antaḥpurāṇi sphītāni ca kośakoṣṭhāgārāṇy apāsya pravrajitāḥ; aham asminn alaṅkāramātre sakto 'nayena vyasanam āpatsye? yady ahaṃ na nīcakulotpannaḥ syām aham api svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajya udyujyeyaṃ, ghaṭeyaṃ, (
body.translated_text:
) sighing deeply, he was shaving the hair. <s>Bhadrika</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> king, said: '<s>Upālin</s>, why do you weep?' He said, with words halting and sorrowful with compassion: 'My lord, I have served the foremost men of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>. Now I shall have to serve ordinary men. Better the loss of life than a life abandoned by you.' <s>Bhadrika</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> king, said: 'Enough, <s>Upālin</s> — you have shown your devotion and affection for your masters. Restrain your grief. I shall arrange it so that you will not have to serve ordinary men.' Having understood this, he had a cloth spread in a certain place and addressed the <s>Śākya</s> princes: 'Listen, noble princes! This <s>Upālin</s> is our barber who has served us. For the sake of his livelihood, place your ornaments on the cloth. We shall no longer dwell in the household.' They made a great heap upon the cloth of their necklaces, half-necklaces, bracelets, armlets, earrings — ornaments of various kinds set with various jewels. <s>Upālin</s> shaved their hair one by one. They went to bathe. He reflected: 'These princes, endowed with family, wealth, and youth, having abandoned their prosperous inner apartments and prosperous treasuries and granaries, have gone forth. Yet I remain attached to this mere pile of ornaments — through such folly I shall fall into misfortune. If only I were not born of a low family, I too would exert myself, strive, and endeavor in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, for the crossing of the floods and the overcoming of the bonds.'
For it is the natural law (<s>dharmatā</s>) that just as <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s> survey the world three times at night and three times during the day with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, so too do the great disciples. The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> saw the barber <s>Upālin</s> exceedingly agitated. Having seen, he approached the barber <s>Upālin</s>. Having approached, he said to the barber <s>Upālin</s>: 'Why, <s>Upālin</s>, are you so exceedingly agitated, resting your cheek on your hand, consumed by anxiety?' He said: 'Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, how should I not be anxious, when now these princes, endowed with family, wealth, and youth, having abandoned their prosperous inner apartments and prosperous treasuries and granaries, have gone forth — yet I remain attached to this mere pile of ornaments and through such folly shall fall into misfortune? If only I were not born of a low family, I too would, in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>, go forth, exert myself, strive (
