body.translated_text: SBV I 206

body.text: ) vyāyaccheyam oghānām uttaraṇāya, yogānāṃ samatikramaṇāyeti; āyuṣmān śāriputraḥ kathayati: bhadramukha nedaṃ munīndrapravacanaṃ jātisārakaṃ, na gotrasārakaṃ, na śrutasārakam; api tu pratipattisārakam idaṃ munīndrapravacanam;
body.translated_text: ), and endeavor, for the crossing of the floods and the overcoming of the bonds.' The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said: 'Good sir, this teaching of the Lord of Sages is not one whose essence is birth, nor lineage (<s>gotra</s>), nor learning. Rather, this teaching of the Lord of Sages has practice (<s>pratipatti</s>) as its essence.

children.text: athāyuṣmān śāriputraḥ upālinaṃ kalpakam ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavantam idam avocat: ayaṃ bhadanta upālī ākāṅkṣate svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam; tato bhagavān pravrājayatu, upasaṃpādayatu, anukampām upādāyeti; sa bhagavatā ābhāṣitaḥ ehi bhikṣo cara brahmacaryam iti; bhagavato vāco 'vasānasamanantaram eva muṇḍaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ, saṅghāṭīprāvṛtaḥ, pātrakarakavyagrahastaḥ, saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśruḥ, varṣaśatopasampannasya bhikṣor īryāpathenāvasthitaḥ; āha cātra:

children.translated_text: Thus addressed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> with 'Come!',
tonsured, his body clad in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> robe, /
at once he stood with faculties at peace,
adorned by the <s>Buddha</s>'s wish, as if costumed for a role. //

Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>, taking the barber <s>Upālin</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'This <s>Upālin</s>, Venerable Sir, desires ordination and full admission into monkhood in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> ordain and fully admit him, out of compassion.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed him: 'Come, monk! Live the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>).' At the very end of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, he became tonsured, clad in the <s>saṃghāṭī</s> robe, holding bowl and water-pot, with hair and beard as if shaved seven days prior, standing with the deportment of a monk who had been fully ordained for a hundred years. And herein it is said:

children.text: śākyāḥ pravrajitāḥ yathāvṛddhikayā sāmīcīṃ kāryante; bhadrikena śākyarājena sāmīcīṃ kurvatā upālinaḥ pādau pratyabhijñātau, tato mukhaṃ vyavalokitam; sa kathayati: bhagavann eṣa upālī; kim asyāpi mayā pādayor nipatitavyam iti; bhagavān āha: vatsa mānaprahāṇāya pravrajyā; tavaiṣa vṛddho nihatamadamānaḥ; nipateti; sa tasya pādayor nipatitaḥ; ṣaḍvikāraṃ pṛthivīkampo jātaḥ; iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī calati, saṃcalati, saṃpracalati; vyathate, pravyathate saṃpravyathate; pūrvā dig unnamati; paścimāvanamati; paścimā unnamati; purvā avanamati; dakṣiṇā unnamati; uttarā avanamati; uttarā unnamati; dakṣiṇā avanamati; (

); the center rises and the edges sink; the edges rise and the center sinks. Thus they prostrated in order. <s>Devadatta</s> did not prostrate. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Son, going forth is for the abandonment of pride. Prostrate.' He said: 'What authority do you have? I shall not prostrate at his feet.' He did not prostrate. There, <s>Devadatta</s> for the first time defied the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s command.
The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir — when <s>Bhadrika</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> king, performed the greeting to <s>Upālin</s>, a great earthquake of six kinds occurred.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, monks; in the past too, this was the natural law. He who prostrated at [<s>Upālin</s>'s] feet — a great earthquake of six kinds occurred. Listen to that.'

The <s>Śākyas</s>, having been ordained, were performing the customary greeting (<s>sāmīcī</s>) in order of seniority. As <s>Bhadrika</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> king, was performing the greeting, he recognized <s>Upālin</s>'s feet. Then he looked up at his face. He said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, this is <s>Upālin</s>! Must I too prostrate at his feet?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Son, going forth is for the abandonment of pride. He is your senior. Cast down your pride and prostrate.' He prostrated at his feet. A great earthquake of six kinds occurred. This great earth trembles, shakes, and quakes violently; it shudders, heaves, and jolts. The eastern quarter rises and the western sinks; the western rises and the eastern sinks; the southern rises and the northern sinks; the northern rises and the southern sinks (

body.text: Sundara, the student, and Bhadrā, the harlot
body.translated_text: <s>Sundara</s>, the student, and <s>Bhadrā</s>, the harlot

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati, ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca; tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ bhadrā nāma rūpājīvinī prativasati; sundarāś ca nāmnā māṇavakaḥ; sa tasyāḥ sakāśam upasaṅkrāntaḥ kathayati: bhadre āgaccha paricārayāma iti; sā kathayati; santi te pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatānīti;
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was exercising sovereignty. It was prosperous, flourishing, secure, abundant in food, and teeming with a great multitude of people. At that time, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there lived a courtesan named <s>Bhadrā</s>, and a young student named <s>Sundara</s>. He approached her and said: '<s>Bhadrā</s>, come, let us enjoy ourselves.' She said: 'Do you have five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>?'

body.text: sa kathayati, na santi; gaccha, pañca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni gṛhītvā āgaccha; tasya vibhavo nāsti; sa tasyām atyartham adhyavasitaḥ; kālena kālaṃ nānāvicitrāṇi puṣpāṇi, phalāni copanāmyati; tasyās tasminn anunaya utpannaḥ; yāvad apareṇa samayena vārāṇasyāṃ parvā pratyupasthitaḥ; sarvās striyo vastramālyālaṅkāravibhūṣitāḥ svakasvakeṣu krīḍāratiharṣabahulā avatiṣṭhante; tā dṛṣṭvā sundaro māṇavaḥ paritasyati; bhadrā rūpājīvinī saṃlakṣayati: adya vārāṇaseyā manuṣyā vastrālaṅkāravibhūṣitā svakasvakābhiḥ strībhiḥ sārdhaṃ paricārayiṣyanti; sundaro māṇavakaḥ mayā sārdhaṃ paricārayiṣyati; sā caivaṃ cintayati; sundaraś ca māṇavakas taṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ; sā taṃ dṛṣṭvā pūrvopakārasañjanitasaumanasyā kathayati: māṇava gaccha; sugandhāni puṣpāṇy ādāyāgaccha; mayā sārdhaṃ paricārayiṣyasīti; sa naṣṭopalabdhaprāṇa iva vismayāvarjitasantatiḥ prakrāntaḥ; tasyā rūpayauvanacāturyaguṇān vikalpayan madāviṣṭaḥ kṛtsnāṃ rātriṃ jāgaritaḥ; prabhātāyāṃ rajanyām atyarthamiddharparyākulīkṛtanayanas tāvat supto yāvad ādhityodaya iti; sarvopayogāya lokena yadā sarvāṇi puṣpāṇy uccitāni tadā prativibuddhaḥ; puṣpanimittam itaś (
body.translated_text: He said: 'I do not.' 'Go, take five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> and come back.' He had no means. But he was exceedingly devoted to her. From time to time he would bring her various beautiful flowers and fruits. Affection arose in her for him. Then at a later time, a festival was approaching in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. All the women, adorned with garments, garlands, and ornaments, were enjoying their own revelries, delights, and pleasures. Seeing them, the student <s>Sundara</s> was distressed. The courtesan <s>Bhadrā</s> reflected: 'Today the people of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, adorned with garments and ornaments, will enjoy themselves with their own women. The student <s>Sundara</s> will enjoy himself with me.' As she was thinking thus, the student <s>Sundara</s> arrived at that very place. Seeing him, her heart gladdened by his past kindnesses, she said: 'Student, go! Bring fragrant flowers and come back. You shall enjoy yourself with me.' He, as if recovering his breath after death, departed in a daze of astonishment. Fantasizing about the qualities of her beauty, youth, and charm, intoxicated [with desire], he stayed awake the entire night. At dawn, his eyes overwhelmed with extreme drowsiness, he fell asleep until sunrise. By the time the whole world had already gathered all the flowers for their various uses, he awoke. Searching here and there for flowers (

body.translated_text: SBV I 208

body.translated_text: ), he could not find any. Taking <s>śirīṣa</s> (silk-cotton) flowers, he approached her. She spoke a verse:

children.translated_text: Lazy, wearing a deerskin, averse to work,
the lad <s>Sundara</s>, without half a penny — /
today, when the trees are in full bloom,
he presents us <s>śirīṣa</s> flowers! //

children.text: iti viditvā kathayati: gaccha anyāni puṣpāṇy ādāyāgaccheti; kāmān khalu pratisevamānasya saṃyojanāny upacayaṃ gacchantīti sa pravṛddhakāmarāgo grīṣmaṇāṃ paścime māse vyabhre dine vigatabalāhake, sthite madhyāhnasamaye, nagarād ativiprakṛṣṭadeśeṣv araṇyeṣu vaktrāparavaktraṃ gāyan puṣpāṇy uccinoti; rājā ca brahmadatto mṛgavadhāya nirgataḥ; sa tīkṣṇārkaraśmisantāpitaḥ chāyāyāḥ śītalaṃ pradeśam anuprāptaḥ; tasya gītaśabdaṃ śrutvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Having realized this, he said: 'Go, bring more flowers.' Indeed, for one who indulges in sensual pleasures, the fetters only accumulate. He, with his desire and passion greatly increased, in the last month of summer, on a cloudless day free of storm-clouds, at the midday hour, in forests far removed from the city, singing face after face, gathered flowers. And King <s>Brahmadatta</s> had gone out to hunt deer. Scorched by the fierce rays of the sun, he arrived at a cool, shady spot. Hearing the sound of singing, he spoke a verse:

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ tapati ādityaḥ adhastād dahati vālukā /
children.translated_text: Above, the sun burns; below, the sand scorches.

children.text: kasmād gāyasi gātrāṇi na te dahati ātapaḥ // iti;
children.translated_text: Why do you sing? Does the heat not burn your limbs? //
<s>Sundara</s> also spoke a verse:

children.text: na māṃ tāpayaty ādityaḥ saṅkalpās tāpayanti mām /
children.translated_text: The sun does not torment me; desires torment me.

children.text: kāryākāryāṇi loke 'smiṃs tāpayanti tu nātapaḥ // iti;
children.translated_text: What should be done and what should not be done in this world — those torment me, not the heat. //

body.text: rājā saṃlakṣayati: nūnam ayaṃ māṇavaḥ śaityakathāsu kṛtāvī yena sthite madhyāhnasamaye puṣpāṇy uccinotīti; sa tenābhihitaḥ: kuru māṇava śaityāṃ tāvat kathām; śṛṇomīti; sa saṃlakṣayati; nūnam asya rājñaḥ śarīradāhaḥ, yenaivaṃ vadatīti; tena tasya vicitrā śaityakathā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā rājñaḥ śarīradāhaḥ prativigataḥ; rājā abhiprasannaḥ; amātyān pṛcchati; bhavanto yo rājño kṣatriyasya mūrdhābhiṣiktasya jīvitam anuprayacchati, tasya kaḥ pratyupakāraḥ? deva upārdharājyam; tatas sa rājñā abhihitaḥ; māṇava adya rājakule vāsaṃ kalpayasva; upārdharājyaṃ te prayacchāmi iti; tasya rājakule praṇītaṃ śayanāsanaṃ dattam; sa tasmin śayitaḥ bhadrām anusmṛtya cintayati; tad upārdharājyaṃ gṛhṇāmi yatra bhadrā rūpājīvinī iti; bhūyaḥ saṃlakṣayati: kīdṛśaḥ sa rājā yatra upārdharājyaṃ bhuṅkte; yanv aham enam jīvitād vyaparopayeyam iti; punaḥ saṃlakṣayati:
body.translated_text: The king reflected: 'Surely this young man is skilled in cooling tales, since he gathers flowers at the midday hour.' He said to him: 'Young man, tell me a cooling tale; I shall listen.' He reflected: 'Surely this king has a burning sensation in his body, since he speaks thus.' He then told him an elaborate cooling tale. Hearing it, the king's bodily burning subsided. The king, filled with faith, asked his ministers: 'Sirs, one who saves the life of a king, an anointed <s>Kṣatriya</s> — what reward [is given] to him?' 'Your Majesty, half the kingdom.' Then the king said to him: 'Young man, arrange your lodging in the royal palace today; I shall give you half the kingdom.' A fine bed was given to him in the royal palace. Lying on it, recollecting <s>Bhadrā</s>, he thought: 'I shall accept half the kingdom — wherever <s>Bhadrā</s> the courtesan is.' Then again he reflected: 'What sort of king is one who merely enjoys half a kingdom? Let me rather take his life.' Then again he reflected:

body.text: alam anena rājyena yad rājānaṃ praghātya iti; gmathāṃ ca bhāṣate: (
body.translated_text: 'Enough of this kingdom obtained by killing a king.' And he spoke a verse: (

body.translated_text: SBV I 209

children.text: aprāpte arthatarṣaḥ prāpte cārthe na tarṣavinivṛttiḥ /
children.translated_text: When a thing is not obtained, there is thirst for it; when obtained, the thirst does not subside.

children.text: aprāpte ca vighātas tasmād arthe matir anarthāya // iti
children.translated_text: When not obtained, there is frustration. Therefore, desire for wealth leads to ruin. //

body.text: yāvat prabhātā rajanī saṃvṛttā, sa vipratisārajātaḥ śayanād avatīrya kṛṣṇājīnam āstīrya bhūmau śayitaḥ; prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ rājā kathayati: bhavantaḥ śabdayata taṃ māṇavam; upārdharājyaṃ tasmai anuprayacchāmīti; rājadūtā gatāḥ paśyanti; mahāśayanād avatīrya bhūmau śayitaḥ; dṛṣṭvā ca punar aprasādaṃ pravedayanto rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatāḥ kathayanti: deva nāsāv arhati rājyam; rājā kathayati, kimartham? te kathayanti: deva yo hi nāma praṇītaṃ śayanāsanam apahāya bhūmau kṛṣṇājine śayitas tasya hīnādhimuktasya kiṃ rājyeneti; rājā kathayati: bhavantaḥ sa prājñaḥ, kāraṇenātra bhavitavyam; śabdayata iti; tair asau śabditaḥ: rājñā pṛṣṭaḥ: bho māṇava kimarthaṃ tvaṃ mahāśayanāsanād kṛṣṇājine śayita iti; tena yathāvṛttaṃ rājñe samākhyātam; tataḥ kathayati: deva anujānīhi pravrajāmīti; rājā kathayati: samayato 'nujānāmi; yadi pravrajitvā kiñcid guṇagaṇam adhigacchasi mamārocayitavyam iti; tena pratijñātam evaṃ bhavatv iti; tatas tena śāntaṃ pradeśaṃ gatvā anācāryakeṇa anupādhyāyakena pratyekabodhir anugatā; sa pratyekabuddhaḥ saṃlakṣayati; mayā tasya rājñaḥ pratijñātam; gacchāmi tāṃ pūrvikāṃ pratijñāṃ niryātayāmi iti; sa rājñaḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartum ārabdhaḥ; rājā tasya pādayor nipatya gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
body.translated_text: As the night passed, he was seized with remorse. Descending from the bed, he spread a black antelope skin and lay on the ground. At dawn, the king said: 'Sirs, call that young man. I shall give him half the kingdom.' The royal messengers went and saw: he had descended from the great bed and was lying on the ground. Having seen, they returned to the king displeased and said: 'Your Majesty, he does not deserve the kingdom.' The king said: 'Why not?' They said: 'Your Majesty, one who would abandon a fine bed and lie on the ground on a black antelope skin — what use is a kingdom to one of such lowly aspirations?' The king said: 'Sirs, he is wise; there must be a reason. Call him.' They called him. The king asked: 'Young man, why did you leave the great bed and lie on the black antelope skin?' He narrated the full account to the king. Then he said: 'Your Majesty, give me permission — I wish to go forth.' The king said: 'I give permission on a condition: if, having gone forth, you attain some collection of virtues, you must inform me.' He agreed: 'So be it.' Then, having gone to a peaceful place, without a teacher, without a preceptor, he realized the state of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (Solitary Awakened One). That <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> reflected: 'I made a promise to that king. Let me go and fulfill that earlier promise.' He went to the king, rose up into the sky, and began to perform the miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and flashing. The king, falling at his feet, spoke a verse:

children.translated_text: Behold the fruit, arising from a small beginning —
great distinction has been gained by means of a trifle.
Well-gained are the gains of the young man
who went forth seeking what is wholesome! //

And he said: '<s>Gaṅgāpāla</s>, you shall remind me of this verse again and again.' The barber <s>Gaṅgāpāla</s> was exceedingly skilled in his craft. Whenever he performed the beard-trimming service for King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, the king would fall asleep. He would be awakened by the barber's gentle touch. Having awakened, (

body.text: ) ca gaṅgāpālaṃ vareṇa pravārayati, vada kaṃ te varam anuprayacchāmīti; sa kathayati, deva vijñāpayiṣyāmīti; yadā gaṅgāpālo rājānaṃ gāthāṃ smārayati tadā rājñaḥ kāmakathāyām api cittaṃ na krāmati; prāg eva kāmādhyācaraṇe; so 'ntaḥpuraṃ an vyavalokayati; antaḥpurikāḥ kleśamadāviṣṭāḥ gaṅgāpālasya kathayanti: mātula yadā te devo vareṇa pravārayati, tadā vaktavyam, yadi me devo 'bhiprasannaḥ tad asyā gāthāyā arthaṃ vistareṇa saṃprakāśayed iti; rājñā tasyā gāthāyā artho vistareṇa saṃvibhaktaḥ; sa saṃvignaḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati: deva kṛtopasthāno 'ham; pravrajāmy agārād anagārikām iti; rājā kathayati: yadi pravrājitaḥ kiñcid guṇagaṇam adhigamiṣyasi mama nivedayiṣyasīti; sa kathayati: deva evaṃ bhavatu nivedayiṣyāmīti;
body.translated_text: ) he would offer <s>Gaṅgāpāla</s> a boon: 'Speak — what boon shall I grant you?' He replied: 'Your Majesty, I shall make my request later.' Whenever <s>Gaṅgāpāla</s> reminded the king of the verse, the king's mind would not turn even to talk of sensual pleasures — let alone the practice of sensual pleasure. He would not even look at the inner apartments. The women of the inner apartments, possessed by the intoxication of the afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), told <s>Gaṅgāpāla</s>: 'Uncle, when the lord offers you a boon, you should say: "If my lord is pleased with me, let him explain to me in detail the meaning of that verse."' The king explained the meaning of that verse to him in detail. He was deeply moved. Falling at the king's feet, he said: 'Your Majesty, I am ready; I wish to go forth from the household life to the homeless life.' The king said: 'If, having gone forth, you attain some collection of virtues, you must inform me.' He said: 'Your Majesty, so be it; I shall inform you.'

body.text: sa gatvā ṛṣīṇāṃ madhye pravrajitaḥ; tena pañcābhijñāḥ sākṣātkṛtāḥ; tasyaitad abhavat: mayā rājño brahmadattasya pratijñātam; gacchāmi, tāṃ pūrvikāṃ pratijñāṃ niryātayāmīti; sa yena rājā brahmadattas tena upasaṅkrāntaḥ; upasaṅkramya upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kartum ārabhaḥ; asti pṛthagjanasya ṛddhir āvarjanakarī; sa pādayor nipatya kathayati: ārya tvayā evaṃvidhaguṇagaṇā adhigatāḥ? adhigatāḥ; rājā brahmadattaḥ gaṅgāpālasya ṛṣeḥ <pādayor nipatati> ṣaḍvikāraḥ pṛthivīkampo jātaḥ; mātā cāsya gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
body.translated_text: Having gone, he went forth among the sages. He directly realized the five supernatural powers (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>). He thought: 'I made a promise to King <s>Brahmadatta</s>. Let me go and fulfill that earlier promise.' He approached King <s>Brahmadatta</s>. Having approached, he rose up into the sky and began to perform the miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and flashing. The supernatural power of an ordinary person has the capacity to inspire faith. The king, falling at his feet, said: 'Noble sir, have you attained such a collection of virtues?' 'I have attained them.' When King <s>Brahmadatta</s> fell at the feet of the sage <s>Gaṅgāpāla</s>, there was a sixfold earthquake. And his mother spoke a verse:

children.translated_text: This is your divine mango grove, O wise <s>Brahmadatta</s>,

children.text: pravibhajya hi yatraiṣa prāvrajat kṣurabhāṇḍikam // iti;
children.translated_text: having abandoned which, this one went forth with his barber's kit. //

body.text: rājā brahmadatto mātaram anusaṃjñapayan gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
body.translated_text: King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, explaining to his mother, spoke a verse:

children.translated_text: Do not speak thus of <s>Gaṅgāpāla</s>,
who is training in the practices of silence.
He is the doer of this difficult deed,
having done which, men become broadly awakened. //

What do you think, monks? He who at that time, in that era, was the king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> — he was none other than <s>Bhadrika</s>, the <s>Śākya</s> king. He who was the sage named <s>Gaṅgāpāla</s> — he was none other than <s>Upālin</s>. Even then, when <s>Bhadrika</s> the <s>Śākya</s> king, who was <s>Brahmadatta</s>, bowed at the feet of <s>Upālin</s>, who was the sage <s>Gaṅgāpāla</s>, there was a sixfold earthquake. And now too, when <s>Bhadrika</s> the <s>Śākya</s> king bowed at the feet of the ordained <s>Upālin</s>, there was a sixfold earthquake.
Appendix II
Conversion of <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>

children.text: atha bhagavān nandāṃ ca nandabalāṃ ca grāmikaduhitarau dhārmyayā kathayā sandarśayitvā samādāpayitvā samuttejayitvā saṃpraharṣayitvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted <s>Nandā</s> and <s>Nandabalā</s>, the daughters of the village-chief, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, rose from his seat and departed.

children.text: ) atha bhagavataḥ senāyanagrāmakāt prakramyaitad abhavat: astīha magadheṣu janapadeṣu kaścic chramaṇo vā brāhmaṇo vā suśīlaḥ saṃmato yam aham anvāvartayeyaṃ yasmin me 'nvāvṛtte 'lpakṛcchreṇa mahājanakāyo 'nvāvartiṣyate; tena khalu samayenorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo jīrṇo vṛddho mahallako; sa viṃśativarṣaśatiko jātyā māgadhakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ satkṛto gurukṛto mānito pūjito 'rhan saṃmataḥ; paṃcaśataparivāro nadyā nairaṃjanāyās tīra āśramapade śāmyate; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: ayam urubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo jīrṇo mahallakaḥ pūrvavad yāvac chāmyate; yanv aham urubilvākāśyapaṃ jaṭilam anvāvartayeyaṃ yasmin me 'nvāvṛtte 'lpakṛcchreṇa mahājanakāyo 'nvāvartiṣyate (
children.translated_text: ) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having departed from the village of <s>Senāyana</s>, thought: 'Is there here in the <s>Magadha</s> territories any ascetic or <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> who is virtuous and esteemed, whom I might convert? If he were converted by me, with little difficulty a great multitude of people would be converted.' At that time, the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s> was old, aged, and advanced in years. He was one hundred and twenty years old by birth, honored, respected, revered, and worshipped by the people of <s>Magadha</s>, regarded as an <s>Arhat</s>, esteemed, with a retinue of five hundred, dwelling in a hermitage on the bank of the river <s>Nairañjanā</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> thought: 'This matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s> is old and aged' — as before, down to 'he dwells.' 'Let me convert the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s>; when he is converted by me, with little difficulty a great multitude of people will be converted.' (
CPS 24a.4

children.text: ) atha bhagavān yenorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapadaṃ tenopajagāma; adrākṣīd urubilvlākāśyapo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ dūrata eva; dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhagavato 'rthāyāsanaṃ prajñapya bhagavantam idam avocat: āgaccha mahāśramaṇa svāgataṃ mahāśramaṇa; mahāśramaṇaś ciracirasya paryāyam akārṣīd ihāgamanāya; niṣīdatu mahaśṛamaṇaḥ prajñapta evāsane; nyaṣīdad bhagavān prajñapta evāsane; athorubilvākāśyapo bhagavatā sārdhaṃ saṃmodanīṃ saṃrañjanīṃ vividhāṃ kathāṃ vyatisāryaikānte nyaṣīdat; (
children.translated_text: ) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> approached the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s>. The matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar. Having seen, he prepared a seat for the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said to him: 'Come, Great Ascetic! Welcome, Great Ascetic! The Great Ascetic has at last made an occasion to come here. Let the Great Ascetic sit down on the prepared seat.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> sat down on the prepared seat. Then <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s>, having exchanged various pleasant and agreeable conversation with the <s>Bhagavān</s>, sat down to one side. (
SBV I 218

children.text: ) ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ bhagavān urubilvākāśyapaṃ jaṭilam idam avocat: yadi te kāśyapa agurv ahaṃ tavāgnyāgāra ekarātrīṃ vihareyaṃ; na me mahāśramaṇa aguru; api tu tatrāśīviṣo nāgaḥ prativasati; mā te sa viheṭhayiṣyati; aṅga tvaṃ kāśyapa anujānīhi na me sa viheṭayiṣyati; sacen mahāśramaṇa na te viheṭhayati tatra mahāśramaṇa vihara yathāsukham eva; (
children.translated_text: ) To <s>Urubilvā Kāśyapa</s> the matted-hair ascetic seated to one side, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'If it is not burdensome to you, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, may I spend a single night in your fire-hall?' 'It is not burdensome to me, Great Ascetic. But a venomous <s>Nāga</s> (serpent) dwells there. He might harm you.' 'Please give me permission, <s>Kāśyapa</s>; he will not harm me.' 'If, Great Ascetic, he does not harm you, then dwell there, Great Ascetic, at your ease.' (
CPS 24a.9

children.text: ) atha bhagavān bahir agnyāgārasya pādau prakṣālya agnyāgāraṃ parviśya nyaṣīdat paryaṅkam ābhujya ṛjuṃ kāyaṃ praṇidhāya pratimukhāṃ smṛtim upasthāpya; adrākṣīd āśīviṣo nāgo bhagavantaṃ dūrata eva; dṛṣṭvā ca krodhānubhāvena dhūmayati; bhagavān apy ṛddhyānubhāvena dhūmayati; athāśiviṣo nāgaḥ krodhānubhāvena prajvalitaḥ; bhagavāṃś ca tejodhātusamādhiṃ samāpannaḥ; athāśīviṣasya nāgasya krodhānubhāvena bhagavataś ca ṛddhyānubhāvena sarvo 'gnyāgāra ādīptaḥ pradīptaḥ saṃprajvalita ekajvalībhūto dhyāyati; adrākṣīd urubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo rātryāḥ pratyūṣasamaye nakṣatrāṇi vyavalokayamānaḥ sarvam agnyāgāram ādīptaṃ pradīptaṃ saṃprajvalitam ekajvalībhūtaṃ dhyāyantaṃ; (

) dṛṣṭvā ca tasyaitad abhavat: tathā prāsādiko mahāśramaṇaḥ; mā haivāśīviṣeṇa nāgena bhasmīkṛto bhaviṣyati; hā kaṣṭaṃ mama vacanaṃ nāśrauṣīt; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: dharmadeśanārthāya urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya sapariṣatkasya yanv ahaṃ tadrūpān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān abhisaṃskuryāṃ yathāśīviṣasya nāgasya tejasā tejaḥ paryādadyāṃ na cāsya kāyaḥ klāmyeta dāntaṃ ca taṃ kṛtvā pātreṇādāya urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya prayaccheyam; atha bhagavān tadrūpān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān abhisaṃkaroti yathā samāhite citte āśīviṣasya nāgasya tejasā tejaḥ paryādadāti na cāsya kāyaḥ klāmyati; dāntaṃ ca taṃ kṛtvā pātreṇādāya yenorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilas tenopajagāma; (

) tatredānīṃ bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapade viharati vanagulmake; athāpareṇa samayenorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya sarvo 'gnyāgāra ādīptaḥ pradīptaḥ saṃprajvalita ekajvālībhūto dhyāyati (

children.text: ) tatredānīṃ bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapade viharati vanagulmake; tena khalu samayenorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāvasathe saptāhiko yajñaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavat: saced māgadhakā manuṣyā jānīyur evaṃmahardhiko mahāśramaṇa evaṃmahānubhāvaḥ sthānam etad vidyate yad asyaiva kārā kartavyā manyeran na tathā mama; aho bata mahāśramaṇa idaṃ saptāham evānyatra viprakrameta; atha bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya cetasā cittam ājñāya tat saptāham evānyatra viprakrāntaḥ; tat khalu saptāham urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya mahāṃ lābhasatkāraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ prabhūtaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ saṃpannaṃ mahājanakāyaś ca vaśe vṛttaḥ; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya tasya saptāhasyātyayād etad abhavat: aho tat saptāhaṃ me mahāṃ lābhasatkāraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ prabhūtaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ saṃpannaṃ mahājanakāyaś ca vaśe vṛttaḥ; aho bata mahāśramaṇa āgacchet so 'pītaḥ paribhuṃjīta; atha bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya cetasā cittam ājñāya yenorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilas tenopajagāma (
children.translated_text: ) At that time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, in a forest thicket. At that time, a seven-day sacrifice had arisen at the dwelling of the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>. Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> thought: 'If the people of <s>Magadha</s> were to know that the Great Ascetic is of such great supernatural power and majesty, it is possible that they would think that offerings should be made only to him, not to me. Oh, if only the Great Ascetic would go elsewhere for these seven days!' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the mind of the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> with his own mind, went elsewhere for those very seven days. During those seven days, a great gain and honor arose for the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> — abundant hard and soft food was prepared, and a great crowd of people was under his sway. Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, after the passing of those seven days, thought: 'During those seven days, great gain and honor arose for me — abundant hard and soft food was prepared, and a great crowd of people was under my sway. Oh, if only the Great Ascetic would come! He too should partake of this.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the mind of the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> with his own mind, approached the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>. (

children.text: ) adrākṣīd urubilvākāśyapo bhagavantaṃ dūrata eva; dṛṣṭvā ca punar evam āha: āgato 'si mahāśramaṇa; āgato 'smi kāśyapa; kasyārthaṃ tvaṃ mahāśramaṇa tat saptāham evānyatra viprakrāntaḥ; nanu te kāśyapa etad abhūd yadi māgadhakā manuṣyā jānīyur evaṃmaharddhiko mahāśramaṇa evaṃmahānubhāvaḥ sthānam etad vidyate yad asyaiva pūrvavad yāvad aho bata mahāśramaṇa idaṃ saptāham evānyatra viprakrameta; evaṃ mahāśramaṇa; ahaṃ tava cetasā cittam ājñāyānyatra viprakrāntaḥ; kasyārthaṃ tvaṃ mahāśramaṇa āgataḥ; nanu te kāśyapa tasya saptāhasyātyayād etad abhavad aho tat saptāhaṃ me mahāṃ lābhasatkāraḥ prādurbhūtaḥ prabhūtaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ saṃpannaṃ mahājanakāyaś ca vaśe vṛttaḥ; aho bata mahāśraṃaṇa āgacchet so 'pītaḥ paribhuṃjīta; evaṃ mahāśramaṇa; ahaṃ tava cetasā cittam ājñāyāgataḥ; paribhuṃktāṃ mahāśramaṇo yathāsukham eva; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavad āścaryaṃ yāvan maharddhiko mahāśramaṇo mahānubhāvaḥ; api tv aham apy arhan
children.translated_text: ) The matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> from afar. Having seen, he said: 'You have come, Great Ascetic!' 'I have come, <s>Kāśyapa</s>.' 'For what purpose, Great Ascetic, did you go elsewhere for those seven days?' 'Did you not, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, have this thought: "If the people of <s>Magadha</s> were to know that the Great Ascetic is of such great supernatural power and majesty, it is possible that they would think that offerings should be made only to him" — as before, up to — "Oh, if only the Great Ascetic would go elsewhere for these seven days"?' 'Indeed so, Great Ascetic.' 'I, knowing your mind, went elsewhere.' 'For what purpose have you come, Great Ascetic?' 'Did you not, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, after the passing of those seven days, have this thought: "During those seven days, great gain and honor arose for me — abundant hard and soft food was prepared, and a great crowd of people was under my sway. Oh, if only the Great Ascetic would come! He too should partake of this"?' 'Indeed so, Great Ascetic.' 'I, knowing your mind, have come.' 'Let the Great Ascetic partake at his ease.' Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> thought: 'How wonderful! How great is the supernatural power and majesty of the Great Ascetic! But I too am an <s>Arhat</s>.'

children.translated_text: ) At that time the <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling in the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, in a forest thicket. Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Then, Great Ascetic, dwell nearby. I shall provide for you with provisions.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> accepted the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>'s [invitation] by his silence. Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, having prepared food for the <s>Bhagavān</s>, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is time, Great Ascetic — the freshly-cooked food [is ready]. Let the Great Ascetic do as he sees fit.' 'Then, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, go ahead. I shall come presently.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> had just recently departed, entered such a <s>samādhi</s> that, with his mind concentrated, from the <s>jambu</s> tree by which the continent of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is known, he took a bowl full of <s>jambu</s> fruit endowed with color, fragrance, and flavor, and approached the hermitage of the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>. Having approached, he sat on the seat that had been prepared. Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> arrived afterward. The matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> saw the <s>Bhagavān</s> seated in the hermitage. Having seen, he said: 'You have come, Great Ascetic!' 'I have come, <s>Kāśyapa</s>.' 'What is in your bowl, Great Ascetic?' 'After you had just recently departed, I entered such a <s>samādhi</s> that, with my mind concentrated, from the <s>jambu</s> tree by which <s>Jambudvīpa</s> is known, I took a bowl full of <s>jambu</s> fruit endowed with color, fragrance, and flavor, and came. If you wish, partake.' 'Let the Great Ascetic partake at his ease.' Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> thought: 'How wonderful! How great is the supernatural power and majesty of the Great Ascetic! (
) But I too am an <s>Arhat</s>.' (

children.text: ) yathā jambupeśīnāṃ tathāpi āmalakapeśīnām; uttarakurudvīpaṃ gatvā akṛṣṭoptānāṃ taṇḍulaphalaśālīnāṃ pātrapūram ādāya yenorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapadaṃ tenopajagāma; upetya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat; tataḥ paścād āgata urubilvākāśyapo jaṭilaḥ; adrākṣīd urubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo bhagavantam āśramapade niṣaṇṇam; dṛṣṭvā ca punar evam āha: āgato 'si mahāśramaṇa; āgato 'smi kāśyapa; kin nu te mahāśramaṇa pātre; ihāham aciraprakrānte tvayi tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte uttarakurudvīpaṃ gatvā akṛṣṭoptānāṃ taṇḍulaphalaśālīnāṃ pātrapūram ādāya āgataḥ; saced ākāṃkṣasi paribhuṃkṣva; paribhuṃktāṃ mahāśramaṇo yathāsukham eva; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavat: āścaryaṃ yāvan maharddhiko mahāśramaṇo mahānubhāvaḥ; api tv aham apy arhan
o) Śakra supplies the Buddha with water

) tatredānīṃ bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapade viharati vanagulmake; athorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo bhagavato 'rthāya bhojanaṃ pratipādayitvā yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma; upetya bhagavantam idam avocat; samayo mahāśramaṇa sadyo bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ mahāśramaṇaḥ kālaṃ manyate; atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya yenorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapadaṃ tenopajagāma; upetya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat; athorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilaḥ sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ bhagavantaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena pātraṃ pūrayitvā partipāditaḥ; atha bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāntikāt piṇḍapātam ādāya anyatarasmiṃ pradeśe bhaktakṛtyam akārṣīt; tatra bhagavata udakenodakakāryam utpannam; atha śakro devendro bhagavata udakenotpannam udakakāryaṃ viditvā bhagavataḥ purataḥ pāṇinā pṛthivīṃ parāhanti; tatra mahad udapānaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ vāriviṣyandi; yato bhagavān udakakāryam akārṣīt; adrākṣīd urubilvākāśyapo jaṭila āśramapade caṃkraman mahad udapānaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ vāriviṣyandi; dṛṣṭvā ca tasyaitad abhavat: na idaṃ pūrve udapānaṃ mayā dṛṣṭam: etarhi udakaṃ kuta āgatam: athorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma; upetya bhagavantam idam avocat: jānīhi mahāśramaṇa; ihāham āśramapade caṃkramann adrākṣaṃ mahad udapānaṃ vāriviṣyandi; dṛṣṭvā ca mamaitad abhavat: na idaṃ mahāśramaṇa pūrve udapānaṃ mayā dṛṣṭaṃ, etarhi udakaṃ kuta āgataṃ; atra tava kāśyapa antikāt piṇḍapātam ādāya anyatarasmiṃ pradeśe bhaktakṛtyaṃ kṛtvā mama udakenodakakāryam (

) utpannam; atha śakro devendro mama udakenotpannam udakakāryaṃ viditvāsmiṃ pradeśe pāṇinā pṛthivīṃ parāhanti; atra mahad udapānaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ yato 'ham udakenodakakāryam akārṣam; pāṇikhātā nāma kāśyapa eṣā puṣkariṇī; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavat: āścaryaṃ yāvan maharddhiko mahāśramaṇo mahānubhāvaḥ; api tv aham apy arhan
p) An arjuna-tree inclines the branch

) tatredānīṃ bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapade viharati vanagulmake; atha bhagavān sāyāhne pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya yena pāṇikhātā puṣkariṇī tenopajagāma; upetya pāṇikhātāyāḥ puṣkariṇyās tīre ekāntaṃ cīvarakāṇy upanikṣipya pāṇikhātāṃ puṣkariṇīm abhyavagāhya gātrāṇi pariṣicya pāṇikhātāyāḥ puṣkariṇyā uttartukāmo yena kakubhavṛkṣas tena bāhuṃ prasārayati; tataḥ sā mahatī kakubhaśākhā natā yām avalaṃbya bhagavān pāṇikhātāyāḥ puṣkariṇyā uttīrṇaḥ; adrākṣīd urubilvākāśyapo jaṭila āśramapadam anvāhiṇḍan pāṇikhātāyāḥ puṣkariṇyās tīre mahatīṃ kakubhaśākhāṃ natāṃ; dṛṣṭvā ca tasyaitad abhavat: naiṣā me pūrve kakubhaśākhā namati; na ko mahatīṃ kakubhaśākhāṃ namayati; athorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma; upetya bhagavantam idam avocat: jānīhi mahāśramaṇa; ihāhaṃ āśramapadam anvāhiṇḍann adrākṣaṃ pāṇikhātāyāḥ puṣkariṇyās tīre mahatīṃ kakubhaśākhāṃ natām; dṛṣṭvā ca mamaitad abhavat: naiṣā me mahāśramaṇa pūrve kakubhaśākhā namati; mā kaścin mahatīṃ kakubhaśākhāṃ namayati; ihāhaṃ kāśyapa sāyāhne pratisaṃlayanād vyutthāya yena pāṇikhātā puṣkariṇī tenopajagāma; upetya pāṇikhātāyāḥ puṣkariṇyās tīre ekāntaṃ cīvarakāṇy upanikṣipya pāṇikhātāṃ puṣkariṇīm abhyavagāhya; gātrāṇi pariṣicya pāṇikhātāyāḥ puṣkariṇyā uttartukāmo yena kakubhavṛkṣas tena bāhuṃ prasārayami; tataḥ sā mahatī kakubhaśākhā namati yām avalaṃbya pāṇikhātāyāḥ puṣkariṇyā aham uttīrṇaḥ; bāhugṛhīto nāma kāśyapa eṣa kakubhaḥ; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavat: āścaryaṃ yāvan maharddhiko mahāśramaṇo mahānubhāvaḥ; api tv aham apy arhan
q) Śakra makes the washing of clothes possible
) tatredānīṃ bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapade viharati vanagulmake; tena khalu samayena bhagavataḥ śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni saṃpannāni; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: kutra nv ahaṃ śāṇakāni (

) pāṃsukūlāni praviṣiṃceyam; atha khalu śakro devendro bhagavataś cetasā cittam ājñāyānyatarasmāt pradeśāṃ mahatīṃ pāṣāṇaśilām ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma; upetya bhagavantam idam avocat: iha bhagavāñ śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni praviṣiṃcatu; tatra bhagavatā śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni praviṣiktāni; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: kutra nv ahaṃ śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni śocayeyam; atha khalu śakro devendro bhagavataś cetasā cittam ājñāyānyatarasmāt pradeśān mahatīṃ pāṣāṇaśilām ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma; upetya bhagavantam idam avocat: iha bhagavāñ śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni śocayatu; tatra bhagavatā śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni śocitāni; adrākṣīd urubilvākāśyapa āśramapadam anvāhiṇḍaṃs te mahatyau pāśāṇaśile; dṛṣṭvā ca tasyaitad abhavat: naite mahatyau pāṣāṇaśile pūrve abhūtam; kena te etarhy ānīte; atha urubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma; upetya bhagavantam idam avocat: jānīhi mahāśramaṇa; ihāham āśramapadam anvāhiṇḍann adrākṣaṃ mahatyau pāṣāṇaśile; dṛṣṭvā ca mamaitad abhavat: naite mahatyau pāṣāṇaśile pūrve abhūtam; kena te etarhy ānīte; iha mama kāśyapa śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni saṃpannāni; tasya me etad abhavat: kutra nv ahaṃ śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni praviṣiṃceyam; atha khalu śakro devendro mama cetasā cittam ājñāyānyatarasmāt pradeśāṃ mahatīṃ pāṣāṇaśilām ādāya yenāhaṃ tenopajagāma; upetya mām idam avocat: iha bhagavāñ śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni praviṣiṃcatu; tatra mayā śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni praviṣiktāni; tasya me etad abhavat: kutra nv ahaṃ śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni śocayeyam; atha khalu śakro devendro mama cetasā cittam ājñāyānyatarasmāt pradeśān mahatīṃ pāṣāṇaśilām ādāya yenāhaṃ tenopajagāma; upetya mām idam avocat: iha bhagavāñ śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni śocayatu; tatra mayā śāṇakāni pāṃsukūlāni śocitāni; yakṣāhṛtā nāma kāśyapa eṣā mahatī pāṣāṇaśilā; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavat: āścaryaṃ yāvan maharddhiko mahāśramaṇo mahānubhāvaḥ; api tv aham apy arhan
r) Buddha's command on the element water

) tatredānīṃ bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapade viharati vanagulmake; tena khalu samayena nairaṃjanāyā mahodakavāhaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ; atha bhagavān sādhikapauruṣeṇodakaskandhena parikṣipto reṇuhate 'bhyavakāśe caṃkramati; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavat: tathā prāsādiko mahāśramaṇaḥ; mā haivodakavāhena hṛto bhaviṣyati iti mahāśramaṇaṃ samanveṣiṣyāmīty ekavṛkṣikāṃ (

) nāvam adhirohan bhagavantaṃ samanveṣati; adrākṣīd urubilvākāsyapo jaṭilo bhagavantaṃ sādhikapauruṣeṇodakaskandhena parikṣiptaṃ reṇuhate 'bhyavakāśe caṃkramantam; dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhagavantam idam avocat: jīvasi mahāśramaṇa; jīvāmi kāśyapa; adhiroha mahāśramaṇa; adhirokṣyasi mahāśramaṇa ekavṛkṣikāṃ nāvam; adhirohāmi kāśyapa; atha bhagavata etad abhavat: yanv ahaṃ tadrūpān ṛddhyābhisaṃskārān abhisaṃskuryāṃ yathā samāhite citte yathodakam eva ekavṛkṣikāṃ nāvam adhiroheyam; atha bhagavān tadrūpan ṛddhyābhisaṃskārān abhisaṃskaroti yathā samāhite citte yathodakam eva ekavṛkṣikāṃ nāvam adhirohati; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavat: āścaryaṃ yāvan maharddhiko mahāśramaṇo mahānubhāvaḥ; api tv aham apy arhan
Conversion of Urubilvākāśyapa and of his five hundred students

) atha bhagavān urubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya cetasā cittaṃ ājñāya urubilvākāśyapaṃ jaṭilam idam avocat: naiva tvaṃ kāśyapārhan naivārhatvaphalasākṣātkriyāṃ samāpanno naivājānāsy arhatvamārgam; athorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyaitad abhavat: jānāti me mahāśramaṇaś cetasā cittam; iti viditvā bhagavantam idam avocat: labheyāhaṃ mahāśramaṇasyāntike pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam; careyam ahaṃ mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryam; atha bhagavān urubilvākāśyapam āmantrayate: avalokitā te kāśyapa pariṣan no śramaṇa; tena hi kāśyapa pariṣadaṃ tāvad avalokaya; pariṣadavalokanam eva sādhu yathāpitat tvādṛśānāṃ yaśasvināṃ jñātamanuṣyāṇām; athorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo māṇavakān āmantrayati: ahaṃ māṇavakā mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyāmi; bhavantaḥ kiṃ kariṣyanti; yat kiñcid vayam upādhyāya prajānīmaḥ sarvaṃ tad upādhyāyam āgamya; saced upādhyāyo mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyati te vayam upādhyāyaṃ pravrajitam anupravrajiṣyāmaḥ; tena hi yūyaṃ māṇavakā etāny ajināni valkalāni daṇḍakamaṇḍalūni srugbhājanāni nadyāṃ nairaṃjanāyāṃ prakṣipata; evam upādhyāya; iti te māṇavakā ajināni valkalāni daṇḍakamaṇḍalūni srugbhājanāni nadyāṃ nairaṃjanāyāṃ prakṣipya yenorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilas tenopajagmuḥ; upetyorubilvākāśyapaṃ jaṭilam idam avocan: upādhyāya evam asmābhiḥ kṛtam; asti kiṃcit karaṇīyam; athorubilvākāsyapo jaṭilaḥ paṃcaśataṃ jaṭilamāṇavakān ādāya yena bhagavāṃs tenopajagāma; upetya bhagavantam idam avocat: avalokitā me mahāśramaṇa pariṣat; labheyāhaṃ svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ (
children.translated_text: ) Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known the mind of the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> with his own mind, said this to the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>: 'You, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, are not an <s>Arhat</s>, nor have you attained the direct realization of the fruit of <s>Arhatship</s>, nor do you know the path to <s>Arhatship</s>.' Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> thought: 'The Great Ascetic knows my mind with his mind.' Knowing this, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I obtain ordination (<s>pravrajyā</s>), full ordination (<s>upasaṃpad</s>), and monkhood (<s>bhikṣubhāva</s>) in the presence of the Great Ascetic. I would practice the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) under the Great Ascetic.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>: 'You have consulted your assembly, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, not a mere ascetic. Therefore, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, first consult your assembly. Consulting the assembly is indeed proper, as befits renowned men of good family such as yourself.' Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> addressed the young students: 'Students, I shall practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic. What will you do?' 'Whatever we know, teacher, all of that depends on you. If the teacher will practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic, then we, following our ordained teacher, shall go forth as well.' 'In that case, students, cast these antelope skins, bark garments, staffs, water-pots, ladles, and vessels into the river <s>Nairaṃjanā</s>.' 'Yes, teacher.' Those students, having cast the antelope skins, bark garments, staffs, water-pots, ladles, and vessels into the river <s>Nairaṃjanā</s>, approached the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>. Having approached, they said to the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>: 'Teacher, we have done as instructed. Is there anything further to be done?' Then the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, taking five hundred matted-hair students, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'I have consulted my assembly, Great Ascetic. May I obtain ordination, full ordination, (
SBV I 229

children.text: ) bhikṣubhāvam; careyam ahaṃ mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryam; labdhavān urubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam; sā evāsyāyuṣmataḥ pravrajyābhūd upasaṃpad bhikṣubhāvaḥ
children.translated_text: ) and monkhood (<s>bhikṣubhāva</s>) in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. I would practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic.' The matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> obtained the holy life in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. That itself was the Venerable One's ordination, full ordination, and monkhood.

children.text: Conversion of Nadī- and Gayākāśyapa with their two hundred and fifty students
children.translated_text: Conversion of <s>Nadī</s>- and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s> with their two hundred and fifty students
CPS 25b.1

children.text: ) tena khalu samayenorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasya nadīgayākāśyapau bhrātarāv ardhatṛtīyaśataparivārau nadyā nairaṃjanāyā adhastādbhāgenāśramapade śāmyete; adrāṣṭāṃ nadīgayākāśyapau bhrātarāv ajināni valkalāni daṇḍakamaṇḍalūni srugbhājanāni nadyāṃ nairaṃjanāyām uhyamānāni; dṛṣṭvā ca kāśyapayor etad abhavat: mā haivāvayoḥ sabrahmacāriṇāṃ kaścid evādīnavo bhaviṣyati rājato vā caurato vā agnito vā udakato vā; yanv cāvāṃ sabrahmacāriṇo 'nveṣeva; atha nadīgayākāśyapau bhrātarāv anveṣantāv urubilvākāśyapaṃ yenorubilvākāśyapasya jaṭilasyāśramapadam tenopajagmatuḥ; tena samayenorubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo muṇḍaḥ saṃghāṭīprāvṛto bhagavataḥ purato niṣaṇṇaḥ dharmaśravaṇāya; apaśyatāṃ nadīgayākāśyapau bhrātarāv urubilvākāśyapaṃ jaṭilaṃ muṇḍaṃ saṃghāṭīprāvṛtaṃ bhagavataḥ purato niṣaṇṇaṃ dharmaśravaṇāya; dṛṣṭvā coruvilvākāsyapaṃ jaṭilam idam ūcatuḥ; etat kāśyapa varaṃ nedam; idaṃ kāśyapau varaṃ naitat; atha nadīgayākāśyapayor etad abhavat: na batāvaro buddho bhaviṣyati nāvaraṃ dharmākhyānaṃ yatredānīṃ urubilvākāśyapo jaṭilo jīrṇo vṛddho mahallakaḥ sa viṃśativarṣaśatiko jātyā māgadhakānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito 'rhan sammataḥ sa mahāśramaṇasyāntike dvir api pravrajyām upagataḥ; yanv āvām api mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryāṃ careva; iti viditvā bhagavantam idam avocatāṃ: labhevahy āvāṃ mahāśramaṇa svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam; careva āvāṃ mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryam; avalokitā vāṃ kāśyapau pariṣan no mahaśramaṇa; tena hi kāśyapau pariṣadaṃ tāvad avalokayatām; pariṣadavalokanam eva sādhu yathāpitad yuṣmadvidhānāṃ yaśasvināṃ jñātamanuṣyāṇām; atha nadīgayākāśyapau bhrātarau yena svakīyāśramas tenopajagmatuḥ; upetya svakān māṇavakān idam avocatām: āvāṃ māṇavakā mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyāvaḥ; bhavantaḥ kiṃ kariṣyanti; yat kiṃcid vayam upādhyāyau prajānīmaḥ sarvaṃ tad upādhyāyāv āgamya; saced upādhyāyau mahāśramaṇasyāntike brahmacaryaṃ cariṣyatas te vayam upādhyāyau pravrajitāv anupravrajiṣyāmaḥ; children.translated_text: ) At that time, the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> had two brothers, <s>Nadīkāśyapa</s> and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>, with a retinue of two hundred and fifty, dwelling at a hermitage downstream on the river <s>Nairaṃjanā</s>. The two brothers <s>Nadī</s>- and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s> saw antelope skins, bark garments, staffs, water-pots, ladles, and vessels being carried along in the river <s>Nairaṃjanā</s>. Having seen, the two <s>Kāśyapas</s> thought: 'Let no misfortune befall our fellow practitioners — whether from a king, a thief, fire, or water. Let us go search for our fellow practitioners.' Then the two brothers <s>Nadī</s>- and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>, searching, approached <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>'s hermitage. At that time, the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> was sitting tonsured, wrapped in a <s>saṃghāṭī</s> robe, before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, listening to the <s>Dharma</s>. The two brothers <s>Nadī</s>- and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s> saw the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s> sitting tonsured, wrapped in a <s>saṃghāṭī</s> robe, before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, listening to the <s>Dharma</s>. Having seen, they said to the matted-hair ascetic <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>: 'Is this better, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, or is this not?' '<s>Kāśyapas</s>, this is better, not that.' Then the two <s>Nadī</s>- and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s> thought: 'The <s>Buddha</s> must indeed not be inferior, nor the <s>Dharma</s>-teaching inferior, since even now <s>Urubilvākāśyapa</s>, the matted-hair ascetic — old, aged, elderly, one hundred and twenty years of age by birth, honored, esteemed, respected, worshipped, regarded as worthy, accepted by the <s>Māgadha</s> people — has gone forth a second time under the Great Ascetic. Let us too practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic.' Knowing this, they said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May we, Great Ascetic, obtain ordination, full ordination, and monkhood in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. We would practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic.' 'Have you consulted your assemblies, <s>Kāśyapas</s>? Not a mere great ascetic. Therefore, <s>Kāśyapas</s>, first consult your assemblies. Consulting the assembly is indeed proper, as befits renowned men of good family such as yourselves.' Then the two brothers <s>Nadī</s>- and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s> went to their own hermitage. Having arrived, they said to their own students: 'Students, we shall practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic. What will you do?' 'Whatever we know, teachers, all of that depends on you. If our teachers will practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic, then we, following our ordained teachers, shall go forth as well.' 'If so, students, the time is now.' Then the two brothers <s>Nadī</s>- and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s>,

Having approached, they said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'We have consulted our assemblies, Great Ascetic. May we obtain ordination, full ordination, and monkhood in the presence of the Great Ascetic. We would practice the holy life under the Great Ascetic.' The two brothers <s>Nadī</s>- and <s>Gayākāśyapa</s> obtained the holy life from the <s>Bhagavān</s>. body.text: The sermon at Gayāśīrṣa
body.translated_text: The sermon at <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s>

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tad jaṭilasahasraṃ pravrājayitvopasaṃpādayitvā yathābhiramyam urubilvāyāṃ vihṛtya yena gayā tena cāryāṃ prakrāntaḥ; anupūrveṇa cāryāṃ caran gayām anuprāptaḥ; viharati gayāśīrṣe caitye sārdhaṃ bhikṣusahasreṇa sarvaiḥ purāṇajaṭilaiḥ; tatra bhagavāṃs tad bhikṣusahasraṃ tṛbhiḥ prātihāryair avavadati; ṛddhiprātihāryeṇādeśanāprātihāryeṇānuśāsanīprātihāryeṇa; tatredaṃ bhagavata ṛddhiprātihāryam; atha bhagavāṃs tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte svasminn āsane 'ntarhitaḥ pūrvasyān diśy upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya caturvidham īryāpathaṃ kalpayati caṃkramati tiṣṭhati niṣīdati śayyāṃ kalpayati; tejodhātum api samāpadyate; tejodhātuṃ samāpannasya buddhasya bhagavato vividhāny arcīṃṣi kāyān niścaranti nīlāni pītāni lohitāny avadātāni māṃjiṣṭhāni spaṭikavarṇāni; yamakāni ca prātihāryāṇi vidarśayati; adhaḥ kāyaḥ prajvalati; uparimāt kāyāc chītalā vāridhārāḥ syandante; uparimaḥ kāyaḥ prajvalati; adhaḥ kāyāc chītalā vāridhārāḥ syandante; evaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ paścimasyām uttarasyān diśy; atha caturdiśaṃ caturvidhaṃ vividham ṛddhiprātihāryaṃ vidarśayitvā tān ṛddhyabhisaṃskārān pratiprasrabhya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane nyaṣīdat; idaṃ tatra bhagavata ṛddhiprātihāryam; tatredaṃ bhagavata ādeśanāprātihāryam; yuṣmākaṃ bhikṣavaś cittam evam; mana idam; vijñānam idaṃ; vitarkayatedaṃ mā vitarkayatedam; manasikurutedaṃ; na manasikurutedam; prajahatedaṃ; mā prajahatedam; idaṃ kāyena sākṣātkṛtvopasaṃpadya viharata; idaṃ tatra bhagavatā ādeśanāprātihāryam; tatredaṃ bhagavato 'nuśāsanīprātihāryam; sarvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ ādīptaṃ; kiṃ ca sarvam ādīptaṃ; cakṣur ādīptaṃ rūpaṃ cakṣurvijñānaṃ cakṣuḥsaṃsparśaḥ; yad api cakṣuḥsaṃsparśapratyayam ādhyātmam utpadyate vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkham asukhaṃ vā tad apy ādīptaṃ; evaṃ śrotraṃ ghrāṇaṃ jihvā kāyo mana ādīptam; ādīptaṃ manovijñānaṃ manaḥsaṃsparśaḥ; yad api manaḥsaṃsparśapratyayam (
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having ordained and fully admitted that thousand matted-hair ascetics, and having dwelt at <s>Urubilvā</s> as long as he wished, set out on his journey toward <s>Gayā</s>. Traveling by stages, he reached <s>Gayā</s>. He dwelt at the <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s> shrine together with a thousand monks, all former matted-hair ascetics. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> instructed that thousand monks by means of three miracles (<s>prātihārya</s>): the miracle of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhiprātihārya</s>), the miracle of mind-reading (<s>ādeśanāprātihārya</s>), and the miracle of instruction (<s>anuśāsanīprātihārya</s>). Herein, this was the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s miracle of supernatural power: the <s>Bhagavān</s> entered such a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) that, with his mind composed, he vanished from his own seat and, rising up into the sky in the eastern direction, manifested the four modes of deportment — he walked, stood, sat, and lay down. He also entered the fire-element (<s>tejodhātu</s>). When the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> had entered the fire-element, various rays emanated from his body — blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored. He also displayed the twin miracles (<s>yamaka prātihārya</s>): from the lower part of his body flames blazed forth; from the upper part of his body cool streams of water flowed. From the upper part of his body flames blazed forth; from the lower part of his body cool streams of water flowed. Likewise in the southern, western, and northern directions. Then, having displayed in the four directions the fourfold, manifold miracle of supernatural power, withdrawing those volitional formations of supernatural power, he sat down on the very seat prepared before the community of monks. This was the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s miracle of supernatural power therein. Herein, this was the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s miracle of mind-reading: 'Your minds, monks, are thus; your mental intentions are this; your consciousness is this; you think this — do not think that; attend to this — do not attend to that; abandon this — do not abandon that; directly realize this and dwell having attained it.' This was the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s miracle of mind-reading therein. Herein, this was the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s miracle of instruction: 'Everything, monks, is burning. And what is everything that is burning? The eye is burning; visible form is burning; eye-consciousness is burning; eye-contact is burning. Whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact — whether pleasant, painful, or neither pleasant nor painful — that too is burning. Likewise the ear, the nose, the tongue, the body, and the mind are burning. Mind-consciousness is burning; mind-contact is burning. Whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact,

body.text: ) adhyātmam utpadyate vedayitaṃ sukhaṃ vā duḥkhaṃ vā aduḥkham asukhaṃ vā tad apy ādīptaṃ; kenādīptaṃ; rāgāgninā dveṣāgninā mohāgninā; ādīptaṃ jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ; ādiptaṃ duḥkheneti; idaṃ tatra bhagavato 'nuśasanīprātihāryam; asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe tasya bhikṣusahasrasyānupādāyāsravebhyaś cittaṃ vimuktaṃ
body.translated_text: ) whether pleasant, painful, or neither pleasant nor painful — that too is burning. Burning with what? Burning with the fire of passion (<s>rāga</s>), the fire of hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), the fire of delusion (<s>moha</s>). Burning with birth, old age, sickness, death, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish. Burning with suffering.' This was the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s miracle of instruction therein. While this discourse was being spoken, the minds of that thousand monks were liberated from the defilements (<s>āsrava</s>) through non-clinging.

body.text: Story of Kauṇḍinya

bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ asminn eva bhadrake kalpe varṣasahasrāyuṣi prajāyāṃ kāśyapo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi, vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān; *sa vārāṇasīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati karakacchedake parvate; yāvad apareṇa samayena kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya, pātracīvaram ādāya vārāṇasīṃ praviśati; pañcamātrāṇi ca goṣṭhikaśatāni nirgacchanti; adrākśus te goṣṭhikās taṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṅkṛtam, aśityā cānuvyañjanair virājitagatram, vyāmaprabhālaṅkṛtaṃ, sūryasahasrātirekaprabham, jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam; sahadarśanāc ca prasādajātāḥ sañjalpaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ: bhavanto 'smābhir asya sakāśe pravrajitavyam iti; teṣām evaṃ kṛtasaṅketānāṃ kecin mahāsamudram avatīrṇāh; kecid deśāntaraṃ gatāḥ; kecit kāladharmeṇa saṃyuktāḥ; ṣodaśajanāḥ pariśiṣṭāḥ; te kara<ka>cchedakaṃ parvataṃ gatvā kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya sakāśe pravrajitāḥ; te tatra dhyānādhyayanayogenāvasthitāḥ; yāvad apareṇa samayena kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalaṃ buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgniḥ ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtah; teṣāṃ devatābhir ārocitam: bhavantaḥ kāśyapaḥ parinirvṛtaḥ; saptāhaparinirvṛtasya cāsya śāsanam antarhitam; kiṃ yūyam aphalakaṃbukā puratastiṣṭhata iti; te śrutvā akṛtakāryatvān mahatā duḥkhenābhyāhatāh; pañca sahaśravaṇād eva karakacchedakāt parvatād avatīrya vārāṇasīṃ praviṣṭāḥ; ṣaḍbhis tenaiva saṃvegena vīryam avalambya pratyekabodhiḥ sākṣātkṛtā; pañca paścād avatīrya vārāṇasīṃ praveṣṭum (

children.text: ) ārabdhāḥ; yāvac chakaṭasārtho nirgacchati; ekasya śākaṭikasya balīvardā durbalāḥ; sa tān pratodayaṣṭyā bhūyo tāḍayati; durbalaprāṇatvān na śaknuvanti gantum; sa ca śākaṭikas tasya śakaṭasārthasyāgrato yāyī; sa tair bhikṣubhir uktaḥ: bhoḥ śākaṭika taveme balīvardā durbalāḥ; kim etān pratodayaṣṭyā bhūyobhūyas tāḍayasi? yadi na śaknuvanti gantum, visrabdhagatipracāratayā pṛṣṭhato 'nugaccheti; sa kathayati: mamāgrato gacchato na śakyam anena śakaṭasārthena sārdhaṃ gantum; yady ahaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nugacchāmi, nūnam ayaṃ śakaṭasārtho chorayitvā gacchatīti; te śākaṭikasyāntike asadvikalpasaṃjñanitavaimukhyāḥ parasparaṃ kathayanti: bhavantaḥ kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe parinirvṛte vayaṃ vilambitā ity anenāsmākam eṣā codanā kṛtā; yan nu vayaṃ vīryam ārabhemahi; iti viditvā gāthāṃ bhāṣante:
children.translated_text: ) and set out. Just then a cart-caravan was departing. One carter's oxen were weak. He kept striking them again and again with a goad-stick. Being of feeble strength, they were unable to move. That carter was one who traveled at the front of the caravan. Those monks said to him: 'Good carter, your oxen are weak. Why do you keep striking them again and again with a goad-stick? If they cannot move, let them go at a relaxed pace and follow behind.' He said: 'When I go at the front, I cannot travel together with this caravan. If I follow behind, the caravan will surely leave me behind and go on.' Those monks, turning away from the carter's improper thought, said to each other: 'Sirs, we have been delayed while <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> — by this we have been admonished. Let us therefore exert effort.' Having understood, they spoke a verse:

children.text: yady apy antarhito dharmaḥ kāśyapasya mahāmuneḥ /
children.translated_text: Though the <s>Dharma</s> of <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the great sage, has disappeared,
we shall not let our effort, taught by the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, slacken. //

body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), when the lifespan of beings was a thousand years, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (perfectly awakened one) named <s>Kāśyapa</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone (<s>Sugata</s>), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. He dwelt near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> on Mount <s>Karakacchedaka</s>. Then at a later time, <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robes, entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Five hundred assemblies of guild-members were going out. Those guild-members saw the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great man, his body resplendent with eighty minor characteristics, adorned with the radiance of a fathom-wide aura, surpassing in brilliance a thousand suns, like a moving jewel-mountain, auspicious on all sides. At the very sight, faith arose in them and they began to discuss: 'Sirs, we should go forth in his presence.' But of those who had thus made this agreement, some crossed the great ocean; some went to other lands; some died. Sixteen persons remained. They went to Mount <s>Karakacchedaka</s> and went forth in the presence of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. They remained there, engaged in the practice of meditation and study. Then at a later time, <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, having completed all the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without residue at <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> in the Deer Park. The deities informed them: 'Sirs, <s>Kāśyapa</s> has attained final <s>nirvāṇa</s>. Seven days after his <s>parinirvāṇa</s>, his teaching has disappeared. Why do you stand here fruitless and without achievement?' Hearing this, stricken with great sorrow at not having accomplished their goal, five of them immediately descended from Mount <s>Karakacchedaka</s> and entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Six of them, through that very sense of urgency, mustered effort and directly realized <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (solitary awakening). Five others descended later to enter <s>Vārāṇasī</s> (

children.text: parikṣayaṃ na yāsyanti yady apy asmākam āsrāvāḥ /
children.translated_text: Though our <s>āsravas</s> (defilements) may not be completely exhausted,
we shall become foremost among the disciples of the <s>Śākyasiṃha</s> (Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>), the Protector. //

body.text: te vārāṇasīṃ praviśya piṇḍapātaṃ caritvā punar api karakacchedakaṃ parvataṃ gatvā dhyānādhyayanayogenāvasthitāḥ; teṣāṃ catvāraḥ kālagatāḥ; eko 'vasthitaḥ; sa utsuka udānam udānayati: ayam eva sa karakacchedakaḥ parvato yatra mayā kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ paryupāsitaḥ; dṛṣṭaś ca tasya viṃśatibhikṣusaharāṇām ekaḥ
body.translated_text: They entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, went on alms-round, and again went to Mount <s>Karakacchedaka</s>, where they remained engaged in the practice of meditation and study. Of them, four died. One remained. He, longing, uttered an inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>): 'This is that very Mount <s>Karakacchedaka</s> where I attended upon <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. And I saw that of his twenty thousand monks, he was the only one

body.text:
sakalajambūdvīpe 'pi saṅghāṭīdhvajadhārīti; sa praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: yan mayā bhagavati kāśyape samyaksaṃbuddhe yāvadāyur brahmacaryaṃ caritam; na kaścid guṇagaṇo 'dhigataḥ; anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena yo 'sau bhagavatā kāśyapena samyaksaṃbuddhena uttaro nāma māṇavo vyākṛtaḥ, bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ māṇava varṣaśatāyuṣi prajāyāṃ śākyamunir nāma tathāgataḥ arhan samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ iti; tasyāhaṃ śāsane pravrajya tatprathamataḥ sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkuryām; māṃ ca bhagavān śākyamuniḥ saṅghāṭīdhvajadhāriṇām agraṃ nirdiśed iti.
  kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ? yo 'sau tena kālena samayena bhagavataḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya parinirvṛtasya viṃśatibhikṣusaharāṇām (
body.translated_text:
in all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s> to bear the banner of the patchwork robe (<s>saṅghāṭī</s>).' He began to make a vow: 'By all the holy life I have lived as long as life lasted under the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, yet I have not attained any qualities — by this root of merit, may I, in the dispensation of that one whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> prophesied about, the young man named <s>Uttara</s>: "You, young man, when the lifespan of beings is a hundred years, will become a <s>Tathāgata</s> named <s>Śākyamuni</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>" — in his dispensation, having gone forth, may I be the very first to realize <s>Arhatship</s> through the complete abandonment of all defilements. And may the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śākyamuni</s> designate me as foremost among those who bear the banner of the patchwork robe.'
What do you think, monks? He who at that time, after the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, was the one monk remaining of twenty thousand (

body.text: SBV II 4

) sakalajambūdvīpe eko bhikṣur avaśiṣṭaḥ saṅghāṭīdhvajadhārī, yena tatkarakacchedake parvate praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam, eṣa evāsau kauṇḍinyo bhikṣuḥ; tatpraṇidhānvaśād etarhi bhagavatā saṅghāṭīdhvajadhāriṇām agratāyāṃ nirdiṣṭaḥ; iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ, ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ, vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ; tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca, ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogaḥ karaṇīyaḥ; ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam.
  yadā bhagavatā āyuṣmataḥ kauṇḍinyasya ākāryākārya dharmo deśitaḥ, ājñātas te kauṇḍinya dharmaḥ? ājñato bhagavan; ājñatas te kauṇḍinya dharmaḥ? ājñatas sugata, iti, tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātaḥ sarvasaṃśayachettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kiṃ bhadanta ājñātakauṇḍinyena karma kṛtaṃ yenāsya bhagavatā ākāryākārya dharmo deśitaḥ, ājñātas te kauṇḍinya dharmaḥ? ājñato bhagavan; ājñatas te kauṇḍinya dharmaḥ? ājñatas sugata iti; bhagavān āha: kauṇḍinyenaiva bhikṣavo bhikṣuṇā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pūrvavad yāvat phalanti khalu dehinām.
body.translated_text:
) in all of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, the bearer of the patchwork-robe banner, who made that vow on Mount <s>Karakacchedaka</s> — that is none other than this monk <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>. By the power of that vow, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has now designated him as foremost among bearers of the patchwork-robe banner. Thus, monks, the result of exclusively black <s>karmas</s> is exclusively black; of exclusively white ones, exclusively white; of mixed ones, mixed. Therefore, monks, abandoning exclusively black <s>karmas</s> and mixed ones, you should direct your efforts to exclusively white <s>karmas</s> alone. Thus should you train, monks.
When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had taught the Venerable <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> the <s>Dharma</s> of what should and should not be done: 'Have you understood the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>?' 'I have understood, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'Have you understood the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>?' 'I have understood, <s>Sugata</s>.' Then, monks, doubts having arisen, they asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'Venerable Sir, what <s>karma</s> did <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s> perform that the <s>Bhagavān</s> taught him the <s>Dharma</s> of what should and should not be done: "Have you understood the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>?" "I have understood, <s>Bhagavān</s>." "Have you understood the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>?" "I have understood, <s>Sugata</s>."' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> himself, monks, who performed and accumulated <s>karmas</s>, whose conditions were gathered, as before... indeed, <s>karmas</s> ripen for embodied beings.'

body.text:
Story of Kāśisundaraka (Kṣāntivādin)
(concerning a previous birth of Kauṇḍinya)
body.translated_text:
Story of <s>Kāśisundara</s> (<s>Kṣāntivādin</s>)
(concerning a previous birth of <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>)

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ brahmadatto nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati, ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca; so 'pareṇa samayena devyā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati; tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ devī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā; aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā; dārako jātaḥ, abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ; tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate, kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti; amātyāḥ ūcuḥ: deva ācaritaṃ madhyadeśe yo 'bhirūpo bhavati prāsādikaḥ sa sundara ity ucyate; ayaṃ ca dārakaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ, kāśirājasya ca putraḥ; bhavatu dārakasya kāśisundara iti nāmeti; tasya kāśisundara iti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitam; kāśisundaro dārakaḥ aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattaḥ; dvābhyām aṅgadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was exercising sovereignty — it was prosperous, flourishing, secure, abundant in food, and teeming with a great multitude of people. At a later time, while sporting, enjoying, and dallying with his queen, the queen became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, pleasing, endowed with all major and minor limbs. At his birth, having performed the birth-celebration, a name was assigned: 'What shall the boy's name be?' The ministers said: 'Your Majesty, it is the custom in the central land that one who is handsome and pleasing is called <s>Sundara</s> (Beautiful). This boy is handsome, good-looking, and pleasing, and he is the son of the king of <s>Kāśi</s>. Let the boy's name be <s>Kāśisundara</s>.' The name <s>Kāśisundara</s> was assigned. The boy <s>Kāśisundara</s> was given to eight nurses — two body-nurses, two milk-nurses, two

body.text: maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyām; aṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate kṣīreṇa (
body.translated_text: washing-nurses, and two play-nurses. Raised by eight nurses with milk,

body.text: SBV II 5

body.translated_text: ) curds, butter, ghee, skimmed ghee, and other choice provisions, he grew quickly like a lotus in a lake.

children.translated_text: Once again, while the king was sporting, enjoying, and dallying, the queen became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born. On the very day he was born, a great quarrel arose among the citizens and country-folk of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Having performed the birth-celebration, a name was assigned: 'What shall the boy's name be?' The ladies of the inner palace said: 'Your Majesty, at his birth a great quarrel arose among the citizens and country-folk of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. Therefore, let the boy's name be <s>Kalibhū</s> (Born of Strife).' King <s>Brahmadatta</s> was ruling by both righteous and unrighteous means. Prince <s>Kāśisundara</s> saw his father ruling by both righteous and unrighteous means. Having seen, he thought: 'I too, after my father's death, will become king. I too, having ruled by both righteous and unrighteous means, will be destined for hell. Let me go forth from the household life into homelessness.' He approached his father, fell at his feet, and said: 'Father, give permission — I shall go forth from the household life into homelessness.' He said: 'Son, that for the sake of which sacrifices are offered, oblations are poured, and austerities are performed — that kingdom is in the palm of your hand. For whose sake are you renouncing it and going forth?' He spoke a verse:

children.text: varaṃ vane valkalacīravāsasā phalāśinā vyāḍamṛgaiḥ sahoṣitam /
children.translated_text: Better to dwell in the forest clad in bark and hides, eating fruits, living among wild beasts,

children.text: na rājyahetor vadhabandhatāḍanaṃ budhena kartuṃ paralokabhīruṇā // iti;
children.translated_text: than for a wise man fearing the next world to inflict execution, imprisonment, and beating for the sake of kingship. //

body.translated_text: The king said: 'Know this, prince — you are our only son, dear, agreeable, patient, and not unpleasant. We would be separated from you unwillingly only by death, but we shall not abandon you while living.' Prince <s>Kāśisundara</s> said: 'Father, if you will grant permission, that is well. If you will not grant permission, from today I shall neither eat nor drink.' Thereupon Prince <s>Kāśisundara</s> undertook one meal-fast, two, three, up to six meal-fasts.   Then the sons of ministers and sons of the chaplain approached King <s>Brahmadatta</s>. Having approached, they said to King <s>Brahmadatta</s>: 'Please give permission to the dear prince <s>Kāśisundara</s>. What will you do with one who is as if dead? For going forth is praised by the wise. If he finds delight, you will see him alive; if he does not find delight, sages do return. What other course is there for a son, apart from his parents?'
  King <s>Brahmadatta</s> said: 'Young men, if that is so, he has permission.' Then the sons of ministers, sons of the chaplain, and the princes approached prince <s>Kāśisundara</s>. Having approached, they said to prince <s>Kāśisundara</s>: 'Indeed, dear friend prince, you should know — you have been given permission by the king for going forth. Now do as you see fit.'
  Then prince <s>Kāśisundara</s>, having performed the farewell circumambulation, and having generated steadfastness, strength, and vigor of body, departed from <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and went forth among the sages. By his exertion and striving, having cultivated dispassion toward sensual pleasures, he attained <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). He became exceedingly compassionate toward all beings. Through his loving-kindness, even wild beasts came to trust in his hermitage and did no harm. He came to be known by the name <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> (the Patience-preacher). Then, after some time

  Then, after some time, King <s>Kalabhū</s>, when the spring season had arrived, when the trees were in full bloom, went out to the garden grounds together with his inner apartments, to a forest grove resounding with the cries of geese, herons, peacocks, parrots, <s>śārikā</s> birds, cuckoos, and <s>jīvañjīvaka</s> birds. Having enjoyed himself there in the garden, he became weary and was overcome by drowsiness. The womenfolk, greedy for flowers and fruits, began to wander here and there in that garden. Then they saw the sage <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> seated in solitude in a peaceful deportment. Having seen him, their hearts filled with reverence, they paid homage to the sage and stood around him. The sage <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> began to teach the <s>Dharma</s> to those women in a most tranquil deportment. Meanwhile, King <s>Kalabhū</s>, having dispelled the fatigue of sleep, awoke and did not see the women of the inner apartments. Taking his sword, he began to search for the young women. Then he saw them standing around the sage <s>Kṣāntivādin</s>. Having seen this, his mind overwhelmed by anger born of jealousy, he approached the sage. The womenfolk, seeing the king's approach, fled in terror. The king said haughtily to <s>Kṣāntivādin</s>: 'Fellow, who are you?' He said: 'I am <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> (the Patience-preacher).' King <s>Kalabhū</s> said: 'When I am enraged, you claim to be the Patience-preacher? Now let us see whether you are truly patient or not!' Then he cut off his hands. Again he asked: 'Who are you?' He said: '<s>Kṣāntivādin</s>.' Then he cut off his feet. As his limbs were being cut off, he spoke a verse:

children.translated_text: Even if you cut me into a hundred sesame-like pieces and scatter my body on the earth,

children.text: tāṃ notsahe vihantuṃ sutam iva sutavatsalā jananī //
children.translated_text: that I cannot bear to destroy, as a mother loving her child [cannot abandon] her child. //

children.text: janakāyas tām eva rātriṃ balimālyopahāraṃ samudānīya tad udyānaṃ gataḥ; rājā cāntaḥpurasahīyaḥ; tato janakāyena śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavanīpakebhyo dānāni datvā devatāsthāne ca mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā sā devatā kṣamitā; tato rājā ṛṣeḥ kṣāntivādinaḥ sakāśaṃ gatvā pādayor nipatya kṣamayitum ārabdhaḥ: kṣamasva me maharṣe yan mayā viṣayādhyavasitena krodhaparyākulīkṛtamatinā tavāparāddham iti; kṣāntivādī kathayati: kṣāntaṃ mahārāja; yathākathaṃ jñāyate? sa gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: The people, that very night, having gathered offerings of tribute, garlands, and gifts, went to that garden — and the king too, together with his inner apartments. Then the people, having given gifts to ascetics, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the destitute, and beggars, and having performed a great worship at the deity's shrine, propitiated that deity. Then the king, having gone to the sage <s>Kṣāntivādin</s>, fell at his feet and began to ask forgiveness: 'Forgive me, great sage, for I, absorbed in sensual objects and with mind overwhelmed by anger, have wronged you.' <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> said: 'It is forgiven, great king.' 'How is it known [that you have forgiven]?' He spoke a verse:

children.text: gātreṣu vahasi śastraṃ maitrī me sarvasatveṣu /
children.translated_text: You bear a weapon against my limbs, yet <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness) toward all beings is in me.

children.text: yadi saṃśayo 'tra bhavatāṃ paśyata rudhiraṃ prasannaṃ me // iti;
children.translated_text: If there is doubt among you, behold — my blood flows clear! //

children.text: tasya tad rudhiraṃ parāvṛtam; pāpakarmakārī sa rājā prātihāryasandarśanenāpi na śraddhatte; sa bhūyaḥ kathayati, kṣamasva maharṣe; kṣāntaṃ mahārāja; yathākathaṃ jñāyate? tato bodhisatvaḥ chinnāny aṅgapratyaṅgāni yathāsve sthāne sthāpayitvā satyopayācanayā gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: His blood turned back; the evil-doing king was not convinced even by the demonstration of miracles. He again said: 'Forgive me, great sage.' 'It is forgiven, great king.' 'How is it known?' Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having placed his severed limbs back in their proper places, spoke a verse through a declaration of truth (<s>satyopayācanā</s>):

children.text: chidyamāneṣu gātreṣu tvayā rājan yathā na me /
children.translated_text: Just as when my limbs were being cut by you, O king, /

children.text: āghāto 'sti susūkṣmo 'pi syān me kāyas tathā purā // iti;
children.translated_text: there was not even the subtlest anger in me — so may my body be as before. //

children.text: tasya satyopayācanayā śarīraṃ yathāpuraṃ saṃvṛttam; tato rājā vismayotphullalocano gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
children.translated_text: Through his declaration of truth, his body became as before. Then the king, his eyes wide with astonishment, spoke a verse:

children.text: aho vratam idaṃ siddham aho dharmas svanuṣṭhitaḥ /
children.translated_text: Oh, this vow is accomplished! Oh, the <s>Dharma</s> is well-practiced! /

children.text: chidyamāneṣu gātreṣu yasya te nāsti vikriyā //
children.translated_text: He whose limbs are being cut shows no agitation! //

A deity devoted to him then released a calamity upon <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: mice, locusts,
and parrots became numerous; the god did not rain; the people were dying. The king, having summoned the soothsayers, asked: 'Sirs, why does the god not rain? Mice, locusts, and parrots have become numerous, and the people are dying.' They said: 'Your Majesty, it is the wrath of a deity. The deity devoted to the sage <s>Kṣāntivādin</s> is angered; she has released this calamity.' The king said: 'Sirs, what should be done about this?' The soothsayers said: 'Your Majesty, angered deities are propitiated with offerings of tribute, garlands, and gifts. Having made offerings of tribute, garlands, and gifts, you should seek the forgiveness of both the deity and the sage.' Then the king had a bell-proclamation made in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: 'Let the citizens dwelling in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> hear! The deity dwelling in the garden is devoted to the sage <s>Kṣāntivādin</s>. She has released a calamity, due to which the god does not rain; mice, locusts, and parrots have become numerous; and the people are dying. Therefore, for the purpose of averting the calamity, you must go tomorrow to the garden with offerings of tribute, garlands, and gifts, and worship her.' (
