body.translated_text:
In the past, monks, there were two caravan leaders named <s>Viśvabhuj</s> and <s>Suyātra</s>, each with a retinue of forty thousand merchants. Among them, <s>Suyātra</s> delighted in renunciation. He went forth among the sages. Exerting himself alone, without a teacher, without a preceptor, he directly realized the thirty-seven factors of awakening (<s>saptatriṃśad bodhipakṣyā dharmāḥ</s>) and attained <s>Pratyekabodhi</s> (Solitary Awakening). His caravan members, not seeing their caravan leader, began to search here and there. When they could not find him anywhere, they approached the caravan leader <s>Viśvabhuj</s>: 'We have searched but could not find him. What should be done?' He said: 'Wait, do not be hasty. We shall search for the caravan leader.' Then <s>Viśvabhuj</s>, the caravan leader, surrounded by eighty thousand merchants, began to search for the caravan leader <s>Suyātra</s> in parks, rest-houses, and ascetic groves. He was seen and asked: 'Why did you abandon the caravan and go forth?' The teaching of those great beings is physical, not verbal. That caravan leader, together with his retinue, was won over by the miracles of blazing, heating, raining, and flashing. He then told those eighty thousand merchants, having gathered them with material inducements: 'Make offerings to this one. Offerings made to this one will certainly bear fruit.' They made many offerings to him.
What do you think, monks? He who was the caravan leader <s>Viśvabhuj</s> — that was none other than myself (

When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had brought the group of five monks across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> and shared with them the jewels of the faculties, powers, and factors of awakening, and satisfied them with the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts:

body.text: saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhadanta bhagavatā paṃcakā bhikṣavaḥ saṃsārakāntārād uttārya saddharmarasena saṃtarpitā iti; bhagavān āha: kim atra, bhikṣava, āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ mayā vigatarāgeṇa vigatadveṣeṇa vigatamohena parimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ sarvajñena sarvākārajñena sarvajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena paṃcakā bhikṣavaḥ saṃsārakāntārād uttarya saddharmarasena saṃtarpitāḥ; yat tu mayāpi atīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijārāvyadhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ sārthavāhabhūtena paṃcakaiḥ kāntāramārge kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptāḥ salilaṃ vinā prāṇair viyujyamānā devatāyācanaṃ kṛtvā māhendrā salilavarṣeṇa saṃtarpitāḥ; tac chrūyatām.
body.translated_text: 'See, Venerable Sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has brought the group of five monks across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> and satisfied them with the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What is wonderful about this, monks, that now I, who am free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, omniscient, knowing all aspects, having attained mastery over all knowledge and knowable things, have brought the group of five monks across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s> and satisfied them with the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>? But even in the past, when I was still possessed of passion, hatred, and delusion, unliberated from birth, old age, disease, death, sorrow, lamentation, suffering, dejection, and despair, being a caravan leader, the group of five, having reached dire straits on the wilderness road, deprived of water, about to perish, made a prayer to the deities, and were satisfied by a great rain from <s>Māhendra</s> (the domain of <s>Indra</s>). Listen to that.'

body.translated_text: In the past, monks, a caravan leader named <s>Viśvabhuj</s>, accompanied by five hundred merchants, set out trading along a waterless wilderness road. Traveling gradually, he reached the <s>Vindhya</s> forest. All their water was exhausted. The merchant caravan, deprived of water, was on the verge of perishing. Five merchants, unable to obtain water, became extremely agitated. The caravan leader <s>Viśvabhuj</s>, seeing them in such a state, his heart stirred by compassion, facing upward, began to make a prayer to the deities: 'May the honorable gods — <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Kubera</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, and others — hear! By the truth, by this true utterance, that my compassion is equally extended toward all — by this truth, by this true utterance, may the great <s>Māhendra</s> rain fall!' By the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s power, the <s>Māhendra</s> palace was shaken. <s>Śakra</s>, Lord of the Gods, has the ability of knowledge and vision below him. He considered: 'By whom has the <s>Māhendra</s> palace been shaken?' He saw — by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s power. He released such a great <s>Māhendra</s> rain that the merchant caravan was satisfied and crossed over the wilderness road. (

In the past, monks, there was a great caravan leader named <s>Dhanaratha</s>. Together with five caravan leaders, he set out for the great ocean. Those caravan leaders developed mutual affection through pleasant conversation and friendly exchanges with that caravan leader. In due course, having reached the ocean shore, they each prepared their vessels. At the time of embarking, they said to the caravan leader <s>Dhanaratha</s>: 'Caravan leader, without you we cannot find courage.' He said: 'If so, board right here; let the vessels be released.' They boarded, and a wind arose. To the frightened ones, <s>Dhanaratha</s> said: 'Sirs, do not be afraid. When the vessel meets destruction, hold on to my neck. body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> there dwelt a householder named <s>Saṃdhāna</s>, wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive holdings, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, a rival of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth. At that time, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> ruled the kingdom of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, and it was prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. Then the soothsayers predicted a twelve-year drought. King <s>Brahmadatta</s> had a bell-proclamation made throughout his realm: 'Let the citizens dwelling in my realm hear! The soothsayers have predicted a twelve-year drought. Therefore, those among you who have provisions of food and drink for twelve years should remain in my realm; the rest should disperse in various directions. After the twelve years have passed, they should return.' Then the householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s>

) bhaviṣyati iti; <tataḥ saṃdhāno gṛhapatiḥ saparivāro niṣaṇṇaḥ> janakāyaḥ samantād vidrutaḥ; mahad durbhikṣaṃ prādurbhūtaṃ kṛcchraḥ kāntāraḥ durlabhaḥ piṇḍako yācanakena; asati buddhānām utpāde pratyekabuddhā loke utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakā prāntāśayanāsanabhaktā ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya; tena khalu samayena vārāṇasyāṃ nātidūre anyatamasminn āśramapade paṃca pratyekabuddhaśatāni prativasanti; yadā durbhikṣakālamṛtyubhayabhīto janakāyaḥ samantād vidrutaḥ tadā teṣāṃ piṇḍakā samucchinnāḥ; te sarva eva saṃbhūya saṃdhanasya gṛhapates sakāśam upasaṃkrāntāḥ kathayanti: gṛhapate, asmākaṃ paṃcānāṃ pravrajitaśatānām piṇḍakena yogodvahanaṃ kuruṣva iti; sa kathayati: koṣṭhāgārkaṃ tāvad avalokayāmi iti; sa koṣṭhāgārikam āmantrayate: asti bhoḥ puruṣa asmākaṃ koṣṭhāgāre annapānam yad asmākaṃ syād eṣāṃ ca paṃcānāṃ pravrajitaśatānāṃ dvādaśavarṣāṇi iti; sa kathayati ārya bhaviṣyati iti; saṃdhānena gṛhapatinā paṃcānāṃ pravrajitaśatānāṃ piṇḍaka upanibaddha iti; śrutvā aparāṇi paṃca pratyekabuddhaśatāni saṃdhānasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntāni; upasaṃkramya saṃdhānaṃ gṛhapatim idam avocan: gṛhapate asmākaṃ paṃcānāṃ pravrajitaśatānāṃ piṇḍakena yogodvahanaṃ kuruṣva iti; sa kathayati: āryakā dattam eva yuṣmākaṃ kiṃ bhūyaḥ prārthayata iti; te kathayanti gṛhapate anye te vayam anye iti; sa kathayati: āryakā, yady evaṃ koṣṭhāgārikaṃ tāvad avalokayāmi iti; sa koṣṭhāgārikaṃ puruṣam āmantrayate: bhoḥ puruṣa asti asmākaṃ koṣṭhāgāre annapānaṃ yad asmākaṃ syād asya ca pravrajitasahasrasya dvādaśavarṣāṇi iti; sa kathayati: bhaviṣyati iti; tena te pratyekabuddhā uktā: āryakā tiṣṭhata; ko yuṣmākaṃ bhaktakāla iti; te kathayanti: gṛhapate apariṇato madhyāhnaḥ; tataḥ saṃdhānena gṛhapatinā dānaśālā māpitā dānādhisthāyikaḥ puruṣaḥ sthāpitaḥ kālārocakaś ca; te pratidinam āgamya bhaktakṛtyaṃ kurvanti; tasya pratyekabuddhasahasrasya yaḥ saṃghasthaviraḥ so 'tīva prāsādikaḥ chatrākāraśirās tāṃ parṣadaṃ chatrīkṛtyāvatiṣṭhate; saṃdhānasya gṛhapater duhitā tasya saṃghasthavirasya (
body.translated_text: ) there will be.' Then the householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s> remained with his household, while the populace dispersed in all directions. A great famine arose — harsh, dire, difficult to obtain even a morsel of alms-food by begging. When <s>Buddhas</s> do not arise in the world, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (solitary awakened ones) arise — compassionate toward the lowly and wretched, fond of secluded dwelling and eating places, each individually worthy of offerings to the world. At that time, not far from <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in a certain hermitage, five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> were dwelling. When the populace, terrified by famine, death, and danger, had dispersed in all directions, their alms-food was cut off. All of them, having assembled together, approached the householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s> and said: 'Householder, undertake the provision of alms-food for us five hundred renunciants.' He replied: 'Let me first inspect the storehouse.' He addressed the storehouse keeper: 'Good man, is there in our storehouse food and drink sufficient for us and for these five hundred renunciants for twelve years?' He replied: 'Sir, there will be.' The householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s> took upon himself the provision of alms-food for the five hundred renunciants. Having heard this, another five hundred <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> approached the householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s>. Having approached, they said to the householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s>: 'Householder, undertake the provision of alms-food for us five hundred renunciants.' He replied: 'Noble ones, it has already been given to you. Why do you ask again?' They said: 'Householder, they are different; we are different.' He replied: 'Noble ones, if so, let me first inspect the storehouse.' He addressed the storehouse keeper: 'Good man, is there in our storehouse food and drink sufficient for us and for this thousand renunciants for twelve years?' He replied: 'There will be.' He then told them: 'Noble ones, remain. What is your meal-time?' They said: 'Householder, before the midday has turned.' Then the householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s> had a meal-hall constructed, appointed a man to oversee the donations, and a meal-time announcer. They came daily and performed their meal duties. The elder of that community of a thousand <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> was exceedingly pleasing in appearance, with an umbrella-shaped head, and he stood presiding over that assembly like an umbrella. The daughter of the householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s>, seeing that community elder's (

body.text: SBV II 16

) chatrākāraśiraskatāṃ varṇapuṣkalatāṃ dṛṣṭvātīvābhiprasannā; yāvad apareṇa samayena bhaktakāle devo varṣitum ārabdhaḥ; tataḥ tayā dārikayā saṃghasthavirasya mūrdhni chatraṃ dhāritam; bhuktasya ca pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam: anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syāṃ yādṛśo 'yam āryaḥ yathā cāyaṃ chatrīkṛtya parṣadi niṣaṇṇaḥ evam aham api chatrīkṛtya parṣadaṃ niṣīdeyam iti.
  kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ? yāsau saṃdhānasdya gṛhapater duhitā eṣa evāsau
body.translated_text:
) umbrella-shaped head and the excellence of his complexion, was exceedingly pleased. Then on another occasion, at mealtime, it began to rain. Then that girl held an umbrella over the community elder's head. After he had eaten, she fell at his feet and made this aspiration: 'By this root of merit, may I become the possessor of such qualities as this noble one has, and just as he sits presiding over the assembly like an umbrella, so may I too sit presiding over an assembly like an umbrella.'
  What do you think, monks? The one who was the daughter of the householder <s>Saṃdhāna</s> — that is none other than the monk <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>. Because, when she was a young girl, she held an umbrella over the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> community elder and made the aspiration 'May I become the possessor of such qualities and sit presiding over an assembly like an umbrella,'

body.text:
kauṇḍinyo bhikṣuḥ; yad anena kumārikābhūtena pratyekabuddhasaṃghasthavirasya chatraṃ vidhārya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇānāṃ lābhī syāṃ chatrīkṛtya ca parṣadaṃ niṣīdeyam iti, tad etarhi sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ chatrīkṛtya ca parṣadam avasthitaḥ; iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ pūrvavad yāvad evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam.
  yadā bhagavatā ājñātakauṇḍinyam āgamya aśītir devatāsahasrāṇi saddharmarasena saṃtarpitāni tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhadanta bhagavatā āyuṣmantam ājñātakauṇḍinyam āgamya aśītir devatāsahasrāṇi saddharmarasena saṃtarpitāni; bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ mayā vigatarāgeṇa vigatadveṣeṇa vigatamohena parimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ sarvajñena sarvākārajñena sarvajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena ājñātakauṇḍinyam āgamya aśītir devatāsahasrāṇi dharmarasena saṃtarpitāni? yat tu mayātīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijārāvyadhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ vinipatitaśarīreṇa tiryagyonāv upapannena aśitikīṭasahasrāṇi kauṇḍinyaṃ kīṭikībhūtam āgamya svarudhireṇa saṃtarpitāni; tac chrūyatām.
body.translated_text:
now, through the abandonment of all defilements, she has directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> and stands presiding over the assembly like an umbrella. Thus, monks, for exclusively black actions the result is exclusively black — as before, up to — thus you should train, monks.
  When the <s>Bhagavān</s>, through the story of <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>, had satisfied eighty thousand deities with the flavor of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the monks, having doubts, questioned the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has satisfied eighty thousand deities with the flavor of the true <s>Dharma</s> through the story of the Venerable <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>!' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What is remarkable about that, monks, that now I — free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish, omniscient, knowing all aspects, having attained mastery over all knowledge and the knowable — have satisfied eighty thousand deities with the flavor of the <s>Dharma</s> through the story of <s>Ājñātakauṇḍinya</s>? But in the past, when I was with passion, with hatred, with delusion, unliberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish, with a body fallen into an animal birth, I satisfied eighty thousand insects, having become a kind of insect, through <s>Kauṇḍinya</s> with my own blood. Listen to that.

The story of the tortoise
(concerning a previous birth of Kauṇḍinya)
body.translated_text:
The story of the tortoise
(concerning a previous birth of <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>)

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ, bhikṣava, aniyatarāśyavasthito bodhisatvo mahāsamudre kacchapeṣūpapannas teṣām adhipatir babhūva; yāvat paṃcavaṇikśatāni mahāsamudrayānapātraṃ pratipadya mahāsamudram (
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in a certain state of existence, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was born among tortoises in the great ocean and became their chief. Then five hundred merchants, having boarded an ocean-going vessel, (

body.text: SBV II 17

) avatīrṇāni; tato nānāratnasaṃgrahaṃ kṛtvā pratinirvṛttāni; yāvad vahanaṃ makareṇa matsyajātenānayena vyasanam āpāditam; tatra mahān kolāhalo jātaḥ; tacchabdaśravaṇāt kacchapo mahāsamudrād utthitaḥ; sa teṣāṃ sakāśam upasaṃkramya kathayati: alaṃ bhavatāṃ viṣādena mama pṛṣṭham abhiruheta ahaṃ vas tārayiṣyāmi iti; te naṣṭopalabdhaprāṇāḥ sarve kūrmapṛṣṭham abhirūḍhāḥ; sa tān ādāya samudratīrābhimukhaḥ saṃprasthitaḥ; atyantabhārāvaṣṭabdho 'pi vīryam āsthāya viṣādaṃ nāpadyate; sa śrāntakāyaḥ teṣu saṃkīrṇeṣu grīvām abhiprasārya suptaḥ; tasya nātidūre kīṭikānāṃ nagaram; tasmād ekā kīṭikā paribhramantī gandhaṃ ghrātvā tasya sakāśam upasaṃkrāntā; tatas taṃ mahatpramāṇākāravikāraṃ dṛṣṭvā tvaritagatipracārikī kīṭikānagaram abhigatā; svasvasaṃjñayā kīṭikāḥ prabodhya aśītiḥ kīṭikāsahasrāṇy ādāya kacchapasakāśaṃ gatā; tataḥ taṃ suotaṃ mṛtam iva niśceṣṭaprāṇaṃ bhakṣayitum ārabdhāḥ; yadāsya sthūlaṃ māṃsaṃ bhakṣayanti śramanaparikhinno gāḍhamiddhāvaṣṭabdho na cetayate; yadā tu marmasthāneṣu māṃsaṃ bhakṣayanti tadā prabuddhaḥ paśyati kīṭikābhiḥ sarvaṃ śarīram ākīrṇam; sa saṃlakṣayati: yadi kāyaṃ calayiṣye
body.translated_text: ) set out upon the great ocean. Having gathered various jewels, they turned back. Then the vessel was brought to destruction by a <s>makara</s> (sea-monster), a creature of the fish kind. There arose a great uproar. Hearing that sound, the tortoise rose up from the great ocean. Having approached them, he said: 'Enough of your despair! Climb onto my back — I shall carry you across.' They, having recovered their lives as if from death, all climbed onto the tortoise's back. Carrying them, he set out toward the ocean shore. Though pressed down by the extreme weight, he exerted effort and did not give in to despair. Exhausted in body, when they had settled upon him, he stretched out his neck and fell asleep. Not far from him was a city of insects. From there, one insect, wandering about, caught the scent and approached him. Then, having seen his great size and form, she went with hurried steps to the insect city. Having roused the insects by their own signals, she took eighty thousand insects and went to the tortoise. Then they began to devour him, lying asleep and motionless as if dead. When they ate his thick flesh, exhausted and overcome by deep sleep, he did not feel it. But when they ate the flesh at his vital points,

body.text:
vā saṃparivartayiṣye vā niyatam etāḥ praghātayiṣyāmi; kāmaṃ prāṇaviyogo na tu prāṇoparodhaḥ; iti viditvā chidyamāneṣu marmasu mucyamāneṣu saṃdhiṣu praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ: yathā mayā etāni aśītir kīṭikāsahasrāṇi māṃsarudhireṇa saṃtarpitāni, tāny evam aham anāgate 'dhvani anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhya saddharmarasena saṃtarpayeyam iti.
  kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ? yo 'sau kīṭikānāṃ mārgoddeśika eṣa evāsau kauṇḍinyo bhikṣuḥ; yāni tāni aśītir kīṭikāsahasrāṇi tam āgamya māṃsarudhireṇa saṃtarpitāni, tāny aśītir devatāsahasrāṇi; tadāpy etānimayā svarudhireṇa saṃtarpitāni; etarhy apy etāni mayā saddharmarasena saṃtarpitāni; iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānām iti yāvad evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam.
  yadā bhagavatā paṃcakā bhikṣavaḥ saddharmarasena saṃtarpya saṃsārakāntārād uttāryātyantaniṣṭhe yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitā (
body.translated_text:
he awoke and saw that his entire body was covered with insects. He reflected: 'If I move my body or turn over, I will certainly crush them. Better the loss of my own life than the destruction of their lives.' Having realized this, even as his vital points were being cut and his joints severed, he began to make this aspiration: 'Just as I have satisfied these eighty thousand insects with my flesh and blood, so in the future, having attained unsurpassed perfect awakening (<s>anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi</s>), may I satisfy them with the flavor of the true <s>Dharma</s>.'
  What do you think, monks? The one who was the guide of the insects — that is none other than the monk <s>Kauṇḍinya</s>. Those eighty thousand insects that were satisfied with flesh and blood through him — those are the eighty thousand deities. At that time too, they were satisfied by me with my own blood; now too, they have been satisfied by me with the flavor of the true <s>Dharma</s>. Thus, monks, for exclusively black actions — as before, up to — thus you should train, monks.
  When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had satisfied the five monks with the flavor of the true <s>Dharma</s>, and having carried them across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, established them in the ultimate, supreme security of <s>Nirvāṇa</s> (

body.text: SBV II 18

) tadā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhadanta bhagavatā bhikṣavaḥ saddharmarasena saṃtarpya saṃsārakāntārād uttāryātyantaniṣṭhe yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ iti; bhagavān āha: kim atra bhikṣava āścaryaṃ yad idānīṃ mayā vigatarāgeṇa vigatadveṣeṇa vigatamohena parimuktena jātijarāvyādhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsaiḥ sarvajñena sarvākārajñena sarvajñānajñeyavaśiprāptena paṃcakā bhikṣavaḥ saddharmarasena saṃtarpya saṃsārakāntārād uttāryātyantaniṣṭhe yogakṣeme nirvāṇe pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ? yat tu mayātīte 'dhvani sarāgeṇa sadveṣeṇa samohenāparimuktena jātijārāvyadhimaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsair ete svarudhireṇa saṃtarpya paṃcasu vratapadeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ; tac chrūyatām.
body.translated_text: ) the monks, having doubts, questioned the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has satisfied the monks with the flavor of the true <s>Dharma</s>, carried them across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and established them in the ultimate, supreme security of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What is remarkable about that, monks, that now I — free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion, liberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish, omniscient, knowing all aspects, having attained mastery over all knowledge and the knowable — have satisfied the five monks with the flavor of the true <s>Dharma</s>, carried them across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and established them in the ultimate, supreme security of <s>Nirvāṇa</s>? But in the past, when I was with passion, with hatred, with delusion, unliberated from birth, old age, sickness, death, grief, lamentation, suffering, mental distress, and anguish, they were satisfied with my own blood and established in five precepts. Listen to that.

body.text: The story of the king Vajrabāhu
body.translated_text: The story of King <s>Vajrabāhu</s>

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ vajrabāhur nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca yāvad ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca; sa rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśayaḥ ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ sarvapradaḥ sarvaparityāgī niḥsaṅgaparityāgī ca mahati tyāge vartate; tenātyantaṃ maitrī svabhyastā; trir divasasya maitrīṃ samāpadyate; tasya maitrīṃ samāpadyamānasya yācanakajano vihanyate; tenāmātyānām ājñā dattā; bhavanto vārāṇasyāṃ caturṣu nagaradvāreṣu dānaśālā māpayitvā śramaṇabrāhmaṇakṛpaṇavaṇīpakādhvagayācanakebhyo yo yenārthī tasmai tad anuprayacchata iti; evaṃ deva ity amātyā rajño vajrabāhor pratiśutya vārāṇasyāṃ caturṣu nagaradvāreṣu dānaśālā māpayitvā annapānavastraśayanāsanahiraṇyasuvarṇamuktāvaiḍūryaśaṃkhaśilāpravāḍajātarūparajatāśmagarbhamusāragalbalohitikādakṣiṇāvartādidravyasaṃbhārenāvasthitāḥ yācanakajanaṃ saṃtarpanāya; yāvad apareṇa
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Vajrabāhu</s> was exercising sovereignty — it was prosperous, and so on, teeming with a great multitude of people. That king was faithful, virtuous, of good intentions, devoted to the welfare of himself and others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, tender toward his subjects, a giver of all things, one who renounces all, who renounces without attachment, and who engaged in great acts of generosity. He had thoroughly cultivated <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness). Three times a day he entered the meditation of loving-kindness. While he was entering the meditation of loving-kindness, beggars were turned away. Therefore he gave a command to his ministers: 'Sirs, having built alms-halls at the four city gates of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, give to ascetics, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, the poor, travelers, wanderers, and beggars whatever each one needs.' 'Yes, Your Majesty!' The ministers, having assented to King <s>Vajrabāhu</s>, built alms-halls at the four city gates of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and were stationed there, furnished with supplies of food, drink, clothing, bedding, seats, gold, silver, pearls, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (beryl), conch, crystal, coral, refined gold, silver, emeralds, <s>musāragalva</s>, <s>lohitikā</s> (rubies), <s>dakṣiṇāvarta</s> (right-spiraling conch), and other materials, to satisfy the people who came to beg. Then at a later time

body.translated_text: ) brought them across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and established them in the ultimate security of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What is so wonderful, monks, that now I, free from passion, and so on, having attained mastery over all knowledge and the knowable, have satisfied the group of five monks with the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>, brought them across the wilderness of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and established them in the ultimate security of <s>nirvāṇa</s>? But that in the past, when I was still subject to passion, as before... and to suffering, mental distress, and anguish, I satisfied them with my own blood and established them in the five precepts — hear about that.'

body.text: The story of Maitrabala
body.translated_text: The story of <s>Maitrabala</s>

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ maitrabalo nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca yāvad bahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca; maitryātmakaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā sarvasatveṣu dayāvān;
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Maitrabala</s> was exercising sovereignty — it was prosperous, and so on, teeming with a great multitude of people. He was one whose nature was loving-kindness, compassionate, great-souled, having compassion for all beings.

body.text: yāvad apareṇa samayena vaiśravaṇena rājñā aḍakavattāyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ paṃca ojohārā yakṣāḥ kasmiṇcid eva aparādhe pravāsitāḥ; te taṃ janapadam anvāhiṇḍya vārāṇasīm anuprāptāḥ; teṣāṃ na kaścid balimālyopahāraṃ kurute; taiḥ prakopam āpannair ītir utsṛṣṭā; vārāṇasyāṃ janakāyo mriyate; amātyai rājñe maitrabalāya niveditam: deva vārāṇasyām atīva janakāyo mṛta iti; rājñā teṣām ājñā dattā: gacchata vārāṇasyām evaṃ ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kārayata: bhadanto rājā maitrabalaḥ samājñāpayati, ahaṃ sarvasatvahitādhyāśayatatpareṇa manasā rātrindivam atinamayāmi; tad yuṣmābhir api sarvasatvānugatā maitrī manasi kartavyā; evaṃ vaḥ śāntir bhaviṣyatīti; te sarvasatvānugatāṃ maitrīṃ manasi kartum ārabdhā; ojohārā yakṣā vārāṇasīsāmantakena paribhramitum ārabdhāḥ; praveśaṃ na labhante; te praveśam alabhamānā gopālakāṃ paśupālakān tṛṇahārakāṃ kāṣṭhahārakāṃ pathājīvān utpathājīvāṃś ca manuṣyān dṛṣṭvā kathayanti: bhavanto na yūyam asmad bibhīta? iti; te kathayanti: na bibhīmaḥ; kiṃ kāraṇaṃ? vayaṃ hi yad rājā maitrabalaś cintayati tac cintayāmaḥ; kiṃ maitrabalo rājā cintayati? sarvasatvānugatāṃ maitrīṃ; te saṃlakṣayanti: idam atra kāraṇaṃ yena vayam idānīm avatāraṃ na labhāmaha iti; te vārāṇasyāṃ dvāreṇa (
body.translated_text:
At a later time, King <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> banished five essence-stealing <s>yakṣas</s> from the royal capital <s>Aḍakavatī</s> for some offense. They wandered through that region and reached <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. No one offered them oblations, garlands, or tribute. Enraged, they released a plague. In <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, people began to die. The ministers reported to King <s>Maitrabala</s>: 'Your Majesty, in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> an exceedingly great number of people have died.' The king gave them a command: 'Go, have a bell-proclamation made in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> as follows: "Sirs, King <s>Maitrabala</s> commands thus: I pass day and night with a mind wholly intent on the welfare of all beings. Therefore, you too should cultivate loving-kindness directed toward all beings. Thus shall you have peace."' They began to cultivate loving-kindness directed toward all beings. The essence-stealing <s>yakṣas</s> began to wander around the vicinity of <s>Vārāṇasī</s> but could not gain entry. Unable to gain entry, they saw cowherds, shepherds, grass-gatherers, wood-gatherers, those who live on the roads and off the roads — various people — and said: 'Sirs, do you not fear us?' They said: 'We do not fear. Why? Because we think what King <s>Maitrabala</s> thinks.' 'What does King <s>Maitrabala</s> think?' 'Loving-kindness directed toward all beings.' They reflected: 'This is the reason why we now cannot gain entry.' They wandered from gate to gate in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>: 'Perhaps at some time we shall see King <s>Maitrabala</s>.' Then at a later time, King <s>Maitrabala</s> set out for the outer garden. Then those <s>yakṣas</s>, having transformed themselves into the guise of <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, approached the king with peaceful deportment. Having approached, they congratulated the king with wishes of victory and long life and said: 'Your Majesty, we are hungry. Show favor with food.' The king summoned his ministers and said: 'Sirs, satisfy these <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with excellent food.' They said: 'Your Majesty, we eat flesh and blood.' The king instructed his ministers: 'Sirs, if there is no supply of meat or blood, give them meat and blood obtained in a lawful and righteous manner from the marketplace.' 'Your Majesty, we eat the flesh and blood of freshly slaughtered [animals]. Show favor with freshly slaughtered meat.' The king reflected: 'Where is a supply of freshly slaughtered flesh and blood to be had without causing harm to another? Let me give them my own blood.' Then, having summoned the physicians, he said: 'Sirs, make incisions in all my veins throughout my body — I shall satisfy the beggars.' The physicians said: 'Your Majesty, we shall not lay a blade upon Your Majesty's body for the sake of common men.' <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are skilled in various arts and crafts. He himself made incisions in five limbs. Then, having satisfied them with his own blood, he gave them such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> that, having heard it, those <s>yakṣas</s> were established in the five precepts.
  What do you think, monks? He who was the king named <s>Maitrabala</s> — that was I at that time, in that era. Those five essence-stealing <s>yakṣas</s> —

  When the <s>Bhagavān</s> had practiced austerities for six years, attained unsurpassed perfect awakening, gone to <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and turned the Wheel of the <s>Dharma</s>, disciplined the group of five, along with the additional groups of five, sixty <s>Bhadravargīyas</s>, and various multitudes, and the number of monks had grown, then the monks, doubts having arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has performed <s>karma</s> by the ripening of which he practiced austerities for six years.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, monks, who in the past, in other births, performed and accumulated <s>karmas</s>, whose conditions were gathered, as before, up to: indeed, <s>karmas</s> ripen for embodied beings.' body.text: The story of Nandapāla the Potter (= Ghaṭīkarasutta, MN 81, cf. MV I 319ff.)
body.translated_text: The story of <s>Nandapāla</s> the Potter (= <s>Ghaṭīkarasutta</s>, MN 81, cf. MV I 319ff.)

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo vaibhiḍiṅgī nāma grāmanigamo 'bhūd ṛddhaś ca sphītaś ca bahujanamanuṣyaś ca; vaibhiḍiṅgyāṃ bhikṣavo grāmanigame nyagrodho nāma brāhmaṇamahāśālaḥ prativasati, āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ sphītaḥ, vaibhiḍiṅgīṃ paribhuṃkte sotsadāṃ satṛṇakāṣṭhodakāṃ kṛkinā rājñā brahmadeyāṃ dattām; nyagrodhasya khalu bhikṣavo brāhmaṇamahaśālasya uttaro nāmo māṇavo 'ntevāsī upeto mātṛtaḥ pitṛtaḥ saṃśuddho gṛhiṇyām anākṣipto jātivādena gotravādena ca yāvad āsaptamaṃ mātāmahapaitāmahaṃ yugam upādāya; adhyāpako mantradharo trayāṇāṃ vedānāṃ pāraṃgataḥ sanighaṇṭukaiṭabhānāṃ sākṣaraprabhedānām itihāsapaṃcamānāṃ sādṛśo vyākarakaḥ, abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ; nyagrodhasya brāhmaṇamahaśālasya paṃcamātrāṇi māṇavakaśatāni brāhmaṇakān mantrān vācayanti; vaibhiḍiṅgyāṃ bhikṣavo grāmanigame nandīpālo ghaṭīkaraḥ prativasati; buddhe 'bhiprasanno dharme saṃghe 'bhiprasannaḥ; buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gato dhammaṃ saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ; buddhe ekāntiko dharme saṃghe ekāntikaḥ; buddhe niṣkāṃkṣo nirvicikitso dharme saṃghe niṣkāṃkṣo nirvicitaḥ; duḥkhe samudaye nirodhe mārge niṣkāṃkṣo nirvicikitso dṛṣṭasatya āgataphalābhisamitavāṃ nikṣiptaparṇamusalo na svahastaṃ pṛthivīṃ khanati na khānayati; nānyatra, yat tad bhavati dakaprarugnaṃ vā mūṣikotkirā vā tataḥ kāyena mṛttikāṃ saṃhṛtya niṣprāṇakenodakena tīmayitvā bhājanāni kṛtvā ekāntam upanikṣipya evam āha: eta āryā eta bhadramukhā tilān vā taṇḍulān vā mudgaprabhṛtīn vā māṣaprabhṛtīn vā ekānta upanikṣipya yo vā yena bhājanenārthī sa tad ādāya prakrāmatu iti; sa tasmād andhau mātāpitarau bibharti; kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kālena (
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, there was a market-town named <s>Vaibhiḍiṅgī</s>, which was prosperous, flourishing, and teeming with a great multitude of people. In the market-town of <s>Vaibhiḍiṅgī</s>, monks, there lived a wealthy <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householder named <s>Nyagrodha</s> — rich, of great wealth and great possessions, prosperous. He enjoyed <s>Vaibhiḍiṅgī</s> with its pastures, along with its grass, wood, and water, given as a <s>brahmadeya</s> (royal land-grant) by King <s>Kṛkin</s>. Now, monks, <s>Nyagrodha</s> the wealthy <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householder had a resident pupil named <s>Uttara</s>, of pure descent on both mother's and father's side, unassailed in his household by reproach of birth or lineage up to the seventh generation of maternal and paternal ancestors; a teacher, master of sacred formulas, one who had reached the far shore of the three <s>Vedas</s> together with their <s>Nighaṇṭu</s> (glossary) and <s>Kaiṭabha</s> (ritual manual), their phonetic analysis, and the <s>Itihāsa</s> (histories) as a fifth, an able grammarian — handsome, good-looking, and pleasing. Five hundred students were reciting <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sacred formulas under <s>Nyagrodha</s> the wealthy <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> householder. In the market-town of <s>Vaibhiḍiṅgī</s>, monks, there lived a potter named <s>Nandīpāla</s>. He had faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>. He had gone for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>. He was devoted exclusively to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>. He was free from doubt and uncertainty regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>. He was free from doubt and uncertainty regarding suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path. He had seen the truths, attained the fruit, and realized the <s>Dharma</s>. Having laid down the pestle of husking, he did not dig the earth with his own hand nor have it dug. Only when there was earth broken by water or mole-hills would he gather the clay with his body, moisten it with water free of living organisms, make vessels, place them in a spot, and say: 'Come, noble ones! Come, good-faced ones! Place sesame, rice, mung beans, black beans, or the like in a spot. Whoever needs whichever vessel, let him take it and go.' From that [livelihood] he supported his blind parents. He provided <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> with alms-food from time to time (

Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> and sat down to one side. As <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter was seated to one side,

body.text: nandīpālaṃ ghaṭīkaraṃ kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati; anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm; atha nandīpālo ghaṭīkaraḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā utthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ; tena khalu samayena uttaro māṇavaḥ sarvaśvetaṃ vaḍavāratham abhiruhya sauvarṇena daṇḍakamaṇḍalunā dhāryamānena māṇavakagaṇaparivṛto māṇavakagaṇapuraskṛto vaibhiḍiṅgyān niryāti; bahir vaibhiḍiṅgyāḥ brāhmaṇakān mantrān vācayitukāmaḥ adrākṣīd uttaro māṇavo nandīpālaṃ ghaṭīkaraṃ dūrād eva; dṛṣṭvā ca punar evam āha: kutas tvaṃ somya nandīpāla etarhy āgacchasi? ito 'haṃ somya uttara etarhy āgacchāmi kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paryupāsya; ehy āvāṃ somya uttara gamiṣyāvāḥ; kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paryupāsiṣyāvahe; alaṃ somya nandīpāla kāśyapena samyaksaṃbuddhena dṛṣṭenālaṃ paryupāsitena; tat kasya hetoḥ; kutas tasmin muṇḍake śramaṇake bodhiḥ; bodhir hi paramaduṣkarā; mā tvaṃ somya uttara evaṃ vada: kutas tasmin śramaṇake bodhiḥ; bodhir hi paramaduṣkarā; api tu buddhaḥ sa bhagavān, buddhāś cānena sarvadharmā iti; dvir api trir api nandīpālo ghaṭīkaraḥ uttaraṃ māṇavakam idam avocat: ehy āvāṃ somya uttara gamiṣyāvaḥ; kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paryupāsiṣyāvahe iti; dvir api trir api uttaro māṇavo nandīpālaṃ ghaṭīkaram idam avoat: alaṃ somya nandīpāla kāśyapena samyaksaṃbuddhena dṛṣṭena alaṃ paryupāsitena; tat kasya hetoḥ? kutas tasmin muṇḍale śramaṇake bodhiḥ; bodhir hi paramaduṣkarā; mā tvaṃ somyottara evaṃ vada kutas tasmin muṇḍake śramaṇake bodhiḥ; bodhir hi paramaduṣkarā; api tu buddhaḥ sa bhagavān, buddhāś cānena sarvadharmā iti; atha nandīpālo ghaṭīkara uttarasya māṇavasya ratham abhiruhya uttaraṃ māṇavam idam avocat: ehy āvāṃ somya uttara gamiṣyāvaḥ; kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paryupāsiṣyāvahe iti; athottarasya māṇavasyaitad abhavat: na batāvaro buddho bhaviṣyati; (
body.translated_text: <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened him with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter bowed his head at the feet of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, rose from his seat, and departed. At that time, the young man <s>Uttara</s>, having mounted an all-white mare-chariot, with a golden staff and water-pot being held for him, surrounded and preceded by a group of young men, was going out of <s>Vaibhiḍiṅgī</s>. Wishing to recite <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> sacred formulas outside <s>Vaibhiḍiṅgī</s>, the young man <s>Uttara</s> saw <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter from afar. Having seen him, he said: 'Where are you coming from just now, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s>?' 'I am coming from here just now, dear <s>Uttara</s>, having attended upon <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>.' 'Come, dear <s>Uttara</s>, let us go. Let us attend upon <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>.' 'Enough, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s> — enough of seeing <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, enough of attending upon him. And why? How can there be <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening) in that shaven ascetic? For <s>Bodhi</s> is supremely difficult to attain.' 'Do not speak thus, dear <s>Uttara</s>: "How can there be <s>Bodhi</s> in that ascetic? For <s>Bodhi</s> is supremely difficult to attain." Rather, he is the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s> have been awakened to by him.' A second and a third time, <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter said this to the young man <s>Uttara</s>: 'Come, dear <s>Uttara</s>, let us go. Let us attend upon <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>.' A second and a third time, the young man <s>Uttara</s> said this to <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter: 'Enough, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s> — enough of seeing <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, enough of attending upon him. And why? How can there be <s>Bodhi</s> in that shaven ascetic? For <s>Bodhi</s> is supremely difficult to attain.' 'Do not speak thus, dear <s>Uttara</s>: "How can there be <s>Bodhi</s> in that shaven ascetic? For <s>Bodhi</s> is supremely difficult to attain." Rather, he is the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and all <s>dharmas</s> have been awakened to by him.' Then <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter, having climbed onto the young man <s>Uttara</s>'s chariot, said this to the young man <s>Uttara</s>: 'Come, dear <s>Uttara</s>, let us go. Let us attend upon <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>.' Then the young man <s>Uttara</s> thought: 'Surely the <s>Buddha</s> must not be insignificant, (

body.text: SBV II 24

) nāvaraṃ dharmākhyānaṃ; yatredaṇīṃ nandīpālo ghaṭīkaro dīrgharātram acaṇḍo 'rabhaso 'karkaśa 'sāhasikaḥ keśagrahaṇam apy agamad iti viditvā nandīpālaṃ ghaṭīkaram idam avocat: somya nandīpāla ato 'pi yāvat; somya uttara, ato 'pi yāvat; ato 'pi yāvat somya nandīpāla; ato 'pi yāvat, somya uttara; tena hi somya nandīpāla muṃca, gamiṣyāvaḥ, kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ paryupāsiṣyāvahe; athottaro māṇavo nandīpālaś ca ghaṭīkaraḥ ratham abhiruhya yena kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntau; tayor yāvatī yānasya bhūmis tāvad yānena gatvā yānād avatīrya yena kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntau; upasaṃkramya kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇau; ekāntaniṣaṇṇo nandīpālo ghaṭīkaraḥ kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat: ayaṃ bhadanta uttaro
body.translated_text: ) nor the proclamation of the <s>Dharma</s> insignificant — seeing that <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter, who has for a long time been gentle, unhurried, not harsh, and not reckless, has even gone so far as to seize me by the hair.' Having understood, he said this to <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter: 'Even more than this, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s>?' 'Even more than this, dear <s>Uttara</s>.' 'Even more than this, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s>?' 'Even more than this, dear <s>Uttara</s>.' 'Then, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s>, let go — we shall go. Let us attend upon <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>.' Then the young man <s>Uttara</s> and <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter, having mounted the chariot, approached <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. As far as the ground was passable by vehicle, they went by vehicle; then, having descended from the vehicle, they approached <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> on foot. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> and sat down to one side. <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter, seated to one side, said this to <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>: 'Venerable Sir, this young man <s>Uttara</s>

body.text:
māṇavo na buddhe 'bhiprasanno na dharme na saṃghe 'bhiprasannaḥ; sādhv asya bhagavān tathā dharmaṃ deśayed yathā uttaro māṇavo buddhe 'bhiprasīded dharme saṃghe 'bhiprasīded iti; adhivāsayati kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddha uttaraṃ māṇavaṃ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati; anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm; athottaro māṇavo nandīpālaṃ ghaṭīkaram idam avocat: kasmāt tvaṃ, somya nandīpāla, svākhyātaṃ dharmavinayaṃ śrutvā na pravrajasi samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anāgārikām? na tvaṃ, somya kumāra, jānīṣe yathāham andhaṃ mātāpitaraṃ bibharmi,
kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ kālena ca kālaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādayāmi; pravraja tvaṃ somya nandīpāla mā vā; ahaṃ tāvat pravrajiṣye iti; atha nandīpālo ghaṭīkaraḥ kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat: ayaṃ bhadanta uttaro māṇava ākāṃkṣati svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvam; taṃ bhagavān pravrājayatūpasaṃpādayatu anukaṃpām upādāya iti; adhivāsayati kāśyapaḥ (
body.translated_text: has no faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, or the <s>Saṅgha</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> teach him the <s>Dharma</s> in such a way that the young man <s>Uttara</s> may come to have faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and the <s>Saṅgha</s>.' <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> consented. He instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened the young man <s>Uttara</s> with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then the young man <s>Uttara</s> said this to <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter: 'Why, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s>, having heard the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>, do you not go forth with perfect faith from the household life into homelessness?' 'You do not know, dear friend, that I support my blind parents and provide <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> with alms-food from time to time. You go forth, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s>, or do not — I at least shall go forth.' Then <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter said this to <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>: 'Venerable Sir, this young man <s>Uttara</s> desires ordination, full admission, and monkhood in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> ordain and fully admit him, out of compassion.' <s>Kāśyapa</s> (

body.text: SBV II 25

) samyaksaṃbuddho nandīpālasya ghaṭīkarasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvena; atha nandīpālo ghaṭīkaraḥ kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ; atha kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaś aciraprakrāntaṃ nandīpālaṃ ghaṭīkaraṃ viditvā uttaraṃ māṇavaṃ pravrājya upasaṃpādya yathābhiramyaṃ vaibhiḍiṃgyāṃ vihṛtya yena vārāṇasī kāśīnāṃ nigamas tena cārikāṃ prakrāntaḥ; anupūrveṇa cārikāṃ caran vārāṇasīm anuprāptaḥ; vārāṇasyāṃ viharati ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve.
  aśrauṣīt kṛkī rājā kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ kāśiṣu janapade cārikāṃ caran vārāṇasīm anuprāpto vārāṇasyāṃ viharati ṛṣivadane mṛgadāve iti; śrutvā ca punar vārāṇasyāḥ niṣkramya yena kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya upasaṃkramya kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇau; ekāntaniṣaṇṇaṃ kṛkiṃ rājānaṃ kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati; anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm; atha kṛkī rājā utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṃgaṃ kṛtvā yena kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya kāśyapam idam avocat: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena iti; adhivāsayati kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ kṛkino rājñas tūṣṇīṃbhāvena; atha kṛkī rājā kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā kāsyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvotthāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ; atha kṛkī rājā tām eva rātriṃ śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ samudānīya kālyam evotthāyāsanakāni prajñapya udakamaṇiṃ pratiṣṭhāpya
body.translated_text:
) the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> consented to <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter by his silence. Then <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter, having understood the consent of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> through his silence, bowed his head at the feet of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, rose from his seat, and departed. Then <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, knowing that <s>Nandīpāla</s> the potter had recently departed, ordained and fully admitted the young man <s>Uttara</s>, and after dwelling as long as he wished in <s>Vaibhiḍiṅgī</s>, set out on a wandering tour toward <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, the market-town of <s>Kāśi</s>. Wandering by stages, he arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. In <s>Vārāṇasī</s> he dwelt at <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> in the Deer Park.
  King <s>Kṛkin</s> heard that <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, wandering in the <s>Kāśi</s> country, had arrived at <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and was dwelling at <s>Ṛṣivadana</s> in the Deer Park. Having heard, he departed from <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and approached <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> and sat down to one side. <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened King <s>Kṛkin</s>, seated to one side, with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having instructed, inspired, encouraged, and gladdened him in many ways with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then King <s>Kṛkin</s>, having risen from his seat, arranged his upper robe over one shoulder, joined his palms toward <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, and said to <s>Kāśyapa</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to a meal tomorrow in the inner palace together with the community of monks.' <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> consented to King <s>Kṛkin</s> by his silence. Then King <s>Kṛkin</s>, having understood the consent of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> through his silence, bowed his head at the feet of <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, rose from his seat, and departed. Then King <s>Kṛkin</s>, that very night, having prepared pure and excellent food and drink, rising early, having arranged seats and set out a water-pitcher,

body.text: kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya dūtena kālam ārocayati: samayo bhadanta sajjaṃ bhaktaṃ yasyedānīṃ bhagavān kālaṃ manyate iti; atha kāsyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya bhikṣugaṇaparivṛto bhikṣusaṃghapuraskṛto yena kṛkeḥ rājño bhaktābhisāras tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya purastād bhikṣusaṃghasya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; atha kṛkī rājā sukhopaniṣaṇṇaṃ buddhapramukhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghaṃ viditvā śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpayati saṃpravārayati; anekaparyāyeṇa śucinā praṇītena khādanīyabhojanīyena svahastaṃ saṃtarpya saṃpravārya kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ bhuktavantaṃ viditvā dhautahastam apanītapātraṃ sauvarṇaṃ bhṛṅgāram ādāya kāśyapasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya (
body.translated_text: announced the time to <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> through a messenger: 'It is time, Venerable Sir; the meal is ready. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> come when he deems it the proper time.' Then <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, having dressed in the morning and taken his bowl and robes, surrounded and preceded by a community of monks, approached the place of King <s>Kṛkin</s>'s meal. Having approached, he sat down on the seat prepared at the head of the community of monks. Then King <s>Kṛkin</s>, seeing that the community of monks headed by the <s>Buddha</s> was comfortably seated, with his own hands served and satisfied them with pure and excellent food and drink. Having served and satisfied them in many ways with pure and excellent food and drink, and knowing that <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> had finished eating, his hands washed and bowl set aside, taking a golden pitcher, [he approached] <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> (

body.text: SBV II 26

) purato 'sthād āyācamānaḥ: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān traimāsīṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena; ahaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya paṃca vihāraśatāni māpayiṣyāmi; paṃca maṃcapīṭhavṛṣikocavabimbopadhānacaturaśrakaśatāni kārayiṣyāmi; anena caivaṃrūpena parṇopagūḍhena śālinā bhagavantaṃ upasthāsyāmi bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca; alaṃ mahārājā kṛtam etāvad yāvad eva cittam abhiprasannam; dvir api trir api kṛkī rājā kāśyapaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat: adhivāsayatu me bhagavān traimāsīṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ bhikṣusaṃghena; ahaṃ bhagavato 'rthāya paṃca vihāraśatāni māpayiṣyāmi; paṃca maṃcapīṭhavṛṣikocavabimbopadhānacaturaśrakaśatāni kārayiṣyāmi; anena caivaṃrūpena parṇopagūḍhena śālinā bhagavantaṃ upasthāsyāmi bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca; dvir api trir api kāśyapaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ kṛkiṃ rājānam idam avocat: alaṃ mahārājā kṛtam etāvad yāvad eva cittam abhiprasannam; atha kṛkī rājā kāśyapaṃ saṃyaksaṃbuddham idam avocat: asti kaścid bhagavan yo 'py evaṃrūpa upasthāyakaḥ tadyathā aham etarhy? asti mahārāja tavaiva vijite vaibhiḍiṃgī nāma grāmanigamaḥ; tatra nandīpālo nāma ghaṭīkara prativasati; sa buddhe 'bhiprasanno dharme saṃghe 'bhiprasannaḥ; buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gato dhammaṃ saṃghaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ; buddhe ekāntiko dharme saṃghe ekāntikaḥ; buddhe niṣkāṃkṣo nirvicikitso dharme saṃghe duḥkhe samudaye nirodhe mārge niṣkāṃkṣo nirvicikitso dṛṣṭasatye āgataphalo 'bhisamitavāṃ nikṣiptaparṇamusalaḥ sa na svahastaṃ pṛthivīṃ khanati na khānayati; nānyatra, yat tad bhavati dakaprarugnaṃ vā mūṣikotkirā vā tataḥ kāyena mṛttikāṃ saṃhṛtya niṣprāṇakenodakena tīmayitvā bhājanāni kṛtvaikāntam upanikṣipyaivam āha: eta āryā eta bhadramukhā tilān vā taṇḍulān vā mudgaprabhṛtīn vā māṣaprabhṛtīn vā ekānta upanikṣipya yo vā yena bhājanenārthī bhavati sa tad ādāya prakrāmatu; sa tasmād andhaṃ mātāpitarau bibharti; māṃ ca kālena kālaṃ piṇḍakena pratipādayati; (
body.translated_text: ) he stood before him requesting: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept from me, together with the community of monks, the three-month [provision of] robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick. I shall build five hundred monasteries for the <s>Bhagavān</s>; I shall have made five hundred sets of beds, chairs, rugs, cushions, bolsters, pillows, and square seats; and I shall serve the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the community of monks with such rice covered with leaves.' 'Enough, great king; it suffices that your mind is filled with faith.' A second and third time, King <s>Kṛki</s> said to <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept from me, together with the community of monks, the three-month [provision of] robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick. I shall build five hundred monasteries for the <s>Bhagavān</s>; I shall have made five hundred sets of beds, chairs, rugs, cushions, bolsters, pillows, and square seats; and I shall serve the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the community of monks with such rice covered with leaves.' A second and third time, <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> said to King <s>Kṛki</s>: 'Enough, great king; it suffices that your mind is filled with faith.' Then King <s>Kṛki</s> said to <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>: 'Is there anyone, <s>Bhagavān</s>, who is such an attendant as I am now?' 'There is, great king. In your very domain there is a village-town named <s>Vaibhiḍiṃgī</s>. There dwells a potter named <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s>. He has faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>; he has gone for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>; he is exclusively devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>; he is free from doubt and perplexity regarding the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Saṃgha</s>, suffering, its origin, its cessation, and the path; he has seen the truth, attained the fruit, and comprehended it. He has laid aside the pestle and winnowing fan — he does not dig the earth with his own hand, nor cause it to be dug. Except when there is earth broken open by water or rodent-mounds, from there he gathers clay with his body, moistens it with lifeless water, makes vessels, sets them aside in a place, and says thus: "Come, noble ones! Come, good people! Deposit sesame seeds, or rice grains, or green lentils and the like, or black beans and the like in this place; whoever needs whichever vessel, let him take it and go." From that [livelihood] he supports his blind parents and also provides me with alms-food from time to time.' (

body.text: SBV II 27
body.translated_text: SBV II 27

body.text: ) ekam ahaṃ mahārāja samayaṃ vaibhiḍiṃgīṃ grāmanigamam upaniśritya viharāmi; so 'haṃ pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya vaibhiḍiṃgīṃ grāmanigamaṃ piṇḍāya prāvikṣam;
body.translated_text: ) 'On one occasion, great king, I was dwelling near the village-town of <s>Vaibhiḍiṃgī</s>. In the forenoon, having dressed and taken my bowl and robe, I entered <s>Vaibhiḍiṃgī</s> for alms.

body.text:

body.translated_text: While going on alms-round through <s>Vaibhiḍiṃgī</s> with due care, I approached the dwelling of <s>Ghaṭīkāra</s>. Having approached, I gently and softly knocked on the door-bolt. At that time, <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s> had gone out on some errand. The blind parents of <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s> heard the sound of the door-bolt being knocked. Having heard, they said: "Who is this noble one, who is this good person, gently and softly knocking on the door-bolt?" I said to them: "I am <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, in need of alms-food." They said: "Enter, noble one! Enter, good person! Here are boiled grains in the pot and curry in the bowl. If you wish, take it yourself and eat. Your attendant has gone out." So I, great king, having invoked the <s>Uttarakuru</s> rule, took the boiled grains from the pot and the curry from the bowl myself, and ate. Afterwards, <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s> returned. <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s> saw that the boiled grains in the pot and the curry in the bowl had been eaten. Having seen, he said to his blind parents: "Mother, father, who has eaten the boiled grains in the pot and the curry in the bowl?" They said: "Here, dear <s>Nandīpāla</s>, shortly after you left, we heard the sound of the door-bolt being knocked. Having heard, we said: 'Who is this noble one, who is this good person, gently and softly knocking on the door-bolt?' He said: 'I am <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, in need of alms-food.' We said to him: 'Enter, noble one! Enter, good person! Here are boiled grains in the pot and curry in the bowl. If you wish, take it yourself and eat. Your attendant has gone out.' He must have eaten the boiled grains in the pot and the curry in the bowl." Then <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s> thought: "Fortunate am I, truly fortunate, that <s>Kāśyapa</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> has such extreme trust and confidence in my family!" Knowing this, with that very joy and delight, he spent seven days in a single cross-legged posture, and for half a month his constant, uninterrupted mindfulness did not leave his body — it continued unbroken in his body. For seven days, [he provided] his parents, as before, boiled grains from the pot and curry from the bowl, and likewise rice from the pot and curry from the bowl. On one occasion, great king, (

body.translated_text: ) I was dwelling near the village-town of <s>Vaibhiḍiṃgī</s> for the rains-retreat. My monastery was being rained upon by the first rain of the season. At that time, the workshop of <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s> was freshly thatched with new grass. I addressed the attendant monks: "Go, monks, to the workshop of <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s> — strip the freshly grass-thatched workshop and thatch my monastery with it." They, having assented with "Yes," began to strip the freshly grass-thatched workshop of <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s>. At that time, <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s> had gone out on some errand. Knowing this, with that very joy and delight, he spent seven days in a single cross-legged posture, and for half a month his constant, uninterrupted mindfulness did not leave his body — it continued unbroken in his body. 'Fortunate indeed is <s>Nandīpāla Ghaṭīkāra</s>, that the <s>Bhagavān</s> has such extreme trust and confidence in his family.'

What do you think, monks? He who was the young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Uttara</s> — that was none other than myself at that time, in that era. The harsh speech I directed against the fully awakened <s>Kāśyapa</s> — 'How could that shaven-headed ascetic attain awakening? For awakening is supremely difficult' — by the ripening of that deed, I now practiced austerities for six years. Had I, however, repudiated awakening [altogether], I would have had to toil for three more incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) for the sake of self-awakening. Thus, monks, for purely dark deeds the result is purely dark — as before, down to: effort should be made only toward purely bright deeds. Thus, monks, you should train.

body.translated_text: On the very day the <s>Bodhisattva</s> departed, <s>Yaśodharā</s> became pregnant. When the <s>Bodhisattva</s> was practicing austerities, the inner apartments too began to practice austerities. <s>Yaśodharā</s>'s embryo went into dormancy. When the <s>Bhagavān</s>, understanding that fruitless austerity is pointless, began to breathe in comfort and breathe out in comfort, to take solid food — rice and barley gruel — to anoint his limbs with ghee and oil, and to bathe his body with warm water, the inner apartments too then breathed in comfort, breathed out in comfort, took solid food — rice and barley gruel — anointed their limbs with ghee and oil, and bathed their bodies with warm water. 'What shall the boy's name be?' His kinsmen said: 'At his birth, <s>Rāhu</s> seized the moon; therefore let the boy's name be <s>Rāhula</s>.' When the prince was born, the <s>Śākyas</s> spoke even more [mockingly] to his mother. She, having made a declaration of truth (<s>satyopayācana</s>), placed <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> on the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s exercise-stone and immersed him in the pleasure-pool: 'If this one was begotten by the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, let him float.' He began to float. She said: 'Let him come from the far side to the near side.' He came from the far side to the near side. They were struck with astonishment. <s>Yaśodharā</s> said: 'I shall demonstrate further to you that this one was begotten by the <s>Bodhisattva</s> and that I have not been unfaithful.'
When the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having crossed over the six years and attained full awakening, arrived at <s>Kapilavastu</s>, one day he ate in the royal palace, another in the inner apartments. Then <s>Yaśodharā</s> thought: 'What stratagem might there be by which I could draw the <s>Bhagavān</s> back to me?' Now in <s>Kapilavastu</s> there was a certain female wanderer (<s>parivrājikā</s>) exceedingly skilled in love-charms and similar rites. <s>Yaśodharā</s> gave her five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s>: 'Noble lady, prepare a love-charm with these coins and send it.' She prepared a love-charm sweet-ball and sent it to <s>Yaśodharā</s>. <s>Yaśodharā</s> placed it in <s>Rāhula</s>'s hand and said: 'Son, give this to your father.' At that point, nothing is unknown, unseen, ununderstood, or unrecognized by <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> considered: 'A false rumor has gone out about <s>Yaśodharā</s>. I must act on behalf of her who is innocent.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> created five hundred emanations of <s>Buddhas</s>. <s>Rāhula</s>, having looked at all the <s>Buddhas</s>, gave it to the <s>Bhagavān</s> who stood at the head. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having taken it, gave it back to him. <s>Rāhula</s> ate it. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having given a teaching in thanks for the offering, departed. The prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> followed behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>; even when turned back, he would not turn back — he cried. When <s>Rāhula</s> had thus recognized the <s>Bhagavān</s>, King <s>Śuddhodana</s> together with the people of the inner apartments and the <s>Śākyas</s> were struck with the utmost astonishment and became exceedingly devoted to <s>Yaśodharā</s>. Thus <s>Yaśodharā</s>'s vindication was entirely accomplished. The <s>Bhagavān</s> began to ordain the prince <s>Rāhula</s>. King <s>Śuddhodana</s> heard of it. He approached the <s>Bhagavān</s> and said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, if the prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> must absolutely be ordained, let him remain for one day today while I perform a celebration for him.' King <s>Śuddhodana</s> held a great festival for <s>Rāhula</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s>: 'Ordain the prince <s>Rāhula</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and the prince <s>Rāhulabhadra</s> was ordained.
The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, the Venerable <s>Rāhula</s> was recognized by the <s>Bhagavān</s> among a great multitude by means of a sweet-ball.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, monks — in the past too I was recognized by this <s>Rāhula</s> by means of a garland. Listen to that.'

She said: 'Noble husband, do so.' He took goods and set out for the great ocean. He met his death right there. Then his wife, having completed her mourning, raised, nourished, and brought up that boy by the strength of her hands and the support of her kinsmen. Not far from them lived a weaver, skilled in his own craft. Everything prospered for him through his craft. She, seeing the prosperity from his craft, said: 'Better the weaver's craft than setting out for the ocean. When one goes to the ocean, one meets with calamity and misfortune.' She said to that weaver: 'Brother, teach this nephew of mine the weaver's craft as well.' He said: 'Very well.' (

body.translated_text: ) 'So be it.' He began to train him. The boy was quick and clever. In a short time, he learned the weaver's craft. The weaver would bathe well, dress well, and eat fine food. The boy said: 'Uncle, you do the same work as I do; I too do the same. Then why do you bathe well, dress well, and eat fine food, while I cannot manage to do so?' He replied: 'Nephew, I do two types of work — weaving by day and thieving by night.' The boy said: 'Uncle, if so, I too shall do thieving.' 'Nephew, will you be able to steal?' 'Uncle, I shall be able.' He reflected: 'Let me first test him.' He took him to the market. There he bought a hare and gave it to him: 'Nephew, cook this while I go and bathe.' He went and bathed. The boy quickly cooked it and ate one leg. The weaver returned from bathing. 'Nephew, is the hare cooked?' 'Uncle, it is cooked.' 'Let me see.' The boy presented it. He saw three legs. He said: 'Nephew, where has the fourth leg gone?' The boy said: 'Uncle, a hare has no fourth leg. Where would it go?' He reflected: 'I am merely a thief, but this one is a great thief.' He took him and the three-legged hare and entered a tavern: 'Nephew, let us drink liquor.' 'Let us drink.' The two drank. The weaver said: 'Nephew, let us deny paying for the liquor.' The boy said: 'Uncle, whoever drank should deny it. I did not drink at all — why should I deny it?' The weaver reflected: 'This is a great thief. It is possible to commit theft together with him.' He began committing thefts together with him. The weaver put his head through the breach in the wall. The boy said to him: 'Uncle, you do not even know how to steal properly! The feet should be put through first, not the head. If the head is cut off, the body is recognized, and the entire family is destroyed. Put your feet through.' He put his feet through. Then a cry arose: 'Thief! Thief!' and he was caught by the feet. A great crowd of people gathered. The boy alone could not pull him out. He cut off his head, took it, and departed. The ministers reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, a thief entered through a breach and was caught. Someone cut off his head, took it, and departed.' The king said: 'Sirs, the one who (

and began seizing a woman by the neck, then a man, then a tree, then a horse, then a bull, then a buffalo, then a goat, then a dog. When the people recognized him as a madman, then he seized that headless corpse by the neck, wept to his heart's content, and departed. The royal officers reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, a madman seized that corpse by the neck, wept to his heart's content, and departed.' The king said: 'Sirs, that is the very same lone thief. It was not well done that he was not seized. Now seize him.' The lone thief reflected: 'Should I not honor my uncle?' He disguised himself as a cart-driver, filled a cart with firewood, went to that spot, placed the cart full of firewood upon the corpse, released the oxen, set fire to the cart, and departed.
By the burning of the cart, that headless corpse was cremated. The royal officers reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, that lone thief has been cremated.' The king said: 'By whom?' They reported what had happened. The king said: 'Sirs, that cart-driver is the very same lone thief. It was not well done that he was not seized. Seize him.' The lone thief reflected: 'Should I not perform the funerary rites for my uncle at the cremation ground?' He disguised himself as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, begged for alms at the capital, cooked those alms at the cremation ground, offered five <s>piṇḍas</s> (funerary rice-balls) at the spot where the corpse had been cremated, and departed. The royal officers reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> begged for alms at the capital, and at the very spot where that corpse was cremated, he offered five <s>piṇḍas</s> and departed.' The king said: 'Sirs, that is the very same lone thief. It was not well done that he was not seized.' The lone thief reflected: 'Should I not cast my uncle's bones into the <s>Gaṅgā</s>?' body.translated_text: ) It was not well done that he was not seized. In any case, you stand aside — I myself shall seize him.' The king had a water-garden made on the <s>Gaṅgā</s> with boats. Guards were stationed on both banks. The king's daughter, who was beautiful, lovely, and charming, was placed in that water-garden. She was told: 'If anyone seizes you, you must cry out.' And the guards were commanded: 'When she cries out, you must go to the water-garden. If there is any man there, seize him and bring him to me.' The lone thief reflected: 'Should I not enjoy myself with the king's daughter?' He positioned himself downstream in the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. There he began throwing empty pots. One was thrown; the guards, thinking 'Thief!', ran over. It was smashed by their blows. A second was thrown; it too was smashed. A third was thrown; it too was smashed. The guards thought: 'These are just empty pots being carried along,' and they stood indifferent. Then the lone thief, putting his head into an empty pot, was carried by the current to that spot. He climbed onto the boat and said to the girl: 'Do not make a sound. I will not kill you.' Terrified, she remained silent. Having enjoyed himself with her, he departed. She began to wail: 'This thief has enjoyed himself with me and is leaving!' The guards said: 'When he was enjoying himself with you, you were silent. Now that he has enjoyed himself and left, you cry. Where shall we search for him now?' The guards reported what had happened to the king. The king said: 'It was not well done that he was not seized.' body.translated_text:
) There is a quick miraculous power that can win over ordinary people. Let me win over the inner palace by the miracle of supernatural power.' Having decided thus, he rose up into the sky in the eastern direction and manifested the four modes of deportment — namely, he walked, stood, sat, and lay down. He also entered the fire-element (<s>tejodhātu</s>). When the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> had entered the fire-element, various rays emanated from his body — namely, blue, yellow, red, white, crimson, and crystal-colored. He also displayed the twin miracles (<s>yamaka prātihārya</s>): from the lower part of his body flames blazed forth; from the upper part of his body cool streams of water flowed. From the upper part flames blazed forth; from the lower part cool streams of water flowed. Just as in the eastern direction, so too in the southern, western, and northern directions — displaying the fourfold, manifold miracle of supernatural power in the four directions, withdrawing those volitional formations of supernatural power, he sat down on the very seat prepared before the community of monks. Then those women, having seen the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s miracle of supernatural power, won over, like trees cut at the root, fell at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known their inclinations, latent tendencies, nature, and character, gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> as penetrates the Four Noble Truths. Having heard it, sixty thousand women headed by <s>Gopikā</s> and <s>Mṛgajā</s> directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). But <s>Yaśodharā</s>, being exceedingly overpowered by sensual passion, did not attain the vision of the truths. She thought: 'Let me entice the <s>Bhagavān</s> through the craving for taste.' Having decided, she herself prepared food and drink for the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s sake and declared: 'Today I shall satisfy the <s>Bhagavān</s> with my own hands.' Having heard, the monks informed the <s>Bhagavān</s>: '<s>Yaśodharā</s>, Venerable Sir, wishes to entice the <s>Bhagavān</s> with her own hands through the craving for taste.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Formerly, monks, I was with passion, with hatred, with delusion — I perceived taste and perceived the passion for taste. Now I am free from passion, free from hatred, free from delusion — I perceive taste but do not perceive the passion for taste. How then could <s>Yaśodharā</s> entice me through the craving for taste?'
  The monks, doubts having arisen, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir — <s>Yaśodharā</s> has set about trying to entice the <s>Bhagavān</s> with a bewitching sweet.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, monks — in the past too I was enticed by her with a sweet. Hear about that.' (

body.translated_text: dwelt. He was one of severe austerities, eating roots, fruits, and water, clothed in antelope skins and bark. He had directly realized the five supernatural powers (<s>pañcābhijñā</s>). Even wild beasts dwelt in his hermitage grounds with complete trust. He had set out to a certain place to relieve himself. A doe followed behind him. He urinated while aroused. That [urine] was drunk by the doe. The female organ was licked by her tongue. Inconceivable is the ripening of <s>karma</s> for beings — she became pregnant. When the time of delivery came, she returned to that very place and gave birth. A boy was born. Having smelled [him], knowing him to be a being of a different species, she was frightened; leaving behind urine and excrement, she fled. Meanwhile, that sage arrived at the place. He saw the boy. He began to consider: 'Whose son is this?' He saw — his own. He took him to his hermitage, fed him, nourished him, and raised him. As the boy grew, deer-horns appeared on his head. Because his horns were like those of a deer, the name <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> ('Deer-Horned') was given to him. In time, the sage became ill. The sage was attended with proper remedies, but the disease would not subside. When mortal suffering appeared and he knew he would die before long, he addressed his son: 'Son, to this hermitage, sages dwelling in various regions come from time to time. You should welcome them with greetings and courteous hospitality for my sake, invite them to sit, and provide them as best you can with fruits and roots.' Having said this —

body.translated_text: ) The rain-god ceased to rain. A great famine arose in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. People dispersed in all directions. The king summoned soothsayers and asked: 'Sirs, by whose power does the rain-god not rain?' They said: 'Your Majesty, because of a sage's wrath. If that sage can be caused to fall from his austerity, then the rain-god will rain; otherwise not.' The king remained absorbed in worry. The women of the inner palace and the ministers and princes said: 'Your Majesty, why are you so absorbed in worry?' He said: 'Because of a sage's wrath the rain-god does not rain. And the soothsayers say thus: "If that sage is caused to fall from his austerity, then the rain-god will rain; otherwise not." But it is not known — who can cause him to fall from his austerity?'

body.text: iti; tasya rājño duhitā śāntā nāma; sā kathayati: deva yady evam alpotsuko bhava; ahaṃ tathā kariṣyāmi yathāsau riṣis tasmāt tapasaḥ calati iti; sa kathayati kenopāyena? sā kathayati: māṃ brāhmaṇakān mantrān pāṭhaya anyāṃś ca kanyāḥ; nausaṃkrame ca āśramapadaṃ kāraya puṣpaphalasalilasaṃpannam iti; tena brāhamṇakān mantrān pāṭhitā anyāś ca kanyāḥ, nausaṃkrame ca tādṛśam āśramapadaṃ kāritaṃ, tataḥ tayā tāni phalāni vaśīkaraṇadravyaiḥ madyena ca samāpūritāni; aparāṇi ca nānāvicitrāṇi ca phalāni kāritāni; riṣiveṣaḥ kṛtaḥ; sā cīvaravalkalaprāvṛtā; sā tābhiḥ kanyābhiḥ brāhmaṇakān mantrān pāṭhayantī āśramapadaṃ gatā; riṣeḥ śiṣyair niveditam upādhyāya bahavas tavāśramapadaṃ riṣaya āgatāḥ; svāgataṃ riṣīṇāṃ praviśantu iti; te praviṣṭāḥ; sa dṛṣṭvā gāthāṃ bhāṣate:
body.translated_text: The king had a daughter named <s>Śāntā</s>. She said: 'Your Majesty, if that is so, be at ease. I shall act in such a way that that sage falls from his austerity.' He said: 'By what means?' She said: 'Have me taught <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> mantras, and other maidens as well. And have a hermitage built on a boat, endowed with flowers, fruits, and water.' He had her taught <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> mantras, and the other maidens as well; and such a hermitage was built on a boat. Then she filled those fruits with bewitching substances and liquor, and had various other artfully made fruits prepared. She put on the guise of a sage. children.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s>. At a later time, he went out to hunt deer. Gradually he entered a mountain cave. There he saw a <s>Kinnara</s> (celestial musician) and a <s>Kinnarī</s>. The <s>Kinnara</s> was sleeping; the <s>Kinnarī</s> was awake. The king, having drawn his bow to full stretch, struck the <s>Kinnara</s> with an arrow in a vital spot. He was separated from life. The king seized the <s>Kinnarī</s> to take as his wife. The king set out taking her with him. She said: 'Your Majesty, wait — give me permission to perform the funeral rites for this <s>Kinnara</s>'s body.' The king considered: 'Where will she go? Let me see how she performs the funeral rites for his body.' She was permitted by him. Then she propped up the <s>Kinnara</s> with logs, lit the funeral pyre, and threw herself [into it]. A deity spoke a verse:

children.text: anyathā cintito py artha anyathā parivartitaḥ /
children.translated_text: The matter was conceived one way, but turned out another —
'I shall enjoy the <s>Kinnarī</s>' — instead, a double killing of living beings was accomplished. //
