body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo viśvapuryāṃ rājadhānyām viśvāmitro nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca sphītaṃ ca kṣemaṃ ca subhikṣaṃ ca ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca praśāntakalikalahaḍimbaḍamarataskararogāpagataṃ śālīkṣugomahiṣīsaṃpannaṃ; dhārmiko dharmarājo dharmeṇa rājyaṃ kārayati; sa ca rājā śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśayaḥ ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ prajāvatsalaḥ; so 'pareṇa samayena devyā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati; tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ kālāntareṇa patnī āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā; sā aṣṭānāṃ va nāvānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā; dārako jātaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gauraḥ kanakavarṇaḥ chatrākāraśirāḥ pralambabāhur vistīrṇalalāṭaḥ saṃgatabhrūs tuṅganāsaḥ sarvāṅgapratyaṅgopetaḥ; tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate; kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāma? iti; jñātaya ūcuḥ; ayaṃ dārako viśvāmitrasya rājñaḥ putraḥ; tasmād bhavatu dārakasya viśvantara iti nāma iti; viśvantaro dārakaḥ aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradattaḥ; dvābhyām aṃśadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikadhātrībhyāṃ; so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpirmaṇḍena anyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣair āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam; sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttaḥ tadā lipyām upanyastaḥ saṅkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāṃ; yāni tāni rājñāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktānāṃ
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the royal capital of <s>Viśvapurī</s>, a king named <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was exercising sovereignty — it was prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, teeming with many people, free from strife, quarrels, disputes, altercations, thieves, and diseases, abounding in rice, sugarcane, cattle, and buffalo. He was righteous, a <s>Dharma</s>-king, ruling his kingdom according to <s>Dharma</s>. That king was faithful, virtuous, of good intentions, devoted to the welfare of himself and others, compassionate, great-souled, a lover of <s>Dharma</s>, and tender toward his subjects. At a later time, he enjoyed, amused, and attended to his queen. As he enjoyed, amused, and attended to her, in the course of time the queen became pregnant. After the passing of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, charming, fair-skinned, golden-complexioned, with an umbrella-shaped head, long arms, a broad forehead, joined eyebrows, a high nose, and endowed with all major and minor limbs. At his birth, a birth-celebration was held and a name was to be assigned. 'What shall the boy's name be?' The kinsmen said: 'This boy is the son of King <s>Viśvāmitra</s>; therefore let the boy's name be <s>Viśvantara</s>.' The boy <s>Viśvantara</s> was entrusted to eight nurses: two for carrying, two for nursing, two for bathing, and two for play. He was raised and nourished by those eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, skimmed ghee, and other choice refined provisions, and grew quickly like a lotus in a lake. When he had grown up, he was instructed in writing, arithmetic, calculation, and seal-making. Those various arts and crafts and practical skills that belong to anointed <s>Kṣatriya</s> kings

children.translated_text: The <s>Bodhisattva</s> said: 'In the end, separation must inevitably come for us both — such is the nature of the world. But you are accustomed to the finest food, drink, bedding, seats, and garments, and your body is supremely delicate. In the forest of austerities, one must sleep on the ground covered with grass and leaves; roots and fruits are the food; one must walk upon ground strewn with <s>darbha</s> grass, pebbles, and thorns; one must frequently observe fasting; one must show oneself attentive to all people; guests must be honored with every effort. And there too, I must necessarily give gifts according to my ability. You must feel no regret about any of this. body.translated_text:
The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel Feeding-ground). At that time, in <s>Campā</s>, there lived a householder named <s>Potalaka</s> — wealthy, of great riches and great possessions, with extensive and vast holdings, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> in wealth, a competitor with <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>'s wealth. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He sported, enjoyed, and dallied with her. As he sported, enjoyed, and dallied, in the course of time his wife became pregnant. She was attended to with provisions suitable for cold in cold weather, provisions suitable for heat in hot weather, and foods prescribed by physicians — neither too bitter, nor too sour, nor too salty, nor too sweet, nor too pungent, nor too astringent, devoid of the six tastes of bitter, sour, salty, sweet, pungent, and astringent. Her limbs adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, she moved about like an <s>Apsaras</s> in <s>Nandana</s> garden, going from couch to couch, from seat to seat, never descending to the lower floor. And no unpleasant sound reached her ears until the ripening of the child in the womb.
  At that time, the householder <s>Potalaka</s> had gone to <s>Rājagṛha</s> on some business. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth under the <s>Śravaṇa</s> constellation. A boy was born — handsome, good-looking, and pleasing. On the soles of his feet, hairs of golden color, four finger-breadths long, had grown. Then <s>Potalaka</s>'s servant hurried to <s>Rājagṛha</s> and told the householder <s>Potalaka</s>: 'Congratulations, householder — a son has been born to you!' Filled with joy and delight, he asked again: 'What are you saying, householder — a son has been born to me?' He asked again: 'What are you saying?' Then that man thought: 'Why does this householder keep asking again and again? Could he be trying to make me babble on?' Knowing this, he stood silent. The householder said: 'Good man, you are a miser with words! If you had uttered even a hundred words, I would have filled your mouth with gold for each one!' Then the householder <s>Potalaka</s> filled the man's mouth with gold three times.

body.translated_text: ) him in <s>Campā</s> a shared revenue grant of seven elephants.' The householder <s>Potalaka</s>, having paid respects to King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, returned to <s>Campā</s>. Then the householder's kinsmen, over twenty-one days of three weeks, performed the birth-celebration for the newborn, and a name was assigned: 'What shall the boy's name be?' Others said: 'This boy was born under the <s>Śravaṇa</s> constellation. And his father gave twenty <s>koṭis</s> of gold as his nursing allowance at his birth. Therefore, let the boy's name be <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> (Śroṇa of the Twenty Koṭis).' The name <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> was assigned. The boy <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two body-nurses, two milk-nurses, two washing-nurses, and two play-nurses. Raised by eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, skimmed ghee, and other choice provisions, he grew quickly like a lotus in a lake. When he was grown, he was trained in writing, arithmetic, calculation, seal-craft, withdrawal, deposit, appraisal of goods, appraisal of cloth, appraisal of gems, appraisal of wood, appraisal of elephants, appraisal of horses, appraisal of young men, and appraisal of young women. In those eight appraisals, he became an opener [of cases], an expert reader, learned, sharp in practice. Having heard of his great merit and renown, families of equal standing gave him many daughters. His father had three mansions built for him — one for winter, one for summer, and one for the rainy season. Three gardens were laid out — one for winter, one for summer, and one for the rainy season. Three inner apartments were established — senior, middle, and junior. Ascending to the upper terrace of the palace, he sported, enjoyed, and dallied with unmanned musical instruments. Every day, food was prepared for five hundred persons for his meals.

Then King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, having had ghee drunk by the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and wishing to bring him the cream, set out for the <s>Veṇuvana</s> bearing the cream-dish. <s>Ajātaśatru</s> saw him. He threw a golden [object]. The king, being skilled in detecting sounds, [dodged], and so his cream-dish was broken. The king turned back from that very spot.

<s>Devadatta</s> incited Prince <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: 'Prince, when all kings have grey hair on their heads, they establish the eldest prince in sovereignty and kingship and go forth [as renunciants]. Your father's hair has turned to a third shade. Even so, he remains engrossed in sensual pleasures and does not become calm.' (

body.text: bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate: vinipātito maudgalyāyana ajātaśatruṇā akalyāṇamitropagūḍhena tathāgatasya piṇḍapātaḥ; gaccha campāyāṃ potalakaputrasya sakāśāt piṇḍapātam ādāya iti; evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpannaḥ yathā samāhite citte rājagṛhe 'ntarhitaś campāyāṃ pratyaṣṭhāt; śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśaḥ ādityabhaktaḥ; sa dine dine kālyam evotthāya ādityaṃ namasyati; āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyayānaḥ ṛddhyā ādityamaṇḍalaṃ bhitvā avatīrṇaḥ; atha śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśaḥ dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ: pratyakṣam evāham ādityaṃ svena rūpeṇa paśyāmi iti; dṛṣṭvā ca punar gāthāṃ bhāṣate
body.translated_text: the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s alms-food has been destroyed by <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, who is in the grip of an evil companion, <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>. Go — take alms-food from the son of <s>Potalaka</s> in <s>Campā</s>.' 'Yes, Venerable Sir,' the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s> and entered such a <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) that, with his mind concentrated, he vanished from <s>Rājagṛha</s> and appeared in <s>Campā</s>. <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> was a devotee of the sun. Every day, rising early, he would pay homage to the sun. The Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, by his supernatural power, broke through the orb of the sun and descended. Then <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, seeing this, was overcome with supreme wonder: 'With my own eyes I behold the sun in his very form!' And having seen, he spoke a verse:

children.translated_text: Who is this who, having pierced the sun, earthward
now approaches my dwelling with equal swiftness? /

body.text: ājñāpaya kim āgamanaprayojanam iti; sa kathayati: bhagavataḥ piṇḍapātam anuprayaccha; ko 'sau bhagavān? asti gṛhapatiputra śramaṇo gautamaḥ śākyaputraḥ śākyakulāt keśaśmaśrv avatārya kāṣāyāṇi vastrāṇy ācchādya samyag eva śraddhayā agārād anagārikāṃ pravrajitaḥ; so 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisambuddhaḥ; sa eṣa gṛhapatiputra buddho nāma; tasya buddha ity aśrutapūrvaṃ ghoṣaṃ śrutvā saromakūpāṇy āhṛṣṭāṇi; tenābhiprasannena sa eva paṃcaśatikaḥ pākaḥ āyuṣmate mahāmaudgalyāyanāya pratipāditaḥ
body.translated_text: 'Command me — what is the purpose of your coming?' He said: 'Offer alms-food to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' 'Who is this <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 'There is, son of a householder, an ascetic <s>Gautama</s>, a son of the <s>Śākyas</s>. Having shaved his hair and beard and donned saffron robes, he has gone forth from the household life into homelessness with perfect faith, from the <s>Śākya</s> clan. He has awakened to unsurpassed perfect <s>Samyaksaṃbodhi</s> (complete awakening). He, son of a householder, is known as the <s>Buddha</s>.' Upon hearing the word '<s>Buddha</s>' — a sound never heard before — the hair on his body stood on end. Filled with faith, he offered that very five-hundred-portion meal to the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>.

King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s> was approaching the <s>Bhagavān</s> carrying a second pot-cooked meal. He saw the entire <s>Veṇuvana</s> suffused with various (

surabhiṇā āhāragandhena sphuṭaṃ; sa saṃlakṣayati nūnaṃ śakreṇa devendreṇa anyābhir devatābhir bhagavataḥ piṇḍapātaḥ upanītaḥ; yathedaṃ veṇuvanaṃ nānāvidhena surabhiṇā āhāragandhena sphuṭam; iti viditvā bhagavantam idam avocat: kiṃ bhadanta śakreṇa devendreṇa anyābhir devatābhir bhagavataḥ piṇḍapāta upanītaḥ? yena veṇuvanaṃ nānāvidhena surabhiṇā āhāragandhena sphuṭam iti; bhagavān āha: na mahārāja śakreṇa devendreṇa nāpy anyābhir devatābhir upanītaḥ; api tu tavaiva vijite campāyāṃ potalakaputrasya dine dine paṃcaśatikaḥ sthālīpākaḥ sādhyate; tato maudgalyāyanena bhikṣuṇā ānitaḥ iti; tasya bhagavān varṇaṃ bhāṣitum ārabdhaḥ iti śrutvāpi tasya darśanakāmatā utpannā; bhagavāṃs tasya cetasā cittam ājñāya kathayati: mahārāja puṇyamaheśākhyas sa satvaḥ; mā tasya ājñāṃ dāsyasi; mā te puṇyaparikṣayo bhaviṣyati; api tu mahārāja paribhuṅkṣva pātraśeṣaṃ; sa kathayati: aham asmi bhadanta rājā; bhadanta kṣatriyo mūrdhābhiṣiktaḥ; na mayā kasyacit pātraśeṣaṃ paribhuktapūrvaṃ; kiṃtu bhagavān dharmatayā pitā bhavati; yadi bhagavān ājñāpayati <tarhi paribhuṃje iti> paribhoktum ārabdhaḥ; bhagavān āha: asti mahārāja tvayā kadācid evaṃrūpam annapānaṃ paribhuktapūrvaṃ? rājā kathayati: ayaṃ bhadanta rājakule vṛddho, rājā ca saṃvṛttaḥ nābhijānāty evaṃrūpam annapānam āsvāditapūrvaṃ; puṇyamaheśākhyo mahārāja sa satvaḥ ya īdṛśam annapānaṃ paribhuṅkte
body.translated_text: was pervaded with various fragrant food-aromas. He thought: 'Surely <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, or other deities, have brought alms-food for the <s>Bhagavān</s>, since this <s>Veṇuvana</s> is pervaded with various fragrant food-aromas.' Having understood this, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Venerable Sir, have <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, or other deities, brought alms-food for the <s>Bhagavān</s>? For this <s>Veṇuvana</s> is pervaded with various fragrant food-aromas.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'No, great king, neither <s>Śakra</s> nor any other deities have brought it. Rather, in your own domain, in <s>Campā</s>, a five-hundred-course pot-meal is prepared daily for the son of <s>Potalaka</s>. It was brought from there by the monk <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> began to praise him. Having heard, the king developed a desire to see him. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing his mind with his own, said: 'Great king, that being is called Great-in-Merit. Do not give him a command, lest there be a diminution of your merit. But, great king, partake of the remainder in the bowl.' He said: 'I am a king, Venerable Sir — an anointed <s>Kṣatriya</s>. I have never before eaten anyone's bowl-leavings. But the <s>Bhagavān</s> is, in the order of <s>Dharma</s>, a father. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> commands it, I shall partake.' He began to eat. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Have you, great king, ever before partaken of such food and drink?' The king said: 'This one, Venerable Sir, has grown old in a royal family and become king — he does not recall ever having tasted such food and drink.' 'Great-in-Merit is that being, great king, who partakes of such food and drink.'

body.text: King Bimbisāra desires to see Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa
body.translated_text: King <s>Bimbisāra</s> desires to see <s>Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa</s>

body.text: atha rājā māgadhaḥ śreṇyo bimbisāraḥ bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā bhagavato 'ntikāt prakrāntaḥ; tena amātyānām ājñā dattā: sannāhayantu bhavantaḥ caturaṅgaṃ balakāyaṃ; campāṃ gamiṣyāmi; kasyārthe? potalakaputraṃ draṣṭuṃ; devasyāsau viṣayanivāsī; ihaivāhūyatāṃ; puṇyamaheśākhyo 'sau satvaḥ; na tasya ājñā dātavyā; deva vayaṃ tathā kariṣyāmaḥ, yathā ājñāṃ na dāsyāmaḥ; sa cāgamiṣyati; evaṃ kuruta iti; taiś campāyā lekho 'nupreṣitaḥ; bhavanto nagaraśobhāṃ kuruta; yavasayogāsanaṃ ca samdānayata; rājā āgamiṣyati; iti śrutvā parituṣṭāḥ; bhūyo lekho 'nupreṣitaḥ; bhavanto na rājā āgamiṣyati; api tu kumāra āgacchati it; te santrastāḥ: karkaśaḥ (
body.translated_text: Then King <s>Śreṇya Bimbisāra</s> of <s>Magadha</s>, having bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet, departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. He gave an order to his ministers: 'Sirs, equip the four-division army. I shall go to <s>Campā</s>.' 'For what purpose?' 'To see the son of <s>Potalaka</s>.' 'Your Majesty, he is a resident of your domain. Let him simply be summoned here.' 'That being is called Great-in-Merit. No command should be given to him.' 'Your Majesty, we shall act in such a way that we give no command, and yet he will come.' 'Do so.' They sent a letter to <s>Campā</s>: 'Sirs, prepare a city-festival and also prepare fodder, stables, and seats. The king is coming.' Hearing this, they were delighted. Then another letter was sent: 'Sirs, the king is not coming. Rather, the prince is coming.' They were alarmed: 'The prince is harsh (

body.text: SBV II 139
body.translated_text: SBV II 139

body.text: ) kumāraḥ, kadācid āgata anarthaṃ kariṣyati iti; bhuyo likhitaṃ; na rāja āgacchati; nāpi kumāraḥ; api tu yuṣmābhir gaṅgā tathā baddhavyā yathā pratilomā vahati; iti śrutvā campānivāsinaḥ paurās sannipatitāḥ: bhavanto nūnam asmān rājā daṇḍayitukāmaḥ, yenaivaṃ likhati iti tair amātyānām anena arthena lekho 'nupreṣitaḥ; tair vācayitvā punas teṣāṃ yathābhūtaṃ sandiṣṭaṃ: bhavantaḥ eṣa paramārthaḥ; na rājā āgacchati; na kumāraḥ; nāpi gaṅgābandhena kiṃcit prayojanam; api tu devaḥ potalakaputraṃ
body.translated_text: ) — if he comes, he might cause harm.' Another message was written: 'Neither the king is coming, nor the prince. Rather, you must dam the <s>Gaṅgā</s> so that it flows in reverse.' Hearing this, the citizens of <s>Campā</s> assembled: 'Sirs, surely the king wishes to punish us, since he writes thus.' They sent a letter about this matter to the ministers. The ministers had it read, and then informed them truthfully: 'Sirs, this is the real intent. The king is not coming; nor the prince; nor is there any purpose in damming the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. But His Majesty wishes to see the son of <s>Potalaka</s>

body.text: draṣṭukāmaḥ; tair avacarakaḥ puruṣaḥ preṣitaḥ; tenāpy evam eva samākhyātaṃ; tatas te saṃbhūya potalakasya gṛhapateḥ sakāśaṃ gatāḥ; gṛhapate devaḥ śroṇaṃ koṭiviṃśaṃ draṣṭukāmaḥ; preṣaya amātyair asmākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sandiṣṭam; avacarakapuruṣeṇapi sa evārthaḥ samākhyātaḥ iti; sa kathayati: bhavanto na preṣayāmi; yo mama bhāgas taṃ suvarṇapiṇḍair api badhnīyām iti; te kathayanti: gṛhapate yady apy evaṃ tathāpi paścimā janatā anukampitavyā iti; sa kathayati: bhavanto yady evaṃ samayataḥ anujānāmi; yadi yuṣmākam api putrāḥ śroṇena sārdhaṃ gacchati iti; te kathayanti: gṛhapate evaṃ bhavatu; gacchantu bhavantaḥ
body.translated_text: .' They sent a trustworthy man. He too told them the same thing. Then they gathered together and went to the householder <s>Potalaka</s>: 'Householder, His Majesty wishes to see <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>. Send him. The ministers have told us the true state of affairs. A trustworthy man has also reported the same thing.' He said: 'Sirs, I shall not send him. I would bind my share of him with ingots of gold rather [than let him go].' They said: 'Householder, even so, compassion should be shown to the rest of the people.' He said: 'Sirs, if so, I consent on a condition: your sons also go with <s>Śroṇa</s>.' They said: 'Householder, so be it. Let them go, sirs.'

children.text: Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa goes to Rājagṛha to visit Bimbisāra
children.translated_text: <s>Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa</s> goes to <s>Rājagṛha</s> to visit <s>Bimbisāra</s>

children.text: atha potalako gṛhapatir yena śroṇakoṭīviṃśas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya śroṇaṃ koṭīviṃśam idam avocat: putra imepaura evaṃ kathayanti iti; sa kathayati: tāta yady evaṃ gacchāmi iti; putra nūnaṃ sa rājā tava pādayoḥ suvarṇavarṇāni romāṇi draṣṭukāmaḥ; na tvayā tasya pādau utkṣipya darśayitavyau; rājāna asthānaprakopinaḥ; mā te anarthaṃ kariṣyanti; ayaṃ muktāhāraḥ; etaṃ rājñaḥ pādayoḥ sthāpayitvā praṇāmaṃ ca kṛtvā tasya purastāt paryaṅkaṃ badhvā niṣīda; tato romāṇi drakṣyati iti; tataḥ potalako gṛhapatiḥ saṃlakṣayati: katareṇa yānena śroṇaṃ preṣayāmi? kiṃ hastiyānena? aśvayānena? rathayānen? uta nauyānena iti; tasyaitad abhavat; nauyānam eṣāṃ varaṃ; nauyānena preṣayāmi iti; tena nadyāṃ gaṅgāyāṃ nausaṅkramo māpitaḥ; tatra vicitram udyānaṃ kāritaṃ nānāpuṣpaphalasaṃpannaṃ haṃsakrauñcamayūraśukaśārikākokilādivihaṅganikūjitaṃ; vividhāni vāditrāṇi, naryaś ca nānālaṅkāravibhūṣitāḥ samāropitāḥ; tad anayā vibhūtyā jalamadhyena preṣitaḥ; (

children.translated_text: SBV II 140

children.text: ) so 'nupūrveṇa rājagṛhasamīpaṃ gataḥ; rājñā bimbisāreṇa śrutaṃ potalakaputraḥ āgacchati iti; tena yāvac ca rājagṛhaṃ, yāvac ca nādī gaṅgā atrāntarāt khātam asyāḥ pūrayitvā tanmadhyena naur ākṛṣṭā; rājagṛhaṃ ca tan nagaram apagatapāṣāṇaśarkarakaṭhallaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ candanavāripariṣiktaṃ surabhidhūpaghaṭikopanibaddham āmuktapaṭṭadāmakalāpam ucchṛtadhvajapatākaṃ nānāpuṣpāvakīrṇaṃ ramaṇīyaṃ devānām iva nandanavanodyānaṃ; so 'nayā vibhūtyā rājagṛhaṃ nagaraṃ praveśitaḥ; tato 'sau rājñaḥ siṃhāsanasthasya muktāhāraṃ pādayor datvā, śirasā praṇamya, purastāt paryaṅkaṃ badhvā niṣaṇṇaḥ; rājā tasya pādatalayoḥ suvarṇavarṇāni romāṇi dṛṣṭvā paraṃ vismayam āpannaḥ: aho puṇyamaheśākhyaḥ śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśaḥ iti
children.translated_text: ) Gradually he arrived near <s>Rājagṛha</s>. King <s>Bimbisāra</s> heard that the son of <s>Potalaka</s> was coming. He had a canal dug from <s>Rājagṛha</s> to the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>, filled it with water, and had the boat drawn through it. The city of <s>Rājagṛha</s> was cleared of stones, gravel, and rubbish, sprinkled with sandalwood water, adorned with fragrant incense-burners, festooned with silk-banner garlands, with raised banners and pennants, strewn with various flowers — beautiful, like the <s>Nandana</s> garden of the gods. With this splendor, he was brought into the city of <s>Rājagṛha</s>. Then he, placing the pearl necklace at the feet of the king seated on his lion-throne, bowing his head, sat cross-legged before him. The king, seeing the golden-colored hairs on the soles of his feet, was filled with the utmost wonder: 'How great in merit is <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>!'

Then the householder <s>Potalaka</s> approached <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>. Having approached, he said to <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>: 'Son, these citizens say thus.' He said: 'Father, if so, I shall go.' 'Son, surely the king wishes to see the golden-colored hairs on your feet. You must not raise your feet to show him. Kings are prone to anger without cause. They may do you harm. Here is a pearl necklace. Place it at the king's feet, bow your head, and sit down cross-legged before him. Then he will see the hairs.' Then the householder <s>Potalaka</s> considered: 'By what conveyance shall I send <s>Śroṇa</s>? By elephant? By horse? By chariot? Or by boat?' He thought: 'A boat-journey is best for them. I shall send him by boat.' He had a boat-bridge constructed on the river <s>Gaṅgā</s>. There he had a beautiful garden built, rich in various flowers and fruits, resounding with the songs of geese, herons, peacocks, parrots, <s>śārikā</s> birds, cuckoos, and other birds. Various musical instruments and women adorned with various ornaments were placed aboard. With this splendor, he was sent by way of the water. (

body.text: Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa and King Bimbisāra go together to the Bamboo grove in order to see the Buddha
body.translated_text: <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> and King <s>Bimbisāra</s> go together to the Bamboo Grove to see the <s>Buddha</s>

body.text: dṛṣṭvā kathayati: śroṇa dṛṣṭas te bhagavān? no deva; āgaccha gacchāmaḥ; sa pṛcchati deva kiṃ bhagavān yānena gaccchati? āhosvīt pādābhyām? iti; rājā kathayati
body.translated_text: Having seen [the hairs], the king said: '<s>Śroṇa</s>, have you seen the <s>Bhagavān</s>?' 'No, Your Majesty.' 'Come, let us go.' He asked: 'Your Majesty, does the <s>Bhagavān</s> travel by vehicle or on foot?' The king said:

body.text: pravrajito 'sau; kiṃ tasya yānena? iti; sa kathayati: deva yady evam aham api pādābhyām eva gacchāmi iti, pādābhyām eva saṃprasthitaḥ; tasya pauruṣeyair vastrāṇi pṛthivyām āstīrṇāni; sa kathayati: kiṃ bhagavān āstīrṇena gacchati? āhosvis anāstīrṇena? iti; te kathayanti anāstīrṇena iti; sa kathayati: apanyata vastrāṇi; aham apy anāstīrṇena gacchāmi iti; pauruṣeyair vastrāṇi apanītāni; amanuṣyakair āstīrṇāni; sa kathayati: bhavanto yūyaṃ mayā nivāritāḥ? iti; te kathayanti: deva nivāritāḥ; atha kena punar āstīrṇāni? iti; deva puṇyamaheśākhyas tvam; amanuṣyakair āstīrṇāni iti; tenāśayato vāṅ niścāritā apanayantu amanuṣyā vastrāṇi iti; tair apanītāni; tena pṛthivyāṃ pādo nyastaḥ; ṣaḍvikāraḥ pṛthivīkampo jātaḥ; iyaṃ mahāpṛthivī calati, saṃcalati, saṃpracalati; vyathate saṃvyathate saṃpravyathate; pūrvo digbhāga unnamati, paścima avanamati; paścima unnamati; pūrvo 'vanamati; dakṣiṇa unnamati, uttaro 'vanamati; uttara unnamati, dakṣiṇo 'vanamati; anta unnamati, madhyo 'vanamati; madhya (
body.translated_text: 'He is a renunciant. What vehicle does he need?' He said: 'Your Majesty, if so, I too shall go on foot.' He set out on foot. His servants spread cloths on the ground. He asked: 'Does the <s>Bhagavān</s> walk on spread [cloth] or on unspread [ground]?' They said: 'On unspread ground.' He said: 'Remove the cloths. I too shall walk on unspread ground.' The servants removed the cloths. But non-human beings spread them [invisibly]. He said: 'Sirs, were you not stopped by me?' They said: 'Your Majesty, [we were] stopped. But then by whom were they spread?' 'Your Majesty, you are Great-in-Merit. Non-human beings have spread them.' Then, with intent, he uttered the words: 'Let the non-human beings remove the cloths.' They removed them. He placed his foot on the bare earth. A sixfold earthquake occurred. This great earth trembled, shook, and quaked violently. The eastern part rose up and the western sank down; the western rose up and the eastern sank down; the southern rose up and the northern sank down; the northern rose up and the southern sank down; the edges rose up and the center sank down; the center (

body.text: SBV II 141
body.translated_text: SBV II 141

body.text: ) unnamati, anto 'vanamati; tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: ito bhikṣava ekanavataṃ kalpam upādāya na kadācit potalakaputreṇa anāstīrṇāyāṃ pṛthivyāṃ pādo nyastaḥ; etarhi nyasto dharmagauravataḥ, no tu puṇyaparikṣayāt; tenāyaṃ ṣaḍvikāraḥ pṛthivīkampo jātaḥ iti
body.translated_text: ) rose up and the edges sank down. There the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Monks, for ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) up to now, the son of <s>Potalaka</s> has never placed his foot on unspread ground. Now he has placed it, out of reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, not from a decline of merit. By that, this sixfold earthquake has occurred.'

body.text: The Buddha converts Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa
body.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> converts <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>

body.text: atha śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśo yena bhagavān tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇaḥ; tato bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñatvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā śroṇena koṭīviṃśena viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ; sa dṛṣṭasatya utthāya āsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā, yena bhagavāṃs tena añjaliṃ praṇamayya bhagavantam idam avocat: labheyāhaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaya pravrajyām upasaṃpadaṃ bhikṣubhāvaṃ careyam ahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam iti; bhagavān āha: na khalu gṛhaputra tathāgatā vā tathāgataśrāvakā vā ananujñātaṃ kulaputraṃ mātāpitṛbhyāṃ pravrājayanti upasaṃpādayanti vā; gaccha mātāpitarāv avalokaya iti; rājā kathayati ahaṃ bhadanta prabhuḥ sarvādhikaraṇānām; arthe mamaiva dharmatayā ayaṃ putro bhavati; aham enam anujānāmi; pravrājayatu bhagavān yathāsukham iti; tato bhagavatā ehibhikṣukayā ābhāṣitaḥ ehi bhikṣo cara brahmacaryam iti; tato vāco 'vasānasamanantaram eva muṇḍaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; saṅghāṭīprāvṛtaḥ; pātrakarakavyagrahastaḥ saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmasruḥ varṣaśatopasaṃpannasya bhikṣor īryāpathenāvasthitaḥ; āha cātra
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat down to one side. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing his disposition, latent tendencies, nature, and temperament, gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> as penetrates the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>). Having heard it, <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, shattering with the thunderbolt of knowledge (<s>jñānavajra</s>) the mountain of the view of the perishable aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising with twenty peaks, directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). He who had seen the truth, rising from his seat, arranging his upper robe over one shoulder, and joining his palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I, Venerable Sir, obtain ordination, full admission, and monkhood in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s>-<s>Vinaya</s>. May I live the holy life in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Son of a good family, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> and the disciples of the <s>Tathāgata</s> do not ordain or fully admit a young man who has not been given permission by his mother and father. Go, take leave of your parents.' The king said: 'I, Venerable Sir, am the sovereign of all jurisdictions. In the order of <s>Dharma</s>, this one is indeed my son. I give him permission. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> ordain him at his ease.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed him with the <s>Ehibhikṣuka</s> (Come-monk) ordination: 'Come, monk, live the holy life.' Immediately upon the conclusion of those words, his head became shaven, his body was clad in the <s>saṅghāṭī</s> robe, his hands held the bowl and water-pitcher, and with hair and beard as if shaved seven days prior, he stood with the deportment of a monk who had been ordained for a hundred years. And it is said:

children.translated_text: Addressed thus by the <s>Tathāgata</s>: 'Come!' —
shaven-headed, his body clad in the <s>saṅghāṭī</s> robe,
he stood at once, with senses perfectly stilled,
as if fulfilling the <s>Buddha</s>'s heartfelt wish. //

body.text: ṣaḍvargīyās
body.translated_text: The group of six [monks]

body.translated_text: ) Urged by them, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he said to the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, what meditation conducive to yoga has the <s>Bhagavān</s> prescribed for a monk who is wholly devoted to effort?' 'Venerable <s>Śroṇa</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "By walking meditation, one's concentration will be unimpaired and long-lasting." Therefore he went to the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground and took up walking meditation.' There the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> dwelt at <s>Rājagṛha</s> in the <s>Śītavana</s> charnel ground, yoked to effort, devoted to constancy, assiduity, and the practice of cultivating the factors conducive to awakening (<s>bodhipakṣya dharma</s>).

body.text: Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa gives himself to severe penances. The example of the lute

atha āyuṣmataḥ śroṇakoṭīviṃśasya ekākino rahogatasya pratisaṃlīnasya evaṃ cetasi cetaḥparitarka udapādi; yāvantaḥ khalu bhagavataḥ śrāvakāḥ ārabdhavīryā viharanti; ahaṃ teṣām anyatamaḥ; atha ca punar me nānupādāyāsravebhyaś cittaṃ vimucyate; saṃvidyante ca me jñātiṣu vipulā bhogāḥ; yannv ahaṃ niṣadya kāmāṃś ca paribhuṅjīya; dānāni ca dadyāṃ; puṇyāni ca kuryām iti
  atha bhagavān āyuṣmataḥ śroṇasya cetasā cittam ājñāya anyatamaṃ bhikṣum āmantrayate: ehi tvaṃ bhikṣo; yena śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśas tenopasamkrāma; upasaṃkramya śroṇaṃ koṭīviṃśam evaṃ vada śāstā tvāṃ śroṇa āmantrayate iti; evaṃ bhadantety sa bhikṣur bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya yanāyuṣmān śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya āyuṣmantaṃ śroṇaṃ koṭīviṃśam idam avocat: śāstā tvām āyuṣman śroṇa āmantrayate iti; evam āyuṣman ity āyuṣmān śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśas tasya bhikṣoḥ pratiśrutya yena bhagavāṃś tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekāṇte sthitaḥ; āyuṣmantaṃ śroṇaṃ koṭīviṃśaṃ bhagavān idam avocat: na te śroṇa ekākino rahogatasya pratisaṃlīnasya evaṃ cetasi cetaḥparitarka udapādi? yāvantaḥ khalu bhagavataḥ śrāvakāḥ ārabdhavīryā viharanti; ahaṃ teṣām anyatamaḥ; atha ca punar me nānupādāya āsravebhyaḥ cittaṃ vimucyate; saṃvidyante ca me (
body.translated_text:
Then in the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, who was alone, in seclusion, withdrawn in meditation, this thought and deliberation arose in his mind: 'Among the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s disciples who dwell with aroused effort, I am one of them. Yet my mind is not liberated from the defilements (<s>āsrava</s>) through non-clinging. And there are abundant possessions among my kinsmen. What if I were to return to lay life and enjoy sensual pleasures, give gifts, and perform meritorious deeds?'
  Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the Venerable <s>Śroṇa</s>'s mind with his own mind, addressed a certain monk: 'Come, monk. Go to <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>. Having approached, tell <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>: "The Teacher summons you, <s>Śroṇa</s>."' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' That monk, having assented to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, approached the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>. Having approached, he said to the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>: 'The Teacher summons you, Venerable <s>Śroṇa</s>.' 'Yes, Venerable One.' The Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, having assented to that monk, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and stood to one side. The <s>Bhagavān</s> said to the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>: 'Did there not arise in you, <s>Śroṇa</s>, while alone, in seclusion, withdrawn in meditation, this thought and deliberation: "Among the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s disciples who dwell with aroused effort, I am one of them. Yet my mind is not liberated from the defilements through non-clinging. And there are abundant possessions among my kinsmen (

  atha āyuṣmataḥ śroṇasya koṭīviṃśasya etad abhavat: jānāti me bhagavān cetasā cittam; iti viditvā bhītas trastas saṃvignaḥ āhṛṣṭaromakūpo bhagavantam idam avocat: evaṃbhadanta; tena hi śroṇa tvām eva pṛcchāmi; yathā te kṣamate tathainaṃ vyākuru; kiṃ manyase śroṇa? kuśalas tvam abhūḥ pūrvam āgārikaḥ san vīṇāyāṃ tantrīsvane; tathyam ahaṃ bhadanta kuśalo 'bhūvaṃ pūrvam āgārikaḥ san vīṇāyāṃ tantrīsvane: kiṃ manyase śroṇa? yasmin samaye vīṇāyās tantryaḥ atyātatā bhavanti, api nu tasmin samaye
body.translated_text:
). What if I were to return to lay life and enjoy sensual pleasures, give gifts, and perform meritorious deeds"?'
  Then the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> thought: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> knows my mind with his mind.' Knowing this, frightened, alarmed, agitated, with hair standing on end, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is so, Venerable Sir.' 'Well then, <s>Śroṇa</s>, I shall ask you a question. Answer it as you see fit. What do you think, <s>Śroṇa</s>? Were you not formerly, when you were a householder, skilled in the <s>vīṇā</s> (lute) and the sound of its strings?' 'Indeed, Venerable Sir, I was formerly, when a householder, skilled in the <s>vīṇā</s> and the sound of its strings.' 'What do you think, <s>Śroṇa</s>? When the strings of the <s>vīṇā</s> are overly taut, is the <s>vīṇā</s> at that time

body.text: vīṇā valgusvarā bhavati? manojñasvarā vā svaravatī vā karmaṇyā vā? no bhadanta; yasmin samaye vīṇāyās tantryaḥ atiślathā bhavanti api nu tasmin samaye vīṇā valgusvarā bhavati? manojñasvarā vā svaravatī vā karmaṇyā vā? no bhadanta; atha punar yasmin samaye vīṇāyās tantryaḥ nātyātatā bhavanti nātiślathāḥ saha guṇeṣu pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ, nanu tasmin samaye vīṇā valgusvarā vā bhavati? manojñasvarā vā svaravatī vā karmaṇyā vā? evaṃ bhadanta; evam eva śroṇa atyārabdhaṃ vīryam atyauddhatyāya saṃvartate; atilīnaṃ cittaṃ kausīdyāya saṃvartate; tasmāt tvaṃ śroṇa samatāṃ pratipadyasva; tena ca mā maṃsthāḥ; tasmiṃś ca pramādaḥ; tasmiṃś ca nimittam udgṛhṇīṣva; anena tvaṃ śroṇa vihāreṇa viharan nacirād eva āsravāṇāṃ kṣayād anāsravāṃ cetovimuktiṃ prajñāvimuktiṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñayā sākṣātkṛtvā, upasaṃpadya pravedayase kṣīṇā me jātiḥ; uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ; kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ; nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmi iti
body.translated_text: sweet-sounding? Pleasant-sounding, melodious, or workable?' 'No, Venerable Sir.' 'When the strings of the <s>vīṇā</s> are overly slack, is the <s>vīṇā</s> at that time sweet-sounding? Pleasant-sounding, melodious, or workable?' 'No, Venerable Sir.' 'But when the strings of the <s>vīṇā</s> are neither overly taut nor overly slack, but set at the right pitch, is the <s>vīṇā</s> at that time sweet-sounding? Pleasant-sounding, melodious, or workable?' 'Yes, Venerable Sir.' 'Just so, <s>Śroṇa</s> — overly aroused effort leads to restlessness; an overly lax mind leads to sloth. Therefore, <s>Śroṇa</s>, practice equanimity. And in that, do not be conceited. In that, do not be negligent. In that, apprehend the sign. By dwelling with this practice, <s>Śroṇa</s>, before long, through the destruction of the defilements, you will directly realize the defilement-free liberation of mind (<s>cetovimukti</s>) and liberation by wisdom (<s>prajñāvimukti</s>) in this very life, by your own direct knowledge, and having attained it, you will declare: "Birth is exhausted. The holy life has been lived. What had to be done has been done. I know there is no further existence beyond this."'

) and rightly and with faith go forth from the household life into homelessness — that unsurpassed culmination of the holy life, he directly realized in this very life by his own direct knowledge, attained it, and declared: 'Birth is exhausted. The holy life has been lived. What had to be done has been done. I know there is no further existence beyond this.' The Venerable One became an <s>Arhat</s>, well-liberated in mind.
  Then the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, having attained <s>Arhatship</s>, experiencing the bliss of liberation, thought: 'This is the time for me to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to see him, to attend upon him.' Then the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, in the evening, having emerged from seclusion, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having approached, he bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

Then the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, having rejoiced in and approved of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Then the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>, having been admonished by the <s>Bhagavān</s> with this simile of the lute, dwelling alone, withdrawn, heedful, ardent, and resolute, exerted himself. body.text: The discourse of Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa
body.translated_text: The discourse of <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>

body.text: yo 'sau bhadanta bhikṣur bhavati arhan kṣīṇāsravaḥ kṛtakṛtyaḥ kṛtakaraṇīyaḥ apahṛtabhāraḥ anuprāptasvakāryaḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaḥ sa tasmin samaye ṣaṭ sthānāny adhimukto bhavati; naiṣkramyam adhimukto bhavati; trṣṇākṣayam upādānakṣayam asaṃ moṣaṃ ca cetasā adhimukto bhavati; syāt khalu bhadanta ihaikatyasya evaṃ śraddhāmātrakaṃ, bata ayam āyuṣmān niśritya naiṣkramyam adhimukta iti; na khalv evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ kṣayād bhadanta rāgasya kṣayād dveṣasya kṣayān mohasya naiṣkramyam adhimukto bhavati; syāt khalu ihaikatyasya evaṃ śīlamātrakaṃ bata ayam āyuṣmān niśritya avyābādhyam adhimukta iti; na khalv evaṃ draṣṭuṃ; kṣayād bhadanta rāgasya kṣayād dveṣasya kṣayān mohasya avyābādhyam adhimukto bhavati; syāt khalu bhadanta ihaikatyasya evaṃ lābhasatkāraślokamātrakaṃ (
body.translated_text: 'That monk, Venerable Sir, who is an <s>Arhat</s>, whose defilements are exhausted, who has done what had to be done, accomplished what had to be accomplished, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, completely destroyed the fetters of existence, and is well-liberated through right knowledge — at that time he is resolved upon six states. He is resolved upon renunciation (<s>naiṣkramya</s>). He is resolved upon the destruction of craving, the destruction of clinging, and non-confusion — these he is resolved upon in his mind. Someone might think, Venerable Sir: "It is merely out of faith that this venerable one is resolved upon renunciation." But it should not be seen thus. It is through the destruction of passion, Venerable Sir, through the destruction of hatred, through the destruction of delusion, that he is resolved upon renunciation. Someone might think: "It is merely on account of his moral conduct that this venerable one is resolved upon non-harmfulness." But it should not be seen thus. It is through the destruction of passion, Venerable Sir, through the destruction of hatred, through the destruction of delusion, that he is resolved upon non-harmfulness. Someone might think, Venerable Sir: "It is merely for the sake of gain, honor, and fame that (

body.text: SBV II 145
body.translated_text: SBV II 145

body.text: ) bata ayam āyuṣmān parimṛgayamāṇāḥ prāvivekyam adhimukta iti; na khalv evaṃ draṣṭavyaṃ; kṣayād bhadanta rāgasya kṣayād dveṣasya kṣayān mohasya tṛṣṇākṣayam upādānakṣayam asaṃmoṣaṃ ca cetasā adhimukto bhavati; yo 'sau bhadanta bhikṣur bhavati arhan, kṣīṇāsravaḥ kṛtakṛtyaḥ kṛtakaraṇīyaḥ apahṛtabhāraḥ anuprāptasvakāryaḥ parikṣīṇabhavasaṃyojanaḥ samyagājñāsuvimuktacittaḥ tasmin samaye imāni ṣaṭ sthānāny adhimukto bhavati; yo 'sau bhadanta bhikṣur bhavati śaikṣa asaṃprāptamānasaḥ sa uttaraṃ yogakṣemaṃ nirvāṇam abhiprārthayamānarūpo bahulaṃ viharati; tasmin samaye śaikṣaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati śaikṣaiś cendriyaiḥ; so 'pareṇa samayena āsravāṇāṃ kṣayād anāsravāṃ cetovimuktiṃ prajñāvimuktiṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñayā sākṣātkṛtya upasaṃpadya pravedayate; kṣīṇā me jāti, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ; kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ; nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmi iti; sa tasmin samaye aśaikṣaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati aśaikṣaiś cendriyaiḥ; tadyathā dahraḥ kumārako bālo mandaḥ uttānaśāyī tasmin samaye dahraiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati dahraiś cendriyaiḥ; so 'pareṇa samayena vṛddher anvayāt, indriyāṇāṃ paripākāt sa tasmin samaye vṛddhaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati vṛddhaiś cendriyaiḥ; evam eva yo 'sau bhikṣur bhavati śaikṣa asaṃprāptamānasaḥ sa uttaraṃ yogakṣemaṃ nirvāṇam abhiprārthayamānarūpo bahulaṃ viharati; sa tasmin samaye śaikṣaiḥ samanvāgato bhavatiṃ śaikṣaiś cendriyaiḥ; so 'pareṇa samayena āsravāṇāṃ kṣayād anāsravāṃ cetovimuktiṃ prajñāvimuktiṃ dṛṣṭa eva dharme svayam abhijñayā sākṣātkṛtva upasaṃpadya pravedayate; kṣīṇā me jāti, uṣitaṃ brahmacaryaṃ; kṛtaṃ karaṇīyaṃ; nāparam asmād bhavaṃ prajānāmi iti; sa tasmin samaye aśaikṣaiḥ śīlaiḥ samanvāgato bhavati aśaikṣaiś cendriyaiḥ; tasya cet bhṛśāny api cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi cakṣuṣa ābhāḥ samāgacchanti nāsya tāṃ cetovimuktiṃ prajñāvimuktiṃ paryādadate; sthitam evāsya tat cittaṃ bhavati, adhyātmam aviparītaṃ suvimuktaṃ subhāvitaṃ; (
body.translated_text: ) this venerable one, seeking them, is resolved upon seclusion." But it should not be seen thus. It is through the destruction of passion, Venerable Sir, through the destruction of hatred, through the destruction of delusion, that he is resolved upon the destruction of craving, the destruction of clinging, and non-confusion in his mind. That monk, Venerable Sir, who is an <s>Arhat</s>, whose defilements are exhausted, who has done what had to be done, accomplished what had to be accomplished, laid down the burden, attained his own goal, completely destroyed the fetters of existence, and is well-liberated through right knowledge — at that time he is resolved upon these six states. That monk, Venerable Sir, who is a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), who has not yet attained the full state of mind, dwells for the most part aspiring to the ultimate security, <s>nirvāṇa</s>. At that time he is endowed with the morality of a learner and the faculties of a learner. At a later time, through the destruction of the defilements, he directly realizes the defilement-free liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in this very life, by his own direct knowledge, attains it, and declares: "Birth is exhausted. The holy life has been lived. What had to be done has been done. I know there is no further existence beyond this." At that time he is endowed with the morality of one beyond training (<s>aśaikṣa</s>) and the faculties of one beyond training. Just as a small child, young, foolish, undeveloped, lying on its back, is at that time endowed with the morality of a child and the faculties of a child; at a later time, through growth and the maturation of faculties, he is at that time endowed with the morality of an adult and the faculties of an adult — even so, that monk who is a learner, who has not yet attained the full state of mind, dwells for the most part aspiring to the ultimate security, <s>nirvāṇa</s>. At that time he is endowed with the morality of a learner and the faculties of a learner. At a later time, through the destruction of the defilements, he directly realizes the defilement-free liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom in this very life, by his own direct knowledge, attains it, and declares: "Birth is exhausted. The holy life has been lived. What had to be done has been done. I know there is no further existence beyond this." At that time he is endowed with the morality of one beyond training and the faculties of one beyond training. Even if intense visual forms cognizable by the eye impinge upon his eye, they do not overwhelm that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. His mind remains stable — inwardly unperturbed, well-liberated, well-cultivated. (

body.translated_text: SBV II 146

body.text: ) vyayaṃ cāsyānupaśyati; tasya ced bhṛśā api śrotavijñeyāḥ śabdāḥ ghrāṇavijñeyāḥ gandhāḥ jihvāvijñeyā rasāḥ kāyavijñeyāni spraṣṭavyāni manovijñeyā dharmāḥ manasa ābhāḥ samāgacchanti nāsya tāṃ cetovimuktiṃ prajñāvmukti paryādadate; sthitam evāsya tac cittaṃ bhavati; adhyātmam aviparītaṃ suvimuktaṃ subhāvitaṃ;
body.translated_text: ) And he observes their passing away. Even if intense sounds cognizable by the ear, odors cognizable by the nose, tastes cognizable by the tongue, tactile objects cognizable by the body, or mental objects cognizable by the mind impinge upon his mind, they do not overwhelm that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom. His mind remains stable — inwardly unperturbed, well-liberated, well-cultivated.

body.text: vyayaṃ cāsyānupaśyati; tadyathā nagarasya vā nigamasya vā nātidūre mahāśailaḥ parvataḥ syāt, akhaṇḍaḥ acchidraḥ asuṣiraḥ susaṃvṛttaḥ ekaghanaḥ; tasya cet pūrvasyā diśo bhṛśo vāyuvega āgacchen nainaṃ calayet, nainaṃ kampayet, nainaṃ paścimāyāṃ diśy upasaṃharet; saced dakṣiṇasyāḥ paścimāyāḥ uttarasyā diśo vāyuvegaḥ āgacchen nainaṃ calayet, nainaṃ kampayet, nainaṃ dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśy upasaṃharet; yatas tato vā bhṛśo vāyuvega āgacchen nainaṃ calayet, nainaṃ kampayet, nainaṃ yatas tata upasaṃharet; evam eva tasya bhṛśāny api cakṣurvijñeyāni rūpāṇi cakṣuṣa ābhāḥ samāgacchanti; nāsya tāṃ cetovimuktiṃ prajñāvimuktiṃ paryādadate; sthitam evāsya tac cittaṃ bhavati adhyātma aviparītaṃ suvimuktaṃ subhāvitaṃ; vyayaṃ cāsyānupaśyati iti; idam avocad āyuṣmān śroṇaḥ koṭīviṃśaḥ; idam uktvā arhann athāparam etad uvāca sthaviraḥ
body.translated_text: and he observes its passing away. Just as not far from a town or village there might be a great rocky mountain — unbroken, without cracks, without hollows, well-formed, of a single mass — if from the eastern direction a fierce blast of wind were to come, it would not shake it, would not move it, would not carry it westward; if from the southern, western, or northern direction a blast of wind were to come, it would not shake it, would not move it, would not carry it in any direction; from wherever a fierce blast of wind might come, it would not shake it, would not move it, would not carry it in that direction — even so, even fierce forms cognizable by the eye come into the range of his eye; they do not overwhelm his liberation of mind, his liberation by wisdom. His mind remains steady, inwardly undistorted, well-liberated, well-developed — and he observes its passing away. Thus spoke the Venerable <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>. Having spoken thus, the elder, an <s>Arhat</s>, further said:

children.translated_text: For one resolved upon renunciation, with an untroubled mind, /
for one resolved upon seclusion and delighting in the destruction of craving, //
for one resolved upon the destruction of attachment, with an undeluded mind, /
having known the arising and cessation of the sense-bases, then the mind is liberated. //

bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kiṃ bhadanta āyuṣmatā śroṇena karma kṛtam yasya karmaṇo vipākena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ; suvarṇavarṇāni ca romāṇi pādatalayor jātāni; paṃcaśatikaś cāsya dine dine sthālipāka upasthāpyate; ita ekanavataṃ kalpam upādāya na kadācid anāstīrṇe pṛthivīpradeśe pādo nyastaḥ; jātamātreṇa viṃśatihiraṇyakoṭyaḥ avalehikāmūlyaṃ labdhāḥ; bhagavataś ca śāsane praviśya sarvakleśaprahāṇās arhatvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti
  bhagavān āha: śroṇenaiva bhikṣavaḥ koṭīviṃśena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyabhāvīni; śroṇakoṭīviṃśena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau; api tu
body.translated_text:
The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'What deed, Venerable Sir, was done by the Venerable <s>Śroṇa</s>, by the ripening of which deed he was born into a wealthy family of great riches and great possessions; golden-colored hairs grew on the soles of his feet; five hundred pot-cooked meals were prepared for him daily; for ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> (aeons) counting from that time, he never once placed his foot on unspread ground; at the very moment of his birth, he obtained twenty <s>koṭis</s> (ten millions) of gold as the cost of his licking-ceremony; and, having entered the teaching of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, through the abandonment of all afflictions, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>?'
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'It was <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> himself, monks, who performed deeds, accumulated them, gathered their provisions, whose conditions had ripened, which stood present like a flood, which were inevitably bound to occur. Who else would experience the deeds that <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> performed and accumulated? Monks, deeds that have been performed and accumulated do not ripen externally in the earth element, nor in the water element, nor in the fire element, nor in the wind element; rather

body.text: upātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
body.translated_text: , deeds performed ripen in the appropriated aggregates, elements, and sense-bases themselves — both wholesome and unwholesome ones:

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api /
children.translated_text: Deeds do not perish even after hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (aeons); /

children.text: sāmagrīm prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām //
children.translated_text: when the right conditions and time are met, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings. //

body.text:
The story of Vipaśyin
(concerning a previous birth of Śroṇakoṭīviṃśa)
body.translated_text:
The story of <s>Vipaśyin</s>
(concerning a previous birth of <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s>)

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ ekanavate kalpe vipaśyī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi, vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devamanuṣyāṇāṃ buddho bhagavān; sa dvāṣaṣṭibhikṣusahasraparivāraḥ janapadacārikāṃ caran bandhumatīrājadhānīm anuprāptaḥ; tena khalu samayena bandhumatyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ saṃbahulā goṣṭhikāḥ prativasanti; taiḥ śrutaṃ vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ dvāṣaṣṭibhikṣusahasraparivāraḥ janapadacārikāṃ caran ihānuprāptaḥ iti; śrutvā ca punaḥ sarve saṃbhūya yena vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ; upasaṃkramya vipaśyinaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ; ekāntaniṣaṇṇān sambahulān goṣṭhikān vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśayati samādāpayati samuttejayati saṃpraharṣayati; anekaparyāyeṇa dharmyayā kathayā saṃdarśya (
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> ago, a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the Well-Gone One, Knower of the World, Unsurpassed, Charioteer of Persons to Be Tamed, Teacher of Gods and Humans, <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s>. With a retinue of sixty-two thousand monks, wandering through the countryside on a teaching tour, he arrived at the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>. At that time, in the royal capital of <s>Bandhumatī</s>, many guild-members dwelt. They heard: 'The fully awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, with a retinue of sixty-two thousand monks, wandering through the countryside on a teaching tour, has arrived here.' Having heard, they all gathered and approached the fully awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>. Having approached, they bowed their heads at the feet of <s>Vipaśyin</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> and sat to one side. <s>Vipaśyin</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted the many guild-members seated to one side with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>. Having in many ways (

body.text: SBV II 148
body.translated_text: SBV II 148

body.text:
) samādāpya samuttejya saṃpraharṣya tūṣṇīm; atha sambahulā goṣṭhikāḥ utthāyāsanād ekāṃsam uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā yena vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhas tenāñjaliṃ praṇamayya vipaśyinaṃ samyaksaṃbuddham idam avocan: adhivāsayatv asmākaṃ bhagavān traimāsīṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātaśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkāraiḥ sārdhaṃ saṃghena iti / adhivāsayati vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ saṃbahulānāṃ goṣṭhikānāṃ tūṣṇīṃbhāvena
  atha saṃbahulā goṣṭhikā vipaśyinaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya tūṣṇīṃbhāvena adhivāsanāṃ viditvā bhagavato bhāṣitam abhinandyānumodya bhagavato pādau śirasā vanditvā uttahāyāsanāt prakrāntaḥ; te saṃsthāgāre sannipatya sañjalpaṃ kartum ārabdhāḥ; katham asmābhir bhavanto bhagavān bhojayitavyaḥ kiṃ saṃbhūya āhosvid ekaikena iti; tatraike kathayati; yadi dine dine saṃbhūya bhojayitavyo 'sau asmākaṃ kṛṣikarmāntāḥ samucchetsyanti; tad yadi bhavatām abhirucitaṃ vāreṇa vāraṃ bhojayāmaḥ iti; te vāreṇa vāraṃ gaṇādhīnaṃ bhojayitum ārabdhāḥ; yathāvibhavataś cātmīyam asyānuprayacchanti; tatraiko brāhmaṇadārako daridraḥ; sa mātuḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ kathayati: amba goṣṭhikaiḥ kriyākāraḥ kṛtaḥ, bhagavān vāreṇa vāraṃ bhojayitavyaḥ iti; tad ahaṃ tanuvibhavaḥ; kathaṃ mayā bhojayitavyaḥ iti; sā kathayati: putra yady evam apaścimaṃ divasaṃ gṛhāṇa; tvam iyatā kālena kiṃcit samudānayiṣyasi; gaṇasantakāc ca kiṃcid utsadanadharmakaṃ bhaviṣyati iti; tena paścimo divaso gṛhītaḥ; tatra gaṇasantakād utsadanadharmakaṃ prabhūtām saṃpannaṃ; tenāpi kiṃcit samudānītaṃ; tatas tena
body.translated_text:
) instructed, inspired, encouraged, and delighted them with a discourse on the <s>Dharma</s>, he fell silent. Then those many guild-members, rising from their seats, arranging their upper robes over one shoulder, and joining their palms toward <s>Vipaśyin</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>, said this to <s>Vipaśyin</s>: 'May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept from us the three-month provision of robes, alms-food, lodging, and medicine for the sick, together with the <s>Saṅgha</s>.' <s>Vipaśyin</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> consented to the many guild-members by his silence.
Then the many guild-members, having understood the consent of <s>Vipaśyin</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> through his silence, rejoicing and approving of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, bowed their heads at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, rose from their seats, and departed. They gathered in their assembly hall and began to deliberate: 'Sirs, how shall we feed the <s>Bhagavān</s> — together, or one by one?' Thereupon some said: 'If we feed him collectively every day, our agricultural enterprises will be ruined. If it pleases you, let us feed him by turns.' They began to feed him by turns, according to the group. Each contributed his share according to his means. Among them was one poor young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. He approached his mother and said: 'Mother, the guild-members have made a pact — the <s>Bhagavān</s> is to be fed by turns. But I am of modest means. How am I to feed him?' She said: 'Son, if so, take the last day. By then you will have accumulated something. And there will be surplus provisions from the guild treasury.' He took the last day. From the guild treasury, ample surplus provisions had accumulated. He too had gathered something. Then

body.text: layanaṃ kāritaṃ; tad vastrair ācchāditaṃ; koṇeṣu paṃca kārṣāpaṇaśatāni sthāpitāni; ṛkṣacarma cāsya saṃpannaṃ; tad api layanadvāre prajñaptaṃ; tataḥ paṃcaśatikaṃ pākaṃ sādhayitvā mahatā satkāreṇa vipaśyī samyaksaṃbuddho bhojitaḥ; pādayoś ca praṇipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo jāyeya; mā kadācid anāstīrṇe pṛthivīpradeśe pādau sthāpayeyaṃ; yādṛśāni ca vipaśyinaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya suvarṇavarṇāni caturaṅgulamātrāṇi romāṇi pādatalayor jātāni, mamāpy evaṃvidhāni syuḥ; evaṃvidhānāṃ ca guṇānāṃ lābhī syāṃ; evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ; mā virāgayeyam iti (
body.translated_text: he had a shelter built, covered it with cloths, placed five hundred <s>kārṣāpaṇas</s> in the corners, and he also obtained a bear-skin, which he spread at the entrance of the shelter. Then, having prepared five hundred pot-cooked meals, with great honor he fed <s>Vipaśyin</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. And bowing at his feet, he made a vow: 'By this wholesome root, may I be born into a wealthy family of great riches and great possessions. May I never place my feet on unspread ground. Just as the fully awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s> has golden-colored hairs four fingers long growing on the soles of his feet, may I too have such hairs. May I obtain such virtues. And may I please a teacher just like this one — may I never displease him.' (

body.translated_text:
)
What do you think, monks? He who was that guild-member, the young <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> — that is this very <s>Śroṇa Koṭīviṃśa</s> at that time, in that era. Because he performed service to <s>Vipaśyin</s> the <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s> and made that vow, by the ripening of that deed he was born into a wealthy family of great riches and great possessions. Golden-colored hairs four fingers long grew on the soles of his feet. For ninety-one <s>kalpas</s> counting from that time, he never once placed his feet on unspread ground. At the very moment of his birth, he obtained twenty <s>koṭis</s> of gold. And having gone forth under my teaching, through the abandonment of all afflictions, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>. Thus, monks, for purely dark deeds the result is purely dark; for purely bright deeds, purely bright; for mixed deeds, mixed. Therefore, monks, abandoning purely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only toward purely bright deeds. Thus, monks, you should train.

body.translated_text: The people of <s>Rājagṛha</s> begin to murmur against <s>Ajātaśatru</s> and <s>Devadatta</s>

body.text: yadā ajātaśatruṇā devadattākalyāṇamitropagūḍhena rājño bimbisārasya kanakaḥ kṣiptaḥ tadā rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ paurāḥ avadhyātum ārabdhāḥ; tatra kecid rājñaḥ akarṇaṃ bhāṣante ayaṃ pituḥ śatrutve vyākṛtaḥ; kasmān na jātamātra eva praghātitaḥ iti; apare kathayanti: na bhavanto rājño 'parādhaḥ; kiṃ sarveṣāṃ vyākaraṇaṃ bhūtaṃ bhavati? vinīta evāyaṃ kumāraḥ; api tu devadattenāyam akalyāṇamitreṇa vipralabdhaḥ, yena evaṃkriyāsu pravartate iti; apare kathayanti; na bhavanto rājño doṣaḥ nāpi devadattasya; api tu bhagavata eva doṣaḥ; yena devadattaḥ pravrājitaḥ; no tu lokadhātvantaraṃ nītvā avasthāpitaḥ iti; apare kathayanti: bhagavato nāyam aparādhaḥ; api tu saṃghasya yenāsya utkṣepanīyaṃ karma na kṛtam iti; tatra yena rājñaḥ akarṇaṃ bhāṣyate tena (
body.translated_text: When <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, led astray by <s>Devadatta</s> his evil friend, cast a stone at King <s>Bimbisāra</s>, then the inhabitants of <s>Rājagṛha</s> began to criticize. Some spoke ill of the king: 'He was prophesied to be hostile to his father. Why was he not killed at birth?' Others said: 'Sirs, it is not the king's fault. Are all prophecies true? This prince was well-mannered. But he has been deceived by <s>Devadatta</s>, his evil friend, and that is why he acts thus.' Others said: 'Sirs, it is neither the king's fault nor <s>Devadatta</s>'s. The fault lies with the <s>Bhagavān</s> himself, who ordained <s>Devadatta</s> but did not take him away to another world-realm and keep him there.' Others said: 'It is not the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s fault. It is the <s>Saṅgha</s>'s fault, for they did not perform the act of suspension against him.' There, when someone spoke ill of the king (

body.text: SBV II 150
body.translated_text: SBV II 150

) na rājā ārtīyate karmāṇy etāni mayā pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu kṛtāni upacitāni iti; yena tu bhagavataḥ saṃghasya ca akarṇaṃ bhāṣyate, tena rājā atyartham ārtīyate; madīyena durnītena loko bhagavataḥ saṃghasya ca akarṇaṃ bhāṣate iti
  bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / paśya bhadanta anyair aparāddham
body.translated_text:
), the king was not distressed — 'These are deeds I performed and accumulated in former lives.' But when someone spoke ill of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s>, the king was exceedingly distressed — 'Because of my misconduct, the world speaks ill of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and the <s>Saṅgha</s>.'
The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, others have committed the offense

body.text: anye doṣeṇa lipyante iti, bhagavān āha: na bhikṣava etarhi; yathā atīte 'py adhvany anyair aparāddham anye doṣeṇa liptāḥ; tac chrūyatāṃ
body.translated_text: , yet others are tainted by the blame.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, monks — in the past too, others committed the offense and others were tainted by the blame. Listen to that.'

The king heard this. At dawn, he gave a command to his ministers: 'Sirs, search for the one by whom I was informed with a verse during the night.' They gave orders to the guards: 'Search, sirs — by whom was His Majesty informed with a verse during the night?' They reported: 'By a country dog.' The king said: 'Sirs, conduct an investigation — was it eaten by <s>Kūla</s> and <s>Upakūla</s>, or by other dogs?' The ministers, having assembled, began to deliberate: 'Sirs, His Majesty has given the command to investigate the dogs. How then should the investigation be carried out?' Others said: 'What is there to investigate? Give them a hair-ball and make them vomit.' Then <s>Kūla</s> and <s>Upakūla</s> vomited up pieces of leather. This was reported to the king. The king abandoned those two. Safety was granted to the rest.
  What do you think, monks? <s>Kūla</s> and <s>Upakūla</s> — those are none other than <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Ajātaśatru</s> at that time, in that era. Even then those two committed the offense and others were stained by the blame. Now too those two have committed the offense and others are stained by the blame. And listen further to how <s>Devadatta</s> is ungrateful and unappreciative.

In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was exercising sovereignty — it was prosperous, thriving, secure, well-provisioned, and teeming with many people. He had two dogs, <s>Kūla</s> and <s>Upakūla</s>. Those two had chewed the king's horse-harness equipment. Then at a later time, a battle arose for King <s>Brahmadatta</s>. He gave a command to his ministers: 'Sirs, inspect the horse-harness equipment.' They began to inspect, and saw it all gnawed and torn to pieces. They reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, the horse-harness equipment has been eaten by a dog.' The king said: 'Sirs, if so, I have abandoned the dogs.' Thereupon some were killed, while some fled. Then a certain country dog was going from the countryside to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. He saw those fleeing dogs and asked them: 'Sirs, why are you so terrified?' They told him what had happened. He said: 'Why did you not inform the king?' They said: 'Who is able to inform the king? Others were killed. We somehow escaped.' He said: 'Wait. I shall inform the king on your behalf.' Reassured by him, they turned back. Then, at the time of the audience, standing at the listening-post, he informed the king with a verse:

body.translated_text: ) Those bewildered ones called out: 'Good man, save us!' Then that deer-hunter, understanding the situation, first pulled out the lion. The lion fell at his feet and said: 'I shall be grateful to you. But a black-haired one sits in there. You should not pull him out. These humans are ungrateful.' Having said this, he departed. Then the deer-hunter pulled out all the rest, one by one. Then at a later time, the lion killed a deer and that deer-hunter arrived at that place. The lion, recognizing him, laid the deer at his feet as a gift. At another time, King <s>Brahmadatta</s> went out to the park with his inner palace retinue. There in the park, having enjoyed himself, he fell asleep. The women of the inner palace wandered about the park freely — walking, standing, sitting, falling asleep, washing their garments, removing their ornaments and placing them beside them. Then a certain woman of the inner palace removed her ornament, placed it beside her, and fell asleep. The hawk seized it and, out of gratitude, gave it to that hunter. King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, having shaken off his drowsiness, hastily entered <s>Vārāṇasī</s>. The inner palace, princes, ministers, citizens, and countryfolk also went in great haste. Then that woman of the inner palace searched for her ornament but did not find it. She reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, my ornament has been stolen in the park.' The king gave a command to his ministers: 'Sirs, an ornament has been stolen in the park. Find out who took it.' They began to search. That black-haired man visited the deer-hunter from time to time. While visiting his house, he secretly discovered: 'He has an ornament.' Out of ingratitude, he went and reported it to the king. Then the king, extremely angry, had the deer-hunter summoned by his officers and said: 'Good man, you stole the ornament from the park!' Then the terrified hunter explained what had happened and presented the ornament to the king. Even so, that man was bound in chains and imprisoned. In the past, monks, a seven-day untimely storm arose. As the rain-god rained, a mongoose entered a hermitage. A mouse too entered that very place. A venomous snake too, wandering about in fear of the rain, entered that very place. Then that mongoose began to charge at the mouse. The venomous snake said: 'Sirs, we have reached hardship, difficulty, and constriction. Do not harm each other. Remain still.' There, the venomous snake's name was <s>Priyasena</s>, the mongoose's name was <s>Nanda</s>, and the mouse's name was <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>. <s>Priyasena</s> and <s>Nanda</s> told <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>: 'Go unnoticed and search for food for us.' He was honest and well-intentioned. With genuine intent, he began to search for food for those two. He found nothing. <s>Nanda</s> said to <s>Priyasena</s>: 'If <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> comes back without food, I shall eat him.' <s>Priyasena</s> reflected: 'Even in hardship and constriction, this one strives to kill him. How much more so if <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> returns without food! By all means, a message must be sent to him.' He sent him a message. <s>Nanda</s> said thus: 'If <s>Gaṅgadatta</s> comes back without food, I shall eat him.' <s>Gaṅgadatta</s>, while searching for food, found nothing. He reflected: 'That one will surely eat me.' He sent a message to <s>Priyasena</s>:
