) rājagṛham ekaṃ muktvā sarvo magadhaviṣayo labdhaḥ iti; sa kathayati: īdṛśaṃ parākramasya phalaṃ; bhūyaḥ parākramasva iti; sa magadhaviṣayaṃ nāśayitum ārabdhaḥ; magadhaviṣayanivāsinā janakāyena rājā bimbisāro vijñaptaḥ; deva kumāro magadhaviṣayaṃ nāśayati; nivartyatām iti; sa rājñā āhūyoktaḥ kumāra kimarthaṃ magadhaviṣayaṃ nāśayasi iti; sa kathayati deva prabhūto janakāyo na puṣyati iti; rājā kathayati; kumāra yady evaṃ kośam ekaṃ muktvā sarvaṃ tavaiva bhavatu iti; sa rājagṛham api gṛhītvā devadattasya sakāśaṃ gataḥ kathayati: ārya mayā kośam ekaṃ muktvā, sarvabhogā labdhāḥ iti; sa kathayati parākramaphalam etat; api tu kośabalino hi rājānaḥ; yasya kośaḥ sa rājā; kośārthaṃ parākramasva iti; sa rājagṛham api nāśayitum ārabdhaḥ; rājagṛhanivāsī janakāyaḥ anyaś ca magadhanivāsī campeyaś ca sarva eva santrastāḥ yathā ajātaśatrur na paśyati tathā dūtasaṃpreṣaṇena rājānaṃ vijñapayitum ārabdhāḥ: devena vayaṃ putravat paripālitāḥ; kumāreṇātyantaṃ niḥsvīkṛtāḥ; prāyo devasya janapadā niṣpalāyitāḥ; vayam api niṣpalāyāmaḥ iti; dharmapradhānaḥ sa rājā; karuṇātmakaś ca; tena samutpannamanyunā ajātaśatrur āhūya priyamadhuravaconukūlatayā śiras parāmṛśyoktaḥ: putra mayā tava sarvajanapadā dattāḥ; kimartham udvejayasi? pratipālaya iti; sa kathayati: deva kośabalino rājānaḥ; mama kośabalaṃ nāsti; kiṃ karomi iti; a kathayati: yady evam antaḥpuram ekaṃ muktvā sarvaṃ tavaiva bhavatu iti; tathāpy asau duṣṭaprakṛtiḥ pāpasahāyaś ca nāśayaty eva, nāvatiṣṭhate; rājñā sopālambham uktaḥ: sakośakoṣṭhāgārajanapadās tavaiva dattāḥ; idānīṃ kimarthaṃ nāśayasi iti
Ajātaśatru casts his father in prison, there to die of hunger

sa evam ukte ruṣitaḥ amātyānāṃ kathayati: bhavanto yo rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktaṃ paribhāṣate, tasya ko daṇḍaḥ iti; amātyāḥ kathayanti: deva vadho daṇḍaḥ iti; sa kathayati: pitā mama; katham enaṃ praghātayāmi? gacchata; cārakāvabaddham enaṃ sthāpayata iti; sa cārake prakṣiptaḥ; anuraktapaurajānapadaḥ sa rājā; tadviṣayanivāsī ca janakāyaḥ śrutvā (
SBV II 156
) durmanāḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; ajātaśatruś caṇḍo rabhasaḥ karkaśaḥ iti nāsya kaścit parivādaṃ mantrayati; rājā

bimbisāraś cārake karmaparāyaṇo 'vatiṣṭhate; tasya ca vaidehī sthālīpākaṃ praveśayati: ajātaśatruś cārakapuruṣān pṛcchati: bhavantaḥ kathaṃ vṛddharājā yāpayati? iti; te kathayanti: deva jananī te sthālīpākaṃ praveśayati iti; ajātaśatruṇā ājñā dattā: dhārayata bhaktaṃ pānaṃ ca yathā na bhūyaḥ praveśayati iti; antaḥpure cājñā dattā na kenacic cārake bhaktaṃ pānaṃ praveśayitavyaṃ; yaḥ praveśayati tasya vadho daṇḍaḥ iti; tasya raudrakarmatāṃ jñātvā na kaścid bhaktaṃ sādhayati; kuta eva praveśayiṣyati; tato vaidehī bhartṛsnehoparuddhyamānahṛdayā saktukalkena gātrāṇi mrakṣayitvā nūpurāṇi ca pānīyasya pūrayitvā praveśayitum ārabdhā; tenāsau yāpayati; cārakapuruṣaiḥ so 'py upāyo vijñātaḥ; kiṃtu anurāgāt tasya rājñaḥ ajātaśatror na nivedayanti; bhūyaḥ ajātaśatruś cārakapuruṣān pṛcchati: bhavanto vṛddharājā kathaṃ yāpayati? iti; tair istareṇa samākhyātaṃ; sa kathayati: bhavanto vaidehīṃ dhārayata, yathā na bhūyaḥ praviśati iti; tato bhagavān tatkuśalamūlāvaropaṇārthaṃ gṛddhrakūṭaparvate vātāyanābhimukhaṃ caṃkramitum ārabdhaḥ; rājā bimbisāraḥ vātāyanena bhagavantam avalokya prāmodyam utpādayati yena prāṇair na viyujyate; ājātaśatruḥ ca bhūyaś cārakapuruṣān pṛccchati bhavantaḥ annapānaṃ vidhāritaṃ; idānīṃ vṛddharājaḥ kathaṃ yāpayati iti; te kathayanti: bhagavāṃs tasyānugrahārthaṃ gṛddhrakūṭe parvate caṃkramyate; tam asau sthitaḥ pratidinaṃ parīkṣate iti; sa kathayati vātāyanānāni pithayantu; tasya ca pādau kṣureṇa nirlikhata iti; tair vātāyanānāni pihitāni; tasya ca pādau ksureṇa nirlikhitau; sa duḥkhavedanārto bāṣpoparuddhyamānagadgadakaṇṭhaḥ aśruparyākulekṣaṇaś cintayati: na māṃ bhagavān kṛcchrasaṅkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaṃ samanvāharati iti
The Buddha sends Maudgalyāyana to visit and comfort the old king
atrāntare nāsti kiṃcit buddhānāṃ bhagavatām ajñātam adṛṣṭam aviditam avijñātaṃ; dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttānām ekārakṣāṇāṃ (

children.text: ) śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitamatīnāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ pañcāṅgaviprahīnānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānām aṣṭāṅgamārgadeśikānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ daśabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trī rātres trir divasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate: ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkataprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃkaṭasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ ko 'pāyanimnaḥ ko 'pāyapravaṇaḥ ko 'pāyaprāgbhāraḥ kam aham apāyād uddhṛtya svarge mokṣe ca pratiṣṭhāpayeyaṃ; kasya anavaropitāni kuśalamulāni avaropayeyaṃ? kasyāvaropitāni paripācayeyaṃ? kasya pakvāni vimocayeyam iti; tatra bhagavān āyuṣmantaṃ mahāmaudgalyāyanam āmantrayate: gaccha maudgalyāyana; rājānaṃ bimbisāraṃ madvacanād ārogya; evaṃ sa vada: bhagavān kathayati: yat kalyāṇamitreṇa karaṇīyaṃ kṛtaṃ tat te mayā; uddhṛtas te narakatiryakpretebhyaḥ pādaḥ; pratiṣṭhāpito devamanuṣyeṣu; paryantīkṛtaḥ saṃsāraḥ; ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ; laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ; pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi; vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi; api tu tvayaivaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyabhāvīni; tvayaiva karmāṇi kṛtāny ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na mahārāja karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau; api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api /
sāmagrīm prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām //

body.text: tasmāt tarhi te mahārāja karmaparāyaṇena bhavitavyam iti; evaṃ bhadantety āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavataḥ pratiśrutya
tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte gṛddhrakūṭe (
SBV II 158

) antarhitaś cārake pratyaṣṭhāt, rājño bimbisārasya purastāt; evaṃ cāha: mahārāja bhagavāṃs te ārogayati; vande bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana bhagavantaṃ ca; bhagavān mahārāja evam āha: yat kalyāṇamitreṇa karaṇīyaṃ kṛtaṃ tat te mayā; uddhṛtas te narakatiryakpretebhyaḥ; pratiṣṭhāpito devamanuṣyeṣu; paryantīkṛtaḥ saṃsāraḥ; ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ; laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ; pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi; vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi; api tu tvayaivaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyabhāvīni; tvayā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na mahārāja karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau; api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;

children.text: na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api /
sāmagrīm prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām //

body.text: tasmāt tarhi te mahārāja karmaparāyaṇena bhavitavyam iti; sā cārakāvaruddhaḥ kṣurapādābhilikhanānnapānaviyogaduḥkhair abhyāhataḥ kathayati: kutra bhadanta mahāmaudgalyāyana praṇīta āhāro bhujyate iti; sa kathayati: mahārāja cāturmahārājakāyikeṣu deveṣu ity uktvā ayuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanaḥ tadrūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpanno yathā samāhite citte cārake antarhito gṛddhrakūṭaparvate pratyaṣṭhāt

children.text: The tardy repentance of Ajātaśatru and the death of Bimbisāra

ajātaśatroḥ putrasya udayabhadrasya aṅgulyāṃ piṭako jātaḥ, sa rudann ajātaśatroḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ; sa tam aṅke sthāpayitvā āliṅgati cumbati pariṣvajati; tathāpy asau rudaty eva; nāvatiṣṭhate; ajātaśatruṇā tatsantikā aṅguliḥ mukhe prakṣiptā; sphoṭako mukhe sphuṭitaḥ; ajātaśatruṇā pūyaśoṇitaṃ pṛthivyāṃ choritam; udāyibhadraḥ kumāraḥ pūyaśoṇitaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhūyasā roditum ārabdhaḥ iti; vaidehyā vipuṣpitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ajātaśatruḥ kathayati: amba kim idam iti; sā kathayati: putra yuṣmākam eṣa pitṛparyāgatavyādhiḥ tavāpyāsīt; tava tu pitrā aṅgulyāṃ mukhe prakṣiptāvāṃ sphoṭakaḥ sphuṭitaḥ; mā tvaṃ rodiṣyasīti pūyaśoṇitam abhyavahṛtaṃ; na pṛthivyāṃ choritaṃ; sa kathayati: amba īdṛśo 'haṃ pituḥ priya (

) āsaṃ sā kathayati: īdṛśaḥ; tataḥ ajātaśatroḥ pitur antike dveṣaparyavasthānaṃ vigatam; anunaya utpannaḥ; tenāmātyā uktāḥ: bhavanto yo mama kathayati vṛddharājo jīvatīti, tasyāham upārdharājyaṃ dadāmi iti; anuraktapaurajānapadaḥ sa rājā; mahājanakāyaś cārakābhimukho dhāvitum ārabdhaḥ; rājā śabdaṃ śrutvā saṃlakṣayati: idānīṃ kām api pratyavarāṃ kāraṇāṃ kariṣyati; iti santrasto dīrghaṃ niśvasya kālagataḥ; vaiśravaṇasya mahārājasya putratvam abhyupagataḥ; aṅke niṣaṇṇo divyāṃ sudhāṃ paribhuṅkte; vaiśravaṇaḥ kathayati; kas tvam iti; sa kathayati: jinarṣabho 'smi mahārājeti; tasya jinarṣabho jinarṣabha iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā

bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: kiṃ bhadanta rājñā bimbisāreṇa karma kṛtaṃ yasya karmaṇo vipākena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge rājakule jātaḥ; bhagavato 'ntike satyadarśanaṃ kṛtaṃ; kṣureṇa pādau nirlikhitau; cārakāvabaddhaś ca kṣutpipāsābhibhūtaḥ kālagataḥ iti; bhagavān āha: bimbisāreṇaiva bhikṣavo rājñā karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyabhāvīni; bimbisāreṇa karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhye pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante, nābdhātau, na tejodhātau, na vāyudhātau; api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca;
na praṇaśyanti karmāṇy api kalpaśatair api /
sāmagrīm prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām //

body.text:
The story of a potter
(concerning a previous birth of King Bimbisāra)
bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ buddhānām utpāde pratyekabuddhā loka utpadyante hīnadīnānukampakāḥ prāntaśayanāsanabhaktāḥ ekadakṣiṇīyā lokasya; yāvad anyatamaḥ pratyekabuddho janapadacārikāṃ caran
vārāṇasīm anuprāptaḥ; vārāṇasyām anyatamasya kumbhakārasya āveśanaśālāyāṃ rātriṃvāsam upagataḥ; sārthaś ca tasyām (
SBV II 160

) eva śālāyām uṣitaḥ; tatraikena uccāraḥ kṛtaḥ; sārthaḥsarātram evotthāya prakrāntaḥ; asamanvāhṛtyārhatāṃ pratyekabuddhānām eva jñānadarśanaṃ na pravartate; pratyekabuddhas tatraivāvasthitaḥ; ihaiva piṇḍapātam aṭiṣyāmi iti; yāvat kumbhakāraḥ prabhātāyāṃ rajanyām āveśanaśālāyāṃ praviṣṭaḥ; paśyati aśucinā nāśitā; aparīkṣakā bhavanti prākṛtapuruṣāḥ; tena pratyekabuddhasyāntike cittaṃ pradūṣitaṃ; sa praduṣṭacittaḥ kathayati: bhoḥ pravrajita kiṃ tava pādau kṣureṇa likhitau? yena tvayā āveśanaśālāyām uccāraḥ kṛtaḥ; na bahir nirgataḥ iti; tenāsau dvāraṃ badhvā sthāpitaḥ ihaiva jighatsaya kālaṃ kuruṣva iti; sa mahātmā saṃlakṣayati: kṣato 'yaṃ tapasvī; yady ahaṃ dvāram avamucya gamiṣyāmi bhūyasyā mātrayā kṣato bhaviṣyati iti; sa tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ; yāvat kumbhakārasya bhojanavelā āsannā; tasya dveṣaparyavasthānaṃ vigataṃ; sa kathayati bhoḥ pravrajita āgaccha; bhuñjmahe; pratyekabuddhaḥ kathayati: bhadramukha kālabhojino vayam; atikrāntaḥ kālaḥ iti; sa kathayati: yady evam ihaiva śvo bhuktvā gamiṣyasi iti; tena tasyānukampārtham adhivāsitaṃ; sa tenāparasmin divase praṇītenānnāhāreṇa santarpitaḥ; kāyikī teṣāṃ mahātmanāṃ dharmadeśanā na vācikī; sa upari vihāyasam abhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprāṭihāryāṇi kartum ārabdhaḥ; āśu pṛthagjanasya ṛddhir āvarjanakarī; sa mūlanikṛtta iva drumaḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati; avatara mahādakṣiṇīya; mama kāmapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāram anuprayaccha iti; so 'vatīrṇaḥ; tena tasya pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ; yan mayā evaṃvidhe sadbhūtadakṣiṇīye apakāraḥ kṛtaḥ, mā asya karmaṇo bhāgī syāṃ; yat tu kāraḥ anenāhaṃ kuśalamūlena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jāyeya; evaṃvidhānāṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ lābhī syāṃ; prativiśiṣṭataraṃ cātaḥ śāstāram ārāgayeyaṃ mā virāgayeyam iti
  kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ? yo 'sau kumbhakāraḥ eṣa eva sa rājā bimbisāraḥ tena kālena tena samayena; yat pratyekabuddhasyāntike cittaṃ pradūṣya kharaṃ vākkarma niścāritaṃ tasya karmaṇo vipākena pādau nirlikhitau; cārakāvabaddhaś ca jighatsayā kālagataḥ; yat tu tena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ, tasya karmaṇo vipākena āḍhye mahādhane mahābhoge kule jātaḥ; mamāntike viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ (
SBV II 161

) jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ; iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ; ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ; vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ; tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogāḥ karaṇīyaḥ ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam*
The distress of Ajātaśatru at the death of King Bimbisāra, the arrival of a dancer from the south, and the extraordinary effects of Buddha's smile

amātyair ajātaśatror ārocitaṃ deva vṛddharājaḥ kālagataḥ iti; sa śrutvā mūrcchitaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nipatitaḥ; jalapariṣekapratyāgataprāṇaḥ śokāgāraṃ praviśyāvasthitaḥ; tasya na kaścit śaknoti cittavinodanaṃ kartuṃ; amātyās tasya cittavinodopāyaṃ

children.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, there was a certain woman whose husband was abroad. Before her, a crow cawed most sweetly. She said: 'Fly away, fly away, crow! If my husband returns safely and in good health, I shall give you a golden cap.' Then her husband returned safely. The crow cawed most sweetly before her again, seeking the golden cap. Then she gave him the golden cap. He wandered here and there wearing it. Because of the golden cap, a hawk struck off his head. A deity spoke a verse:
Even wealth becomes a source of ruin when it is bound up with the basis of ruin —
as shown by the pleasure-seeking one whose head was adorned with gold! //

In the past, monks, a <s>Himalayan</s> elephant descended to drink water. Behind him, a jackal descended. He saw the elephant's footprint and began to measure it with his own foot. He thought: 'These are my footprints.' Jumping and leaping to place his feet [in the elephant's prints], he was impaled on a sharp stake of splintered bamboo. A deity spoke a verse:

body.text: āhūyoktaḥ: bhoḥ ācārya śakṣyasi tvam īdṛśaṃ yantraṃ kartuṃ yaḥ paṃcabhiḥ puruṣaśataiḥ āmreḍyate? iti; sa kathayati: ārya śakṣyāmi iti; tena tasya śatasahasro muktāhāro dattaḥ; manuṣyasahasraṃ ca dattam; uktaś ca; yatra sthāne bhagavāṃs tiṣṭhati, tanmukhaṃ gṛdhrakūṭasyopari yantraṃ sajjīkuru iti; tatra paṃca manuṣyaśatāni sthāpitāni, ye tad yantram āmreḍayanti; aparasmin sthāne ardhatṛtīyāni śatāni sthāpitāni, uktāni ca; yadi śramaṇo gautamo yantreṇa na praghātyate, yuṣmābhiḥ praghātayitavyaḥ iti; aparasminn api sthāne tadarthena ardhatṛtīyāni manuṣyaśatāni; sarve ca samādiṣṭāḥ: yeṣāṃ yuṣmākaṃ śramaṇo gautamo bhāgaprāpto bhavati, taiḥ praghātayitavyaḥ iti; ātmanā cāparasmin pradeśe sthitaḥ; eṣāṃ paribhraṣṭo mayā praghātayitavyaḥ iti; yāvat tāni paṃca puruṣaśatāni yantram āmreḍayitum ārabdhāni; saṃjalpaṃ kurvanti: kasyārthe yantram āmreḍyate iti
body.translated_text: summoned him and said: 'Master, can you build such a catapult that requires five hundred men to operate?' He said: 'Noble sir, I can.' He gave him a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [coins] and a thousand men, and told him: 'Prepare the catapult atop <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>, aimed at the place where the <s>Bhagavān</s> dwells.' Five hundred men were stationed there to operate the catapult. At another spot, two hundred and fifty were stationed, and told: 'If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> is not killed by the catapult, you must kill him.' At yet another spot, two hundred and fifty men were stationed for the same purpose. All were instructed: 'Whichever of you the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> comes within range of, those must kill him.' He himself stood at another spot [thinking]: 'If he escapes from these, I shall kill him.' Then those five hundred men began to operate the catapult. They conversed among themselves: 'For whose sake is this catapult being operated?'

children.text: ) svajīvitaparityāgaḥ, na tu devamanuṣyapūjitasya buddhasya bhagavataḥ prāṇaghātaḥ; parityajata yantram iti; te yantraṃ parityajya gṛdhrakūṭe itaś cāmutaś ca paribhramanti, katareṇa sthānena yantram avatārayāmaḥ, yatra devadatto na paśyed iti; teṣāṃ cetasā cittam ājñāya bhagavatā sopānaṃ nirmitaṃ; teṣāṃ sopānaṃ dṛṣṭvā etad abhavat: bhavantaḥ kuto 'tra sopānaḥ? bhagavata eṣo 'nubhāvaḥ iti; bhūyasyā mātrayā cittam abhiprasādya sopānena avatīrya, yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntāḥ; bhagavān api tadvinayanāpekṣayaiva gṛdhrakūṭe parvate caṅkramyamāṇo 'vasthitaḥ; tatas te bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā purastān niṣaṇṇā dharmaśravaṇāya: bhagavatā teṣām āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñatvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā, yāṃ śrutvā tair viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ; te dṛṣṭasatyās trir udānam udānayanti: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā; na rājñā neṣṭena svakanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair, na śramaṇabrāhmaṇaiḥ, yat bhagavatā asmākaṃ kṛtaṃ; uddhṛto narakatiryakpretebhyaḥ pādaḥ; pratiṣṭhāpito devamanuṣyeṣu; paryantīkṛtaḥ saṃsāraḥ; ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ; laṅghitā asthiparvatāḥ; pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi; vivṛtāni svargadvārāṇi; anādikālopacitaṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ; abhikrāntā vayaṃ bhadanta, abhikrāntāḥ; ete vayaṃ bhagavantaṃ śraṇaṃ gacchāmaḥ, dharmaṃ ca bhikṣusaṃghaṃ ca; upāsakāṃ ca asmān bhagavān dhārayatu adyāgreṇa yāvajjīvaṃ prāṇopetān, śaraṇāgatān, abhiprasannān; ity uktvā bhagavato 'ntikāt paṃca śikṣāpadāni grahitum ārabdhāḥ
children.translated_text: ) [better] the sacrifice of one's own life than the killing of the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who is worshipped by gods and humans. Abandon the catapult!' They abandoned the catapult and wandered about here and there on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>: 'By which way shall we bring the catapult down, where <s>Devadatta</s> will not see us?' The <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing their minds with his own mind, created a staircase. Seeing the staircase, they thought: 'Sirs, where did this staircase come from? This is the power of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' With even greater faith in their minds, they descended by the staircase and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> too, with the very purpose of subduing them, remained walking back and forth on <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>. Then they bowed their heads at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known their dispositions, latent tendencies, temperaments, and natures, gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> as penetrates the Four Noble Truths. Hearing it, they shattered the mountain of the view of a self-existent individual (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), which rises with twenty peaks, with the diamond of knowledge, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>srotaāpattiphala</s>). Having seen the truths, they uttered a solemn declaration three times: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father, nor by the king, nor by friends, nor by our kinsmen and relatives, nor by departed ancestors, nor by ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us. Our foot has been lifted from the hells, the animal realm, and the realm of hungry ghosts. We have been established among gods and humans. <s>Saṃsāra</s> has been brought to its end. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up. The mountains of bones have been surmounted. The doors to the lower realms have been shut. The doors to heaven have been opened. The mountain of the view of a self-existent individual, accumulated since beginningless time, has been shattered with the diamond of knowledge, and the fruit of stream-entry has been directly realized. We are blessed, Venerable Sir, blessed! We go for refuge to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, to the <s>Dharma</s>, and to the community of monks. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consider us lay followers from today onward, for as long as we live, who have taken refuge and are filled with faith.' Having spoken thus, they began to take the five precepts from the <s>Bhagavān</s>.
Then they saw the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> below. They said: 'Sirs, better (

body.text: ) abhiroḍhum ārabdhaḥ; paśyati tāni bhagavato 'ntikād dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti; dṛṣṭvā ca bhūyasyā mātrayā saṃjātāmarṣo 'nyatomukho gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvatam abhirūḍhaḥ; yāvat paśyati yantrakalācāryo 'pi niṣpalāyitaḥ; svayam eva paṃcaśataparivāro yantram āmreḍayitum ārabdhaḥ; bhagavān saṃlakṣayati: mayaiva etāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavat pratyupasthitāny avaśyabhāvīni; mayaiva etāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati? iti viditvā tāni paṃca manuṣyaśatāni idam avocat: bhavanto devadattas tīvraparyavasthānāvasthito gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvatam abhirūḍhāḥ; gacchata; mamaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāni iti; tatas tāni paṃca manuṣyaśatāni niṣpalāyitāni; devatānām adhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate
body.translated_text: ). He saw that they were listening to the <s>Dharma</s> in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence. Seeing this, with even greater anger, he turned away and climbed <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain. He saw that the catapult-master too had fled. He himself, with his retinue of five hundred, began to operate the catapult. The <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected: 'I myself performed these deeds, accumulated them, gathered their provisions, whose conditions had ripened, which stood present like a flood, which were inevitably bound to occur. I myself performed and accumulated these deeds — who else would experience them?' Knowing this, he said to those five hundred men: 'Sirs, <s>Devadatta</s>, consumed by fierce resentment, has climbed <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain. Go — these are deeds I performed.' Then those five hundred men fled. Deities have the ability of vision below.

body.text: atha vajrapāṇer yakṣasyaitad abhavat: devadatto bhagavato vadhāya parākramati iti viditvā yena kumbhīrayakṣas tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya kumbhīraṃ yakṣam idam avocat: devadatto gṛdhrakūṭād yantreṇa bhagavataḥ śilāṃ kṣeptum ārabdhaḥ; tava ca bhavane bhagavān viharati; tad ahaṃ yatnam āsthāya antarīkṣe etāṃ śilāṃ vajreṇa cūrṇayāmi; tvayāpi sāhāyye vartitavyaṃ; kadācic cūrṇitāyāḥ khaṇḍaḥ bhagavata upariṣṭān nipated ti; sa kathayati: evaṃ bhavatu iti; bhagavān abhyavakāśe sthitvā parvatavivare praviṣṭaḥ; devadattena paṃcaśataparivāreṇa yantram āmreḍya bhagavataḥ śilā kṣiptā; vajrapāṇinā yakṣeṇa cūrṇitā; ardhaṃ bhagavataḥ sthāne patitukāmaṃ kumbhīrayakṣeṇa gṛhṇatā na sugṛhītaṃ kṛtaṃ; sa tena praghātitaḥ; bhagavatā utplutya pāṣāṇaśarkarayā pādaḥ kṣataḥ kṛtaḥ; bhagavāṃs tasyāṃ velāyāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣate
body.translated_text: Then the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> thought: '<s>Devadatta</s> is striving to kill the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Knowing this, he approached the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Kumbhīra</s>. Having approached, he said this to the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Kumbhīra</s>: '<s>Devadatta</s> has begun to hurl a boulder from <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> with a catapult at the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> dwells in your domain. I, exerting myself, shall pulverize this boulder in mid-air with my thunderbolt. But you too must help — lest a fragment of the pulverized boulder fall upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' He said: 'So be it.' The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having stood in the open, entered a mountain cave. <s>Devadatta</s>, with his retinue of five hundred, operated the catapult and hurled the boulder at the <s>Bhagavān</s>. The <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Vajrapāṇi</s> pulverized it. Half of it, about to fall on the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s spot, was not properly caught by the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Kumbhīra</s> as he tried to seize it. He was killed by it. The <s>Bhagavān</s>, having leapt aside, was wounded on the foot by a stone splinter. The <s>Bhagavān</s> at that moment spoke a verse:

children.translated_text: Neither in the sky, nor in the midst of the ocean,

there exists no place on earth

body.text: kumbhīro 'pi yakṣaḥ kuśalacittaḥ kālagataḥ; kālaṃ kṛtvā praṇīteṣu trayastriṃśeṣu deveṣu upapannaḥ; dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇā iti sa paśyati: yakṣebhyaś cyutaḥ, praṇīteṣu trayastriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ bhagavato (
body.translated_text: The <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Kumbhīra</s> too, having died with a wholesome mind, was after death reborn among the noble <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. It is the natural law that when a divine son or divine maiden has recently been reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where did I pass away? Where have I been reborn? By what deed?' He saw: 'I passed away from among the <s>yakṣas</s>, was reborn among the noble <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, by having generated faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s (

body.translated_text: SBV II 169

body.translated_text: ) presence.' Then this divine son, formerly a <s>yakṣa</s>, thought: 'It would not be fitting for me to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> to see him after having spent the night [away].

yan nv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrameyam iti
  atha sa yakṣapūrvī devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍaladharo hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātras tām eva rātriṃ divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamāndārakāṇāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṃgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ gṛdhrakūṭaṃ parvatam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavataṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya; tato bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī caturāryasatyasaṃprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā yakṣapūrviṇā devaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ; sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā kṛtaṃ; neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa; na rājñā na devatābhir na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇaiḥ yad bhagavatā asmākaṃ kṛtam; ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ; laṃghitā asthiparvatāḥ pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi; pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu āha ca
body.translated_text:
Let me approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> to see him without having spent the night [away].'
Then that divine son, formerly a <s>yakṣa</s>, wearing swaying, pure crystal earrings, his body adorned with necklaces and half-necklaces, that very night, having filled his lap with divine <s>utpala</s>, lotus, <s>kumuda</s>, <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>māndāraka</s> flowers, illuminating the whole of <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain with an extraordinary radiance, showered the <s>Bhagavān</s> with flowers and sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having known his disposition, latent tendencies, temperament, and nature, gave such a teaching on the <s>Dharma</s> as penetrates the Four Noble Truths. Hearing it, the divine son formerly a <s>yakṣa</s> shattered the mountain of the view of a self-existent individual, which rises with twenty peaks, with the diamond of knowledge, and directly realized the fruit of stream-entry. Having seen the truths, he uttered a solemn declaration three times: 'This, Venerable Sir, was not done for us by our mother, nor by our father — not by friends, nor by our kinsmen and relatives; not by the king, not by deities, not by departed ancestors, not by ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — what the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us. The oceans of blood and tears have been dried up. The mountains of bones have been surmounted. The doors to the lower realms have been shut. The doors to heaven and liberation have been opened. We have been established among gods and humans.' And he said:

children.translated_text: By your power, the terrible /
path of the lower realms, fraught with many faults, has been blocked; /
the meritorious path to heaven has been opened wide,
and the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been found by me. //
Through reliance on you, I have today obtained
the pure, well-purified eye, free from fault. /
I have attained the peaceful state, dear to the noble ones,
and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering. //
In the world, worshipped by <s>Daityas</s>, humans, and gods,
free from birth, old age, death, and disease, /
a sight rarely seen in thousands of existences —
fruitful today is your sight, O Sage! //

body.text:
avalambya tataḥ pralambahāraḥ
  caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātaharṣaḥ /
  parigamya ca dakṣiṇaṃ jitāriṃ
  suralokābhimukho divaṃ jagāma // (

Then, with his necklace hanging down,
having bowed at both feet, his heart filled with joy, /

he departed toward the heavens, facing the world of the gods. // (

body.text:
upapannaḥ; sa imāṃ rātriṃ matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ; tasya mayā dharmo deśitaḥ; sa dṛṣṭisatyaḥ svabhavanaṃ gataḥ; iti hi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipākaḥ; ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklaḥ; vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśraḥ; tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣv eva karmasv ābhogāḥ karaṇīyaḥ ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam*
  bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhadanta kumbhīreṇa yakṣeṇa bhagavataḥ arthāya ātmā parityaktaḥ iti; bhagavān āha: na bhikṣava etarhi yathā atīte 'py adhvani anena mamārthāya ātmā parityaktaḥ; tac chrūyatāṃ
body.translated_text:
. This night he came to my presence. I taught him the <s>Dharma</s>. Having seen the truths, he returned to his own abode. Thus, monks, for purely dark deeds the result is purely dark; for purely bright deeds, purely bright; for mixed deeds, mixed. Therefore, monks, abandoning purely dark deeds and mixed deeds, effort should be made only toward purely bright deeds. Thus, monks, you should train.'
The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, the <s>yakṣa</s> <s>Kumbhīra</s> sacrificed himself for the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s sake.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, monks — in the past too he sacrificed himself for my sake. Listen to that.'

) that one who dwells nearby should not slaughter the deer — thus between them the perception of father and son arose. The hunter addressed the <s>ṛṣi</s> (sage) as 'father,' and the <s>ṛṣi</s> addressed the hunter as 'son.' Then at a later time, King <s>Brahmadatta</s>, having risen early in the morning, went out to hunt deer. He struck a deer with a succession of arrows. It leaped up and entered the hermitage of the <s>ṛṣi</s>. There too the king struck it in the vital spot with a steel-tipped arrow, and it died. The <s>ṛṣi</s>, overcome by anger, said: 'You are a sinful king, of evil conduct, who has slain the deer that took refuge with me!' When this was said, the king, his mind fixed in enmity, said to his ministers: 'Sirs, what is the punishment for one who insults a king, a consecrated <s>kṣatriya</s>?' The ministers said: 'The punishment is death.' The king said: 'If so, this <s>ṛṣi</s> is abandoned by me.' The ministers began to slay the <s>ṛṣi</s>. By chance, the hunter came to the <s>ṛṣi</s>'s presence. Having arrived, he observed: 'While I am alive, how can the <s>ṛṣi</s> be slain?' He began to fight. The <s>ṛṣi</s> fled. The hunter was slain by the great army.
  The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who was the <s>ṛṣi</s> — that was I myself at that time, in that era. He who was the hunter — that is none other than <s>Kumbhīra</s> the <s>yakṣa</s> at that time, in that era. Even then he sacrificed himself for my sake; now too he has sacrificed himself for my sake.'

In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Brahmadatta</s> was exercising sovereignty — prosperous, flourishing, secure, abundant in food, and teeming with a great multitude of people. At that time, not far from the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, in a certain hermitage rich in roots, flowers, fruits, and water, resounding with the cries of various birds, a sage dwelt — practicing severe austerities, eating fruits, roots, and water, wearing antelope skins and bark garments. Near that hermitage, a deer-hunter made his living by killing deer after deer. From time to time he would visit that sage. That sage would attend to him when he was weary with roots and fruits. body.translated_text: . Blood kept flowing and would not stop. <s>Jīvaka</s>, the king of physicians, who attended to the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s ailments, approached three times daily. The faithful populace dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, as well as wealthy men, guild-masters, and caravan-leaders endowed with right view who had come from various lands — among them some said: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, this medicine is excellent for this.' Others said: 'This is excellent.' <s>Jīvaka</s>, the king of physicians, said: 'There is a medicine that produces immediate relief. But it is difficult to obtain.' The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> said: '<s>Jīvaka</s>, what is it?' He said: '<s>Gośīrṣacandana</s> (ox-head sandalwood).' At that time, the supply of <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> had been completely cut off. But a certain merchant had kept <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> stored for emergencies, thinking: 'This King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> is fierce, violent, and harsh. If by chance he should have need of <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> (

body.translated_text: SBV II 172

), he would surely have me beheaded for not having it. That is why I have been selling <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> from time to time.' He heard that <s>Jīvaka</s>, the king of physicians, had prescribed <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> for relieving the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s ailment. He reflected: 'This <s>Ajātaśatru</s> has been led astray by <s>Devadatta</s> and is hostile in his mind toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If I give the <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is possible that he will cause me harm.' Then he reflected again: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> is worshipped by gods and humans. If the loss of my life should come about for his sake, so be it. I shall give the <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Taking the <s>gośīrṣacandana</s>, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, bowed at his feet, and said: '<s>Bhagavān</s>, I have learned that the <s>Bhagavān</s> has need of <s>gośīrṣacandana</s>. Here it is. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> accept it out of compassion.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'Accept, <s>Ānanda</s>, the <s>gośīrṣacandana</s> from this great-souled one.' The Venerable <s>Ānanda</s> accepted it. Then that merchant, filled with joy and delight, bowed his head at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and departed from the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s presence.
  Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> performed a wonder. For it is the nature of things that when <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>Bhagavāns</s>, display a smile, rays of blue, yellow, red, and white issue from their mouths — some go downward, some go upward.

children.translated_text: Those that go downward pass through <s>Sañjīva</s>, <s>Kālasūtra</s>, <s>Saṅghāta</s>, <s>Raurava</s>, <s>Mahāraurava</s>, <s>Tāpana</s>, <s>Pratāpana</s>, <s>Avīci</s>, <s>Arbuda</s>, <s>Nirarbuda</s>, <s>Aṭaṭa</s>, <s>Hahava</s>, <s>Huhuva</s>, <s>Utpala</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> hells. Having gone there, in the hot hells they fall as coolness; in the cold hells they fall as warmth. By this, the particular sufferings of those beings are alleviated. They think: 'Have we, sirs, passed away from here, or have we been reborn elsewhere?' To generate faith in them, the <s>Bhagavān</s> sends forth an emanation. Having seen the emanation, they think: 'We have, sirs, neither passed away from here nor been reborn elsewhere. Rather, this is an unprecedented being. By his power our particular sufferings have been alleviated.' Having generated faith in the emanation, having exhausted the <s>karma</s> that led to their hellish experience, they take rebirth among gods and humans where they become vessels for the truths.
Strive forth, renounce, apply yourselves to the <s>Buddha</s>'s teaching! /

children.translated_text: Variegated, adorned with a thousand colors,

by which the directions all around have been illuminated,

body.translated_text:
Then those rays, having traversed the great trichiliocosm, followed behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to declare past <s>karma</s>, they disappear behind him; if he wishes to declare future events, they disappear in front; if he wishes to declare rebirth in hell, they disappear at the soles of his feet; if he wishes to declare rebirth as an animal, they disappear at the heels; if he wishes to declare rebirth as a hungry ghost, they disappear at the big toe; if he wishes to declare rebirth as a human, they disappear at the knees; if he wishes to declare a universal monarch by force, they disappear at the left palm; if he wishes to declare a wheel-turning monarch, they disappear at the right palm; if he wishes to declare rebirth among gods, they disappear at the navel; if he wishes to declare the awakening of a <s>Śrāvaka</s> (disciple), they disappear at the mouth; if he wishes to declare the awakening of a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, they disappear at the <s>ūrṇā</s> (hair-tuft between the brows); if he wishes to declare unsurpassed perfect awakening, they disappear at the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown protuberance).
  Then those rays, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, disappeared at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

Then those rays, having traversed the three-thousandfold great thousand world-system, return and follow behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> wishes to declare a past <s>karma</s>, they vanish behind the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If he wishes to declare a future [event], they vanish before him. If he wishes to declare a rebirth in hell, they vanish at the soles of his feet. If he wishes to declare a rebirth as an animal, they vanish at his heels. If he wishes to declare a rebirth as a hungry ghost, they vanish at his big toe. If he wishes to declare a human rebirth, they vanish at his knees. If he wishes to declare a lesser universal monarch, they vanish in his left palm. If he wishes to declare a universal monarch, they vanish in his right palm. If he wishes to declare a divine rebirth, they vanish at his navel. If he wishes to declare the awakening of a disciple (<s>śrāvaka</s>), they vanish at his mouth. If he wishes to declare the awakening of a solitary buddha (<s>pratyekabuddha</s>), they vanish at his <s>ūrṇā</s> (tuft between the eyebrows). If he wishes to declare unsurpassed perfect awakening, they vanish at his <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance).
  Then those rays circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times and vanished at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s <s>ūrṇā</s>. Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with joined palms, questioned the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
Free from birth, with lowliness and pride abandoned,
<s>Buddhas</s> are the supreme cause in the world. /
Not without reason do the Conquerors, who have vanquished their foes,
display a smile as white as conch, lotus-fiber, and snow. //
And he spoke these verses:

children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Did you see, <s>Ānanda</s>, that girl who, having placed her faith in my presence, gave milk?' 'I saw her, Venerable Sir.' 'This girl, <s>Ānanda</s>, by this wholesome root, by this arising of the aspiration-mind, and by the relinquishing of this gift, shall become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one) named <s>Kṣīraprada</s> ("Milk-Giver"). This was her gift — namely, her act of faith in my presence.'

'At this very time, having realized it yourself through wisdom, O steadfast one, /
for the sake of listeners who are yearning, O ascetic, Lord of Conquerors, /
with steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words, O Bull among Sages, /
dispel the doubt that has arisen.' /

body.translated_text: In the past, monks, not far from a certain settlement, there was a garden endowed with roots, tubers, flowers, fruits, and water, resounding with the calls of various birds. A sage dwelt there, eating fruits, roots, and water, clothed in antelope skins and bark, and skilled in sacred formulas and mantras. In that settlement dwelt a householder. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. He enjoyed, amused, and attended to her. As he enjoyed, amused, and attended to her, in the course of time his wife became pregnant. After the passing of eight or nine months, she gave birth. A boy was born. After performing the birth celebration in full for twenty-one days, a name was assigned. He was raised, nourished, and grew to adulthood. Whether walking,

body.translated_text: standing, or lying down, he performed wholesome and supremely wholesome deeds. The people gave him the name <s>Dharmakāma</s> ('Lover of <s>Dharma</s>'). Seeking what is wholesome, he left the settlement and from time to time approached that sage, and performed services for him. Because he approached the ascetic, he came to be known as <s>Tāpasa</s> ('Ascetic'), 'The Ascetic, the Ascetic.' Then at a later time, a poisonous boil arose on him. He was treated with many medicines and sacred formulas, but the illness did not subside. He was brought by his parents to that sage: 'Great Sage, your attendant is about to die from the poisonous boil. Treat him.' The sage began to make a declaration of truth: (

children.translated_text:
<s>Devadatta</s>, unhappy, displeased, and regretful, thought: 'In vain did I hurl a stone at the ascetic <s>Gautama</s>. The ascetic <s>Gautama</s> was not killed, and it has become widely known among the people.' He went to the foot of a tree, consumed with worry, and sat there with legs crossed in an artificial pose. The monks, in various places, began to reproach, censure, and disparage him: 'See, Venerable Sirs, how cruel-minded is <s>Devadatta</s>, who even attacked the <s>Bhagavān</s> after having gone forth! He hurled a stone from above!' <s>Kokālika</s>, <s>Khaṇḍadravyaka</s>, <s>Kaṭamoraka</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, and <s>Samudradatta</s> said: 'Why do you speak without examining? Do you not see <s>Devadatta</s> there at the foot of the tree? He has attained the fourth <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). He is a great soul. How could he do such a thing?'
  The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, these <s>Kokālika</s>, <s>Khaṇḍadravyaka</s>, <s>Kaṭamoraka</s>, <s>Tiṣya</s>, and <s>Samudradatta</s> — themselves shameless, they speak in praise of the shameless <s>Devadatta</s>.' body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo rājagṛhīyakair manuṣyaiḥ rājñā ca kenacit kāraṇena kriyākāraṃ kṛtvā dve śmaśāne vyavasthāpite, ekasmin pradeśe puruṣāś chorayitavyāḥ ekasmin striyaḥ iti; yāvad apareṇa samayena paṇḍakaḥ kālagataḥ; sa na ekasmin śmaśāne avakāśaṃ labhate, na dvitīye; rājagṛhasyānyatamasmin pradeśe udyānaṃ mūlakandapuṣpaphalasalilasaṃpannaṃ nānāvihaganikūjitaṃ; tasmiṃś ca khustaśirā ṛṣiḥ prativasati; phalamūlāmbubhakṣaḥ ajinavalkalavāsāḥ; tasmiṃś ca pradeśe trikaṇṭakedārairaṇḍavṛkṣāś ca santi; tatra sa paṇḍako choritaḥ; kuṇapagandhena sṛgāla āgataḥ;
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, the people of <s>Rājagṛha</s>, together with the king, by a certain regulation established two charnel grounds: in one area men were to be cremated, in another women. Then at a later time, a eunuch died. He could not find a place in either charnel ground. In a certain area of <s>Rājagṛha</s> there was a garden, abundant in roots, bulbs, flowers, fruits, and water, resounding with the songs of various birds. There a sage named <s>Khustaśiras</s> (Tonsured-head) dwelt, subsisting on fruits, roots, and water, clothed in antelope-skin and bark garments. In that area there were also thorn-hedges, fields, and castor-oil trees. The eunuch was cremated there. Attracted by the smell of the corpse, a jackal came.

body.text: sa taṃ paṇḍakaṃ bhakṣayitum ārabdhaḥ; kākaś ca eraṇḍavṛkṣāgratas tiṣṭhati; tasya buddhir utpannā: sṛgālasya varṇaṃ bhāṣe; kadācid bhakṣitaśeṣaṃ dadyād iti; sa tasya gāthayā varṇaṃ bhāṣitum ārabdhaḥ:
body.translated_text: He began to devour the eunuch. A crow was perched atop a castor-oil tree. The thought arose in him: 'Let me speak in praise of the jackal — perhaps he will give me his leftovers.' He began to praise him with a verse:

children.text: siṃhasya te yathā grīvā ṛṣabhasya yathā kaṭiḥ /
children.translated_text: Your neck is like a lion's; your haunches like a bull's. /

children.text: mṛgarāja namas tubhyaṃ bhuktaśeṣaṃ labhemahi // iti
children.translated_text: O king of beasts, obeisance to you — may we obtain your leftovers! //
The jackal looked up and replied:
Who is this one at the top of this finest of trees, the best of the twice-born indeed? /

children.text: avabhāsya diśaḥ sarvāḥ bhrājate ratnapiṇḍavat // iti
children.translated_text: Illuminating all the directions, he shines like a cluster of jewels! //
The crow says:
I am here, O fortunate one — I have come for the purpose of seeing you. /

children.text: mṛharāja nams tubhyaṃ bhuktaśeṣaṃ labhemahi // iti
children.translated_text: O king of beasts, obeisance to you — may we obtain your leftovers! //
The jackal says:
You have the neck of a peacock, O crow, pleasing to behold! /

Then the sage entered the fire-sanctuary and saw the water-pot smashed. He reflected: 'This is the deed of that wicked crow, not of anyone else.' Having understood, he spoke a verse:

bhakṣitaḥ; sa pratibuddhaḥ; tasmin pradeśe dharmasya aṃrtaphalodgāraḥ utthitaḥ; adharmeṇa ghrātaḥ; sa kathayati: kasya eṣa udgāraḥ iti; sa kathayati: amṛtaphalasya; kutra labdhaṃ?; sa kathayati: mayā tava suptasya amṛtaphalaṃ labdhaṃ; tan mayā bhakṣitaṃ; tvaṃ notthāpitaḥ: ekasminn eva śarīre vipakṣyate iti; sa kathayati: na śobhanaṃ kṛtam; aham api kālajño bhaviṣyāmi iti; yāvad apareṇa samayena dharmo middham avakrāntaḥ; adharmo jāgarti; tena viṣaphalam uhyamānaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ; tena tad bhakṣitaṃ; tāv ubhāv api mūrcchitau; adharmo viṣaphalena paryākulīkṛtaḥ kathayati: tatra tatropapadyeya, yatra yatra janmani tava vadhakaḥ syāṃ pratyarthikaḥ pratyamitraḥ iti; dharmaḥ kathayati: aham api yatra yatropapadyeya, tatra tatra janmani tava maitryupasaṃhāraṃ kuryām iti
  bhagavān āha: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau dharmaḥ aham eva saḥ tena kālena tena samayena; yo 'sāv adharmaḥ eṣa eva sa devadattaḥ tena kālena tena samayena; tatrāyaṃ mama tatprathamato virūkṣitaḥ; ahaṃ cāsya maitreṇa cittenāvasthitaḥ; bhūyo 'py ayaṃ yathā mama virūkṣitaḥ, ahaṃ cāsya maitracittaḥ; tac chrūyatām
body.translated_text:
himself. <s>Adharma</s> woke up. In that place, the belch of the ambrosia-fruit arose from <s>Dharma</s>. <s>Adharma</s> smelled it. He said: 'Whose belch is this?' <s>Dharma</s> said: 'Of the ambrosia-fruit.' 'Where did you get it?' He said: 'While you were sleeping, I found an ambrosia-fruit. I ate it. I did not wake you up — it will be digested in this one body anyway.' He said: 'You did not act rightly. I too shall know the right time.' Then at a later time, <s>Dharma</s> fell asleep. <s>Adharma</s> remained awake. He saw a poison-fruit being carried along. He ate it. Both of them fell unconscious. <s>Adharma</s>, overwhelmed by the poison-fruit, said: 'May I be reborn wherever I may, and in every birth may I be your killer, your adversary, your enemy!' <s>Dharma</s> said: 'And may I, wherever I may be reborn, in every birth show you the gathering of loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>)!'
  The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who was <s>Dharma</s> — that was I myself at that time, in that era. He who was <s>Adharma</s> — that is this very <s>Devadatta</s> at that time, in that era. There he first became hostile toward me, and I remained disposed toward him with a mind of loving-kindness. Listen further to how he became hostile toward me and how I maintained a mind of loving-kindness toward him.'

The story of Sūryanemi the poet

The story of <s>Sūryanemi</s> the poet

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo vārāṇasyāṃ nagaryāṃ sarjaraso nāma rājā rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca yāvad ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca; tena bhūmyantarasya rājñaḥ sakāśād dārikā labdhā; sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati; tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ sā dārikā kālāntareṇa āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā; sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt sūryodaye prasūtā; dārako (
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, a king named <s>Sarjarasa</s> was exercising sovereignty — it was prosperous, and teeming with a great multitude of people. He obtained a princess from a neighboring king. He sported, enjoyed, and dallied with her. As he sported, enjoyed, and dallied, in the course of time the princess became pregnant. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth at sunrise. A boy (

body.text: SBV II 179

) jātaḥ abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ; tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyte kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāma iti; amātyāḥ kathayanti: ayaṃ dārakaḥ sūryodaye jātaḥ; tasmād bhavatu dārakasya sūryanemīti nāma; tasya sūryanemīti nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ; sūryanemī dārakaḥ aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo dattaḥ; dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ dhātrībhyāṃ; so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpirmaṇḍena anyaiś cottaptottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣair āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam; sa yadā mahān saṃvṛttas tadā lipyām upanyastaḥ saṅkhyāyāṃ gaṇanāyāṃ mudrāyāṃ; yāni rājñāṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ mūrdhābhiṣiktānāṃ janapadaiśvaryasthāmavīryam anuprāptānāṃ mahāntaṃ pṛthivīmaṇḍalam abhinirjitya adhyāvasatāṃ pṛthag bhavanti śilpasthānakarmasthānāni tadyathā hastigrīvāyām aśvapṛṣṭhe rathe tsarau dhanuṣi apayāne niryāṇe aṃkuśagrahe pāśagrahe tomaragrahe chedye bhedye vedhye muṣṭibandhe pādabandhe śikhābandhe dūravedhe śabdavedhe marmavedhe akṣūṇavedhe dṛḍhaprahāritāyāṃ pañcasu sthāneṣu kṛtāvī saṃvṛttaḥ; sa pitrā yauvarājye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ
body.translated_text: ) was born — handsome, good-looking, and pleasing. At his birth, having performed the birth-celebration, a name was assigned: 'What shall the boy's name be?' The ministers said: 'This boy was born at sunrise. Therefore let the boy's name be <s>Sūryanemi</s> (Sun-rim).' The name <s>Sūryanemi</s> was assigned. The boy <s>Sūryanemi</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two body-nurses, two milk-nurses, two washing-nurses, and two play-nurses. Raised by eight nurses with milk, curds, butter, ghee, skimmed ghee, and other choice provisions, he grew quickly like a lotus in a lake. When he was grown, he was trained in writing, arithmetic, calculation, and seal-craft. Those various arts and crafts that pertain to kings, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, anointed sovereigns who have attained the might, valor, and power of their dominions and who dwell having conquered a great expanse of the earth — namely: mounting an elephant's neck, horseback riding, chariot-driving, sword-play, archery, retreating, advancing, goad-handling, lasso-handling, lance-handling, cutting, piercing, penetrating, fist-binding, foot-binding, topknot-binding, far-range striking, sound-range striking, vital-point striking, unerring striking, and firm striking — in these five categories of skill he became proficient. He was established by his father as crown prince.

body.text: sarjarasasya rājñaḥ agramahiṣī dharmā nāma; agrāmātyaś ca goniṣādo nāmnā; tasmiṃś ca rājā atyarthaṃ viśvastaḥ; yāvad apareṇa samayena rājā sarjarasaḥ dharmayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati; tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ dharmā āpannasatvā saṃvṛttā; sā naimittikair vyākṛtā: putraṃ janayiṣyati; sa rājānaṃ jīvitād vyaparopya svayam eva paṭṭe badhvā rājyaiśvaryādhipatyaṃ kārayiṣyati iti; yāvad rājā sarjarasaḥ glānaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; sa upasthīyate mūlagaṇḍapatrapuṣpaphalabhaiṣajyaiḥ; na cāsau vyādhir upaśamaṃ gacchati; śarīrāvasthā paricchinnā; sa saṃlakṣayati: mamātyayāt sūryanemī rājā bhaviṣyati; niyatam asau dharmāṃ ghatayiṣyati; kim atra prāptakālaṃ; iti bhūyaḥ sa saṃlakṣyati: ayam amātyo goniṣādaḥ mayā praṇītair bhogaiḥ saṃvibhaktaḥ, pratipālitaś ca; asya dharmāṃ samarpayāmi iti; tena goniṣāda āhūyoktaḥ:mama dharmā agramahiṣī: tvaṃ cāgrāmātyaḥ; mama śarīrāvasthā paricchinnā; niyatam ahaṃ prāṇāir viyokṣye; tvayā matpriyatayā tathā anuṣṭheyaṃ yathā dharmā sūryaneminā jīvitān na vyaparopyate (
body.translated_text: King <s>Sarjarasa</s>'s chief queen was named <s>Dharmā</s>. His chief minister was named <s>Goniṣāda</s>. The king placed exceedingly great trust in him. Then at a later time, King <s>Sarjarasa</s> sported, enjoyed, and dallied with <s>Dharmā</s>. As he sported, enjoyed, and dallied, <s>Dharmā</s> became pregnant. The soothsayers prophesied: 'She will bear a son. He will kill the king, bind the royal turban himself, and exercise sovereign royal authority.' Then King <s>Sarjarasa</s> fell ill. He was attended to with medicines of roots, fragrances, leaves, flowers, and fruits. But the illness did not subside. His bodily condition was assessed as terminal. He reflected: 'After my death, <s>Sūryanemi</s> will become king. He will certainly kill <s>Dharmā</s>. What is the proper course of action here?' He reflected further: 'This minister <s>Goniṣāda</s> has been shared in my finest enjoyments and has been maintained by me. I shall entrust <s>Dharmā</s> to him.' He summoned <s>Goniṣāda</s> and said: '<s>Dharmā</s> is my chief queen, and you are my chief minister. My bodily condition is assessed as terminal. I shall certainly die. Out of your devotion to me, you must act in such a way that <s>Dharmā</s> is not killed by <s>Sūryanemi</s>. (

body.text: SBV II 180
) iti; sa kathayati: deva tad api na śakyaṃ te kartum; alpotsuko bhavatu devaḥ; tathā kariṣye yathā na praghātyate iti
body.translated_text: ) He said: 'Your Majesty, that too cannot be done by you. Let Your Majesty be unconcerned. I shall act in such a way that he is not slain.'

all unions end in separation; and life ends in death. //

body.text: iti rājā sarjaraḥ kālagataḥ; sa chatradhvajapatākādiśobhayā mahatā satkāreṇa dhyāpitaḥ; sūryanemī mahārājaḥ mahārājābhiṣekeṇa abhiṣiktaḥ; tenāmātyānām ājñā dattā; dharmāṃ ghātayata iti; goniṣādaḥ kathayati: deva kim asamīkṣya praghātyate? na jñāyate kiṃ dārakaṃ janayiṣyati? uta dārikām iti; tad yadi dārakaṃ janayiṣyati sa eva jīvitād vyaparopyate iti; sūryanemī rājā kathayati: evaṃ bhavatu; tvayaiva saṃrakṣyā iti; tena gṛhe sthāpitā; sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā; dārako jātaḥ; tasminn eva divase kaivartī prasūtā; tasyā dārikā jātā; sa jātamātra eva kaivartīṃ dhanena pralobhya parivartitaḥ; goniṣādena rājño niveditaṃ: deva dharmā prasūtā; dārikā jātā iti; rājā kathayati: śobhanaṃ; muktāḥ smaḥ iti; sa dārakaḥ kaivartyā āpāyitaḥ poṣitaḥ saṃvardhitaḥ mahān saṃvṛttaḥ; lipyakṣarāṇi pāṭhitaḥ; kāvyaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ; tasya kaviḥ kaivartadārakaḥ kaviḥ kaivartadārakaḥ iti saṃjñā saṃvṛttā; goniṣādena dharmāyāḥ samākhyātaṃ: putras te kāvyakartā saṃvṛttaḥ iti; sā kathayati: paśyāmi tāvat kīdṛśaḥ iti; sa kathayati: alaṃ; kiṃ tena dṛṣṭena iti; sā kathayati: putrābhilāṣiṇī ākāṃkṣaty eva darśanaṃ nāvatiṣṭhate iti; tasyā goniṣādena avaśyanirbandhaṃ jñātvā upāyasaṃvidhānena matsyāṃ kṛtvā praveśitaḥ; sa praviśann eva naimittikair vyākṛtaḥ:
body.translated_text: Thus King <s>Sarjara</s> died. He was cremated with great honor, adorned with parasols, banners, and flags. <s>Sūryanemi</s> was consecrated as great king with the royal consecration. He gave a command to his ministers: 'Execute <s>Dharmā</s>.' <s>Goniṣāda</s> said: 'Your Majesty, why execute her without examination? It is not known whether she will bear a boy or a girl. If she bears a boy, he alone shall be put to death.' King <s>Sūryanemi</s> said: 'So be it. She is to be guarded by you.' He placed her in his house. After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth — a boy was born. On that very day, a fisherwoman gave birth — a girl was born. As soon as the boy was born, <s>Goniṣāda</s> enticed the fisherwoman with money and swapped them. <s>Goniṣāda</s> reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, <s>Dharmā</s> has given birth — a girl was born.' The king said: 'Excellent! We are free.' That boy was suckled, nourished, and raised by the fisherwoman and grew up. He was taught letters and writing. He began to compose poetry. The designation 'the Poet, the Fisherman's Son' became his name. <s>Goniṣāda</s> told <s>Dharmā</s>: 'Your son has become a poet.' She said: 'Let me see what he looks like.' He said: 'Enough! What is the use of seeing him?' She said: 'A mother who longs for her son desires to see him and cannot restrain herself.' <s>Goniṣāda</s>, knowing her insistent urgency, by a stratagem had him brought in concealed among fish. As he was entering, the soothsayers declared:

body.text: eṣa kaviḥ kaivartadārako rājānaṃ jīvitād vyaparopya, svayam eva paṭṭāṃ badhvā rājyaṃ kārayiṣyati iti; rājñā śrutaṃ; tenāmātyānām ājñā dattā: gṛhṇīta yathā na paribhraśyate iti; tena karṇaparamparayā śrutaṃ; sa itaś cāmutaś ca niṣpalāyamāno vṛddhayuvatyā gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ; sa tayā gopāyitaḥ; tato haridratailena gātrāṇi mrakṣayitvā maṃce āropya mṛta iti kṛtvā niṣkāsitaḥ; sa ca śmaśāne choritaḥ; utthāya niṣpalāyitaḥ; tasmin pradeśe anyatamaḥ puruṣaḥ puṣpaphalāni paryeṣate; tenāsau niṣpalāyamāno dṛṣṭaḥ; tasya pṛṣṭhataś cārakapuruṣāḥ pradhāvitāḥ; tair asau puruṣaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ: bho (
body.translated_text: 'This Poet, the Fisherman's Son, having put the king to death, will himself tie on the royal fillet and exercise sovereignty.' The king heard this. He gave a command to his ministers: 'Seize him so that he does not escape.' He heard this through a chain of whispers. Fleeing here and there, he entered the house of an old woman. She sheltered him. Then, having smeared his limbs with turmeric oil, placing him on a bed and pretending he was dead, she had him carried out. He was left in the charnel ground. Rising up, he fled. In that area, a certain man was searching for flowers and fruits. He saw the one fleeing. Pursuit officers ran after him. They asked that man: 'Good (

body.text: ) puruṣa na tvayā īdṛśaḥ pramāṇena varṇena ca anena pathā gacchan kaścin manuṣyo dṛṣṭaḥ? sa kathayati: dṛṣṭaḥ; anena pathā gacchata iti; te tasya pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddhāḥ; so 'nyatamasmin karvaṭake rajakasya gṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ; tasya ca yathāvṛttam ārocitaṃ; cārakapuruṣaiḥ karvaṭako vicārayitum ārabdhaḥ; rajakena vastravaraṇḍena veṣṭayitvā gardabhe āropya karvaṭakān niṣkāsitaḥ; snānaśālāyāṃ nitvā muktaḥ; utthāya caturdiśaṃ vyavalokya niṣpalāyitaḥ; tatrāpy anyatareṇa puruṣeṇa dṛṣṭaḥ; tena cārakapuruṣāṇāṃ niveditaṃ; bhavanto yadarthaṃ yūyaṃ karvaṭakaṃ pratyavekṣatha, asau puruṣaḥ anena pathā gataḥ; gacchata śīghram iti; te saṃprasthitāḥ; so 'py aparasmin grāme carmakāragṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ; tasya tena yathāvṛttam ārocitaṃ; sa kathayati: pṛṣṭhato mukhe upānahau kuru iti; sa kathayati: na mayā kadācid evaṃrūpā upānahā kṛtapūrvā; sa gāthāṃ bhāṣate
body.translated_text: ) man, have you not seen a person of such height and complexion going by this path?' He said: 'I have. Go by this path.' They pursued him. He entered the house of a washerman in a certain market-town. He told him what had happened. The pursuit officers began to search the market-town. The washerman wrapped him in a bundle of cloth, placed him on a donkey, and took him out of the market-town. Having brought him to a bathhouse, he released him. Rising up, looking in the four directions, he fled. There too he was seen by another man, who reported to the pursuit officers: 'Sirs, the person you are looking for has gone by this path. Go quickly!' They set out. He entered the house of a leather-worker in another village. He told him what had happened. The leather-worker said: 'Put shoes on with the backs facing front.' He said: 'I have never made such shoes before.' He spoke a verse:

body.text: tenāsau carmakāraḥ śikṣitaḥ; carmakāreṇa tādṛśyau upānahau kṛte; kuḍyaparikṣipto 'sau karvaṭakaḥ; sa tena upānahau prāvṛtya upacchidreṇa niṣpalāyitaḥ; cārakapuruṣāḥ upānahā anusṛtya karvaṭakam anvāhiṇḍante; so 'pi niṣpalāyamānaḥ udakaṃ praviṣṭaḥ, nāgair nāgabhavanaṃ praveśitaḥ; rājñā śravaparamparayā śrutaṃ yathā asau nāgair nāgabhavanaṃ praveśitaḥ iti; rājñā amātyānām ājñā dattā: bhavanto ye madviṣayanivāsinaḥ āhituṇḍikāḥ, te sarve matsakāśe āneyāḥ iti; taiḥ sarve viṣayanivāsinaḥ āhituṇḍikāḥ rājñaḥ upanītāḥ; rājñā teṣām ājñā dattā: bhavanto gacchata; amuṣmin nāgabhavane nāgam uddharata iti; evaṃ deveti sarve āhituṇḍikāḥ rājñaḥ pratiśrutya tannāgabhavanaṃ gatāḥ; anyatarasyāṃ cāṭavyāṃ piṅgalo nāma yakṣo māṃsarudhirabhakṣaḥ; tasya bhayāt śvāpadā api tam aṭavīṃ parityajanti; kim uta manuṣyāḥ sā piṅgalāṭavīti prakāśā (
body.translated_text: He instructed that leather-worker. The leather-worker made such sandals. That market-town was surrounded by a wall. Putting on the sandals, he escaped through a gap in the wall. The pursuit officers, following the sandal-tracks, wandered about the market-town. He, still fleeing, entered the water and was taken by the <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings) into their <s>Nāga</s> realm. The king heard through a chain of reports that he had been taken by the <s>Nāgas</s> into the <s>Nāga</s> realm. The king gave a command to his ministers: 'Sirs, bring to me all the snake-charmers dwelling in my domain.' They brought all the snake-charmers of the domain before the king. The king gave them a command: 'Sirs, go and extract the <s>Nāga</s> from that <s>Nāga</s> realm.' 'Yes, Your Majesty' — all the snake-charmers, having assented to the king, went to that <s>Nāga</s> realm. In a certain forest there was a <s>yakṣa</s> named <s>Piṅgala</s>, a devourer of flesh and blood. Out of fear of him, even wild beasts abandoned that forest — how much more so humans! That forest became known as the '<s>Piṅgala</s> Forest.' (

body.text: santrastaḥ piṅgalāṭavyāṃ chorito na śaktas tām atikrāmayituṃ; nāgāḥ saṃjalpaṃ kurvanti: na śobhanam asmābhiḥ kṛtaṃ yad asau piṅgalāṭavīṃ nātikrāmitaḥ; so 'pi piṅgalena yakṣeṇa praghātyate; vayaṃ ca tadartham abhidrutāḥ; katham atra pratipattavyam iti; sa nāgarājaḥ kathayati: etam artham āhituṇḍikānāṃ nivedayāmaḥ iti; tair āhituṇḍikānāṃ samākhyātaṃ: bhavanto yadarthaṃ vayam ākulīkriyāmahe, so 'smābhir arthataḥ praghātita eva, yat piṅgalāṭavyāṃ samutsṛṣṭaḥ iti; āhituṇḍikaiḥ rājña etat prakaraṇaṃ samākhyātaṃ; rājā kathayati: yady apy evaṃ tathāpi samanveṣyatām iti; sa piṅgalāṭavyām itaś cāmutaś ca paribhramitum ārabdhaḥ; piṅgalaś ca yakṣaḥ anyatamasmin pradeśe kukkuraiḥ parivṛtas tiṣṭhati; tenāsau kukkuraiś ca dūrata eva dṛṣṭaḥ; sa saṃlakṣayati: kiṃ mamānena mṛtapravṛttiḥ śrutā? body.translated_text: , terrified, it was left in the <s>Piṅgala</s> Forest, unable to cross beyond it. The <s>Nāgas</s> conferred among themselves: 'It was not well done by us that he was not helped to cross the <s>Piṅgala</s> Forest. He will be slain by <s>Piṅgala</s> the <s>yakṣa</s>, and we shall be pursued on that account. How should we act?' The <s>Nāga</s> king said: 'Let us report this matter to the snake-charmers.' They told the snake-charmers: 'Sirs, the one for whose sake we are being harassed has been effectively killed by us, since he was abandoned in the <s>Piṅgala</s> Forest.' The snake-charmers reported this matter to the king. The king said: 'Even so, search for him.' He began wandering here and there in the <s>Piṅgala</s> Forest. <s>Piṅgala</s> the <s>yakṣa</s> was standing in a certain place surrounded by dogs. He saw the man and the dogs from afar. He thought: 'Has the report of my intent to kill reached him, that he has entered here?' He released his dogs upon him. Fleeing, the man climbed a tree. The dogs and <s>Piṅgala</s> stood at the base of the tree. <s>Piṅgala</s> said: 'Good man, have you not heard that in the <s>Piṅgala</s> Forest there dwells a non-human being named <s>Piṅgala</s>, and that whoever enters there, he slays? Your time has come. Come down.' He said: 'As long as I am alive, I shall stay.' <s>Piṅgala</s> the <s>yakṣa</s>, having tied a lasso, stood there insistently. The man began to shake the tree. He threw his garment upon the <s>yakṣa</s>. The dogs thought: 'That very man has fallen.' Having devoured <s>Piṅgala</s> the <s>yakṣa</s>, they departed. He climbed down slowly from the tree and departed. Wandering here and there, he thought: 'My maternal uncle has gone forth among the <s>ṛṣis</s> (sages). I shall go to him.' That <s>ṛṣi</s> had a garden on a certain mountain, rich in roots, flowers, fruits, and water, adorned with thickets of various trees, resounding with the cries of various birds. Gradually, through a chain of reports, he approached that <s>ṛṣi</s>. Having declared his kinship, he stayed. There too the pursuit officers searched for him. They began to seize him. He threw himself from a mountain precipice. While falling, a certain man grabbed him by the topknot. The topknot was torn off. He fell. They thought: 'He is dead. Let us go.' Taking the topknot, they went to the king and said: (

body.translated_text: and, going to <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, stationed himself in the royal park. The park-keepers saw him and were utterly astonished. Going swiftly, they reported to King <s>Sūryanemi</s>: 'Your Majesty, a woman endowed with such beauty and youth is standing in the park.' He gave the command: 'Bring her.' She was conducted into the royal household with great splendor. King <s>Sūryanemi</s> became exceedingly enamored of her. Then, having found the right moment, she killed him in private. Reversing the spell, he became a man again. Then, tying on the royal fillet himself and informing the minister <s>Goniṣāda</s>, he was established in the kingdom. A deity spoke a verse:

children.text: nāsau hato yaya śiro na chinnaṃ
children.translated_text: He is not slain whose head is not cut off;
he rises again and performs his deeds. /
Truly slain is he who is slain by the one slain by words —
as the son of <s>Sarjara</s> was slain by the Poet. //

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau sūryanemī rājā sarjarasya rājñaḥ putraḥ eṣa eva sa devadattaḥ tena kālena tena samayena; yo 'sau kaviḥ kaivartadārakaḥ aham eva saḥ tena kālena tena samayena; tadāpy eṣa mama vairaprasaktaḥ; etarhy apy eṣa mama vairaprasaktaḥ; bhūyo 'pi yathaiṣa mama vairānubaddhas tac chrūyatām
body.translated_text: What do you think, monks? He who was King <s>Sūryanemi</s>, the son of King <s>Sarjara</s> — that is none other than <s>Devadatta</s> at that time, in that era. He who was the Poet, the Fisherman's Son — that was I myself at that time, in that era. Even then he was bound to me by enmity; now too he is bound to me by enmity. And listen further to how he is bound to me by enmity.

He said: 'I do not have that much money.' He said: 'Give whatever you have.' He took it. The other jeweler heard of this. Filled with resentment, he approached the second one: 'I brought that to my house first. I set a price for it. Why do you take it?' Between them, hostility arose.
  What do you think, monks? He who was the jeweler who set a low price for the jewel-vessel — he is none other than <s>Devadatta</s> at that time, in that era. He who was the second jeweler who set an abundant price — that was I myself at that time, in that era. Even then, hostility arose between us. And again, how hostility arose between us — listen to that.

In the past, monks, in a certain market-town, two jewelers lived; they shared a street and a house. At that time, a certain merchant whose wealth had been exhausted took a jewel-vessel and arrived at that market-town. Having rested from the fatigue of the journey, he approached one of the jewelers and said: 'Appraise this jewel-vessel.' That one set a low price. He said: 'Why do you say such a thing? Even though I have fallen from prosperity, I have not lost my discernment. I myself know its value.' He left that one's presence (

body.translated_text: in the course of time, his wife became pregnant. After eight or nine months, she gave birth — a boy was born. His wife then passed away. He thought: 'Who will raise the boy? I shall bring another.' He brought another wife. He sported, enjoyed himself, and amused himself with her. She too bore a son. She too passed away. The householder thought: 'If I bring another, she too will die. I shall arrange a marriage for my elder son.' He arranged a marriage for his elder son. Many sons and daughters were born to him. His wife said: 'Noble husband, who is this boy to you?' He said: 'My younger brother.' She said: 'Sir, you have many sons; he is but one. An equal share of the household property must be given to these and to him.' He said: 'Dear one, this is the way of the world.' She said: 'If so, have him killed.' Indeed, for one indulging in sensual pleasures, there is no evil deed that cannot be done. Under the pretext of gathering flowers and fruits, he was led to the forest and killed. (

children.translated_text: In the past, monks, in a certain market-town, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> lived. He brought a wife from a family of equal status. He sported, enjoyed himself, and amused himself with her. While he was sporting, enjoying himself, and amusing himself, his wife became pregnant. After eight or nine months, she gave birth — a girl was born, beautiful, good-looking, and graceful. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> thought: 'Whichever <s>brāhmaṇa</s> enters my house today seeking alms, to him I shall give this maiden as an alms-gift.' Then a certain young <s>brāhmaṇa</s> student entered his house seeking alms: 'Blessings! Give alms.' The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> called him and said: 'Young man, this is my daughter. I have given her to you as a maiden-alms.' He said: 'I do not accept today. I shall accept at an auspicious moment and day.' He departed. Then another young <s>brāhmaṇa</s> student entered his house seeking alms: 'Blessings! Give alms.' The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> called him and said: 'Young man, this is my daughter. I have given her to you as a maiden-alms.' He said: 'Another young student entered here seeking alms before me. Why was she not given to him?' He said: 'He says the constellation is inauspicious.' He said: 'If so, let it be reserved.' The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> said: 'And why do you not examine the constellation?' He spoke a verse:

children.text: nakṣatraṃ bhadrakaṃ sarvaṃ sarve kalyāṇakā dināḥ /
children.translated_text: Every constellation is auspicious, and all days are favorable;
when tasks have arisen, all this is propitious. //
Men who are devoted to counting constellations miss their opportunities;

children.text: artho hy arthasya nakṣatraṃ kiṃ kāryaṃ jyotibhiḥ punaḥ //
children.translated_text: opportunity itself is the constellation of opportunity — what further need is there for stars? //

body.text: sa pratigṛhītvā prakrāntaḥ
body.translated_text: Having accepted her, he departed.

children.text: buddho bhagavān rājagṛhe viharati veṇuvane kalandakanivāpe; tena khalu samayena yo 'sau rājñaḥ ajātaśatroḥ dhanapālako nāma duṣṭanāgaḥ pratidinam āvāsān niṣkrāmyamāṇo mahājanavipraghātaṃ karoti; rājagṛhanivāsinā janakāyena rājā ajātaśatrur vijñaptaḥ: deva dhanapālako duṣṭanāgaḥ pratidinam āvāsān niṣkrāmyamāṇo rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu mahājanavipraghātaṃ karoti; tad arhati devaḥ hastidamakānām ājñāṃ dātuṃ yathā na pratidinaṃ niṣkāsayanti; śvo niṣkrāmyate iti ca ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kārayitum iti; rājā kathayati evaṃ bhavatu; gacchata iti; rājñā amātyānām ājñā dattā: āhūyantāṃ bhavanto hastidamakāḥ iti; tair hastidamakā āhūtāḥ; rājā kathayati: bhavanto rājagṛhanivāsinā janakāyena abhihito 'smi dhanapālako duṣṭanāgaḥ pratidinam āvāsān niṣkrāmyamāṇo rathyāvīthīcatvaraśṛṅgāṭakeṣu mahājanavipraghātaṃ karoti; tad arhati devaḥ hastidamakānām ājñāṃ dātuṃ yathā na pratidinaṃ niṣkāsayanti; śvo niṣkrāmyate iti ca ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kārayitum iti; tad yuṣmābhir na pratidinaṃ niṣkrāmayitavyaḥ; śvo niṣkrāmyate iti ca ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kārayitavyam iti; hastidamakāḥ rājñaḥ ajātaśatroḥ pratiśrutya pādayor nipatya prakrāntāḥ (

The <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s> was dwelling at <s>Rājagṛha</s> in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s>. At that time, King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>'s vicious elephant named <s>Dhanapālaka</s>, being let out from its stable each day, caused great destruction of people. The populace dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s> petitioned King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: 'Your Majesty, the vicious elephant <s>Dhanapālaka</s>, being let out from its stable each day, causes great destruction of people in the streets, lanes, squares, and crossroads. May Your Majesty please give orders to the elephant-tamers not to let it out each day, and to have a bell-proclamation made that it will be let out the next day.' The king said: 'So be it. Go.' The king gave orders to his ministers: 'Summon the elephant-tamers.' They summoned the elephant-tamers. The king said: 'Sirs, the populace dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s> has told me: "The vicious elephant <s>Dhanapālaka</s>, being let out from its stable each day, causes great destruction of people in the streets, lanes, squares, and crossroads. May Your Majesty please give orders to the elephant-tamers not to let it out each day, and to have a bell-proclamation made that it will be let out the next day." Therefore, you must not let it out each day, and a bell-proclamation must be made that it will be let out the next day.' The elephant-tamers, having assented to King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>, bowed at his feet and departed. (

body.translated_text: <s>Devadatta</s>'s attempt to kill the <s>Buddha</s> by means of the elephant <s>Dhanapālaka</s>

body.text: rājagṛhe cānyataro gṛhapatiḥ āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogaḥ; tena buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena upanimantritaḥ; devadattena śrutaṃ yathā amukena gṛhapatinā buddhapramuko bhikṣusaṃghaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ iti; tena hastidamakasya śatasahasro muktāhāro dattaḥ; uktaś ca: amukena gṛhapatinā śramaṇo gautamaḥ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktena upanimantritaḥ; tat tvayā dhanapālako hastināgaḥ utsraṣṭavyaḥ iti; sa kathayati: ārya evaṃ bhavatu; kiṃtu yathā vā tathā vā devam avalokaya iti; tato devadatto yena rājā ajātaśatrus tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya rājānam ajātaśatrum idam avocat: śaktas tvaṃ māṃ buddhatve na pratiṣṭhāpayitum;
body.translated_text: Now in <s>Rājagṛha</s> there was a certain householder who was wealthy, of great riches, and of great possessions. He had invited the <s>Buddha</s>-led community of monks for a meal at his home the next day. <s>Devadatta</s> heard that such-and-such a householder had invited the <s>Buddha</s>-led community of monks for a meal at his home the next day. He gave the elephant-tamer a pearl necklace worth a hundred thousand [coins] and told him: 'Such-and-such a householder has invited the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> together with his community of disciples for a meal at his home tomorrow. You must release the bull-elephant <s>Dhanapālaka</s>.' He said: 'Noble sir, so be it. But in any case, please look to the king.' Then <s>Devadatta</s> approached King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>. Having approached, he said this to King <s>Ajātaśatru</s>: 'Were you unable to establish me in Buddhahood?

body.text: api tu tvaṃ pitaraṃ jīvitād vyaparopya rājye pratiṣṭhapitaḥ; aham api śramaṇaṃ gautamaṃ praghātya sarvajñatvaṃ karomi; dhanapālaṃ hastināgam utsṛja iti; ajātaśatruḥ kathayati: na tvayā śrutam? adāntadamakā buddhā bhagavantaḥ iti; sa kathayati: yady adāntadamakāḥ syuḥ aham eva tāvad anena dāntaḥ syām iti; sa taṃ yathā vā tathā vā avalokya hastidamakānāṃ sakāśam upasaṃkramya kathayati: niveditaṃ mayā devasya; tad yuṣmābhiḥ śvo dhanapālako hastināgaḥ utsraṣṭavyaḥ iti; tato hastidamakaiḥ rājagṛhe ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ kāritaṃ: śṛṇvantu bhavanto rājagṛhanivāsinaḥ paurāḥ, śvo hastināgo mucyate; tad yuṣmābhiḥ śvaḥ sarvaprayatnena ātmarakṣā kartavyā iti; gṛhapatiḥ śrutvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ: īdṛśo 'haṃ mandabhāgyaḥ; mayā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ śvo 'ntargṛhe bhaktenopanimantritaḥ; dhanapālakaś ca duṣṭanāgaḥ śvo mucyate; kathaṃ mayā buddhapramukho bhikṣusaṃghaḥ bhojayitavyaḥ iti; punaḥ saṃlakṣayati: sādhayāmi pākaṃ; tatraiva nītvā bhagavantaṃ bhojayāmi iti; sa śuci praṇītaṃ khādanīyabhojanīyaṃ sādhayitvā kālyam evotthāya bhagavataḥ sakāśaṃ gataḥ: bhagavan rājagṛhe ghaṇṭāvaghoṣaṇaṃ śvo dhanapālako hastināgo mucyate; yuṣmābhiḥ śaktitaḥ ātmarakṣā kartavyā iti; tad bhagavatā rājagṛhaṃ na praveṣṭavyam; aham ihaiva annapānam ānayāmi iti; bhagavān kathayati: alpotsukas tvaṃ gṛhapate bhava; annapānaṃ sajjīkuru; vigataṃ tathāgatasya nāgabhayaṃ; praviśāmy ahaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ iti; tato 'sau gṛhapatir āttamanāttamanāḥ svagṛhaṃ gataḥ; annapānaṃ (

) samanvāhṛtya āsanādi prajñapya bhagavantam udīkṣamāṇaḥ avasthitaḥ; atha bhagavān pūrvāhṇe nivāsya pātracīvaram ādāya paṃcabhir bhikṣuśataiḥ sārdhaṃ rājagṛhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ; dhanapālako hastināgaḥ utsṛṣṭaḥ; adrākṣīd dhanapālako hastināgo bhagavantaṃ dūrād eva; dṛṣṭvā ca punar bhrūkuṭiṃ kṛtvā nādaṃ ca muktvā yena bhagavāṃs tena sabalam ājavena prādhāvat

body.text: bhagavān āha: nīco 'si devadatta; pravādaṃ tvaṃ pravadasi daśabalabalinaṃ mām agaṇayitvā; paśyedānīṃ tu balaṃ daśabalabalinaḥ adbhutasya iti; tato bhagavatā dakṣiṇe karatale paṃca siṃhāḥ kesariṇaḥ paṭṭadhāriṇo nirmitāḥ; sa teṣāṃ gandhaṃ ghrātvā mūtrapuriṣam utsṛjan niṣpalāyitum ārabdhaḥ; bhagavatā sarvā diśaḥ ādīptāḥ pradīptāḥ saṃprajvalitāḥ ekajvālībhūtā adhimuktāḥ sthāpayitvā

tvaṃ tāvad bhadramukha pūrvakeṇa duścaritena pratyavarāyāṃ tiryagyonāv utpannaḥ; sa tvam etarhi paraprāṇaharaḥ paraprāṇoparodhena parituṣyasi; itaś cyutasya te kā gatir bhaviṣyasi? kā upapattiḥ ko 'bhisaṃparāyaḥ iti hi bhadramukha sarvasaṃskārā anityāḥ; sarvadharmāḥ anātmānaḥ; śāntaṃ nirvāṇaṃ; mamāntike cittam abhiprasādya adyaiva tiryagyoniṃ virāgayiṣyasi; ity uktvā yena tasya gṛhapater niveśanaṃ tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; upasaṃkramya prajñapta evāsane niṣaṇṇaḥ; dhanapālako 'pi bhagavantaṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ samanubaddhaḥ; bhagavān praviṣṭaḥ; sa dvāramūle sthitaḥ; bhagavantam apaśyan gṛhaṃ bhaṅktum ārabdhaḥ; bhagavatā tad gṛhaṃ sphaṭikamayaṃ nirmitaṃ yatrānāvṛtaṃ buddhabimbaṃ paśyati; sa bhagavnataṃ dṛṣṭvā na bhaṅktum ārabdhaḥ; bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃghaḥ bhuktvā dakṣiṇādeśanāṃ kṛtvā prakrāntaḥ; sa bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nubaddha eva; etat prakaraṇam amātyaiḥ rājño niveditam:; ajātaśatruṇā devadatto 'bhihitaḥ: tvayā mama anarthaḥ kṛtaḥ; taṃ hastinam āgamya sīmāntarā rājānaḥ māṃ nābhidravanti; so 'pi tvayā vimadīkṛtaḥ iti; sa tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ; rājñā amātyānām ājñā dattā; yadā bhagavān nirgato bhavati tadā bhavadbhir dhanapālaḥ hastināgo dvāraṃ badhvā sthāpayitavyaḥ yathā bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ na nirgacchati iti; amātyai api hastidamakānām ājñā dattā dhanapālakaṃ hastināgaṃ dvāraṃ badhvā sthāpayata yathā bhagavataḥ pṛṣṭhato na nirgacchati iti; sa bhagavantam apaśyan pādena śuṇḍām avaṣṭabhya kālagataḥ; cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ; dharmatā khalu devaputrasya vā devakanyāyā vā aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante: kutaś cyutaḥ kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇā iti; sa paśyati nāgebhyaś (
SBV II 190

) cyutaḥ; praṇīteṣu cāturmahārājikeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ; bhagavato 'ntike cittam abhiprasādya iti
  atha nāgapūrviṇo devaputrasyaitad bahavat: na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāya upasaṃkrameyaṃ; yannv aham aparyuṣitaparivāsa eva bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrameyam iti; atha

nāgapūrvī devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍaladharo hārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātraḥ tām eva rātriṃ divyānām utpalapadmakumudapuṇḍarīkamāndārakāṇāṃ puṣpāṇām utsaṃgaṃ pūrayitvā sarvaṃ veṇuvanaṃ kalandakanivāpam udāreṇāvabhāsenāvabhāsya bhagavataṃ puṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya; tataḥ asya bhagavatā āśayānuśayaṃ dhātuṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī dharmadeśanā kṛtā yāṃ śrutvā nāgapūrviṇā devaputreṇa viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhitvā srotaāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtaṃ; sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā kṛtaṃ; na devatābhiḥ; neṣṭena svajanabandhuvargeṇa; na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇaiḥ yad bhagavatā asmākaṃ kṛtam; ucchoṣitā rudhirāśrusamudrāḥ; laṃghitā asthiparvatāḥ pihitāny apāyadvārāṇi vivṛtāni svargamokṣadvārāṇi; pratiṣṭhāpitāḥ smo devamanuṣyeṣu āha ca

avanamya tataḥ pralambahāraḥ
