) he raises up the mind-made body from that body and creates another body — material, mind-made, complete, with faculties unimpaired. Just as a man were to draw a snake from its basket. A man with eyes, having seen it, would know: 'This is the basket; this is the snake; he draws the snake from the basket.' Even so, he raises up the mind-made body from that body and creates another body — material, mind-made, complete, with faculties unimpaired. Just as a man were to draw a sword from its scabbard. A man with eyes, having seen it, would know: 'This is the scabbard; this is the sword; he draws the sword from the scabbard.' Even so, he raises up the mind-made body from that body and creates another body — material, mind-made, complete, with faculties unimpaired.
  80. With his mind thus composed — purified, cleansed, without blemish, free from defilements, straight, workable, steady, having attained imperturbability — he directs his mind toward the knowledge and direct realization of the sphere of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhi</s>). He experiences manifold supernatural powers: having been one, he becomes many; having been many, he becomes one. He experiences, through knowledge and vision, appearing and disappearing. He passes through walls, through mountains, through ramparts, unhindered, with his body, as if through space. He dives in and out of the earth as if in water. He walks on water without breaking the surface, as if on earth. He traverses the sky cross-legged, like a winged bird. He touches and strokes with his hand these sun and moon, so mighty and powerful. He exercises mastery over the body as far as the <s>Brahma</s>-world. Just as a skilled goldsmith or goldsmith's apprentice, knowing a well-prepared piece of gold, whatever ornamental shape he wishes to produce — whether a plate, an earring, a necklace, a hand-ornament, a foot-ornament, a finger-ring, or a golden garland — he quickly and easily produces that shape. Even so, with his mind thus composed, purified, cleansed, without blemish, free from defilements, straight, workable, steady, having attained imperturbability — he directs his mind toward the knowledge and direct realization of the sphere of supernatural power. But these beings, endowed with bodily good conduct, verbal and mental good conduct, who do not revile the noble ones, who hold right views, who undertake actions based on the cause of right-view <s>karma</s> — by reason of that cause and condition, at the breaking up of the body, they are reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, among the gods.' Just as a person with good eyesight, standing at a crossroads, were to see a great multitude of people coming and going, standing and sitting — thus observing their various activities — even so, with his mind thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, free from blemish, free from defilements, pliant, workable, steady, and having attained imperturbability, he directs and inclines his mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge of the passing away and rebirth of beings. With the divine eye, purified and surpassing the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn — fair and foul, high and low, going to good destinations and bad destinations, faring according to their deeds — and he knows them as they truly are: 'These beings, endowed with bodily misconduct, verbal and mental misconduct, who revile the noble ones, who hold wrong views, who undertake actions based on the cause of wrong-view <s>karma</s> — by reason of that cause and condition, at the breaking up of the body, after death, they are reborn in the lower realms, in bad destinations, in the downfall, in hell. But these beings, endowed with bodily good conduct, verbal and mental good conduct, who do not revile the noble ones, who hold right views, who undertake actions based on the cause of right-view <s>karma</s> — by reason of that cause and condition, at the breaking up of the body, they are reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world, among the gods.'
  'What do you think, Great King? Is not the fruit of the ascetic life visible in this world thus shown by me?' 'Truly, Venerable Sir. The fruit of the ascetic life visible in this world has thus been shown by the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'
  85. With his mind thus concentrated, purified, cleansed, free from blemish, free from defilements, pliant, workable, steady, and having attained imperturbability, he directs and inclines his mind toward the direct realization of the knowledge of the destruction of the defilements. He knows as it truly is: 'This is suffering' — the Noble Truth. 'This is the origin of suffering; this is the cessation of suffering; this is the path leading to the cessation of suffering' — the Noble Truth — he knows it as it truly is. For one who knows thus, who sees thus, the mind is liberated from the defilement of sensual desire; from the defilement of existence; from the defilement of ignorance, the mind is liberated. When liberated, there is the knowledge-and-vision that it is liberated: 'Birth is exhausted for me; the holy life has been lived; what was to be done has been done; I know there is no more of this state of existence.' Just as there might be a cesspit near a village or market-town, more than a man's height in depth, and a certain man were submerged in it — head, hands, and feet — and a certain other man were to come along, one who for a long time had wished his welfare, wished his benefit, wished his happiness, wished his safety and security. That man would walk around the cesspit on all sides, thinking: 'Might I find some spot on this man's body not smeared with filth by which I could grab him and pull him out?' Walking around on all sides, he finds no spot on that man's body not smeared with filth — not even a spot the size of a palm — by which he could grab him and pull him out. body.translated_text: He let out a great cry. Hearing it, the <s>Śākyas</s> came running: '<s>Devadatta</s> has entered the <s>Bodhisattva</s>'s inner palace and is committing an outrage against his wife!' They saw him fallen in the pleasure-pond. They began to deliberate: 'Let us kill him.' Then they said again: 'If we kill him, we ourselves will be killed. For he has already been declared by the <s>Bhagavān</s> thus: "<s>Devadatta</s> is bound for a woeful state, bound for hell, destined for an aeon there, incurable."' So they released him. He escaped through a gap in the wall. His garment was torn in two pieces. He considered: 'Very well. By this same fashion, my disciples shall wear their lower garment.'

body.text: ) vāsmākaṃ bhartā syād bodhisatvo veti; tatas tayāvamānito 'ntaḥpurān nirgataḥ; śākyair ukto gaccha bhagavantaṃ kṣamaya; yadi te bhagavān kṣamati paścād rājyaṃ kārayiṣyasīti; sa vatsanābhasya paramatīkṣṇasya viṣasya nakhān pūrayitvā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ; yadi me śramaṇaḥ gautamaḥ kṣamiṣyatīti evaṃ kuśalaṃ; nocet kṣamiṣyati tatraivāsya pādayor nipatito nakhaviṣapūrṇau pādau kariṣyāmīti viditvā bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya bhagavantam idam avocat: kṣamasva bhagavann iti; bhagavān saṃlakṣayati: kīdṛśena cittenāyaṃ mām upasaṃkrānta iti; paśyati vadhacittena; tato bhagavān pādatalād yāvaj jānumaṇḍalam upādāya sphaṭikamayau pādau nirmāya tūṣṇīm avasthitaḥ; sa bhagavataḥ pādau nakhair veddhum ārabdhaḥ; tasya nakhā bhagnāḥ; sa prativibhinnaḥ kathayati: tvāṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchāmi; yasmād uktaṃ tvayā: ye buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchanti na te gacchanti durgatim iti; yadi durgatiṃ gamiṣyāmi idaṃ te mṛṣā iti; abhydīrṇaparipūrṇāni hi karmāṇi śarīrasya patanaṃ nāpekṣante; sa jīvann evāvīcikābhir jvālābhir āliṅgito vikroṣṭum ārabdho dahye ānanda dahye ānandeti; athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kāruṇiko maitryātmakaḥ svajanavatsalaḥ; sa kathayati: ehi devadatta tathāgatam arhantaṃ buddhaṃ śaraṇaṃ gaccheti; tena duḥkhavedanābhibhūtena (
body.translated_text: ) or a <s>Bodhisattva</s> shall be our husband.' Then, humiliated by her, he departed from the inner palace. The <s>Śākyas</s> told him: 'Go and ask forgiveness from the <s>Bhagavān</s>. If the <s>Bhagavān</s> forgives you, afterward you shall exercise kingship.' He filled his fingernails with <s>vatsanābha</s>, an extremely potent poison, and approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, thinking: 'If the ascetic <s>Gautama</s> forgives me, well and good. If he does not forgive me, then right there, having fallen at his feet, I shall poison his feet with my poison-filled nails.' Having determined this, he fell at the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet and said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'Forgive me, <s>Bhagavān</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> observed: 'With what kind of mind has this one approached me?' He saw — with murderous intent. Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, from the soles of his feet up to his kneecaps, created feet made of crystal and remained silent. <s>Devadatta</s> began to try to pierce the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s feet with his nails. His nails broke. Rebuffed, he said: 'I go for refuge to you — since you have declared: "Those who go for refuge to the <s>Buddha</s> do not go to a bad destination." If I do go to a bad destination, then this declaration of yours is false.' For deeds that are fully ripened and complete do not wait for the falling of the body. While still alive, he was enveloped by the flames of <s>Avīci</s> and began to cry out: 'I am burning, <s>Ānanda</s>! I am burning, <s>Ānanda</s>!' Then the Venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, who was compassionate, whose nature was loving-kindness, who was affectionate toward his own kin — he said: 'Come, <s>Devadatta</s>, go for refuge to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>.' children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s> foretells that, on the expiration of a <s>kalpa</s> (aeon), <s>Devadatta</s> will become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, <s>Asthimān</s> by name

children.text: tatra bhagavān bhikṣūn āmantrayate sma: pratisaṃhṛtāni bhikṣavo devadattena kuśalamūlāni; kalpam avīcau mahānarake sthitvā pratyekaṃ bodhiṃ sākṣātkariṣyati; asthimān nāma pratyekabuddho bhaviṣyati; so 'bhisaṃbuddhamātraḥ piṇḍapātam ekānte sthāpayitvā hastau nirmardayan samanvāhariṣyati: kimartham ahaṃ dīrghakālaṃ saṃsāre saṃsṛtaḥ? iti; smanvāharan jñāsyati: janmani janmani mayā bhagavataḥ parākrāntaṃ bodhisatvabhūtasyāpi sarvajñeyavaśitāprāptasyāpi, tac ca lābhasatkārahetor iti; sa tam apy ekapiṇḍapātam aparibhujyoparivihāyasam abhyudgamya jvalanatapanavarṣaṇavidyotanaprātihāryāṇi kṛtvā nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvāsyatīti
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> addressed the monks: 'Monks, <s>Devadatta</s>'s wholesome roots have been withdrawn. Having remained in the <s>Avīci</s> great hell for an aeon, he will directly realize <s>Pratyeka</s> awakening. He will become a <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> named <s>Asthimān</s> ("Possessing Bones"). No sooner will he have attained perfect awakening than, having set aside his alms-food in a secluded place, rubbing his hands together, he will reflect: "Why have I wandered in <s>saṃsāra</s> for so long?" As he reflects, he will come to know: "In birth after birth, I acted against the <s>Bhagavān</s> — against him even as a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and against him even when he had attained mastery over all that is to be known — and that was for the sake of gain and honor." Then, without even eating that single meal of alms-food, he will rise into the sky above and, having performed the miraculous feats of blazing, heating, raining, and illuminating, he will pass into final <s>nirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element without remainder of clinging.'

  The Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said: 'You, <s>Devadatta</s>, say: "Iron mountains come, blazing, burning, flaming, a single mass of fire; they crush me like a sesame seed" — that is because you hurled a boulder from <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> mountain to kill the <s>Bhagavān</s>. This is the fruit of that deed.
  You say: "With double-edged saws, blazing, burning, flaming, a single mass of fire, my limbs and minor limbs are split apart" — that is because you split the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s community of disciples. This is the fruit of that deed.
  You say: "With iron hammers, blazing, burning, flaming, a single mass of fire, my head is crushed again and again" — that is because you struck and killed the <s>Arhat</s> nun <s>Utpalavarṇā</s> with a blow from a bed-frame. This is the fruit of that deed.
  You say: "Elephants come from the four directions; they grind me like flour" — that is because you released the bull-elephant <s>Dhanapālaka</s> to kill the <s>Bhagavān</s>. This is the fruit of that deed.

It was the practice of <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s> to tour the hells from time to time. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> said this to the Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, <s>Devadatta</s> has been prophesied by the <s>Bhagavān</s> for <s>Pratyeka</s> awakening. Come, let the two of us go to the <s>Avīci</s> great hell and console <s>Devadatta</s>.' Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> (

athāyuṣmantau śāriputramahāmaudgalyāyanau yena kokālikaprabhṛtyayas tenopasaṃkrāntau; yāvat kokālikasya hi jihvā halaśatena dhāryate; brahmaṇā sabhāṃpatinā kokālika ucyate; kokālikābhiprasādya śāriputramaudgalyāyanayor bhikṣvor antike cittaṃ peśalayoḥ sabrahmacāribhir vatsalayor iti; evam ukto kokālika āyuṣmantau śāriputramahāmaudgalyāyanau dṛṣṭvā kathayati: ihāpy etau pāpecchāv āgatāv iti; vākpravyāharaṇakālasamanantaram eva kokālikasya halasahareṇa jihvā pāṭayitum ārabdhā; athāyuṣmantau śāriputramahāmaudgalyāyanāv akaraṇīyā hy ete iti viditvā prakrāntau; yena pūrānaḥ kāśyapas tenopasaṃkrāntau
  atha pūraṇaḥ kāśyapa āyuṣmantoḥ śāriputramahāmaudgalyāyanayoḥ pādayor nipatya kathayati: ārya śāriputra mayā mithyādharmadeśanayā mahājanakāyo vipralabdhaḥ; tasya me karmaṇo vipākena jihvāyāṃ paṃca halaśatāni vahanti; yathā yathā ca śrāvakā stūpakārān kurvanti tathā tathā tīvrataravedanāṃ vedayāmi; tad arhasi madīyām avasthāṃ teṣāṃ nivedya nivārayituṃ: mā tasya stūpakāraṃ kariṣyatheti; tatheti pratijñāya āyuṣmantau śāriputramahāmaudgalyāyanau narakacārikāṃ (
body.translated_text:
Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> approached <s>Kokālika</s> and the others. As for <s>Kokālika</s>, his tongue was held by a hundred plowshares. <s>Brahmā Sahāṃpati</s> had once said to <s>Kokālika</s>: '<s>Kokālika</s>, generate faith in the presence of the monks <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Maudgalyāyana</s>, who are gentle and affectionate toward their fellow practitioners.' Thus addressed, <s>Kokālika</s>, seeing the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, said: 'These two evil-minded ones have come even here!' The very instant he uttered these words, <s>Kokālika</s>'s tongue began to be split by a thousand plowshares. Then the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, knowing 'These are beyond help,' departed. They approached <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>.
  Then <s>Pūraṇa Kāśyapa</s>, having fallen at the feet of the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, said: 'Noble <s>Śāriputra</s>, through my false teaching of the <s>Dharma</s>, a great multitude of people was deceived by me. As the fruit of that deed, five hundred plowshares run through my tongue. And as my disciples build <s>stūpas</s> in my honor, the more intensely painful are the sensations I experience. Please inform them of my condition and restrain them: "Do not build a <s>stūpa</s> for him!"' Having assented, the Venerable <s>Śāriputra</s> and <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, having completed their tour of the hells, (

children.translated_text: ) heard and seized him: 'Sirs, this donkey has eaten all this king's bean-field! Let us punish him.' They cut off his ears, tied a mortar around his neck, and released him. Wandering here and there, he was seen by the bull. The bull addressed him with a verse:

children.text: sādhu gītaṃ suṣṭhu gītaṃ prāptaṃ gītasya tat phalam /
children.translated_text: Well sung! Finely sung! The fruit of your singing has been obtained —
since by your singing you have become one bereft of ears! //

In the past, monks, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, while in an indeterminate state of existence among cattle, was born as a bull. By night he would go out from the city and graze in the king's bean-field. By day he stayed in the city. Then a donkey approached him and said: 'Uncle, you are well-fleshed and well-blooded. Yet I never see you grazing.' He said: 'Nephew, I graze by night in the king's bean-field.' The donkey said: 'Uncle, I too shall graze with you.' He said: 'Nephew, you are a loud-mouth — you will cause trouble.' The donkey said: 'Uncle, I'll go — I won't cause any trouble.' The two of them broke through the fence and entered the king's bean-field. The donkey remained silent as long as he was eating his fill. Then he said: 'Uncle, let me sing a little!' The bull said: 'Wait a moment until I get out. After that, do as you please.' Having said this, he fled. The donkey began to bray. The king's men (

children.translated_text: ) came to ruin. Listen further to how he disregarded my words and by this came to ruin.'

Thus indeed it befalls one who does not guard his speech. /
  Wander now, earless one, adorned with a mortar! //
The donkey too replied with a verse:
  Be silent, you broken-toothed one! Be silent, you aged bull! /
  Three men with sticks are searching for you too, right here! //
The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, monks? He who was the bull — that was I myself at that time, in that era. He who was the donkey — that is this very <s>Devadatta</s> at that time, in that era. Even then he disregarded my words and by this [folly] (

body.text:
The story of the bull and the jackal
(concerning a previous life of the Buddha and Devadatta)
body.translated_text:
The story of the bull and the jackal
(concerning a previous life of the <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Devadatta</s>)

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatasmin karvaṭake gṛhapatiḥ prativasati; tasya valīvardo lakṣaṇasaṃpannaḥ; tenāsau śramaṇabrāhmaṇān svajanān anāthakṛpaṇavanīpakān bhojayitvā yatheṣṭapracārī utsṛṣṭaḥ; so 'pareṇa samayena itaś cāmutaś ca paribhraman kaluṣe magno 'vasthitaḥ; tena sūryāstaṃgamanakālasamaye śrutaṃ; samanveṣamāṇas tasya sakāśaṃ (
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in a certain village, a householder dwelt. He had a bull endowed with auspicious marks. Having fed <s>śramaṇas</s>, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, his own relatives, and the destitute, poor, and homeless with offerings, he set the bull free to roam as it pleased. At a later time, the bull, wandering here and there, became stuck in a muddy pool. The householder heard of this at the time of sunset. Having searched, he went to it. (

) gataḥ; sa saṃlakṣayati: na śaknomi aham adhunā samuddhartuṃ; śvaḥ prabhāte samuddhariṣyāmīti; vṛṣaḥ kathayati: mama purastāt pāśaṃ sthāpayitvā gaccha; yadi śṛgāla āgamiṣyati tasyāhaṃ śṛṅge pāśaṃ kṣepsyāmīti; sa tasya
body.translated_text: ) He reflected: 'I am unable to pull it out now. I shall pull it out tomorrow at dawn.' The bull said: 'Place a snare in front of me and go. If a jackal comes, I shall throw the noose around his horns.' Having placed a snare in front of it,

body.text:
purastāt pāśaṃ kṣiptvā prakrāntaḥ; yāvad rātrau śṛgāla āgataḥ; sa kathayati: ko 'yaṃ bisāny utkhanati puṇḍarīkāni ceti; vṛṣaḥ kathayati: ahaṃ nimagnas tiṣṭhāmīti; śṛgālaḥ saṃlakṣayati: bhakṣyo me pratyupasthita iti; sa tam abhidravitum ārabdhaḥ; vṛṣaḥ kathayati: gaccha tvam asmāt pradeśān mā anayena vyasanam āpatsyasa iti; tathāpy asau nivāryamāno 'bhidravaty eva; sa vṛṣo gāthāṃ bhāṣate
  nāhaṃ bisāny utkhanāmi puṇḍarīkāni nāpy aham /
  saced bhakṣitukāmo 'si pṛṣṭhato gaccha bhakṣaya // iti /
śṛgālo bhakṣayāmīti pṛṣṭhato gataḥ; vṛṣeṇa śṛṅge pāśaḥ kṣiptaḥ; śṛgālo grīvāyāṃ baddhaḥ; ākāśe pralambhate; vṛṣo gāthāṃ bhāṣate
  kiṃ naṭo nartako vā tvam uta śobhitadārakaḥ /
  grāme vidarśyatāṃ śilpam araṇye nāsti dāyakaḥ // iti / (
body.translated_text:
he departed. During the night, a jackal came. He said: 'Who is this digging up lotus-stalks and lotuses?' The bull said: 'I am stuck and standing here.' The jackal reflected: 'A meal has presented itself to me!' He began to charge at the bull. The bull said: 'Go away from this place, lest you come to ruin through this folly!' Yet though warned, the jackal kept charging. The bull spoke a verse:
  'I am not digging lotus-stalks, nor am I gathering lotuses. /
  If you wish to eat, go behind me and eat!' //
The jackal went behind, saying 'I shall eat!' The bull threw the noose around his horns. The jackal was bound by the neck. He dangled in the air. The bull spoke a verse:
  'Are you a dancer, or an actor, or a boy dressed for display? /
  Show your skill in the village — in the forest there is no patron!' //
(

body.text: SBV II 267

)
śṛgālo 'pi gāthāṃ bhāṣate
  nāhaṃ naṭo nartako vā nāpi śobhitadārakaḥ /
  dattā śakeṇa me śreṇī brahmalokaṃ vrajāmy aham // iti / (
body.translated_text:
)
The jackal too spoke a verse:
  'I am neither a dancer, nor an actor, nor a boy dressed for display. /
  <s>Śakra</s> has given me a ladder — I am ascending to the <s>Brahma</s>-world!' //
(

body.text: MSV IV 243

)
bhūyo vṛṣo gāthām bhāṣate
  na śakro dadāti śreṇīṃ brahmalokaḥ kutas tava /
  baddho 'si kūṭapāśena na te paśyāmi jīvitam // iti /
kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavaḥ? yo 'sau vṛṣaḥ aham eva sa tena kālena tena samayena; yo 'sau śṛgāla eṣa eva sa devadattas tena kālena tena samayena; tadāpy eṣa mama vacanam avacanīkṛtyānayena vyasanam āpannaḥ; etarhy apy eṣa mama vacanam avacanīkṛtyānena vyasanam āpannaḥ
  bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: bhadanta devadatto bhagavato vacanam aśṛṇvann avīciparāyaṇaḥ saṃvṛtta iti; bhagavān āha: na bhikṣava etarhi yathā atīte 'py adhvani eṣa mama vikrośato vacanam aśṛṇvann avīciparāyaṇaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ; tac chrūyatām
body.translated_text:
)
The bull spoke another verse:
  '<s>Śakra</s> does not give ladders, and how would the <s>Brahma</s>-world be yours? /
  You are caught in a trap-snare — I see no life left for you!' //
What do you think, monks? He who was the bull — that was I myself at that time, in that era. He who was the jackal — that is this very <s>Devadatta</s> at that time, in that era. Even then he disregarded my words and by that folly came to ruin. Now too he has disregarded my words and by that has come to ruin.
  The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'Venerable Sir, <s>Devadatta</s>, not heeding the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s words, has become one destined for <s>Avīci</s> (hell).' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, monks — in the past too, not heeding my warning words, he became destined for <s>Avīci</s>. Listen to that.'

body.text:
The story of the King Caitika and the two sons of the Purohita
(concerning a previous life of the Buddha and Devadatta)
body.translated_text:
The story of King <s>Caitika</s> and the two sons of the <s>Purohita</s>
(concerning a previous life of the <s>Buddha</s> and <s>Devadatta</s>)

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'nyatamasyāṃ rājadhānyāṃ rājā caitiko nāma rājyaṃ kārayati ṛddhaṃ ca yāvad ākīrṇabahujanamanuṣyaṃ ca; puṇyānubhāvād devatā antarīkṣe āsanaṃ dhārayanti; tasya rājñaḥ purohitasya dvau putau jyeṣṭho kanīyāṃś ca; tatra jyeṣṭho naiṣkramyābhinandī; kanīyān paurohityābhinnandī; jyeṣṭhaḥ paśyati pitaraṃ dharmādharmeṇa paurohityaṃ kārayantaṃ; sa samlakṣayati; ahaṃ pitur atyayāt purohito bhaviyāmi; yannv aham api pravrajeyam iti; sa pitaram anujñāpya bhagavacchāsane pravrajitaḥ; yāvad apareṇa samayena purohitaḥ kālagataḥ; sa kanīyān paurohitye pratiṣṭhāpitaḥ; sa adharmeṇa paurohityaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ; janakāyaḥ pīḍyate; yāvad anyatamaḥ puruṣa itaś cāmutaś ca paribhramaṃs tasya (
body.translated_text: In the past, monks, in a certain royal capital, a king named <s>Caitika</s> was exercising sovereignty — it was prosperous, and teeming with a great multitude of people. By the power of his merit, deities held a seat aloft for him in the sky. The king's <s>purohita</s> (royal priest) had two sons — an elder and a younger. The elder delighted in renunciation; the younger delighted in the priesthood. The elder saw his father exercising the priesthood by both righteous and unrighteous means. He reflected: 'After my father's death, I shall become the <s>purohita</s>. Let me rather go forth.' Having obtained his father's permission, he went forth in the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s dispensation. At a later time, the <s>purohita</s> passed away. The younger son was established in the priesthood. He began to exercise the priesthood unrighteously. The people were oppressed. Then a certain man, wandering here and there, approached (

body.text: MSV IV 244
) jyeṣṭhasya (
body.translated_text: ) the elder (

body.text: SBV II 268

) pravrajitasya sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ; sa tena dṛṣṭaḥ: kutas tvam āgacchasīti; tena samākhyātam: amuṣyā rājadhānyāḥ; sa vārttāṃ praṣṭum ārabdhaḥ; sa kathayati: rājñaḥ purohitaḥ kālagataḥ; tasya kanīyān putraḥ paurohitye pratiṣṭhati; so 'dharmeṇa paurohityaṃ
body.translated_text: ) who had gone forth. He was seen by him: 'Where do you come from?' The man told him: 'From such-and-such a royal capital.' The elder began to ask for news. The man said: 'The king's <s>purohita</s> has passed away. His younger son has been established in the priesthood. He exercises the priesthood unrighteously.

body.translated_text: The people are oppressed.' The elder said: 'Wait some time. I shall go there myself and prevent what is harmful and establish what is beneficial, so that he does not oppress the people of the realm.' The man went and reported this matter to the kinsmen. By word of mouth it reached the younger brother. He reported to the king: 'Your Majesty, my elder brother is going to come.' The king said: 'Excellent! He shall be the <s>purohita</s>.' The younger said: 'Your Majesty, then I have served you all this time in vain!' The king said: 'This is the way of the world — he is the elder. However, I can arrange for the priesthood to remain with you by one means.' 'If, when he arrives, you say: "I am the elder."' He said: 'Very well, I shall say so.' When the elder arrived, the entire assembly including the king rose. But the younger did not rise. The elder said to him: 'You are my younger brother — why do you not rise?' He said: 'You are the younger one; I am the elder. If you don't believe me, let us ask the elders at the court and the king.' The elder asked the king: 'Tell me, O king — which of us two is the elder?' The king deliberately spoke a falsehood: 'He is the elder; you are the younger.' At the very moment of speaking those words, the deities (

body.translated_text: What do you think, monks? He who was the elder son of the <s>purohita</s> — that was I myself at that time, in that era. He who was King <s>Caitika</s> — that is this very <s>Devadatta</s> at that time, in that era. Even then, not heeding my warning words, he went to <s>Avīci</s> hell. body.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ: paśya bhadanta devadatto hitam ucyamāno vacanam aśṛṇvann avīciparāyaṇaḥ saṃvṛtta iti; bhagavān āha: na bhikṣava etarhi yathā atīte 'py adhvany eṣa mayā hitam ucyamāno vacanam aśṛṇvann anayena vyasanam āpannaḥ; tac chrūyatām
body.translated_text: The monks, having doubts arise, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, who cuts through all doubts: 'See, Venerable Sir, <s>Devadatta</s>, though told what is beneficial, not heeding the words, has become destined for <s>Avīci</s>.' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Not only now, monks — in the past too, though told by me what is beneficial, not heeding the words, he came to ruin and calamity. Listen to that.'

body.translated_text: ) began to learn the mechanical art. He sought a girl from a householder in a certain market-town. The householder said: 'If you come on such-and-such a day, I will give her; otherwise, no.' He reported this to the master-mechanic: 'Preceptor, in such-and-such a market-town there is a householder. I have sought a girl from him. He says: "If you come on such-and-such a day, I will give her; otherwise, no."' The master-mechanic said: 'Son, if so, let us go. I myself will receive her on your behalf.' Together with him, he mounted a wooden peacock [flying machine] and arrived at the market-town on the very day that was set as the deadline. Having seen it, the householder was filled with supreme amazement. Then, having accepted the girl, he mounted the machine again and returned home. He collected the machine and entrusted it to the mother, saying: 'This son of yours knows the method of operating the machine but not how to stop it. You must not give him the machine.' He repeatedly asked his mother: 'Mother, give me the machine — I shall impress a great multitude of people.' She said: 'Son, the teacher says of you: "This one knows the method of operation but not of stopping. Do not give it to him, or through his arrogance he will meet with disaster." Therefore I do not give it.' He said: 'Mother, I know both the operation and the stopping. But that teacher, out of jealousy, does not give it.' Women are fickle-minded; being persuaded, she gave it. He mounted the machine and set forth. The great multitude was impressed. Then the master-mechanic saw him. He said: 'This one has gone, not to return.' The more frantically he operated the machine (

āyuṣmān upālī buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ pṛcchati: ucyate bhadanta saṃghabhedaḥ ucyate bhadanta saṃghasāmagrī iti; tatra kataro bhedaḥ katarā saṃghasāmagrī; yataś copālin bhikṣavaḥ dharme 'dharmsaṃjñinaḥ adharme dharmasaṃjñino vyagre avyagrasaṃjñinaḥ karmāṇi kurvanti; ayam ucyate saṃghabhedaḥ; yatas tu dharme dharmasaṃjñinaḥ samagre samagrasaṃjñinaḥ karmāṇi kurvanti; iyam ucyate saṃghasāmagrī iti
  yatraiko bhikṣur na tatra saṃgho bhidyate; yatrau dvau yatra trayo yāvad aṣṭau na tatra saṃgho bhidyate; yatra nava bhikṣavo uttare vā tatra dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ saṃgho bhidyate; jñaptikarmaṇā śalākāgrahaṇena ca (
body.translated_text:
The Venerable <s>Upāli</s> asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'It is said, Venerable Sir, "<s>saṅghabheda</s>" (splitting of the community), and it is said, Venerable Sir, "<s>saṅghasāmagrī</s>" (unity of the community). What constitutes a split, and what constitutes unity?' 'When, <s>Upāli</s>, monks who perceive non-<s>Dharma</s> as <s>Dharma</s>, non-<s>Dharma</s> as <s>Dharma</s>, and what is discordant as concordant, perform formal acts — this is called <s>saṅghabheda</s>. But when monks who perceive <s>Dharma</s> as <s>Dharma</s> and what is concordant as concordant perform formal acts — this is called <s>saṅghasāmagrī</s>.'
  'Where there is one monk, the <s>Saṅgha</s> is not split; where there are two, or three, up to eight, the <s>Saṅgha</s> is not split. Where there are nine monks or more, the <s>Saṅgha</s> is split by two means: by a formal act of announcement and by taking of voting-sticks.' (

body.translated_text:
The Venerable <s>Upāli</s> asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has said, Venerable Sir, that by splitting a united community of disciples, one produces a transgression [leading to] <s>Avīci</s> [hell], and one is touched by the <s>karma</s> of an immediate [retribution] transgression. To what extent, Venerable Sir, does a monk, having split a united community of disciples, produce a transgression [leading to] <s>Avīci</s> and become touched by the <s>karma</s> of an immediate [retribution] transgression?'
  '(1) When, <s>Upāli</s>, a monk who perceives non-<s>Dharma</s> as <s>Dharma</s>, who perceives a split as non-<s>Dharma</s>, announces, instructs, teaches, and makes the monks understand, and strives for the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s> — to this extent, <s>Upāli</s>, a monk, having split a united community of disciples, produces a transgression [leading to] <s>Avīci</s> and is touched by the <s>karma</s> of an immediate [retribution] transgression.
  (2) When, <s>Upāli</s>, a monk who perceives non-<s>Dharma</s> as non-<s>Dharma</s>, who perceives a split as <s>Dharma</s>, announces, instructs, teaches, and makes the monks understand, and strives for the splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s> — to this extent, <s>Upāli</s>, a monk, having split a united community of disciples, produces a transgression [leading to] <s>Avīci</s> and is touched by the <s>karma</s> of an immediate [retribution] transgression. body.translated_text:
) Thus there are these eighteen [cases] in total. Of these, in six one is touched by the <s>ānantarya</s> (heinous) offense of that deed — those in which one perceives the schism as non-<s>Dharma</s>. The remaining ones are not touched by the <s>ānantarya</s> offense of that deed.
  The <s>Saṅghabhedavastu</s> (Section on the Splitting of the <s>Saṅgha</s>) in the <s>Vinaya</s> is concluded. // // The <s>Vinayavastvāgama</s> (Received Tradition of Vinaya Topics). // //
